papers.title: As El Niño builds, studies of extreme marine heatwaves must start now
papers.abstract: Researchers must track warming oceans and use the knowledge gained to inform strategies for sustaining fisheries and communities that depend on them.

papers.title: The psychology of imaginary friends — and why they are good for kids
papers.abstract: Children often conjure up invisible pals to keep them company. A psychologist delves into the reasons why.

papers.title: Is the sixth great extinction imminent? Scientists must draw on natural history for clues
papers.abstract: A lack of crosstalk between research disciplines is hampering scholars’ ability to fully examine how people have altered Earth’s biodiversity.

papers.title: Brønsted/Lewis acid-catalyzed divergent cascade cyclization of alkoxyallene for the total synthesis of eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids
papers.abstract: Eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids are two types of biogenetically related polycyclic monoterpenoid alkaloids with distinct structural features. Reported synthetic strategies typically construct the core architectures of eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids independently, and no protocol enabling their simultaneous synthesis has yet been developed. Herein, we describe the assembly of both eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloid skeletons from a common alkoxyallene precursor, a characteristic that aligns with their inherent biogenetic connection. Our investigations reveal that upon Prins-type spirocyclization of the alkoxyallene under Brønsted or Lewis acid catalysis, the intermediate undergoes two discrete tandem reaction pathways: Mannich-like cyclization/migration to construct the skeleton of eburnane alkaloids under Brønsted acid catalysis, whereas nucleophilic addition to the indole iminium assembles the aspidofractinine alkaloids framework under Lewis acid catalysis. The developed divergent cascade cyclization strategy has been successfully applied to the total synthesis of eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids including (−)-eburnamonine, (−)-eburnamenine, (+)-eburnamine, and (±)-aspidofractinine. Eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids are biogenetically related yet structurally distinct polycyclic monoterpenoids, whose syntheses have traditionally proceeded separately. Here, the authors report a divergent cascade from a common alkoxyallene precursor, enabling access to both scaffolds through acid controlled tandem pathways and total syntheses of representative alkaloids.

papers.title: Knowledge-guided machine learning deciphers spatiotemporal dynamics in chemical reactor systems
papers.abstract: Characterizing the spatiotemporal dynamics of complex chemical reactors, especially localized engineering-critical points or regions, remains challenging in process engineering. Although data-driven methods offer computational advantages, the incorporation of domain-specific physical knowledge can further enhance their predictive performance. Here, we present a physics-informed machine learning framework that systematically embeds coking mechanisms and heat transfer principles into neural network architecture and training constraints. Using a coke-accumulating cracking reactor as a prototypical case, the proposed approach reproduces the spatiotemporal distributions of key operational parameters obtained from conventional simulations with high fidelity and achieves a 105-fold computational acceleration. Crucially, the incorporation of mechanistic knowledge enhances prediction fidelity for critical safety indicators, particularly the maximum external wall temperature (error  < 0.5%), enabling precise identification of optimal decoking intervals. This paradigm bridges data efficiency with domain-informed modeling, providing a useful reference for developing real-time monitoring and optimization models for complex industrial systems. A physics-informed neural network embeds coking and heat transfer knowledge via an output integration layer and region-weighted loss to predict reactor spatiotemporal fields; it matches conventional simulation results, improves peak wall temperature accuracy, and runs about five orders of magnitude faster than conventional simulations.

papers.title: Improving molecular property prediction with score-based diffusion models
papers.abstract: We explore diffusion-based training as a flexible approach to molecular property prediction in settings shaped by chemical, biophysical, and latent heterogeneity. To address this, we build on score-based generative diffusion models and introduce a conditional diffusion module for predictive tasks, equipped with a joint training and sampling guidance scheme and an optional gated residual mechanism that regulates feature- vs target-driven information flow across noise levels. The module acts as a plug-in learning block for existing molecular encoders, making it complementary to advances in representation learning. Across diverse feature extractors and graph neural networks, diffusion-based training improves over conventional maximum-likelihood objectives on small-molecule regression benchmarks and matches or exceeds strong baselines on multitask regression and classification datasets. It also produces well-calibrated predictive uncertainty as measured by prediction interval coverage, enables confidence-guided ranking, and performs well in challenging settings including activity cliffs and class-imbalanced multitask prediction. Overall, these results position diffusion as a promising representation-agnostic approach for effective molecular property prediction. This work introduces a diffusion-based approach for small molecule prediction across a range of structure-activity and ADME tasks. It demonstrates strong predictive calibration and support for ensemble-driven uncertainty ranking.

papers.title: Structurally guided wavefront neural encoder for broad-range generalizable 3D holography
papers.abstract: Deep learning has advanced computer-generated holography, but learned models remain coupled to fixed wavelengths and distances, limiting generalization. Here we present the structurally guided wavefront neural encoder (SGWN-Encoder), which integrates diffraction physics with neural networks and employs a structural propagation strategy that analytically strips the parameter-sensitive global phase. This reveals a scale-normalized description of diffraction, letting the network learn transferable light-field evolution rules and generalize across propagation distances and visible wavelengths by direct inference. A dataset-free paradigm built on statistically diverse random fields teaches the model the structural mapping from complex amplitude to phase-only holograms instead of external image distributions. Without fine-tuning, a single SGWN-Encoder maintains a distance-averaged RGB PSNR of 31.9 dB and SSIM of 0.91 over the primary 2–200 mm range, retaining reconstruction up to 500 mm. Numerical and optical experiments on full-color 3D scenes establish a physically grounded route toward adaptive holographic displays. A single AI hologram generator works across distances and color without retraining, by learning how light scales — a step towards versatile, adaptive 3D holographic displays.

papers.title: Encapsulating an iron complex within a heme and anthraquinone codecorated capsule for multiphoton C(sp3)−H bond oxygenation
papers.abstract: The allosteric effect in proteins controls biological function omnipotently, but simulating both the regulatory functions and catalytic processes of analogues faces marked challenges. By encapsulating a non-heme FeIII-complex into the cavity of an anthraquinone and heme co-decorated coordination capsule, herein we report a light-responsive allosteric catalysis for activating O2 and metabolizing C(sp3)−H bonds. Light irradiation initially triggers the bridged FeIII-porphyrins switching into unbridged FeII/O=FeIV-porphyrin pair for substrate oxygenation. Parallelly exciting the anthraquinone groups sensitizes O2 to 1O2 via energy transfer, meanwhile exciting the non-heme FeIII-complexes generates the chlorine radicals via ligand-to-metal charge transfer. The capsules enforce heme and non-heme FeII fragments into proximity, forming an Fe−O − O−Fe intermediate with the reactive 1O2 species for O − O bond cleavage. Synergistic hydrogen abstraction by chlorine radicals and O=FeIV-porphyrin by combining multiple photons selectively and fleetly oxygenates thioxanthene to thioxanthen-9-one within the capsule pocket, therefore reshaping oxygenase for selective metabolism in a supramolecular approach. The allosteric effect in proteins controls biological function omnipotently, but simulating both the regulatory functions and catalytic processes of analogues is challenging. Here, the authors report the allosteric catalysis of a non-heme Fe(III)-complex encapsulated in the cavity of an anthraquinone and heme co-decorated coordination capsule.

papers.title: A precommissural nucleus-cingulate circuit coordinates a stress-induced agitation-like state
papers.abstract: Agitation combines motor restlessness with negative affect, yet the neural circuits coordinating these features remain unclear. We establish a chronic conditioned stress paradigm in mice that evokes a context-dependent agitation-like state marked by increased walking, reduced digging, altered bout kinematics and aversion, distinct from escape-like flight. Conditioned stress recruits predominantly glutamatergic cholecystokinin (CCK)-expressing neurons in the precommissural nucleus (Prc) and enhances their responses to conditioned cues. Projection screening identifies cingulate cortex area 2 (Cg2) as a behaviorally enriched output. Bidirectional manipulations show that Prc-CCK neurons and their Cg2 terminals are both sufficient for and required for key motor and avoidance-related components of this state. Local CCK-B receptor signaling contributes to pathway-evoked behavior. Selected recruitment and activation effects extend to female mice, whereas chronic unpredictable stress and remote retrieval delineate behavioral and temporal boundaries. Here, we show that a diencephalic-cingulate pathway coordinates stress-associated motor restlessness with negative valence. Agitation links motor restlessness with negative affect, but its circuit basis is unclear. Here, the authors show that a stress-sensitive Prc-CCK-to-Cg2 pathway coordinates motor restlessness with aversive behavior in mice.

papers.title: Identification and deployment of a wild soybean FD allele for high-density planting and increased yield
papers.abstract: Shortened internode length is a key agronomic trait that optimizes crop architecture and promotes adaptability to high-density planting. Loci that confer short internodes while increasing yield remain scarce in soybean. Here, using chromosome segment-substitution lines, we identify the REDUCED INTERNODE 2 (RIN2) locus, which encodes the basic leucine zipper (bZIP) transcription factor FDc1 that exerts a negative regulatory effect on internode length. The RIN2ZYD06 allele from wild soybean has a strong ability to suppress internode elongation compared to RIN2SN14 allele from cultivated soybean. The RIN2SN14 promoter exhibits lower expression than that of RIN2ZYD06, thereby fostering internode elongation. RIN2 binds to and activates the STF1 and STF2 promoters, the proteins of which in turn promote gibberellin catabolism in the shoot apex to reduce internode elongation. Dt1, which confers stem-growth habit, physically interacts with RIN2, attenuating RIN2-mediated transcriptional regulation. STF1/2 act downstream of Dt1 and RIN2. At field locations, RIN2ZYD06 confers increased yield per plant and per plot at high planting densities. Taken together, we elucidate the molecular mechanism of RIN2 regulating internode length and identify a wild allele that optimizes soybean architecture for high-density planting. Loci that confer short internodes while increasing yield remain scarce in soybean. Here, the authors report wild soybean-derived basic leucine zipper transcription factor FDc1 that exerts a negative regulator effect on internode length, which enhances dense planting and grain yield.

papers.title: Phenotypic discovery of GABA<sub>A</sub> receptor-mediated general anesthetics with analgesic activity
papers.abstract: General anesthetics are essential for invasive medical procedures; however, there remains a need for safer agents. Using a bespoke 96-well-plate format platform enabling high-throughput imaging of larval zebrafish behavior, we screen 12,000 compounds and identify an isoxazole chemotype that phenocopies the intravenous anesthetics etomidate and propofol. Its optimization via medicinal chemistry yields an anesthetic that we call nidradine. This anesthetic is efficacious in both zebrafish and mice and lacks the problematic adrenal suppression characteristic of etomidate. Mechanistic studies using electrophysiology and structural biology reveal that nidradine, like etomidate and propofol, is a positive allosteric modulator of the GABAA receptor. Remarkably, behavioral assays in mice demonstrate that nidradine differs from most general anesthetics in that it also produces analgesia at subsedative doses. In this study, high-throughput screening in zebrafish led to the discovery of nidradine, a new general anesthetic that acts on GABAA receptors and, unlike most general anesthetics, also relieves pain at non-sedating doses.

papers.title: Co-deficiency of RECQL1 and BLM causes replication stress associated with DNA damage and cohesion loss
papers.abstract: The mechanistic basis for chromosomal instability characteristic of RECQ helicase disorders remain difficult to understand due to their molecular genetic complexity. Here, the authors demonstrated that co-deficiency of RECQL1 and BLM helicases causes pronounced replication stress, DNA damage, and chromatid cohesion loss.

papers.title: Burst-like intracellular antibody infusion via membrane-permeabilizing peptide microcondensates
papers.abstract: Authors show that microcondensates composed of engineered IgGs bearing glutamic acid– and tyrosine-containing tag sequences together with a trimeric membrane permeabilizing L17E peptide [FcB(L17E) 3 ] enable burst-like, rapid intracellular infusion of IgG antibodies.

papers.title: MyoGen: unified biophysical modeling of human neuromotor activity and resulting signals
papers.abstract: Editorial summary: Simulating human motor control usually means treating spinal circuits, muscle mechanics, and EMG separately. Here the authors present MyoGen, an open-source framework that couples these elements and generates decomposable surface and intramuscular EMG.

papers.title: A near-quantum-limited diamond maser amplifier operating at millikelvin temperatures
papers.abstract: Amplifying faint microwave signals at millikelvin temperatures has so far relied entirely on superconducting devices. Here, authors demonstrate a diamond maser amplifier that works without superconductivity, reaching over 30 dB of gain and near-quantum-limited noise.

papers.title: Self-powered bubble motor microswarms for ultrasensitive detection, monitoring and prediction in cancer liquid biopsies
papers.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have shown great potential for disease detection from liquid biopsies. However, the lack of optimized isolation and detection methods limited their clinical application. Here we engineer a bioinspired, reconfigurable, self-powered bubble motor (Butor) microswarm to streamline intelligent isolation and ultrasensitive profiling of circulating EVs for cancer liquid biopsies. Butor microswarm shows jellyfish-like, self-propelled lifting locomotion along lumen-like vertical or inclined tubular path in parallel, allowing rapid isolation (10 min, near 90%) of EV subtypes via three-dimensional directional scanning capture even in high-viscosity biofluids. Furthermore, the buoyancy-activated Butors achieve ultrasensitive EV profiling near a single-particle level, enable early diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer with an accuracy of up to 94% (95% sensitivity) in a pilot cohort and improve the outcome in cancer staging (I–IV) discrimination, response monitoring of surgical treatment and efficacy prediction of immunotherapy in patients with non-small cell lung cancer. Our self-powered motor represents an intelligent, fast, inexpensive, sensitive and multiplexed liquid biopsy tool for accurate cancer diagnostics and treatment monitoring in clinical settings. A self-powered bubble motor inspired by microswarm motion enables ultrasensitive extracellular vesicles profiling, monitoring of surgical treatment response, staging discrimination, prediction of immunotherapy and early diagnosis in patients with non-small cell lung cancer.

papers.title: Two-dimensional material membranes with precisely tunable interlayer spacing from nanometre to submillimetre
papers.abstract: Precise and reversible control over ion channel size in membrane materials is crucial for realizing optimized device performance, but conventional approaches to channel regulation suffer from limited tunability, reversibility and precision. Here we report a deprotonation–ion coordination strategy for the precise, reversible modulation of interlayer spacing over five orders of magnitude in layered material membranes. The interlayer expansion is driven by electrostatic repulsion due to the deprotonation of intercalated cellulose nanofibers and is reversibly tunable via charge compensation through cation coordination. As a result, we achieve an unprecedented degree of structural tunability: porosity from 0% to 78%, interlayer spacing from 1.39 to 152,000 nm and membrane thickness from 43 to 5,400 μm. Our strategy enables on-demand performance customization with the same membrane platform. For example, a slight interlayer expansion (to 1.48 nm) boosts zinc-ion capacitance by 67% relative to non-expanded membranes; a 21,583-fold expansion (to ~30 μm) raises osmotic energy conversion power by 63%, and a 100,719-fold expansion (to ~140 μm) unlocks exceptional pressure sensing. These results establish a generalizable paradigm for nanometric microstructure engineering of various van der Waals materials. A deprotonation–ion coordination strategy is developed for microstructural engineering of layered material membranes, enabling the precise and reversible modulation of interlayer spacing over five orders of magnitude.

papers.title: Controlling the flow of information in optical metrology
papers.abstract: Optical metrology has surpassed the Abbe–Rayleigh limit by leveraging nonlinear phenomena and statistical accumulation, and has recently unlocked subatomic precision using artificial intelligence estimators trained on measurand variations. Here we argue that further gains can be achieved by optimizing the flow of Fisher information carrying metrological content. We show that Fisher information flow need not follow the optical energy flow and that it exhibits resonance, diffraction and interference, singular points, and vorticity. It can exhibit a Talbot-like effect in which Fisher information density patterns repeat periodically with propagation distance, and it can be focused beyond the diffraction limit, mirroring the effect of optical superoscillation. Material composition, resonances, geometry and environment determine where information is generated, how it propagates, and how it can be enhanced and directed to improve precision. This perspective recasts metrology as information flow engineering, for applications ranging from atomic-scale diagnostics and smart manufacturing to remote sensing, radar and LiDAR. By treating Fisher information as a conserved wave quantity, nanophotonic systems can be designed to control information generation and flow, opening a route to improve optical measurement and sensing precision.

papers.title: Interpretable distance-resolved graph learning for cancer gene priority screening
papers.abstract: Systematic screening for cancer genes (CGs) is still a central goal in precision oncology, yet integrating sparse and spatially dispersed oncogenic signals to identify testable candidates remains challenging. Here we present CGMap, an interpretable graph-learning framework that uses a width-oriented parallel architecture to prioritize potential CGs from biomolecular networks and trace mechanistic cues. By constructing distance-resolved channels, CGMap localizes spatially dispersed CG signals across multiple topological scales while avoiding representation homogenization. A global diffusion module quantifies gene cooperativity along pathway contexts and yields traceable virtual interactions that map predictions to potential regulatory hypotheses, providing intrinsic interpretability for model decisions. Across multiple biomolecular networks in a pan-cancer setting, CGMap analysed 12,022 genes, consistently outperformed existing methods while remaining computationally efficient and prioritized 70 reliable candidates, including those previously unannotated in established databases. Importantly, the prioritized candidates were associated with the suppression of tumour-related phenotypes, including reduced cell proliferation, migration and invasion, along with a shift of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-related features toward a non-mesenchymal state, as supported by parallel loss-of-function assays across cancer and non-malignant cell lines. Wang et al. propose CGMap, a distance-resolved graph-learning framework that maps dispersed oncogenic signals into structured priorities, narrowing the cancer gene candidate space and establishing an interpretable path from hypotheses to practical validation.

papers.title: Echidna: a Bayesian framework for integrative inference of copy number alterations impacting phenotypic plasticity
papers.abstract: The ability of cells to adapt their behavior in response to genetic or environmental changes is a fundamental biological process that drives cellular diversity in both normal and pathological contexts, including in tumor evolution. Copy number alterations (CNAs), which can include large-scale changes in genomic ploidy, play a key role in creating adaptive advantages in evolving cell populations. However, tracing these populations across experiments and disentangling the role of CNAs from other sources of transcriptional variability remains challenging and expensive. Here we present Echidna, a Bayesian hierarchical model that integrates single-cell RNA sequencing and bulk whole-genome sequencing data to enable robust integrative inference of CNAs, jointly across samples and treatment time points, to better understand the impact of genomic events on cellular phenotype. Applying Echidna to patient tumor specimens, we demonstrate its superior performance in clonal reconstruction and derive insights into therapy resistance mechanisms. Echidna integrates genomic and transcriptomics data to reveal how copy number alterations shape tumor evolution and therapy resistance.

papers.title: Joint single-cell capture of Cas9 edits and transcriptomes reveals on- and off-target effects on gene expression
papers.abstract: A longstanding barrier in genome engineering with CRISPR–Cas9 has been the inability to measure editing outcomes and their functional effects at single-cell resolution. Here we present Superb-seq, which captures single-cell edits and transcriptome effects by integrating Cas9 editing, T7 in situ transcription and single-cell RNA sequencing. We performed Superb-seq on 35,000 cells from three cell lines. Using seven guide RNAs to target four chromatin remodeler genes in 10,000 K562 cells, Superb-seq detected 5,761 edited cells, all on-target sites and 36 off-target sites. Superb-seq improved estimation of downstream perturbation effects on gene expression compared to Perturb-seq. We compared Superb-seq to 4 bulk off-target detection methods and identified between 6 and 210 edit sites across 3 benchmarking guides. Nineteen off-target edits were associated with differential gene expression, nine of which were cell type-specific. In summary, Superb-seq illuminates the consequences of Cas9 genome editing by connecting single-cell edits with changes in gene expression. Superb-seq integrates CRISPR–Cas9, T7 in situ transcription and scRNA-seq to capture genome edits and gene expression in single cells.

papers.title: Tracing the genetic roots of cellular identity in tumors
papers.abstract: A new Bayesian framework, Echidna, integrates bulk whole-genome sequencing with single-cell RNA sequencing to connect clonal copy-number states with transcriptional programs, providing a tractable way to ask how much of a tumor cell’s identity is encoded by its genome.

papers.title: A CD7-targeted AAV variant enables efficient T and NK cell engineering in vivo
papers.abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors have been applied for precise genome engineering in human T cells but poor tropism restricts their efficiency and translational potential. Here, through directed evolution of the AAV6 capsid in primary human T cells, we identified a family of variants containing an APR motif at residues 455–457. The lead candidate, AAV.APR31, enabled robust transduction of primary T and NK cells at nearly 100–1,000-fold lower doses than AAV6 and outperformed the human T cell-tropic capsid AAV-hT7. CRISPR screening identified CD7 as a lineage-specific entry enhancer alongside the canonical AAVR pathway and structural analysis suggested that the APR motif facilitates CD7 engagement. Unlike existing delivery systems confined to one engineering mode, AAV.APR31 enabled transient transgene delivery, site-specific knock-in and transposon integration in human T and NK cells, generating CAR-T cells functionally equivalent to lentiviral vector-manufactured products. Systemic administration of AAV.APR31-generated CAR-T cells in vivo resulted in potent tumor control in hematologic and solid tumor mouse models. Adeno-associated virus vectors targeted to CD7 enable T and NK cell engineering in vivo.

papers.title: Life-cycle assessment and exergy analysis of enzymatic polyethylene terephthalate recycling
papers.abstract: Zheng-Jie Qian and colleagues model the enzymatic PET recycling process through life-cycle assessment and exergy analysis, identifying the key factors influencing its sustainability. The optimized process reduces global warming potential and resource depletion intensity by 31% and 17%, respectively, compared to the petrochemical route.

papers.title: Quantum annealing for customer segmentation: a proof-of-concept QUBO framework for supply chain clustering
papers.abstract: This article investigates the potential of quantum clustering, specifically through quantum annealing, to enhance supply chain segmentation compared with classical K-Means. Using a proof-of-concept framework, clustering is translated into a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimisation formulation, tested on customer datasets via both classical Simulated Annealing and D-Wave’s Leap hybrid solver, with penalty parameter optimisation introduced to address solver sensitivity. Performance is benchmarked against K-Means on runtime, accuracy metrics, and scalability, across dataset sizes from 200 to 5,000 points. Results show that while K-Means maintains superior inertia and stability, the hybrid quantum approach achieves faster solver-reported runtimes and, on a simplified 200-point, two-feature benchmark, delivers improved silhouette, Davies-Bouldin, Calinski-Harabasz, and Dunn scores once penalties are optimised — metrics which, it is noted, reward the balanced partitions structurally favoured by the pairwise QUBO objective. However, scalability remains constrained by current qubit capacity and solver access, limiting practical deployment beyond mid-sized datasets. The study concludes that classical methods remain dominant for industrial-scale segmentation; the demonstrated framework, penalty-optimisation pipeline, and objective-level analysis nonetheless provide a documented foundation, grounded in a customer segmentation case study, upon which future quantum-assisted supply chain clustering can build as hardware matures.

papers.title: SMFFX: a signal processing-inspired feature extraction framework for viral genomic sequences classification
papers.abstract: In recent years, the coronavirus and other viral diseases increasing rate have attracted significant attention. Viral data can be analyzed at the intracellular level in the form of genomic sequences. This study introduced a signal processing approach applied to the corresponding signals of viral genomic sequences. The Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC) algorithm, based on windowing techniques, enabled examination of genetic samples for feature extraction. Various statistical features were extracted from the resulting feature space, enabling classification algorithms to accurately identify and distinguish among the different virus types with high efficiency. The proposed approach was evaluated on 173,228 samples across 30 types of viruses using both binary and multi-class classification tasks. In the binary classification test, the proposed approach achieved accuracy and F1-scores of more than 0.99 using a decision tree classifier. In the multi-class classification mode, an accuracy of 0.99 and an F1-score exceeding 0.98 were achieved. In the one-versus-rest classes analysis, most classes achieved more than 99% F1-score, and AUC values. The high classification performance indicates the reliable predictive capability of the proposed approach. The feature-importance analysis provides the potential applicability to similar classification tasks involving other viruses or viral variants.

papers.title: An anatomy aware Mamba framework for video based 3D human pose estimation
papers.abstract: Video-based 3D human pose estimation suffers from depth ambiguity and faces great challenges in modeling long‑range spatial and temporal dependencies. Diffusion models have emerged as a powerful paradigm for this task. However, their denoisers commonly rely on Transformer backbones, where quadratic self-attention complexity limits computational efficiency. We propose AnatoMamba, an anatomy-aware Mamba framework for diffusion-driven 3D human pose estimation. AnatoMamba employs Articulated Pyramid Pooling to aggregate multiscale body context, Kinematic Wave Scanning to serialize joints according to skeletal topology, and Anatomical Signature Injection to explicitly encode body-part membership. The derived anatomy-aware features are further refined through bidirectional spatial and temporal state space modeling to capture inter-joint dependencies and cross frame motion patterns. With 243-frame inputs and 10.44 million trainable parameters, AnatoMamba-L achieves an MPJPE of 38.5 mm on Human3.6M. In cross-dataset evaluation on MPI-INF-3DHP, it achieves 98.9% PCK, 87.5 AUC, and 14.7 mm MPJPE. These results demonstrate competitive pose estimation accuracy with a compact parameter footprint.

papers.title: Lifelong vehicle re-identification via ResNet50 with depthwise spatial attention
papers.abstract: The core task of vehicle re-identification is to recognize vehicles with the same identity across different scenes. Existing methods, relying on fixed-dataset training, struggle to cope with continuously updating multi-domain vehicle data in real-world scenarios, and thus suffer significant performance degradation under data distribution shifts. While lifelong learning techniques can gradually accumulate multi-domain knowledge, they suffer from catastrophic forgetting of historical discriminative features and adapt inefficiently to new domains, particularly in preserving cross-domain spatial cues (e.g., component structure, contour details). To address this, this paper proposes a lifelong vehicle ReID model based on ResNet50, which embeds the depthwise spatial attention module. By leveraging depthwise separable convolution to dynamically focus on cross-domain invariant spatial regions such as the grille, headlights and vehicle contours, the model enhances local discriminative features to mitigate feature drift. The model couples two mechanisms: the depthwise spatial attention module preserves historical discriminative spatial features and curbs catastrophic forgetting, while the feature alignment loss maintains consistent multi-domain representations and balances old and new knowledge. Extensive experiments on VeRi-776, VRIC, and VehicleID show that, among the lifelong methods compared under a common protocol, the proposed method attains the highest accuracy—77.0% mAP and 78.7% R1 on average—while storing no historical images and requiring the lowest peak training memory of 7.2 GB.

papers.title: ​​QSVQ-Net: A morphology-conditioned spiking–variational quantum network for interpretable brain tumour MRI classification
papers.abstract: Accurate, interpretable classification of brain tumours from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is central to treatment planning, yet high-performing deep models are often poorly calibrated and rarely tested beyond a single dataset. We present QSVQ-Net, a hybrid quantum-classical framework that couples an EfficientNet-B0 backbone and a complex-valued spiking neural network to a morphology-conditioned variational quantum circuit, in which eighteen morphological and radiomic descriptors parameterise the qubit rotations through a learnable mapping. Evaluation covers five-fold cross-validation with confidence intervals, calibration, a matched multi-seed ablation, intrinsic circuit characterisation, auxiliary localisation for mask-free inference and external validation against classical baselines. On the BRISC-2025 test partition, QSVQ-Net attains 98.8% accuracy with an expected calibration error of 0.006; under five-fold cross-validation it reaches 99.48% (95% CI 98.91–100.0), statistically indistinguishable from EfficientNet-B0 (99.57%; paired t-test p = 0.59). The quantum branch performs within confidence-interval overlap of a parameter-matched classical control, so we claim no quantum accuracy advantage. On an independent mask-free dataset, accuracy falls to 72.6% while classical baselines retain 90–93%, a limitation we trace to the morphology branch. QSVQ-Net thus offers a reproducible, transparently characterised quantum-classical design and a candid account of where morphology-conditioned quantum encoding helps and where it does not.

papers.title: Study on the deformation characteristics and fracture development laws of the shaft coal pockets inner wall
papers.abstract: The shaft coal pocket is a critical component of the transportation system in underground coal mines, its deformation or structural damage poses a direct threat to the safety and continuity of mine operations. As the shaft wall are semi-hidden structures, the deformation and damage are difficult to detect, so the research about the mechanisms of deformation and damage lags behind the development of the coal industry. During the load and unload of coal (gangue) in the shaft coal pocket, the repeated load-unload and dynamic impact of loose granular particles on the bunker wall lead to a complex and variable deformation and damage process. This paper employs comprehensive research methods, including theoretical analysis, mechanical experiments, similarity simulations, and numerical analysis. Study the deformation and damage mechanisms of the shaft wall in underground coal mines. Reveal the deformation and failure mechanism of the shaft coal pocket inner wall. The research indicate that deformation and damage of shaft wall under combined load can be divided into four stages: elastic deformation, plastic deformation, crack propagation and structural instability. The damage mechanisms of shaft wall are primarily related to the applied loads. Once under prolonged external load, the mechanical state of the shaft wall changes, initially cause localized damage. As the damage progresses, cracks and fissures develop. When the stress on the shaft coal inner wall exceeds the allowable stress of the concrete material, structural instability and failure occur. When the primary load on the shaft walls is from internal loose granular particles, the failure type is predominantly shear failure. When the primary load comes from weak rock layers on the exterior, the failure type is primarily tensile failure. When both factors act simultaneously, it results in combined tensile-shear failure.

papers.title: Improved MGLR control charts based on Klein’s sensitizing rules for joint mean and dispersion monitoring under measurement error
papers.abstract: Shewhart-type control charts, despite their simplicity and satisfactory performance in detecting large shifts, are not sufficiently sensitive to small process changes. On the other hand, in many real-world applications, an assignable cause simultaneously affects both the location and dispersion parameters of the process. Furthermore, despite advances in data-collection technologies, measurement errors remain unavoidable, and their effects on control-chart performance should therefore be considered. Motivated by these considerations, this paper has two objectives. First, two enhanced versions of the multivariate generalized likelihood ratio (MGLR) control chart are developed by incorporating Klein’s 2-of-2 and 2-of-3 sensitizing rules to accelerate the detection of small shifts in the process mean, dispersion, or both. Second, the improved charts are modified under an additive covariate model to account for the effect of measurement error. The effectiveness of the proposed monitoring schemes, and the adverse effects of measurement error are evaluated through extensive simulations, considering various out-of-control scenarios and error variance levels using average run length (ARL), standard deviation of the run length (SDRL), and median run length (MRL). Additionally, an extensive sensitivity analysis is conducted to evaluate the effects of subgroup size ($$n$$) and process dimensionality ($$p$$), revealing that increasing the sample size substantially improves the detectability of all charts, whereas process dimensional growth degrades their detection sensitivity. The results indicate that measurement error diminishes the sensitivity of all control charts to process changes, even at low levels of error variance. Nevertheless, the 2-of-2 and 2-of-3 schemes substantially outperform the classical MGLR chart across all shift scenarios and error variance levels, with the 2-of-3 scheme performing slightly better than the 2-of-2 counterpart.

papers.title: Physics-anchored fault-cell localization in electric vehicle battery packs with variable cell counts
papers.abstract: Identifying a faulty cell from battery-management records is difficult when operating trends affect all cells and different diagnostic indicators favour different candidates. Here we present PhyFuseCell, a physics-anchored ranking method for packs with variable cell counts. Both branches reference cell voltages to the pack median: one characterizes charge-residual magnitudes and trends, while the other learns normalized discharge patterns. A shared cell encoder and scorer, together with valid-cell masking, accommodate different pack sizes. The evidence scores are standardized within each pack and combined with equal weights. On CH-BatteryGen packs with 28 or 124 cells, the compact implementation achieved the highest mean Top-1 localization accuracy among the evaluated methods, at 98.0 ± 2.7% across five vehicle-held-out splits, 7.0 percentage points above a validation-tuned clustering baseline. Paired predictions showed how complementary evidence corrected competing cell rankings. In self-discharge transfer without target-group training, adding target-pack charge evidence increased mean accuracy from 61.0 to 83.8% for 28-to-124-cell transfer and from 66.3 to 94.7% in reverse. These results support organizing physical and temporal evidence at the cell level to improve fault localization across the evaluated pack sizes.

papers.title: Research on super-resolution reconstruction technology of atmospheric turbulence phase screens based on deep learning
papers.abstract: Atmospheric turbulence phase screens are commonly utilized to calculate the transmission of light in the atmosphere. The key to accurately generating an atmospheric turbulence phase screen is to satisfy the statistical characteristics of atmospheric turbulence. Traditional methods for generating turbulence phase screens are limited by high computational complexity. Therefore, enhancing the image quality of turbulence phase screens is of utmost importance. This paper presents a super-resolution reconstruction algorithm for atmospheric turbulence phase screens based on deep learning. The proposed model integrates the statistical properties of atmospheric turbulence into the neural network and incorporates the wavefront phase structure function to modify the loss function. Experimental results demonstrate that the atmospheric turbulence phase screens generated by the improved super-resolution convolutional neural networks (ISRCNN) are substantially consistent with theoretical values in terms of statistical characteristics. The proposed method achieves a modest improvement over bicubic interpolation and super-resolution convolutional neural networks (SRCNN) models with respect to statistical properties.

papers.title: Experimental data-based analysis and intelligent prediction of smoke production characteristics for typical PMMA fire loads in substations
papers.abstract: Accurate characterization and early prediction of smoke production are essential for fire-risk assessment in substations, where polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) is a typical fire load. Cone-calorimeter tests were conducted on 5 and 25 mm PMMA specimens, with three replicate trials each. Seven time-resolved combustion variables, including smoke production rate (SPR), heat release rate, and gas concentrations, were recorded throughout the full combustion cycle. Using a 30 s historical window, K-nearest-neighbor (KNN), long short-term memory (LSTM), and Transformer models were trained to forecast SPR at horizons of 5, 15, and 30 s, with one complete trial held out for independent cross-trial testing. The 5 mm specimens showed a short, concentrated smoke-production process, whereas smoke production from the 25 mm specimens persisted for more than 1800 s; despite a 26.8% lower peak SPR, their total smoke production (68.73 ± 15.88 m²) was approximately 10.3 times that of the 5 mm specimens. Among the three PMMA smoke models developed from the experimental data, Transformer achieved R² greater than 0.8 under both scenarios and was the better performing of the three models. Error analysis revealed an increasing tendency to underpredict SPR at longer horizons, and SHAP analysis showed that model reliance shifted from historical SPR toward material consumption and combustion-state features.

papers.title: Timbre variation in weakly coupled multiple-metronome network encourages integrative beat perception and enhances individual differences
papers.abstract: Auditory textures can emerge from large-scale ensembles of rhythmic sound sources, such as insects’ percussive clicks or birds’ vocal calls. These “swarms” of overlapping events are sometimes identified by listeners as a single texture, or perceived as containing certain rhythmic structures, depending on different levels of embedded synchrony. Our previous study demonstrated that even within the same synchrony level, individual listeners’ ability to extract beat-like rhythmicity widely varies. The present study further investigates how introducing timbral variation into such textures affects their perception. Using a generative model of forty phase-coupled oscillators, we presented participants with metronome sounds under varying coupling strengths, either with identical or slight timbre differences and asked them to tap along however they feel the ‘beat.’ Results revealed that slight timbral heterogeneity encouraged more regular tapping responses in weaker coupling conditions in a subset of participants, particularly those who were already able to elucidate regular beats without timbre variation. We suggest that, for some listeners, timbre may serve as a perceptual anchor that facilitates integrative, rather than sequential, rhythm processing. These findings shed light on the interaction between timbre and individual differences in temporal perception.

papers.title: Environmental threat classification from mel-spectrograms using an augmented 2D CNN with sub-second CPU inference
papers.abstract: Illegal logging threatens biodiversity, carbon storage and ecological stability, yet ranger patrols and camera networks are costly, spatially limited and rarely provide timely alerts. This paper presents ForestEar, a proof-of-concept framework that classifies 2-second audio clips as Safe, Illegal Activity or Environmental Risk using a two-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) applied to log-mel spectrograms. In the absence of a labelled forest-threat corpus, classes from the public ESC-50 and UrbanSound8K datasets were remapped as proxy labels, and stochastic augmentation was applied to minority classes. On a held-out test partition, a binary Safe-versus-Illegal-Activity evaluation (n = 338) reached 92.9% accuracy, with recall of 0.95 (Safe) and 0.90 (Illegal Activity). A three-class configuration that adds the Environmental Risk class is demonstrated in a preliminary evaluation, which identified Environmental Risk as the most difficult class. Per-clip inference took approximately 250 ms on a laptop CPU. Because the results derive from proxy benchmark data, a single data split that was not grouped by source recording, and single training runs, they demonstrate feasibility under benchmark conditions rather than field performance. Validation on forest recordings and on embedded hardware remains future work.

papers.title: Broadband amplification of organ of Corti vibrations in the mouse cochlear apex
papers.abstract: Mammalian hearing depends on the active amplification of sound-evoked waves as they travel along the basilar membrane within the cochlea. This amplification is mediated by the outer hair cells (OHCs), which generate force to enhance the vibrations of the surrounding structures. While OHCs at a given location only amplify basilar membrane motion for a narrow frequency range, recent measurements show that the amplification of motions deeper within the organ of Corti is much more broadband. However, the extent to which this broadband amplification influences the motions that are most relevant to inner hair cell stimulation – i.e., at the organ’s apical surface – remains uncertain. Here, optical coherence tomography was used to demonstrate that OHCs nonlinearly amplify the motions near the top of the organ of Corti, including at the reticular lamina and tectorial membrane, over a wide frequency range in the mouse cochlear apex. Responses at all frequencies were physiologically vulnerable and grew compressively with stimulus level. Low-frequency responses also exhibited non-monotonic features that were due to interference between amplified motion and the underlying traveling wave. The data suggest that broadband amplification of motions at the top of the organ of Corti likely explains certain phenomena observed in auditory nerve responses.

papers.title: Time-series field phenotyping and GWAS reveal QTL underlying yield potential in Amaranthus tricolor
papers.abstract: Amaranthus tricolor is a climate-resilient, nutrient-rich crop, but its genetic improvement is hindered by a lack of systematic phenotypic and yield trait data. In this study, 362 genetically diverse accessions were evaluated over two seasons under field conditions using a high-throughput phenotyping platform equipped with the PlantEye F500 multispectral sensor, enabling daily, non-invasive 3D imaging of plant development. Scanner-derived plant height, leaf area, digital biomass, and the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) were quantified throughout growth. Two accessions, VI056855A and VI047897, consistently exhibited superior performance and are potential breeding materials. A genome-wide association study (GWAS) revealed 52 significant SNPs for yield-related traits and 6 for NDVI. ATR1.0CH10_6710679 (yield-related traits) and ATR1.0CH06_11239836 (NDVI) were each detected in both seasons. Accessions carrying the high-NDVI allele of ATR1.0CH06_11239836 exhibited both high- and low-yield performance, suggesting that variation in leaf pigmentation may complicate the interpretation of NDVI as an indicator of plant performance in A. tricolor. By integrating high-throughput phenotyping with GWAS, this study provides a foundation for dissecting the genetic basis of yield-related traits in A. tricolor and a framework that may be applicable to other underutilized crops.

papers.title: Safe and efficient positioning control of an offshore wind turbine installation vessel
papers.abstract: This article proposes a safe and efficient positioning control method for offshore wind turbine installation vessels (OWTIVs), addressing the challenges posed by unmeasured multi-source disturbances and thruster constraints. First, a prescribed-time composite disturbance observer (PTCDO) is developed to accurately estimate multi-source disturbances. Building on this, an adaptive robust prescribed performance control (PPC) law is designed to enhance the dynamic performance of the OWTIV and ensure operational safety. Additionally, a finite-time auxiliary dynamic system is introduced to address the effects of input magnitude and rate constraints. To further improve positioning accuracy, the control framework integrates finite-time command filtered backstepping (FTCFB) technology with PTCDO and PPC, forming a finite-time DP control law with prescribed performance. The finite-time stability of the positioning system is rigorously proven using Lyapunov stability theory. Finally, the proposed positioning control strategy is validated through numerical simulations, including performance assessments under partial failure conditions of the disturbance observer, demonstrating its effectiveness and robustness.

papers.title: Theory of mind inspired mental state reasoning with large language models for empathetic response generation
papers.abstract: As conversational AI expands into emotionally sensitive domains such as mental health support and counseling, empathetic response generation has become a key research challenge. Existing empathetic dialogue systems either reflect the user’s surface level emotions or, when relying on external commonsense knowledge bases, capture only generic patterns. We propose a Theory of Mind inspired framework in which a large language model first infers the speaker’s five mental states of Belief, Desire, Emotion, Intent, and Knowledge from the multi turn dialogue history and then uses them as conditioning signals for empathetic response generation. A preliminary study on a theory of mind benchmark indicates that the LLMs employed perform reasonably on mental state inference in both multiple choice and free form settings. On an empathetic dialogue dataset, injecting the self generated inferences improved response quality under both automatic metrics and LLM as judge evaluation. In the LoRA fine-tuned setting, the ToM condition performed comparably to COMET, an external commonsense knowledge baseline, with higher ROUGE-L point estimates for all four backbones and a significant advantage for one. Shuffled and corrupted descriptions consistently degraded response quality, whereas the ToM condition and a context-grounded factual-summary control performed similarly, indicating that contextual grounding is the primary source of the benefit. These findings suggest that speaker grounded mental state reasoning can be an effective strategy for empathetic dialogue systems.

papers.title: Integrating geometry-aware radial-angular perturbation and topology-aware contrastive learning for heterogeneous graphs
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous information networks (HINs) model multiple node types and semantic relations, but existing heterogeneous graph contrastive learning methods still face two limitations. Random perturbations may disturb fragile cross-type structures, and local message-passing encoders may be limited in capturing long-range dependencies and broader structural cues. To address these limitations, we propose Geometry-aware radial-angular perturbation and Topology-aware contrastive learning (Geo-Top), a heterogeneous graph contrastive learning framework that combines topology-aware encoding with geometry-aware radial-angular latent perturbation. Geo-Top uses an SVD-inspired learnable low-rank topology factorization to model meta-path-induced adjacency relations and injects the resulting structural factors into attention computation through gradient decoupling. This design enables topology-aware attention to couple local semantics with non-local structural cues. Geo-Top further introduces radial-angular perturbations in the latent tangent representation to generate structured augmented samples. Together with shallow feature masking, cross-view contrastive learning, and momentum target encoders, these modules support semantic-view consistency and topology-aware representation learning. Experiments on five public heterogeneous graph datasets show strong node-classification performance. Geo-Top leads the reported clustering metrics on DBLP, AMiner, and Freebase, while the results on ACM and IMDb show that clustering benefits depend on the dataset. Component ablations characterize the contributions of topology-aware encoding and latent augmentation across classification and clustering.

papers.title: Pedagogical incorporation of generative AI in university visual effects courses and its implications for learning assessment and institutional support
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is entering university visual effects courses, but how students’ informal uses become part of teaching and assessment remains unclear. This interpretivist multiple-case study examined practices at three Chinese universities through 45 interviews with 36 teachers, students, and staff, 15 observations, course documents, student work, and available GenAI-use records. Within-case and cross-case analysis developed four themes: uneven movement from student experimentation into course workflows; the use of generated alternatives in comparison and revision; reported uncertainty about technical competence and creative control when outputs appear polished; and attempts to make student decisions and contributions visible. Across the cases, participants’ accounts and available records suggest that the meaning of GenAI use depended on task objectives, teacher guidance, assessment requirements, and institutional support. Process visibility offers a way to examine the boundary between assistance and substitution through students’ intentions, selections, revisions, and explanations. Because the study did not directly measure learning or competence, these are contextual interpretations rather than demonstrated educational effects.

papers.title: Comparison of aluminum and iron electrodes for electrocoagulation of automotive cataphoresis wastewater: removal performance and operating cost
papers.abstract: This study investigated the applicability of the electrocoagulation (EC) process to wastewater generated by the electrocoating (cataphoresis) process used in the painting of vehicle bodies. Samples were obtained from an automotive factory in Bursa, Türkiye. In a laboratory-scale EC reactor equipped with Al–Al or Fe–Fe electrodes, the operating parameters that govern the removal of chemical oxygen demand (COD) and total phosphorus (TP) — inter-electrode distance, current density, and reaction time — were optimized. A Box–Behnken response surface design (Design-Expert 12.0) was used to construct mathematical models, whose adequacy was assessed by analysis of variance (ANOVA). Under the optimum conditions for Al electrodes, removal efficiencies of 74.88% (COD) and 95.37% (TP) were achieved individually, and 74.72% (COD) and 79.28% (TP) simultaneously. With Fe electrodes, the highest measured COD removal was 83.3%, and the TP removal was 61.42% individually and 83.30% (COD) and 46.20% (TP) simultaneously; the quadratic model fitted to the Fe–COD data was not statistically significant and was therefore used only descriptively. Operating costs at current (July 2026) unit prices were 63.8 TL/m³ (US$ 1.35) for Al electrodes and 72.6 TL/m³ (US$ 1.54) for Fe electrodes.

papers.title: Optimal multi-objective configuration of a hybrid walker-star/delta navigation satellite constellation in LEO via MOPSO and reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: Optimal design of satellite constellations in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) for global navigation and positioning applications is of significant importance. This study presents a design framework for LEO satellite constellations based on hybrid Walker-Star/Delta geometric configurations, with the objective of simultaneously minimizing Geometric Dilution of Precision (GDOP) and deployment costs. A multi-objective optimization approach is employed by integrating Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) with Reinforcement Learning (RL) to adaptively tune key optimization parameters and the resulting RL-MOPSO algorithm is validated against conventional MOPSO and NSGA-II on standard benchmark problems. Satellite manufacturing and launch costs are estimated using a combined SSCM/USCM8 cost model and the design tool is further validated against the operational GLONASS constellation. The proposed hybrid configuration is evaluated against conventional Walker-Delta and Walker-Star configurations across multiple orbital altitudes. Results show that the optimized hybrid configuration achieves a notable improvement in mean GDOP compared with both Walker-Delta and Walker-Star configurations, while maintaining a comparable number of satellites and avoiding any significant increase in deployment cost. These findings demonstrate that the proposed RL-MOPSO based hybrid configuration is an effective approach for designing high-accuracy, cost-efficient LEO navigation constellations for future global navigation and precise positioning applications.

papers.title: Comparative evaluation of load transfer and coupling techniques for soil–structure interaction in 3D building models
papers.abstract: The distinct separation of structural and geotechnical numerical modelling often results in inadequate representation of soil–structure interaction (SSI), with simplified coupling methods such as the subgrade reaction approach neglecting nonlinear and time-dependent soil behaviour. This study evaluates a methodological framework for SSI analysis by comparing decoupled modelling approaches against holistic three-dimensional benchmark models developed in SOFiSTiK and PLAXIS for an eight-storey high-rise building on a raft foundation. The framework systematically examines five foundation load transfer approaches (ranging from smeared surface loads to discrete nodal force extraction) and three structural–geotechnical coupling strategies, assessing their accuracy in reproducing benchmark foundation settlements and raft bending moments. The results show that simplified smeared load approaches yield settlement deviations exceeding 15 %, whereas discrete nodal forces with explicit superstructure stiffness achieve near-perfect benchmark agreement. Conventional subgrade reaction moduli, whether constant or variable, exhibit error margins from $$-40$$ to $$+40$$ %, while the exchange of imposed settlement troughs reproduces benchmark results with deviations below 1 %. These findings demonstrate that replacing stiffness-parameter exchange with nodal-displacement transfer substantially reduces settlement and bending moment deviations, providing a practicable and more accurate basis for SSI analysis in structural and geotechnical engineering practice.

papers.title: Analytical investigation of the fractional Gilson-Pickering equation: a study of bright and dark solitons
papers.abstract: In this article, we investigates about the fractional Gilson–Pickering equation by employing the Sine-Gordon expansion method (SGEM) in the framework of the beta derivative. This is a useful tool for analyzing complex nonlinear systems. The classical Gilson–Pickering equation is extended to its fractional form using the beta derivative to capture more realistic dynamics of nonlinear wave propagation. The obtained solutions include solitary wave (soliton), periodic, dark, bright soliton and complex combined dark-bright soliton solutions, which demonstrate the rich dynamical behavior of the fractional model. The influence of the fractional parameter are analyzed, showing that it significantly affects wave amplitude, width, and propagation characteristics. Furthermore, the obtained solutions are illustrated graphically through two-dimensional (2D), three-dimensional (3D), and contour plots, which provide clear insight into the physical behavior and evolution of the wave profiles. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of SGEM and highlight the impact of the fractional parameter on wave dynamics.

papers.title: EPFH-Net: efficient pyramid forward harmonic network for non-alcoholic fatty liver disease detection
papers.abstract: Detecting Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) involves identifying fat accumulation in the liver but not linked to excessive alcohol consumption. NAFLD is a common liver disorder where fat builds up in liver cells, potentially leading to inflammation, liver damage, or liver cancer. Liver biopsy is the therapy used to detect NAFLD in the olden days, which consumed more time and provided inaccurate results. Therefore, the new framework named Efficient Pyramid Forward Harmonic Network (EPFH-Net) is introduced to detect NAFLD effectively. First, the ultrasound liver image sourced from the B-mode fatty liver ultrasound images dataset is fed as the input. Next, the extraction of the region is done by the Region of Interest (ROI) and the features, such as Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM), Pyramid Histogram of Oriented Gradients (PHOG), and Center Symmetric-Local Binary Patterns (CS-LBP), are extracted. Then, Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) is detected using EPFH-Net, which is a combination of Efficient Network (EfficientNet), Pyramid Network (PyramidNet), and harmonic analysis. Finally, the detected outputs are fatty or normal. The experimental outcomes attained by EPFH-Net are 92.12% of accuracy, 92.52% of TPR, and 91.88% of TNR for the k-value of 9.

papers.title: Adaptive EWMA control charts for monitoring dispersed count data: a COM-Poisson-based self-adjusting framework and applications
papers.abstract: Control charts for count data are based on the Poisson (equi-dispersed), Negative Binomial (over-dispersed), or Binomial (under-dispersed) distributions. However, the Conway-Maxwell-Poisson (COM-Poisson) distribution can flexibly model data with varying dispersion levels (under-, over-, and equi-dispersion). Over the past few years, adaptive control charts have gained attention compared to traditional Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) charts because of their ability to dynamically adjust the smoothing constant in response to process shifts. Existing adaptive EWMA charts are primarily restricted to Poisson-based models and therefore fail to provide a unified monitoring framework for under-, equi-, and over-dispersed count data. To overcome this gap, this study is the first to develop two Adaptive Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (AEWMA) control charts for the COM-Poisson distribution, allowing the smoothing constant to dynamically adjust estimated process shifts for a fixed rate parameter under-, equi-, and over-dispersed settings. The COMP-AEWMA-I chart is constructed using either of the two given smoothing strategies, whereas the COMP-AEWMA-II chart utilises dispersion-specific upper-tail quantiles for the COM-Poisson distribution to define intervals that govern the adaptive selection of the smoothing constant. The primary objectives of this study are to detect shifts promptly and to enhance process monitoring accuracy across various dispersion levels. Using the Monte Carlo simulation method, the performance of the proposed control charts is evaluated using key measures, including the average, standard deviation, and percentiles of run lengths for both zero- and steady-state cases. To assess the practical applicability, validity, and robustness of the proposed charts, real-life datasets from different fields are also used.

papers.title: Adaptive Japanese language instruction using behaviorally inferred learner states and multimodal contrastive reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: Intelligent tutoring systems for second-language acquisition have long aspired to deliver instruction that mirrors expert human pedagogy, yet existing approaches rely either on static knowledge-tracing models that ignore real-time cognitive signals or on large language models fine-tuned with fixed curricula that cannot adapt to individual learner trajectories. In the specific and linguistically complex context of Chinese speakers learning Japanese, cross-lingual phonological and orthographic transfer introduces an additional layer of challenge that general-purpose systems fail to address systematically. We identify three core obstacles: (i) the absence of a unified representation that jointly captures acoustic pronunciation quality and lexical comprehension, (ii) the inability of current curriculum planners to reason about latent cognitive load, and (iii) the lack of principled cross-lingual prior injection during feedback generation. To overcome these, we propose CogAdapt, a novel end-to-end framework that fuses a contrastive cross-modal encoder with a reinforcement-learning-based curriculum planner conditioned on continuous cognitive-state estimates, and generates error-aware natural language feedback through a cross-lingual knowledge-grounded decoder. On three public benchmarks—JLPT-Learn, CALL-SJ, and EduLLM-JA—CogAdapt achieves 82.6%, 80.1%, and 78.9% accuracy, outperforming the best baseline by up to 5.5 percentage points, and improves BLEU-4 by 4.7 points, demonstrating that cognitive adaptivity and cross-lingual transfer awareness are jointly essential for robust AI-assisted language learning.

papers.title: Proposed new words and collective identity in human and language model agent groups
papers.abstract: Groups develop distinctive words even when ordinary expressions are sufficient. Such words can symbolize collective identity, and observational studies link language use to community attachment. We examined identity change in temporary groups of one human and four disclosed large language model (LLM) agents, comparing discussions with and without a neologism proposal across recruitment waves. We recruited 100 Japanese participants in two sequential waves; an agent proposed a new word only in the first wave. Mean collective identity change did not differ significantly between waves. Within the proposal wave, favorable ratings of the proposed word were associated with change in identity, but this association did not survive correction for multiple testing (adjusted $$p=0.229$$). The three-way interaction among recruitment wave, message count, and team impression had a nominal $$p=0.027$$ but did not survive correction (adjusted $$p=0.082$$). In a sensitivity analysis, the interaction was not significant after adjustment for midpoint identity (nominal $$p=0.078$$; adjusted $$p=0.624$$). The nonsignificant between-wave comparison and exploratory associations that did not survive correction, together with wave confounding and post-discussion evaluations, limit causal inference and motivate randomized studies with repeated measures to test whether proposed group language affects identification.

papers.title: Context-aware tooth instance segmentation and missing-tooth localization in panoramic radiographs
papers.abstract: Reliable localization and segmentation of individual teeth are fundamental for automated dental diagnostics and computer-aided treatment planning. However, panoramic radiographs pose persistent challenges due to anatomical variability, overlapping structures, and inconsistent image quality, thereby keeping clinical workflows heavily dependent on manual interpretation. This study introduces DentAll, a framework that integrates tooth instance segmentation with contextual estimation of anatomically expected missing-tooth locations. The proposed segmentation with Contextual Spatial Attention Blocks (S-CSAB) integrates dilated convolutions and ROI-based positional encoding to enhance fine-grained boundary delineation while maintaining anatomical coherence across adjacent teeth. Building upon these contextual features, the Missing-Tooth Localization Predictor (MTLP) estimates missing-tooth locations via patient-conditioned coordinate regression, using the target tooth’s identity together with the geometry of its nearest same-arch neighboring teeth, without requiring explicit missing-tooth annotations. DentAll was evaluated on 1,325 panoramic radiographs using instance-level segmentation metrics, COCO-style mask average precision, comparative baselines, and controlled pseudo-missing localization experiments. Under an all-ground-truth evaluation protocol, the framework achieved a DSC of 88.21% (92.74% among successfully matched instances), AP50 of 97.34%, AP75 of 87.20%, and mAP50:95 of 68.58%, while contextual MTLP localization improved the IoU ≥ 0.5 rate from 25.20% (index-only formulation) to 72.58%. These findings demonstrate that integrating instance segmentation with patient-specific anatomical context provides an effective and computationally practical framework for structured analysis of panoramic dental radiographs under anatomical variability.

papers.title: Reproducible laboratory evaluation of speaker independent speech command recognition with an artificial neural network for humanoid robot control
papers.abstract: Voice-controlled humanoid robots can take over hazardous tasks in defence and field scenarios where direct human intervention is risky. Most reported prototypes couple an Android front end to an Arduino through Bluetooth, which restricts on-board signal processing, obscures end-to-end timing, and is seldom evaluated under speaker-independent conditions. This work reports the design, implementation and evaluation of an artificial neural network based speech-command recognition system that controls a humanoid robot prototype from within a single integrated development environment. A custom corpus of 5,000 utterances covering five motion commands was recorded from ten speakers (five male, five female) at 16 kHz under controlled laboratory conditions with a signal-to-noise ratio of at least 30 dB. A six-stage cleaning pipeline retained 4,728 utterances. Two speakers, one male and one female, were held out in full before any frame-level processing; the remaining eight speakers formed a development pool of 3,771 utterances that was further divided by speaker into six training and two validation speakers. Fourteen Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients were extracted from every 25 ms frame with a 10 ms hop and mean-pooled over the voiced frames of an utterance, yielding one 14-dimensional vector per utterance. A 14-50-5 feedforward network with rectified linear hidden units and a softmax output was trained with MATLAB scaled conjugate gradient backpropagation (trainscg) using speaker-defined index partitioning and validation-based early stopping. On a class-balanced speaker-independent test set of 750 utterances (150 per command) the network classified 651 utterances correctly, an overall accuracy of 86.8% with a 95% Wilson confidence interval of 0.842 to 0.890 and macro-averaged precision, recall and F1 score of 0.87. Per-command recall ranged from 84.0% for turn right to 91.3% for stop, the directional pair being hardest to separate because of a shared phonetic prefix. The classifier holds 1,005 parameters and needs about 2.0 kFLOP per utterance, some 33 and 53 times fewer parameters than the one-dimensional convolutional and long short-term memory baselines evaluated here. Command latency, measured from end-of-speech detection to actuator acknowledgement, averaged 149.7 ms with a standard deviation of 3.9 ms. The same feature extraction and classifier framework, with cleaning thresholds adapted to that corpus, was additionally applied to the public Google Speech Commands v0.02 corpus, with the released words forward, backward, right, left and stop standing in for the five commands and with the release’s own speaker-disjoint partition; on a class-balanced test set of the same size it reached 67.5% (95% Wilson interval 0.640 to 0.707) against 95.2% for the convolutional baseline, which indicates that the accuracy reported above is specific to this corpus and suggests that the loss of temporal information caused by utterance-level mean pooling may be an important limitation when the distinguishing material is short, although the present experiments do not isolate it as the sole cause. The contribution is a transparent, reproducible, speaker-independent laboratory baseline for small-vocabulary humanoid robot voice control; it is not evidence of readiness for operational deployment, which would require validation under realistic acoustic and mission conditions.

papers.title: CROWN-UAV: world-model-based planning for risk-aware and auditable UAV navigation
papers.abstract: Autonomous UAV navigation in cluttered warehouses requires anticipation of dynamic and occluded hazards, explicit risk attribution, and recovery-aware action selection. CROWN-UAV integrates an object-centric encoder, a retrained action-conditioned dual world model, stochastic future hypotheses, a calibrated structured risk graph, candidate-level runtime filtering, discrete receding-horizon planning, and planner-grounded audit traces. A frozen, leakage-controlled revision campaign evaluated five implementations on 120 paired NVIDIA Isaac Sim 5.1.0 PhysX cases per method across three warehouse layouts, four hazard families, five disturbance conditions, and two independent scenario seeds. CROWN-Full achieved 59.2% success (95% CI 50.2–67.5%), identical to Greedy and slightly below MPPI (60.8%). Relative to Greedy, CROWN reduced near collisions from 51.7% to 30.8% (paired difference − 20.8% points, Holm-adjusted p = 0.00346) and increased mean minimum clearance by 0.241 m (adjusted p = 5.40e-9), while successful paths were 2.50 m longer and completion was 3.90 s slower on 53 jointly successful cases. At 4.5 s, the DualWorldModel improved UAV ADE (0.313 versus 1.314 m) and occupancy IoU (0.527 versus 0.392) relative to constant velocity, but object ADE was worse (0.772 versus 0.547 m). Full-loop p95 latency was 101.95 ms, with 150/15,170 deadline misses. The evidence supports an implementation-specific proximity-safety trade-off and auditable decision records, not higher task completion, universal predictor superiority, formal safety, or human-validated explainability.

papers.title: Hybrid app-based motivational interviewing to prevent excessive gestational weight gain and improve health-promoting lifestyle: a randomized controlled trial
papers.abstract: Excessive gestational weight gain (EGWG) is a major risk factor for adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Identifying effective interventions to prevent excessive weight gain while promoting healthy lifestyle behaviors and psychological well-being during pregnancy is essential. This study evaluated the effects of hybrid app-based motivational interviewing on preventing EGWG, improving health-promoting lifestyle behaviors, and enhancing psychological health among pregnant women. This randomized controlled trial was conducted from August 2024 to May 2025 among 188 pregnant women at less than 14 weeks of gestation attending prenatal clinics in Babol, Iran. Participants were randomly assigned to the intervention or control group using block randomization (n = 94 per group). Follow-up was completed by 88 participants in the intervention group and 83 in the control group. The primary analysis followed the intention-to-treat (ITT) principle, with missing data handled using multiple imputation. The intervention consisted of six individual motivational interviewing-based counseling sessions over six consecutive weeks (weeks 15–20 of gestation). Sessions 1, 3, and 5 were conducted in person, whereas sessions 2, 4, and 6 were delivered remotely via a mobile application. Psychoeducational materials were provided through the application following each remote session. The control group received routine prenatal care. Maternal weight was measured at baseline, 28 weeks of gestation, and before delivery. Excessive gestational weight gain (EGWG) was defined according to the 2009 Institute of Medicine guidelines. The Health-Promoting Lifestyle Profile II (HPLP-II) and the 28-item General Health Questionnaire (GHQ-28) were administered at baseline, 28 weeks of gestation, and six weeks postpartum. Independent-samples t-tests were used for unadjusted between-group comparisons, repeated-measures ANOVA for within-group comparisons over time, and ANCOVA for adjusted between-group comparisons. By delivery, excessive weight gain was lower in the intervention group (23.4%) than in the control group (40.4%) (P = 0.039). Mean weight gain was 2.06 kg lower at week 28 (95% CI: −2.75 to − 1.37, P < 0.001) and 1.56 kg lower at delivery (95% CI: −2.30 to − 0.82, P < 0.001) in the intervention group. For HPLP-II, a marginally statistically significant between-group difference was observed at baseline (P = 0.049), with higher scores in the intervention group. The intervention group had significantly higher scores at week 28 (127.38 ± 19.43 vs. 107.00 ± 11.52, P < 0.001) and six weeks postpartum (128.78 ± 16.98 vs. 100.31 ± 10.16, P < 0.001). For GHQ, there was no baseline difference (P = 0.308), but the intervention group had lower scores at week 28 (16.44 ± 3.11 vs. 21.55 ± 4.10, P < 0.001) and six weeks postpartum (17.99 ± 3.47 vs. 22.88 ± 3.59, P < 0.001), indicating better general health. The hybrid app-based motivational interviewing intervention was associated with a lower incidence of excessive gestational weight gain (23.4% vs. 40.4%; absolute risk reduction, 17.0% points) and a lower gestational weight gain at delivery (between-group difference, − 1.56 kg; 95% CI: −2.30 to − 0.82), as well as improved HPLP-II and GHQ-28 scores compared with routine prenatal care. The intervention may be considered for routine prenatal care, pending further evaluation of its cost-effectiveness and implementation feasibility. Trial registration The trial was prospectively registered in the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT20200122046228N6) on 21 April 2024, before participant enrollment began.

papers.title: Endocrine, clinical and oxidative stress profiles in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a cross-sectional case-control study
papers.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is a prevalent cause of infertility worldwide.
