This study aimed to assess endocrinological and biochemical alterations and analyze oxidative stress in women with PCOS. A cohort of PCOS patients was examined for various clinical manifestations. We investigated the levels of several key parameters, including antioxidants, hormones (Luteinizing Hormone, Follicle Stimulating Hormone, Estradiol, and Testosterone), and hematological parameters. The study revealed that PCOS patients showed significantly higher levels of testosterone, while LH levels were lower in the non-PCOS group. FSH concentration was reduced in the PCOS group. Antioxidant levels demonstrated statistically significant differences between PCOS and non-PCOS females. A majority of PCOS patients experienced symptoms such as hair loss, hirsutism and menstrual irregularities. Menarche occurred at an early age, with PCOS females experiencing it at 13 years. A substantial portion of the population (84%) reported experiencing pain during periods, yet only a small fraction (14%) were using medication for pain relief. Ultrasonography revealed findings of a thickened endometrium and multiple cysts ranging from 5 to 7 mm. The findings reveal substantial hormonal imbalances, elevated testosterone levels, and significant differences in luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone dynamics, underscoring the endocrinological complexity of PCOS. The high prevalence of distressing clinical manifestations and the underutilization of pain relief medication among PCOS patients emphasize the need for improved symptom management and healthcare interventions.

papers.title: Chattering-attenuated sensorless hybrid PMSM drive using integral hyperbolic sliding backstepping control and EKF: real-time co-simulation on dSPACE DS1104
papers.abstract: This study proposes a Sensorless Hybrid Integral Hyperbolic Sliding Backstepping Control strategy with an Extended Kalman Filter (SH-IHSBSC-EKF) for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) drives. The proposed strategy is developed to enhance the dynamic response, disturbance rejection, and current quality of the drive without mechanical position and speed sensors. The controller is designed through a recursive backstepping procedure, in which the virtual control inputs are derived from Lyapunov theory to guarantee the global exponential stability of the speed and current tracking error dynamics. In the outer speed loop, an integral sliding surface with an exponential reaching law and a hyperbolic tangent switching function ensures fast convergence and attenuates chattering. In parallel, the EKF reconstructs the rotor position and speed from stator current and voltage measurements. The designed strategy is evaluated against the Proportional-Integral (PI-EKF) and Integral BackStepping Control (IBSC-EKF) sensorless strategies under three simulation scenarios using MATLAB/Simulink. Under low-speed operation, the settling time is reduced by 95.68% and 48.00% compared with PI-EKF and IBSC-EKF, respectively, and the load rejection time by 96.41% and 64.37%. Moreover, the stator current Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) is reduced from 2.68% with PI-EKF and 0.56% with IBSC-EKF to 0.24% with SH-IHSBSC-EKF. In all three scenarios, covering variable speed and load, low-speed operation, and parameter variations, stable speed tracking with near-zero steady-state error is preserved. The proposed strategy is further validated through real-time co-simulation on a dSPACE DS1104 platform. Although the EKF remains sensitive to inductance mismatch and assumes a known initial rotor position, the overall performance demonstrates the potential of the proposed strategy for high-performance sensorless PMSM drives.

papers.title: Aspect-grounded heterogeneous graph learning for explainable cross-domain recommendation
papers.abstract: Personalized recommender systems are essential for mitigating information overload. However, existing approaches face challenges in fine-grained preference modeling, behaviorally relevant explanations, and cross-domain transfer. We propose Aspect-Grounded Heterogeneous Graph Learning (AGHGL), a recommendation framework that uses aspect-level sentiment semantics as a common basis for preference modeling, explanation, and cross-domain transfer. AGHGL constructs a heterogeneous sentiment graph integrating users, items, aspects, and opinion expressions, enabling relation-aware message passing and aspect-mediated preference modeling. A margin-based intervention-sensitivity objective couples attention-derived aspect importance with prediction changes under aspect masking, aligning explanations with prediction behavior. A dual-level aspect alignment mechanism facilitates cross-domain transfer by aligning aspect representations at semantic and graph-structural levels. Experiments on real-world datasets show that AGHGL consistently outperforms the evaluated baselines in recommendation accuracy, with larger relative gains under sparse and cold-start conditions in the target domain. Human evaluation indicates improved perceived explanatory quality, while intervention-based analysis shows that higher aspect importance is associated with larger prediction changes. These results suggest that the aspect-grounded framework provides a useful basis for jointly modeling recommendation, explanation, and cross-domain transfer within the evaluated settings.

papers.title: Cognitive mechanisms as a pathway linking schooling and protection against PTSD in contexts of armed conflict
papers.abstract: Schooling represents a protective factor for mental health, but this has not been investigated in populations exposed to armed conflicts, who present very high levels of post-traumatic stress disorder. Schooling is generally associated with better cognitive functioning, and cognitive functioning may serve as a protective factor for mental health. However, few studies have specifically examined whether cognition contributes to the protective effect of schooling on mental health. In this study, we examine the links between schooling, working memory and PTSD in two African samples exposed to high levels of violence: Rwanda (n = 1,570) and North Kivu, in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (n = 1,633). We measured PTSD symptoms with the PCL-5 and working memory with a forward digit-span task, administered in the local language (Kinyarwanda or Swahili). Results of linear mixed models show that higher educational attainment is associated with less PTSD symptoms. This association persisted after accounting for important determinants of PTSD including age, gender, socioeconomic status and trauma exposure. Bootstrapped mediation analysis indicated that digit-span performance explained between 12 and 30% of the relationship between schooling and PTSD. These findings support the conclusion that formal education is associated with less psychopathology at least partly in relation to improvements in cognitive functioning. Results underscore the relevance of education and cognition for population mental health in high-adversity, conflict-affected settings.

papers.title: Assessing pertussis control strategies: a mathematical modeling approach incorporating vaccination and asymptomatic infection
papers.abstract: Pertussis is a highly contagious respiratory disease caused by Bordetella pertussis, which continues to pose a significant public health challenge worldwide. In this study, we develop a deterministic model for pertussis transmission comprising six compartments: susceptible, vaccinated, exposed, symptomatic infectious, asymptomatic infectious, and recovered individuals (SVEIAR). Using the next-generation matrix method, we derive the basic reproduction number $$\mathcal {R}_0$$ of the model without vaccination and the vaccination-adjusted reproduction number $$\mathcal {R}_v$$ at the vaccinated disease-free equilibrium. The disease-free equilibrium is locally asymptotically stable if and only if $$\mathcal {R}_v<1$$ and globally asymptotically stable if $$\mathcal {R}_0<1$$; a unique endemic equilibrium exists whenever $$\mathcal {R}_v>1$$, and an exact quadratic criterion shows that the bifurcation at $$\mathcal {R}_v=1$$ is forward for all parameter values sampled from the literature ranges, although an imperfect vaccine can produce backward bifurcation outside them. Local stability of the endemic equilibrium is established near the threshold (at the baseline values of the other parameters) by centre-manifold analysis and verified numerically away from it. Sensitivity analysis revealed that vaccination, recovery rates, asymptomatic infectiousness, and the proportion of asymptomatic infections were the primary drivers of $$\mathcal {R}_v$$. The transmission rate and a reporting fraction were calibrated to eleven annual counts of reported US cases (CDC, 2014–2024). These parameters are not identifiable from the data: the objective has several local minima, the reported baseline ($$\mathcal {R}_v=0.80$$) is a local optimum, and parameter sets with $$\mathcal {R}_v>1$$ fit at least as well. The calibrated model does not reproduce the 2017–2019 plateau or the 2023–2024 resurgence ($$R^2<0$$) and is used here as a reference scenario, not for forecasting. Furthermore, the uncontrolled SVEIAR model is extended into an optimal control framework by incorporating four time-dependent intervention strategies, with explicitly stated, assumed cost weights, control bounds and horizon. Under these assumptions, strategies that include transmission reduction gave the lowest objective values, and this ranking was unchanged when each weight was halved or doubled; the size of the benefits, however, depended mainly on the assumed control bounds and on the calibration scenario. These rankings are model-based findings under stated assumptions, not predictions of real-world intervention effectiveness. By integrating imperfect vaccination, breakthrough infections, asymptomatic transmission, and temporary immunity, the model offers a framework for exploring the persistence of pertussis in highly vaccinated populations; age structure, seasonality, stochasticity, richer surveillance data and economic evaluation are needed before the results can inform policy.

papers.title: Seasonal decoupling of local climate zone thermal responses in three cold-climate cities of Northeast China
papers.abstract: Urban thermal environments are strongly influenced by urban morphology and land cover, yet the seasonal stability of Local Climate Zone (LCZ)–land surface temperature (LST) relationships in cold-climate cities remains insufficiently understood. In regions with long winters and seasonal snow cover, LCZ-specific surface thermal responses may differ substantially from those observed in temperate cities. This study investigates seasonal thermal responses across LCZ types in three major cold-climate cities in Northeast China—Shenyang, Harbin, and Changchun. LST was retrieved from Landsat 8 imagery on the Google Earth Engine platform, and LCZ maps were produced following the World Urban Database and Access Portal Tools (WUDAPT) framework. Seasonal differences in LCZ thermal responses were examined through intra- and inter-city comparisons of mean LST, LCZ-referenced LST contrasts, and mixed-effects model estimates. To further isolate structural thermal effects from background climatic variability, a linear mixed-effects model was applied with LCZ type, season, and their interaction as fixed effects and city as a random effect. Auxiliary snow-cover and solar-radiation indicators were also incorporated to support the interpretation of seasonal mechanisms. The results show that summer LST patterns are strongly controlled by urban morphology and surface radiative properties. Compact built-up zones (LCZ 1–3), industrial or large impervious areas, and exposed hard surfaces exhibit pronounced warming effects, with Changchun showing the highest mean summer LST among the three cities. In winter, inter-LCZ thermal contrasts become substantially weaker, and low-vegetation, open, or exposed surfaces tend to show stronger cooling under snow-covered and low-radiation conditions. Shenyang maintains the warmest winter condition, whereas Harbin exhibits the strongest winter cold background. The mixed-effects model reveals a significant LCZ × season interaction, indicating a seasonal shift in the mechanisms controlling urban surface temperature. Summer thermal patterns are primarily governed by radiative absorption and urban surface structure, whereas winter thermal dynamics are jointly modulated by snow cover, reduced solar radiation, and heating-season urban energy processes. These findings demonstrate that LCZ–LST relationships in cold-climate cities exhibit pronounced seasonal variability and should not be directly generalized from studies conducted in warmer regions. The results provide a scientific basis for seasonally differentiated, LCZ-specific climate adaptation and thermal environment management in high-latitude cities.

papers.title: DATE: domain-aware transformer ensembles for reliable extremism detection in social media
papers.abstract: Extremist content spreads quickly on social media, so moderation needs classifiers that are accurate and whose confidence can be trusted. We study the Domain-Aware Transformer Ensemble (DATE): a BERTweet-base classifier (pre-trained on 850M English tweets), contextual-substitution and random-edit augmentation applied only inside each training fold, and a soft-voting ensemble of ten fold models. We evaluate on the Social Media Extremism Detection dataset (2,250 training posts, 749 labelled test posts) with a leakage-controlled protocol and report three kinds of evidence separately. (i) Cross-validation: single DATE models reach 0.822 accuracy (±0.027) on held-out folds. (ii) Held-out test posts: the ten-model ensemble reaches 0.843 accuracy (95% CI 0.814–0.868), macro-F1 0.744 and ROC-AUC 0.863, and its expected calibration error is 0.030 against 0.064 for single models (paired bootstrap difference $$-0.029$$, CI $$-0.046$$ to $$-0.010$$); over five training seeds, the ensemble is better calibrated than its members in every run (mean ECE 0.037 against 0.061). (iii) Competition: the submitted DATE ensemble scored 0.8507 on the private leaderboard of the Kaggle challenge ($$\approx$$375 posts), tied for first place with two other teams among 164 teams; this margin is within sampling noise. Controlled ablations repeated over five seeds show that augmentation, class weights and the cosine schedule do not improve accuracy at full data size, although augmentation helps when training data is scarce; BERTweet beats RoBERTa-base in all five seeds (1.9 points on the test posts), and a TF-IDF baseline reaches comparable test accuracy. The study is limited to one English dataset whose annotation details (number of annotators, agreement) are not reported, and the test set has a different class balance from the training set.

papers.title: Identification of 1 H -pyrazolo[3,4 -b ]pyridines as potential inhibitors of Leishmania arginase
papers.abstract: Leishmaniasis, a parasitic disease transmitted by sandflies, remains a significant global health concern, particularly in tropical regions. The arginase enzyme (LaArg) has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in Leishmania amazonensis. This study employs a computer-aided drug design approach to identify novel LaArg inhibitor candidates. A series of 38 compounds featuring a 1H-pyrazolo[3,4-b]pyridine nucleus was evaluated using 3D-QSAR (Py-CoMFA), molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to predict pIC50 values and investigate molecular interactions within the LaArg active site. Our results identified 14 compounds with promising predicted activity (pIC50 ≥ 5.00). Molecular docking analysis revealed that 10 compounds establish strong interactions with key catalytic residues (His127 and His142) and Mn2+ ions, which are crucial for LaArg binding. Molecular dynamics further characterized compounds 1b and 1e as potential arginase inhibitors, though they exhibited distinct thermodynamic profiles. Compound 1b, featuring a nitrile group, demonstrated initial stability and a balanced molecular profile. However, it failed to maintain its binding mode throughout the entire simulation trajectory. Conversely, while 1e remained stable at the site, its bromine substituent incurred a significant solvation penalty, leading to a less favorable binding free energy than 1b. These findings provide significant insights into the structural requirements for arginase inhibition and establish a framework for developing novel therapeutic compounds against leishmaniasis.

papers.title: Factors associated with unmet patient care, sexual health, and health system needs among cancer patients at an oncology center in Southern Ethiopia, 2024
papers.abstract: Unmet health care needs refer to the gap between patients perceived need for services and the care they receive. These needs may occur during the course of cancer diagnosis and treatment and can cause psychological distress, ineffective coping, and reduced quality of life. Evidence on patient care/support, sexuality, and health system needs among cancer patients in Ethiopia is limited. To assess the prevalence and factors associated with unmet patient care/support, sexuality, and health system needs among cancer patients at the Oncology Center of Hawassa University Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Hawassa, Ethiopia, in 2024. An institution-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 321 cancer patients selected via simple random sampling. Data were collected using an interviewer-administered structured questionnaire and analyzed using SPSS 26. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with unmet needs; p < 0.05 was considered significant. Of 311 participants (response rate 96.9%), the mean age was 45.16 years. Unmet needs were highest in the health system and information domain (72.3%), followed by patient care/support (43.4%) and sexuality (27.7%). Low Income (Adjusted Odds Ratio [AOR] = 5.96; 95% Confidence Interval (CI): 2.29–14.13) and middle income (AOR = 4.64; 95% CI: 1.48–14.50) predicted unmet health system needs. Co-existing illness was associated with unmet patient care/support needs (AOR = 1.87; 95% CI: 1.09–3.52), and time since diagnosis predicted unmet sexuality needs (AOR = 1.05; 95% CI: 1.01–1.11). Unmet supportive care needs are high, particularly in the health system and information domain. Interventions addressing income, co-existing illnesses, and disease duration are recommended to improve supportive care and patient quality of life.

papers.title: Protective effects of molsidomine on oxidative stress, inflammation, and VEGF/P-selectin expression in CLP-induced sepsis
papers.abstract: Sepsis-associated liver injury involves oxidative stress, inflammation, and vascular activation. We investigated whether molsidomine pretreatment modifies hepatic injury in rats subjected to cecal ligation and puncture (CLP). Forty male Wistar rats were randomized to sham surgery, molsidomine alone, CLP, or molsidomine plus CLP. Molsidomine (10 mg/kg/day) was administered orally for 14 days before surgery. Four rats in each septic group died before the 24-hour assessment, leaving eight survivors per group. Liver histology, vascular endothelial growth factor and P-selectin immunoreactivity, tissue redox and inflammatory markers, and serum hepatic indices were evaluated. Compared with CLP alone, pretreatment was associated with lower median hepatic damage scores (2 versus 5), lower vascular endothelial growth factor and P-selectin immunoreactivity, higher hepatic reduced glutathione and total antioxidant status, and lower hepatic tumor necrosis factor-α. Other measured hepatic redox indices did not differ significantly between septic groups. Serum albumin, alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase, and lactate dehydrogenase did not differ significantly, whereas total bilirubin was higher with pretreatment. In this shared experimental cohort, prophylactic molsidomine was associated with reduced structural injury and selective tissue biochemical changes. These exploratory findings do not demonstrate improved hepatic function, a causal vascular mechanism, or clinical efficacy when treatment begins after sepsis onset.

papers.title: Seafood intake and urinary total mercury in children: dose–response in three national samples and a paired urine–blood comparison in adolescents
papers.abstract: Urinary mercury is read as a marker of inorganic exposure, and urinary elimination of dietary methylmercury is treated as negligible. Whether urine carries a measurable seafood signal in children is unresolved, and national programs rarely draw blood from young children. The Korean National Environmental Health Survey (Cycle 5, 2021–2023) provided three probability samples: preschoolers (n = 648), schoolchildren (n = 780), and adolescents (n = 901). We fitted survey-weighted log-linear models of habitual seafood intake with a Rao–Wu bootstrap. Each doubling of animal seafood intake was associated with 13.5%, 11.8%, and 15.0% higher creatinine-corrected total mercury in spot urine, pooling to 13.2% (95% CI 11.0, 15.5) with no detectable heterogeneity. Seaweed, the internal negative control, showed no positive association. In 812 adolescents, dietary slopes did not differ detectably between urine and blood (ratio 0.99; 0.72, 1.28), category profiles were similar, and adjustment for blood total mercury halved the urinary dietary slope. Agreement within individuals (n = 872) stayed moderate (weighted Spearman ρ = 0.50, κ = 0.33). Spot urinary total mercury tracks seafood-related mercury exposure at population scale; without speciation, the signal cannot be assigned to methylmercury or inorganic mercury. It cannot stand in for blood mercury in one child.

papers.title: Optimization of asymmetric conical flow channels for efficient yarn conveying via numerical method
papers.abstract: During pneumatic yarn conveying process through an asymmetric conical channel, the channel structural parameters have a significant effect on conveying performance. To balance the computational accuracy and efficiency, an efficient two-way fluid-structure interaction method is employed to establish a dynamic model of the yarn in airflow. Weakly coupled simulations are performed through two-way projection to efficiently capture the interaction between the airflow and yarn motion. The effects of the cone angle, connection tube diameter, and connection tube length on yarn conveying performance are investigated through single-factor and multi-parameter analyses. The results show that the yarn velocity first increases and then decreases with increasing cone angle and connection tube length, whereas increasing the connection tube diameter enhances yarn conveying efficiency. The deviation between the experimental and simulation results is less than 5%, and the optimized structure improves yarn conveying velocity by 35% compared with the original structure. The optimized structure provides a useful reference for the structural optimization of pneumatic yarn conveying devices.

papers.title: Antitumor activity and immune-related gene expression changes following recombinant Mycobacterium smegmatis treatment in a mouse model of bladder cancer
papers.abstract: Bladder cancer requires additional therapeutic strategies because of frequent recurrence and progression risk. We evaluated recombinant Mycobacterium smegmatis expressing a human macrophage migration inhibitory factor–interleukin-7 fusion protein (rSmeg-hMIF-hIL-7) in a syngeneic subcutaneous MBT-2 bladder cancer model. Among mice that developed measurable tumors, intraperitoneally treated mice showed reduced tumor growth and longer endpoint-free survival, defined as time to death or humane-endpoint euthanasia. RNA sequencing of four control and three treated tumors identified 116 differentially expressed genes at a fold-change magnitude ≥ 2 and false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.05. Enrichment analyses highlighted immune-related transcriptional differences, although tissue-collection timing and tumor burden limited their attribution to treatment. Cross-species expression comparison identified five exploratory candidates: CCL15, CCRL2, ST3GAL5, SIGLEC6, and TMEM255A. Four showed FDR-significant survival associations in exploratory unadjusted Cox analyses within the same TCGA-BLCA cohort. Expression patterns concordant with those in treated mouse tumors were also associated with papillary histology. RT-qPCR using the same biological samples supported increased Ccl6 and St3gal5 expression after multiple-testing correction. These findings support the antitumor potential of rSmeg-hMIF-hIL-7 and provide exploratory links between murine tumor transcriptional differences and human bladder cancer characteristics.

papers.title: Prospective associations of urinary bisphenol A and phthalate metabolites in early and school-aged childhood with liver function in adolescence
papers.abstract: People are simultaneously exposed to multiple endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs). We prospectively evaluated the associations of the mixture of urinary bisphenol A (BPA) and phthalate metabolite concentrations measured at 3–5 and 7–9 years of age with liver function in adolescence, as a surrogate indicator of metabolic disease. We analyzed 126 children whose urinary BPA and phthalate metabolite concentrations were measured at 3–5 and 7–9 years of age; their liver enzyme levels were measured in adolescence. The overall association of the urinary biomarker mixture with liver enzyme levels and the variable importance of the biomarker groups—BPA and metabolites of high- and low-molecular-weight phthalates (HMWPs and LMWPs)—were evaluated using Bayesian kernel machine regression. We investigated sex-specific associations and bivariate interactions between urinary biomarkers. In each measurement period, phthalate metabolite concentrations were generally strongly correlated within the HMWP and LMWP groups. Additionally, there were correlations between BPA and several phthalate metabolites at 3–5 years of age but not at 7–9 years of age. For biomarkers measured at 3–5 years, estimated aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels and the AST/alanine aminotransferase (ALT) ratio tended to increase when mixture components were jointly set above their respective medians. For biomarkers measured at 7–9 years, estimated AST, ALT, and gamma-glutamyltransferase (γ-GTP) levels tended to increase as mixture concentrations increased jointly. However, the overall effect was not statistically significant; only an overall trend was detected. LMWPs, particularly monoisobutyl phthalate (MiBP), had the highest variable importance for AST. We evaluated the associations of the mixture of urinary BPA and nine phthalate metabolite concentrations in childhood with liver function in adolescence. The results provide epidemiological evidence on associations between urinary EDC biomarkers and liver enzyme levels, indicating a need for further research.

papers.title: Association of MMP9 (rs17576 and rs3787268) genetic variants with breast cancer susceptibility: integrating molecular and bioinformatics approaches
papers.abstract: Matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP9) plays an important role in extracellular matrix remodeling and has been implicated in tumor invasion and metastasis in several cancers, including breast cancer (BC). This study aims to elucidate the genetic factors influencing breast cancer risk by analyzing the role of MMP9 (rs17576 and rs3787268) variants in cancer susceptibility. We employed a holistic methodology that integrates genetic analysis with sophisticated bioinformatics techniques to elucidate their potential influence on the progression of breast carcinoma using multi-platform functional evidence. A case–control study was conducted including 120 breast cancer patients and 120 age-matched healthy controls. Genotyping of rs17576 and rs3787268 was performed using TaqMan allelic discrimination assays. Logistic regression models were applied to evaluate genotype, allele, and haplotype associations with breast cancer susceptibility. Complementary bioinformatic analyses (GEPIA2, GTEx, TNMplot, muTarget, STRING, I-Mutant, and 3DSNP) were performed to investigate gene expression patterns, eQTL effects, protein stability, and potential molecular interactions. The missense variant MMP9*rs17576 showed a significant association with breast cancer susceptibility under several genetic models (A/G: OR = 2.31, 95% CI = 1.24–4.29, p = 0.007; and G/G: OR = 2.46, 95% CI = 1.16–5.22, p = 0.017). The G allele frequency was higher in patients than in controls (52.5% vs. 41.2%; OR = 1.57, 95% CI = 1.10–2.26, p = 0.013). In contrast, the intronic variant MMP9*rs3787268 showed no independent association with breast cancer susceptibility. Bioinformatic analyses suggested that rs17576 may influence MMP9 function and regulation, including predicted protein destabilization (ΔΔG = − 0.34 kcal/mol), breast-tissue eQTL effects, and potential involvement in tumor-related molecular pathways. Expression analyses also indicated increased MMP9 expression in breast cancer tissues and association with disease progression. These findings suggest that the MMP9*rs17576 variant may contribute to breast cancer susceptibility in Egyptian women, whereas MMP9*rs3787268 showed no independent association. Given the single-population design, these results should be interpreted cautiously and require validation in larger, ethnically diverse cohorts together with functional investigations.

papers.title: The first genome of the Italian hare ( Lepus corsicanus ) and new insights into Lepus phylogenesis
papers.abstract: The Italian hare (Lepus corsicanus) is a Mediterranean endemic species, restricted to Southern and Central Italy, Sicily, and introduced historically in Corsica. It is currently classified as Vulnerable by the International Union for Conservation of Nature, mainly due to habitat loss, population fragmentation, and the widespread introduction of the European hare (L. europaeus). Despite the urgent need of conservation, knowledge on its ecology and genetic traits remain unexplored which weakens the tools for proper species management. Here, we report the first high-quality de novo assembly of L. corsicanus genome, generated using Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing and a co-assembly approach supported by the existing reference genome. The final assembly has a total length of 2.84 Gb, with scaffolds (N50 = 129 Mb) anchored to 23 autosomes and X, Y chromosomes, and a BUSCO completeness of 98.2%. Genomic annotation uncovered 22,159 protein-coding genes, with an average gene length of 50,882 bp, mean exon length of 223 bp, and repetitive elements account for approximately 40% of the genome. A preliminary investigation on phylogenetic position of L. corsicanus relative to other Lepus species present new insights into the evolutionary history of the group. The topology recovered a strongly supported sister relationship between L. corsicanus and L. castroviejoi, as well as L. europaeus and L. timidus. L. capensis and L. tolai formed a clade, which was strongly related to L. yarkandensis with high statistical support, and all together grouped with the L. europaeus-L. timidus clade. These results underline that reference genome for L. corsicanus provides a valuable resource for future research on the evolution studies and conservation.

papers.title: Bent ommatidia in apposition eyes
papers.abstract: The compound eyes of arthropods are typically composed of ommatidia with straight dioptric apparatus and rhabdoms all aligned along the optical axis, a configuration assumed to maximize light capture. Through comparative morphological analyses carried out on 12 species of crustacean amphipods belonging to 9 genera and 7 families, we reveal an unexpected deviation from the canonical architecture: the rhabdoms are markedly bent. This is not found only in Talitrus saltator but in other supralittoral beach-dwelling amphipods with a similar style of life: they rest under the damp sand during the day and perform migrations along the sea–land axis of the beach at night or in dim light. However, occasionally they are forced to leave the damp belt of sand and quickly return to it even during the day, for example due to predation attempts or changes in sea state. This bent organization of rhabdoms, absent in marine and terrestrial amphipods, indicates a new habitat-specific optical specialization and, from an optical point of view, points to a role of the rhabdoms beyond that of simple light guides. Moreover, bent ommatidia are embedded in interommatidial cells filled with a white substance, observed in all amphipods possessing bent rhabdoms. Ray-tracing simulations and optical modelling evoke enhanced light collection by scattering compared with straight ommatidia lacking this substance, albeit at the cost of reduced spatial resolution. We propose that this arrangement improves visual sensitivity in dark, dim, or rapidly changing twilight conditions. Our findings thus reveal a novel structure and mechanism for light harvesting in apposition compound eyes, highlighting a distinct optical strategy for maintaining visual performance in supralittoral and intertidal dwelling amphipods.

papers.title: Applied research on a seismological method for coal mine blasting safety
papers.abstract: The magnitudes of coal mine blasts are generally low, and the yield estimation of which faces significant challenges. In this study, based on measured ground motion data from coal mine blast experiments, the time–frequency characteristics of the signals and the attenuation law of ground motion are analyzed in depth. On one hand, a local magnitude dataset is obtained by establishing a near-field calibration function model, and rapid quantitative yield estimation is achieved through a near-field magnitude-yield empirical formula. On the other hand, drawing on a far-field seismic wave energy calculation model, the physical chain of the radiated energy method and yield is inverted through source spectrum integration and explosive seismic efficiency is elaborated, and a blast yield estimation model based on near-field seismic radiated energy is established. In view of the practical limitations imposed by the monitoring system bandwidth and the signal analysis time window, the systematic underestimation of radiated energy estimates caused by frequency truncation is quantified, and a semi-theoretical, semi-empirical method for analyzing and calculating explosive seismic efficiency is introduced. In this study, the calculated frequency-band compensation coefficient ranges from 0.140 to 0.191, and the seismic explosive efficiency ranges from 0.013 to 0.017. The data from blasts 3–7 were utilized to calibrate all model parameters, including the attenuation coefficients of displacement and velocity, the seismic explosive efficiency, and the parameters for the calibration function and empirical formula in the magnitude-yield relationship, and the data from blasts 1–2 were used for validation. The results show that the radiated energy method provides a physically more explicit approach to yield estimation for small-magnitude coal mine blasts, while the constraints of bandwidth truncation and efficiency dispersion must be acknowledged. A cross-checking framework is recommended, in which the magnitude method serves for rapid preliminary estimation and the energy method provides physical constraints, offering a reference for related yield estimation.

papers.title: Evidence of expanding range and environmental suitability for Culex perexiguus in Northern Italy (Emilia-Romagna, 2025)
papers.abstract: Culex perexiguus, a mosquito typically associated with hot and semi‑arid environments across North Africa, the Middle East, and southwestern Asia, has recently emerged as a potential public health concern in parts of southern Europe due to its demonstrated vector capacity for multiple arboviruses, particularly West Nile virus (WNV). In 2025, 84 specimens of this mosquito were collected across 22 sites in Emilia‑Romagna, northern Italy, within the regional WNV entomological surveillance program; DNA barcoding of 21 individuals confirmed morphological identification. Comparison with entomological data from 2009 revealed a concurrent decrease of another mosquito, Culex modestus, suggesting a possible northward shift in suitable areas for both species. Ecological niche modelling based on presence records of Cx. perexiguus indicated an estimated distribution primarily linked to the availability of suitable breeding habitats, and the meteorological anomalies recorded in 2025 (compared to 2001–2020) likely favoured its presence. The unexpected expansion of Cx. perexiguus into Emilia‑Romagna, in an area characterised by a temperate continental climate, underscores the broader changes in mosquito distribution potentially linked to climate change. Its presence may have significant implications for public health, vector surveillance, and control strategies, and will therefore require careful monitoring in the coming years.

papers.title: Effect of plant-based compost on the growth and biochemical responses of ornamental cabbage under salt stress in peat-based growing media
papers.abstract: Soil salinity is one of the major abiotic stress factors limiting the growth, ornamental quality, and performance of ornamental plants. This study investigated the effects of different compost application rates on plant growth, morphological characteristics, phytochemical composition, and antioxidant defense mechanisms in ornamental cabbage (Brassica oleracea var. acephala ‘Pigeon Red F1’) under salt stress. The experiment was conducted as a two-factor factorial design consisting of three compost rates (0, 20, and 40%) and four NaCl concentrations (0, 25, 50, and 75 mM). Morphological traits, chlorophyll content (SPAD), root characteristics, antioxidant enzyme activities (CAT, POD, and SOD), oxidative stress indicators (MDA and H₂O₂), total phenolic content, total flavonoid content, DPPH radical scavenging activity, and ferric reducing antioxidant power (FRAP) were evaluated. Compost significantly affected plant height, plant diameter, leaf number, plant fresh weight, root length, root fresh weight, and root dry weight. Increasing compost rates generally reduced plant height, plant diameter, and leaf number, whereas mean root length increased. Salinity significantly affected plant height, leaf number, and SPAD values. Compost × salinity interactions were significant for plant height, leaf length, SPAD values, and catalase activity, indicating that responses to salinity depended on the compost rate. Neither compost nor salinity nor their interaction significantly affected plant dry weight or central coloration diameter. The 20% compost treatment improved maintenance of total flavonoid content and antioxidant capacity under moderate salinity conditions, while the 40% compost treatment increased total phenolic content under non-saline conditions. Salinity significantly altered antioxidant enzyme activities and oxidative stress markers, whereas catalase activity, root length, root dry weight, and central coloration diameter were not significantly affected. Overall, compost application modified the physiological and biochemical responses of ornamental cabbage to salt stress in a dose-dependent manner. These findings indicate that compost application may help maintain ornamental quality and improve stress tolerance under saline cultivation conditions, providing a sustainable strategy for ornamental cabbage production.

papers.title: Healthcare provider’s perceptions of digital antimicrobial stewardship in resource-limited settings
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is a key public health concern globally, especially in resource-limited settings, where health system limitations contribute to poor antimicrobial stewardship. Digital health solutions present an opportunity to improve antimicrobial stewardship through better prescribing, surveillance, and clinical decision-making. Nevertheless, there is limited evidence on healthcare providers’ perceptions and contextual factors that affect the implementation of digital antimicrobial stewardship in low-resource settings. The objective of this study is to explore healthcare providers’ perceptions of digital antimicrobial stewardship in resource-limited primary hospitals. A descriptive qualitative study was conducted in public primary hospitals in the Wolaita Zone of Southern Ethiopia, utilizing in-depth interviews with purposively chosen healthcare providers. Data collection was done until thematic saturation was reached. The interviews were recorded on tape, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed through inductive thematic analysis using Opencode version 4.02 software. Fourteen participants were included in the study. Five key themes emerged: infrastructure-related issues, training and digital competency, organizational support and leadership, perceived usefulness of digital tools, and opportunities to enhance antimicrobial stewardship. Respondents identified the possibilities of digital tools to improve the accuracy of prescribing and monitoring; inappropriate digital infrastructure, insufficient training, and lack of institutional support were identified as barriers to successful implementation. The facilitators were leadership dedication, capacity-building efforts, and the incorporation of digital systems in daily clinical operations. Technological, human, and organizational factors are mutually dependent and influence the implementation of digital antimicrobial stewardship in resource-limited settings. Although healthcare providers have good perceptions about digital antimicrobial stewardship, there is a need to bridge the gap in infrastructure and capacity. Digital readiness and institutional support are needed to facilitate the successful implementation and sustainability of digital health interventions to fight antimicrobial resistance.

papers.title: Cardiovascular complications and cardiovascular death are rare in severe COVID-19 presenting with myocardial injury or failure
papers.abstract: SARS-COV2 infection has been linked to cardiovascular complications. Published data suggest that cardiac injury may be a common disease feature and contribute to morbidity and mortality in severe COVID-19. Since early in the pandemic, little data has emerged describing what cardiovascular complications arise from myocardial injury in severe COVID-19 and whether these complications contribute to mortality. We set out to describe the incidence and nature of cardiovascular complications in patients with severe COVID-19 infection and biochemical or imaging evidence of myocardial injury. We analyzed consecutive patients admitted for severe COVID-19 and presenting with biochemical or echocardiographic evidence of myocardial injury across 16 centers within the CARDIO-COVID investigator-initiated consortium. A light-GBM machine learning model was used to identify variables associated with mortality. Our study included 1,328 patients. ICU mortality was 29.4%. Factors most associated with mortality were age, SOFA Cardiovascular score, elevated troponin, intubation, high vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS), high PEEP, and high FiO2. Individual cardiovascular (myocardial infarction, stroke, pulmonary embolism, myocarditis, VT/VF, new onset heart failure) complications were rare (all < 5%) but common in sum (17.6%), and did not present significant association with mortality. Patients with high VIS and SOFA Cardiovascular scores had a significantly higher incidence of secondary bacterial pneumonias suggesting septic shock played a role in their physiology. Investigator-adjudicated cause of death data identified respiratory failure and septic shock as primary causes of mortality. Though cardiovascular complications of severe COVID-19 are common, they do not seem to contribute significantly to mortality. Elevated cardiac enzymes and myocardial dysfunction carry prognostic value likely reflecting myocardial strain in the setting of multisystem organ dysfunction rather than direct myocardial injury by SARS-CoV2.

papers.title: Clinical significance of recurrently mutated genes in VHL wild-type clear cell renal cell carcinoma
papers.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), the most common subtype of kidney cancer, is characterized by its genomic heterogeneity and high risk of recurrence after nephrectomy. While the majority of ccRCC tumors harbor somatic mutations in VHL tumor suppressor gene (VHLmut), approximately 20–25% lack VHL mutations (VHLwt), and may exhibit different progression patterns. VHLwt tumors remain significantly underrepresented in genomic studies. Our objective was to compare prognostic significance of somatic mutations in ccRCC-associated genes between patients with VHLmut and VHLwt tumors. We analyzed genomic and clinical data of 914 ccRCC patients (720 VHLmut and 194 VHLwt) from the Cancer Genomics of the Kidney (CAGEKID) cohort. Prognostic impacts of individual and co-occurring mutations in 12 RCC-related genes as well as chromosomal copy number variations (CNVs), associated with survival, were evaluated in VHLmut and VHLwt groups through survival analyses. Findings were compared between the two groups. Prognostic significance of somatic mutations in BAP1, SETD2 and PBRM1, is dependent on VHL mutational status. Co-occurring mutations in PBRM1 and SETD2 were significantly associated with poorer clinical outcomes in VHLmut tumors, but not in VHLwt tumors. TP53 mutations were associated with poorer survival in VHLwt tumors. The differing prognostic effects of somatic mutations by VHL status suggest distinct underlying mechanisms of disease progression in VHLwt ccRCCs, highlighting the need to consider VHLwt separately from VHLmut tumors in prognostic and predictive models. Further investigations of these observations in independent cohorts are warranted.

papers.title: Underwater dielectric elastomer actuators with large bending deformation for soft robots
papers.abstract: Soft robots are promising platforms for underwater exploration and biological sampling because of their compliance and adaptability. Dielectric elastomer actuators (DEAs), particularly bending DEAs, are appealing for underwater soft robots because they enable diverse robotic architectures. However, existing underwater bending DEAs are limited in deformation magnitude and speed. Here, we present an underwater DEA comprising a layered elastomer with an encapsulated water electrode, an inextensible layer, and transverse reinforcing frames. The inextensible layer restricts deformation on one side of the actuator to induce bending, while the transverse frames further constrain lateral deformation, enabling larger and faster bending deformation. The resulting actuator achieves a maximum bending angle of 308.5° (corresponding to a curvature of 82.8 m− 1), and its voltage dependence is captured by an analytical model. It further attains maximum bending speeds of 161.1°/s and 245.0°/s upon voltage application and removal, respectively, and a blocked force of 57.2 mN, while maintaining stable actuation over 10,000 cycles. The actuator was further demonstrated as an electrically driven biohybrid luminescent device incorporating Pyrocystis lunula and as a soft gripper capable of manipulating a live jellyfish. These results highlight the potential of the proposed DEA for advancing underwater soft robotic systems.

papers.title: Composite approach to quantifying regulating soil-based ecosystem services using multiple indicators
papers.abstract: The spatial evaluation of soil functions and soil-based ecosystem services (SES) is a key challenge and demand nowadays. SES can provide a scientific background to the decision and policy-making. We define them as benefits that humans and the environment derive from soils and their functions. In our studies we presented the first maps of SES on a national scale for Poland. The research was focused on evaluation of regulating SES, which plays a crucial role in the crop production and circulation of matter and processes in the entire environment. Regulating SES contribute to CO2 fluxes and sequestration, nutrient cycling, water cycle regulation, control of erosion and mass movements, among others. In this research we develop the multi-indicators index, grouping four SES and 11 separate indicators. For this reason, we used geometric means for calculating regulating SES and their final integrated index. For the nutrients provision, and carbon sequestration we used digital soil mapping approach with quantile regression forest algorithm, while for the water regulation and erosion control, mechanistic and empirical models were applied. Our results showed that regulating SES in Polish agricultural areas is relatively low, indicating serious limitations for Polish agriculture. In particular, 84% agricultural soils were classified as having very low or low status of regulating SES especially due to natural limitations, whereas only 2% showed high status, mainly due to the limited capacity for erosion control and high water retention capacity. This is an important step in the agricultural studies indicating the main soil health problems and areas of improvement to increase the natural potential of soils. The presented approach, due to the applied statistical and point bonitation methods, can be applied to other SES evaluation, and also allows to implement different indicators that may be more important for different regions in the world.

papers.title: G protein–coupled receptor 41 deficiency exacerbates dextran sulfate sodium-induced colitis and is associated with altered gut microbiota composition
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease comprises chronic, relapsing inflammatory disorders of the gastrointestinal tract. G protein-coupled receptor 41 (GPR41), a receptor for short-chain fatty acids, has been implicated in intestinal immune regulation, but its contribution to colitis and the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the susceptibility of GPR41-deficient (Gpr41-/-) mice to dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis. Gpr41-/- mice exhibited more severe colitis, including greater body weight loss and greater colon shortening, than littermate controls. Under antibiotic treatment, no statistically significant differences in colitis severity were detected between Gpr41-/- mice and littermate controls. Furthermore, 16S rRNA gene amplicon analysis revealed differences in gut microbial diversity and composition between Gpr41-/- mice and littermate controls at steady state, with compositional differences also observed after DSS treatment. GPR41 deficiency was also associated with reduced fecal levels of the iron-binding proteins lipocalin-2 (LCN2) and lactoferrin (LTF) at steady state. Prophylactic administration of recombinant LCN2 was associated with numerically lower colitis severity in Gpr41-/- mice, although the differences were not statistically significant. Together, these findings support a protective role for GPR41 in DSS-induced colitis and identify associated changes in iron-binding protein levels and gut microbiota composition.

papers.title: Development and internal validation of a 12-month recurrence nomogram for non-puerperal mastitis: a two-center retrospective cohort study
papers.abstract: To construct and internally validate a recurrence risk prediction model for non-puerperal mastitis (NPM) by integrating sociodemographic, clinical, pathological, laboratory, imaging, and treatment data. A retrospective study was conducted on 517 patients with first-diagnosed NPM admitted to two hospitals from January 2020 to August 2024. Of the 764 initially assessed patients, 83 were excluded for insufficient follow-up, leaving 681 patients who completed the 12-month follow-up. Among these 681 patients, 164 were further excluded due to predefined inclusion/exclusion criteria or incomplete data, resulting in 517 patients in the final analysis. The index date was the documented resolution of clinical symptoms and active imaging abnormalities after initial treatment. LASSO regression was used to select predictors, and multivariate Logistic regression was applied to construct a nomogram model. Model performance was evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC curve), calibration curve, and decision curve analysis. Internal validation was performed using the Bootstrap method. During the 12-month follow-up, 56 patients (10.8%) experienced recurrence. LASSO regression identified five predictors: age, white blood cell count, monocyte proportion, axillary lymphadenopathy, and surgical procedure. Multivariate Logistic regression showed that elevated white blood cell count (OR = 1.449), axillary lymphadenopathy (OR = 4.513), and minimally invasive surgery (OR = 14.390) were independent risk factors for recurrence, while increasing age (OR = 0.941) and elevated monocyte proportion (OR = 0.716) were protective factors. The apparent AUC was 0.921 (95%CI: 0.894–0.948); the optimism-corrected AUC after 5,000 bootstrap resamples was 0.897. At the Youden-optimal threshold, sensitivity was 0.82, specificity 0.87, positive predictive value 0.43, and negative predictive value 0.98. The calibration curve indicated good agreement between predicted and actual probabilities (Hosmer-Lemeshow test, P = 0.147). Decision curve analysis demonstrated clinical net benefit within the threshold probability range of 0.05–0.80. This exploratory nomogram shows good apparent discrimination in the development cohort, but the surgical-procedure coefficient should be interpreted as a predictive marker rather than a causal effect due to confounding by indication. External and center-specific validation are required before clinical use.

papers.title: Amplification-free detection of antibiotic resistance in Enterococcus faecium using PNA-FISH
papers.abstract: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREfm) is a major nosocomial pathogen, with antibiotic resistance mediated by the vanA and vanB operons. Rapid and accurate detection of antibiotic resistance is critical for the timely treatment of bacteremia and sepsis. Although imaging-based approaches using fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) provide a potential diagnostic solution, detecting mRNAs of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in individual cells remains particularly challenging due to their low copy number and transient expression. Here, we present a peptide nucleic acid (PNA)-FISH method for direct detection of vanA- and vanB-associated resistance in individual VREfm cells. A universal probe targeting the conserved region across vancomycin resistance genes and a set of probes exclusively targeting the vanB gene were designed. The universal probe showed increased fluorescence in the vanA-genotype strain upon vancomycin or teicoplanin treatment, and in the vanB-genotype strain upon vancomycin treatment. In contrast, vanB-specific probes showed increased fluorescence exclusively from the vanB-genotype strain upon vancomycin treatment, confirming their specificity to the vanB gene. Efficient cellular penetration and high target specificity of PNA probes enabled efficient and reliable detection of antibiotic-resistant bacterial cells, even under a wide-field fluorescence microscope. Negligible signals above background were observed in other major bacterial species associated with bacteremia and sepsis, suggesting the potential detection of antibiotic-resistant strains in mixed microbial samples. When integrated with microbe-capturing techniques, this method may enable culture-independent detection of antibiotic resistance without nucleic acid amplification or sequencing, with the potential to reduce diagnostic turnaround time.

papers.title: Screening and reporting of occupational noise related hearing disorders using MySmartOH—a cloud-based analytics solution
papers.abstract: This study was aimed to evaluate the validity and agreement of MySmartOH (a novel cloud-based analytical software), as compared to conventional audiometric test, for screening of occupational noise–related hearing disorders (ONRHDs) among Malaysian workers. Subsequently, the time taken for screening and reporting between MySmartOH and the conventional paper-based approach was compared. This cross-sectional study involved 16 occupational health doctors and 320 audiograms. For each hearing condition, sensitivity and specificity tests were used to determine the software’s validity while Cohen’s kappa coefficient was used to assess its agreement. The time taken to screen and report ONRHDs between MySmartOH and the conventional method was analysed. The sensitivity of MySmartOH ranged from 55.6 to 99.1% while specificity ranged between 70.0 and 99.2%. Cohen’s kappa values for MySmartOH ranged between 0.41 and 0.92. For the left ear, screening and reporting were faster with MySmartOH (0.93 and 0.48 min) than with the conventional method (1.25 and 0.87 min). For the right ear, MySmartOH also shortened screening (0.87 vs. 1.15 min) and reporting times (0.47 vs. 0.83 min). MySmartOH reduced screening time by 24.3–25.6% and reporting time by 43.3–44.8%. MySmartOH demonstrated variable diagnostic performance, with moderate-to-high agreement for screening ONRHDs compared with conventional audiometric assessment. It also offers a faster alternative to the conventional method.

papers.title: High intensity interval training modulates autophagy and apoptosis related markers in the liver of D galactose induced aged rats
papers.abstract: Aging deregulates autophagy and apoptosis, leading to progressive liver dysfunction. This study examined the effects of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on autophagy and apoptosis-related markers in a D-galactose (D-gal)-induced aging model, focusing on the AMPK signaling pathway. Male Wistar rats were allocated into four experimental groups: Control (CTL), HIIT, D-gal, and D-gal+HIIT. Experimental aging was induced by D-galactose administration for eight weeks, while HIIT was performed using a treadmill running protocol. mRNA expression and protein levels of AMPK, Beclin1, NF-κB (p65), ATG9, and caspase-3 were assessed by real-time PCR and Western blotting, respectively. Total antioxidant and total oxidant status were determined using colorimetric methods. Pro-inflammatory indices were measured by ELISA. AMPK mRNA expression and p-AMPK protein levels were higher in the D-gal+HIIT group than in the D-gal group. HIIT upregulated Beclin1 and ATG9 expression at both the mRNA and protein levels and reduced caspase-3 mRNA expression and cleaved caspase-3 protein levels in the D-gal group. HIIT was associated with a reduction in NF-κB mRNA expression and TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β levels, along with restoration of oxidant/antioxidant balance in D-gal-treated rats. These findings suggest that HIIT is associated with coordinated molecular changes that may help maintain liver homeostasis during experimental aging.

papers.title: Passivity-aware reactive diffusion policy for stable contact-rich manipulation
papers.abstract: Contact-rich manipulation demands stable, low-impact interaction with uncertain environments. Reactive diffusion policies (RDP) achieve strong task success, yet their high-frequency corrective actions can inject energy into the contact, producing large contact forces and instability under disturbance. We propose PaRDP (Passivity-Aware Reactive Diffusion Policy), which augments a slow-fast visual-tactile diffusion base with three lightweight, provably passivity-bounded modules: (i) a Passivity-aware Interaction Frame & Hybrid Force-Position (PIF-HFP) module that selects free-motion degrees of freedom in an estimated interaction frame; (ii) a Passivity-Bounded Fast Force Correction (PB-FFC) shell that projects out energy-increasing corrections through an energy tank with a bounded injection allowance; and (iii) Stability-Conditioned Training (SCT), a training-time regularizer that penalizes net energy injection. We prove that the closed-loop system remains stable whenever the environment is passive. On RDP/TactAR, our primary benchmark, PaRDP improves the All score by $$+0.02$$ to $$+0.05$$ over RDP(Force) and reduces peak contact force by up to $$34\%$$ while adding under $$7\%$$ inference overhead; we additionally list published ForceVLA-Data and RH20T baselines as external reference context for force-aware and cross-dataset settings. Ablation and sensitivity studies confirm the contribution of each module.

papers.title: Quasi-experimental evaluation of a human-centric AI tutoring and human-in-the-loop assessment system in advanced STEM education
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping higher education, yet most deployments of large-language-model tutoring and automated grading target introductory courses and pay limited attention to the transparency, trust, and equity concerns that become acute in advanced, safety-critical technical domains. This paper presents a human-centric AI-assisted instructional system and evaluates it in a postgraduate hardware-security course on electromagnetic protection and side-channel analysis. The system couples three human-centric components: (i) a retrieval-augmented tutoring assistant whose answers are grounded in citable course materials to curb hallucination and preserve traceability; (ii) a human-in-the-loop assessment pipeline in which a language model drafts rubric-based feedback that instructors verify item by item; and (iii) an adaptive, tiered project-based learning path that offers differentiated entry points. We evaluated the system in a quasi-experiment with 47 postgraduates (24 experimental, 23 control) taught concurrently by the same instructors in parallel class sections. The experimental group’s competency score rose from 62.4 to 84.7, against 61.8 to 70.2 for the control group, a difference in gains that was statistically significant and associated with a large effect size ($$t(41.2)=4.55$$, $$p<0.001$$, Cohen’s $$d=1.32$$), while its score dispersion contracted from a standard deviation of 14.5 to 7.2. A baseline-by-group interaction indicated significantly stronger differential improvement among initially lower-scoring students in the experimental section, although this distributional finding is interpreted cautiously given the non-randomised design. Human-in-the-loop grading was associated with a 35.7% reduction in marking time while reaching an AI–instructor agreement of quadratic-weighted Cohen’s $$\kappa =0.95$$; because this agreement measures consistency rather than correctness, we interpret it accordingly. We examine how human oversight, citation grounding, and adaptivity may have jointly contributed to these outcomes, treating the intervention as an integrated bundle whose individual components remain to be isolated, and we set out the responsible-AI safeguards that such deployments require.

papers.title: A dual-branch keypoint Transformer for continuous Korean Sign Language recognition
papers.abstract: Continuous Korean Sign Language recognition requires practical models that capture manual and non-manual articulation. We propose KDS-Former, a compact dual-branch keypoint Transformer that encodes hand and body–face motion, fuses the temporal representations, and predicts gloss sequences using connectionist temporal classification. On KSL-Guide, KDS-Former-S achieved word error rates (WERs) of $$6.33 \pm 1.68$$% and $$7.61 \pm 2.09$$% under seen-signer/unseen-sentence and unseen-signer/unseen-sentence protocols, respectively, using 2.59 million parameters and 1.91 model-compute GFLOPs. KDS-Former-M achieved $$5.68 \pm 1.98$$% and $$6.27 \pm 2.24$$% using 14.75 million parameters and 9.93 model-compute GFLOPs. The larger systems of Min et al. and TEMPO achieved lower mean WERs across three runs, whereas KDS-Former required fewer parameters, lower model-compute GFLOPs, and lower peak GPU memory usage. Under both primary protocols, the full KDS-Former-S achieved lower mean WER than all five controlled ablation variants, although the unseen-signer/unseen-sentence single-branch result showed substantial between-run variability. Under controlled input corruption, both KDS-Former variants showed smaller mean WER degradation than ST-GCN. These results position KDS-Former as an efficiency-oriented, model-level alternative rather than an accuracy-leading method. Signer-generalization results are limited by evaluation on only two held-out signers, and the reported latency was measured on an RTX 4090 without upstream keypoint extraction, preprocessing, or CTC decoding; broader signer-disjoint and hardware-specific validation is therefore required.

papers.title: GreenSense: controlled predictive, computational, and carbon-aware evaluation of efficient neural models for fraud detection
papers.abstract: Green artificial intelligence requires model quality to be evaluated together with computational cost, model size, and estimated environmental impact. This study presents GreenSense as a controlled benchmarking framework for energy-aware fraud detection. Seven configurations are compared on two imbalanced transaction datasets: Compact Nonlinear Dense (CND), full-precision and dynamically quantized tabular CNNs and MLPs, an LTC-style state-refinement network, and a sparse NCP-CfC-style network. All training, quantization, and inference measurements were repeated on a single dedicated workstation (Intel Core i5-13500, Windows 11) under one fixed software stack, thread and CPU-affinity setting, and measurement protocol. Each model–dataset configuration is evaluated over five independently seeded training runs, and each inference measurement is repeated five times in fixed-work windows of at least 30 s. CPU-package energy is measured with CodeCarbon and cross-checked against a second software readout of the same hardware energy counter; CO$$_2$$ is derived from a cited national grid-emission factor. Predictive evaluation emphasizes precision–recall area under the curve (PR-AUC), $$F_1$$, recall, precision, and ROC-AUC. On FraudTrain, the LTC-style model achieved the highest mean PR-AUC (0.8015, 95% CI 0.7947–0.8082), followed by MLP-FP32 (0.7679) and NCP-CfC-style (0.7654). On the ULB Credit Card benchmark, MLP-FP32 (0.7554) and CND (0.7528) had the highest mean PR-AUC with overlapping intervals, while CNN-FP32 had the highest mean $$F_1$$ (0.1889). Training accounted for more than 99.9% of lifecycle-equivalent energy for every configuration. Dynamic INT8 quantization reduced MLP storage size by 1.94$$\times $$ (FraudTrain) and 2.09$$\times $$ (ULB) but increased inference energy per transaction in all four FP32–INT8 pairs (by 43–47% for the MLP and 4–6% for the CNN; all paired intervals excluded zero). Its predictive effect was dataset-dependent: FraudTrain MLP PR-AUC decreased by 0.301 (95% CI $$-0.358$$ to $$-0.247$$), whereas the ULB change was only $$-0.003$$. The PR-AUC/lifecycle-energy Pareto sets were CND, MLP-FP32, and LTC-style on FraudTrain and CND and MLP-FP32 on ULB. GreenSense provides a reproducible, task-specific basis for comparing predictive, computational, and estimated environmental operating points; all code, configurations, raw energy logs, and manifests are archived with a DOI.

papers.title: Genetic heterogeneity of Plasmodium falciparum across three areas of varying transmission intensity in Ethiopia based on merozoite surface protein (msp) genes msp1 and msp2
papers.abstract: Plasmodium falciparum malaria continues to be a significant threat in Ethiopia. This study aimed at assessing the genetic heterogeneity of this malaria parasite. Understanding the genetic diversity of P. falciparum is crucial for informing public health strategies, including vaccine development, diagnostic accuracy, treatment efficacy, and targeted control interventions. Samples for this study were collected from three malaria-endemic sites in Ethiopia with varying transmission intensities—Metema (northwest), Wondogenet (south), and Metehara (central-east). A consecutive convenient sampling technique was employed to recruit outpatients initially enrolled in an uncomplicated malaria therapeutic efficacy study in 2015 from these sites, along with additional samples collected from malaria suspects attending the Metehara health centre in 2019. Overall, 661 finger-prick blood samples were collected for malaria microscopy and rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs), while dried blood spot (DBS) samples were obtained on Whatman 903® filter paper for molecular analysis. This study specifically utilized selected 150 quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR)-confirmed P. falciparum monoinfection-positive samples from the previously reported total of 661 samples to investigate previously unreported merozoite surface protein (msp1 and msp2) genes-based genetic heterogeneity. Genotyping of P. falciparum msp1 and msp2 genes was conducted using nested PCR, and the mean multiplicity of infection (MOI), polyclonal infections and expected heterozygosity index (He) were assessed. Out of the 150 samples analyzed, successful genotyping rates of 45.3% were revealed for msp1 and 43.3% for msp2 across the sites. Notable variations in allele frequencies were observed, with the K1 allele predominating for msp1 and the FC27 allele for msp2. Metema exhibited the highest complexity of infections, with mean MOI values of 1.53 for msp1 and 2.14 for msp2, alongside the greatest genetic diversity. The analysis indicated that polyclonal infections were prevalent, particularly in Metema and Wondogenet. The overall pooled mean MOI across all study sites was 1.26 for msp1 and 1.59 for msp2, with an overall polyclonality rate of 35.3% and 44.6%, respectively. Important differences in allele frequencies and a slight reduction in both mean MOI and He were observed over time between samples collected in 2015 and 2019 in Metehara. This study highlights the genetic diversity and regional variations of P. falciparum in Ethiopia, and shifts in population dynamics.

papers.title: Brain tumor classification from contrast-enhanced T1 MRI, a patient-wise deep learning study
papers.abstract: Accurate classification of intracranial tumors on contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI (CE-T1) is challenged by heterogeneous enhancement patterns and strong correlations among multiple slices from the same patient. We propose a compact CE-T1 MRI analysis framework that standardizes image intensities, enhances local CLAHE (contrast using contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization), and applies a lightweight convolutional classifier whose slice-level probabilities are aggregated to obtain a single patient-level prediction. An independent optional U-Net-based pathway provides binary tumor segmentation when spatial delineation is required. Evaluation was performed using a strictly patient-wise, leakage-controlled protocol with stratified five-fold cross-validation on 233 subjects (3,064 slices) comprising glioma, meningioma, and pituitary adenoma. The classifier achieved 99.4% patient-level accuracy, with macro-averaged sensitivity and specificity of 99.3% and 99.0%, respectively. The optional segmentation pathway achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 97.3%. Post-hoc temperature scaling reduced the patient-level expected calibration error from 3.0% to approximately 1.2%, although larger independent cohorts are required to determine the stability of this estimate. The classifier contains 7.8 million parameters and requires approximately 15.9 GFLOPs per $$256\times 256$$ slice, with an end-to-end inference latency of approximately 0.41 s per slice under the evaluated hardware configuration. These findings demonstrate strong patient-level performance within the evaluated retrospective cohort. The framework is intended as a research-stage approach for reproducible evaluation rather than a clinically validated diagnostic system for routine radiology practice. However, no independent quantitative external validation was performed; therefore, multi-centre evaluation across different scanners, acquisition protocols, institutions, and patient populations is required before generalizability or clinical applicability can be established.

papers.title: Multi-agent dual federated learning for intelligent task offloading in hierarchical edge–fog–cloud 6G networks
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks is driving the need for intelligent task offloading frameworks capable of simultaneously satisfying stringent latency, energy efficiency, scalability, and privacy requirements. Existing task offloading approaches are constrained by centralized learning architectures, binary offloading decisions, inadequate handling of heterogeneous non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data, and limited awareness of wireless interference dynamics, resulting in suboptimal resource utilization in hierarchical Edge–Fog–Cloud (EFC) environments. To address these challenges, this study proposes MADFL-6G, a Multi-Agent Dual Federated Learning framework for intelligent task offloading in hierarchical 6G networks — ‘Dual’ referring to MWFA’s two-component aggregation weighting, which jointly combines data-volume proportionality and KL-divergence-based distribution-similarity penalization (Sect. 3.5, Eq. 9). The proposed framework integrates distributed Dueling Deep Q-Network (Dueling DQN) agents with Prioritized Experience Replay (PER), a Mobility-Weighted Federated Averaging (MWFA) strategy for robust aggregation under heterogeneous data distributions, an interference-aware seven-dimensional state representation, and a five-action adaptive partial task offloading mechanism that dynamically distributes computational workloads across edge, fog, and cloud resources. The task offloading process is formulated as a set of coupled, independently learning agents operating within a shared, non-stationary Edge–Fog–Cloud environment, incorporating stochastic wireless channel conditions and queueing dynamics to accurately model realistic 6G environments. Extensive experiments conducted on more than 200,000 real task execution records demonstrate that MADFL-6G achieves an average latency of 61 ms, energy consumption of 0.31 J, and a 98.7% task success rate, outperforming conventional federated deep Q-learning by 28.2%, 31.1%, and 2.6%, respectively, while substantially exceeding heuristic and centralized baselines. Additional analyses, including scalability evaluation, component ablation, statistical significance testing, robustness under non-IID settings, and SHAP-based explainability, confirm the effectiveness, interpretability, and reliability of the proposed framework. These findings demonstrate that MADFL-6G provides a scalable, privacy-aware, raw-data-preserving, and explainable solution for intelligent resource management in emerging 6G applications, including autonomous transportation, industrial Internet of Things, smart cities, and extended reality services.

papers.title: SSG-GAN: spatial-spectral guided generative adversarial network for hyperspectral reconstruction from RGB images
papers.abstract: Hyperspectral reconstruction from a single RGB image provides a practical and low-cost solution for spectral imaging with conventional cameras. However, the task is highly ill-posed because three broad RGB channels must be mapped to multiple continuous narrow spectral bands. Existing methods, including convolutional, Transformer-based, multi-scale, and adversarial reconstruction models, have improved reconstruction accuracy, but many of them still learn RGB spatial structures and hyperspectral reconstruction features in a coupled reconstruction stream, while adversarial constraints mainly focus on spatial distributions. To address these issues, we propose SSG-GAN, a spatially guided hyperspectral reconstruction framework. The generator explicitly decouples RGB spatial-prior extraction from hyperspectral reconstruction through a dedicated multi-scale guidance branch. At corresponding decoding stages, a Cross-Branch Spatial-Spectral Attention (CB-SSA) module uses guidance-derived spatial weights to modulate reconstruction features and further refines them through feature-channel modulation and channel recalibration. Moreover, the discriminator incorporates a dedicated pixel-wise spectral-vector branch to evaluate joint band responses, providing complementary adversarial supervision alongside the multi-scale spatial branches. Experiments on CAVE, Harvard, and ICVL demonstrate the competitive performance of SSG-GAN. Specifically, it achieves MRAE/SAM/RMSE values of 0.0605/0.0734/0.0177 on CAVE, 0.0393/0.0294/0.0041 on Harvard, and 0.0303/0.0309/0.00101 on ICVL.

papers.title: Effects of motor imagery training on landing kinematics in female volleyball players: a randomized controlled trial
papers.abstract: Although the effectiveness of motor imagery (MI) in improving performance in sports is known, there is no research on its effect on jumping and landing in female volleyball players. Thirty female volleyball players were randomized into three groups and followed up for 12 weeks. Participants in the Solo training (ST) and Group training (GT) groups received the motor imagery intervention individually or in a group setting, respectively, whereas the Control group (CG) continued routine volleyball training only. Jump landing was recorded, and hip, knee, and ankle joint angles were measured using the Dartfish Analysis System. Neurocognitive functions were measured using the Computerized Neurocognitive Tests Vital Signs (CNSVS). Initial contact knee varus–valgus and ankle plantarflexion showed significant group × time interactions (right knee: p = 0.024; left knee: p = 0.005; ankle plantarflexion: p = 0.001). Post hoc analysis revealed that for the right knee, the GT group showed greater changes in the varus–valgus angle than the CG (GT vs. CG: p = 0.024). For the left knee, both the ST and GT groups showed greater changes in the varus–valgus angle than the CG (ST vs. CG: p = 0.011; GT vs. CG: p = 0.013). A significant group × time interaction was observed for initial-contact plantarflexion angle; the pre-to-post change was greater in the ST group than in both the GT group (p = 0.002) and the CG (p = 0.008), whereas the GT and CG did not differ. During full contact, hip flexion (p = 0.004), knee flexion (p = 0.027), left knee valgus/varus (p = 0.003), and ankle flexion (p = 0.041) also showed significant group × time interactions. Post hoc analysis revealed greater reductions in hip flexion (ST vs. CG: p = 0.004), knee flexion (ST vs. CG: p = 0.023), and greater changes in ankle flexion (ST vs. CG: p = 0.049) in the ST group, whereas both the ST and GT groups demonstrated greater changes in left knee valgus/varus than the CG (ST vs. CG: p = 0.008; GT vs. CG: p = 0.007). Most neurocognitive outcomes did not show significant group × time interactions. Significant interactions were observed for processing speed and simple attention; however, these findings were not supported by Bonferroni-adjusted post-hoc interaction contrasts, which showed no significant pairwise differences in pre-to-post changes between groups. Motor imagery training was associated with changes in selected laboratory-based landing kinematics in female volleyball players.
