However, no clear evidence was found for meaningful improvements in neurocognitive performance. Further studies including kinetic analyses, injury incidence, and sport-specific landing assessments are needed to determine whether these kinematic changes translate into clinically meaningful reductions in injury risk. Participants were randomly allocated into three groups. This trial was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT07009080). The trial record was initially submitted on May 27, 2025, met the registry’s quality-control criteria on May 29, 2025, and was publicly posted on June 6, 2025. Participant enrolment commenced on June 9, 2025.

papers.title: Efficient color image encoding using chroma-subsampled hybrid quantum representation
papers.abstract: Quantum image representation (QIR) is a fundamental component of quantum image processing, but existing color-image encoding approaches often require substantial qubit resources, gate counts, and circuit depths. This work presents CS-HQR (Chroma-Subsampled Hybrid Quantum Representation), a hybrid quantum classical framework that integrates YCbCr color space transformation and 4:2:0 chroma subsampling with quantum state preparation. The proposed framework preserves the luminance component at full spatial resolution while encoding chrominance components at reduced resolution, thereby reducing the amount of color information requiring quantum encoding. CS-HQR employs a dual circuit architecture in which the luminance component is encoded using 16 qubits and the subsampled chrominance components use 15 qubits including a channel selection qubit. The framework was evaluated using 6097 medical brain MRI images, with circuit level analysis performed across the complete dataset and reconstruction-quality analysis conducted on a representative subset. Compared with MCQI, CS-HQR requires 16 rather than 18 qubits and achieves approximately 54.0% reduction in transpiled gate count and 72.2% reduction in transpiled circuit depth, while maintaining high reconstruction quality. To assess generality beyond grayscale derived medical images, additional experiments were conducted on the Kodak, BSD500, and USC-SIPI natural colour benchmarks, obtaining mean SSIM values of 0.987, 0.981, and 0.984, respectively, with approximately 50% gate reduction. These results indicate that classical perceptual redundancy reduction can be incorporated into quantum image encoding to reduce state preparation resources while maintaining high reconstructed-image quality. The study provides a simulation-based evaluation of CS-HQR and establishes a basis for further investigation on hardware-aware and noise-resilient quantum image processing systems.

papers.title: Determination of suitable reference genes for RT-qPCR analysis in Gryllodes sigillatus (Orthoptera: Gryllidae)
papers.abstract: The tropical house cricket Gryllodes sigillatus is an emerging species in edible insect farming; however, molecular resources for this species remain limited. In particular, the absence of validated reference genes hinders accurate RT-qPCR normalization and reliable gene expression analyses across different tissues. To address this limitation, we evaluated the expression stability of six candidate reference genes (ACTB, EF1α, GAPDH, HisH3, RPL5, and 18 S rRNA) in four tissue types (abdomen, head, legs, and whole body). Gene stability was assessed using geNorm, NormFinder, BestKeeper, the comparative ΔCt method, and RefFinder, while the optimal number of reference genes was determined by pairwise variation (Vₙ/Vₙ₊₁) analysis. Candidate genes were identified from the G. sigillatus genome and annotated by BLAST and reciprocal BLAST analyses, and all experimental procedures complied with the MIQE 2.0 guidelines. ACTB, RPL5, and EF1α were identified as the most suitable reference genes for abdominal samples; ACTB, GAPDH, and RPL5 for head samples; EF1α, RPL5, and ACTB for leg samples; and EF1α, ACTB, and RPL5 for whole-body samples. In contrast, GAPDH and His H3 exhibited relatively unstable expression across most tissues, with the exception of GAPDH in the head. Although 18 S rRNA consistently ranked among the most stable reference genes, its high transcript abundance suggests that its suitability should be carefully evaluated, particularly for the normalization of low-abundance target genes. This study provides the first validated reference gene panel for G. sigillatus, enabling reliable tissue-specific RT-qPCR normalization and supporting future gene expression studies, although validation under additional experimental conditions is still required.

papers.title: Physical activity and sedentary behavior are longitudinally associated with diurnal cortisol rhythms up to 1 year after colorectal cancer treatment
papers.abstract: Less robust diurnal cortisol rhythms are hypothesized to be associated with fatigue, depressive symptoms, psychological distress, sleep disturbances and poorer quality of life. Sedentary behavior and physical activity may influence cortisol rhythmicity, providing mechanistic leads for intervention strategies. We examined longitudinal associations of accelerometer-assessed sedentary behavior and physical activity with diurnal cortisol patterns among patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) up to 12 months post-treatment. Among 74 CRC survivors, total and prolonged sedentary time (in bouts ≥30 min), total physical activity (TPA), and relative amplitude of physical activity reflecting day-night contrast in activity were determined with 7-day thigh-worn accelerometry at 6 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months after cancer treatment. Salivary cortisol was sampled five times daily over two consecutive days at each follow-up timepoint. As a comprehensive assessment of diurnal cortisol rhythms, the relative amplitude of cortisol concentration (RA_cort), diurnal slope, area under the curve and cortisol awakening response (CAR) were derived as comprehensive measures of diurnal cortisol rhythms. We used confounder-adjusted linear mixed models to estimate overall longitudinal associations, with coefficients (β) reflecting differences in SD units of the cortisol parameters per 2 h/day of sedentary time, per 1 hour/day of physical activity, or per 1 SD of the RA of physical activity. More total sedentary time (per 2 h/day) was associated with a weaker decline in cortisol over time and thus a flatter slope (β = 0.19; 95% CI = 0.06,0.33). More prolonged sedentary time (per 2 h/day) was associated with a lower RA_cort (β = − 0.12; 95% CI = − 0.23, − 0.01) and flatter cortisol slope (β = 0.16; 95% CI = 0.04,0.27). More TPA (per 1 h/day: β = 0.23; 95% CI = 0.03,0.43) and a higher relative amplitude of physical activity (per SD: β = 0.15; 95% CI = 0.00, 0.29) were associated with a higher RA_cort. More total sedentary time (per 2 h/day) was associated with a higher CAR (β = 0.14; 95% CI = 0.01, 0.27). Higher physical activity levels, a larger RA of physical activity, and less sedentary time were associated with more robust diurnal cortisol rhythms, mainly driven by inter-individual associations. Intervention studies are needed to determine whether modifying these behaviors may improve cortisol rhythmicity after CRC. Registration: EnCoRe study (https://www.onderzoekmetmensen.nl/).

papers.title: A Wavelet-Change-Point framework for sequence-stratigraphic controls on reservoir quality and geomechanical evaluation: a case study of the Asmari-Ghar succession, SW Iran
papers.abstract: The Oligo-Miocene Ghar-Asmari interval of the Dezful Embayment (SW Iran) is a proven reservoir, but its field-scale sequence-stratigraphic framework is poorly documented. We apply a Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) multi-resolution analysis (Meyer wavelet, detail levels D1-D4) to gamma-ray logs of four wells in the Bahregansar and Hendijan fields. Combining D3-D4 local-wavelet-energy maxima with gamma-ray character and member boundaries, eight maximum flooding surfaces (MFS1-MFS8) were interpreted as depth-domain correlation surfaces. The number of surfaces is not an intrinsic output of the transform: energy-peak counts range from about 6 to 34 per well depending on the threshold, and eight emerges at the 90th-95th percentile. Two change-point algorithms were used as independent checks. Bayesian Online Change-Point Detection (BOCPD) matched 71.9% of the 32 surfaces within ± 8 m, which exceeds the agreement expected from random change points (47%, p = 0.001); Pruned Exact Linear Time (PELT) matched 43.8%, which is not distinguishable from chance (38%, p = 0.27). Reservoir quality, based on delivered effective porosity (PHIE) and water saturation (Sw) curves, ranks A > C > D > B (mean PHIE 0.159, 0.131, 0.099, 0.091) and this ranking is unchanged across 81 alternative cut-off combinations. Well A is the most ductile (Brittleness Index, BI = 36.5), whereas wells B, C and D are more brittle (BI = 53.1–61.5). Within the framework, the best reservoir quality and lowest BI occur in the upper packages (MFS5-MFS8, Ghar clastics) and deteriorate downward into the Asmari carbonates; this pattern persists when the MFS depths are perturbed by ± 4 m. Pore pressure from the Eaton sonic method is statistically indistinguishable from hydrostatic and cannot be calibrated, so a first-pass overburden-bounded mud-weight window of about 9.8 ppg (hydrostatic pore pressure) is given with a sensitivity range. The workflow is a screening tool for mixed siliciclastic-carbonate reservoirs of the Zagros foreland; its picks, petrophysical cut-offs and geomechanical values are uncalibrated against core, biostratigraphy or leak-off data.

papers.title: A federated learning framework for cyber-resilient defense in EV-integrated microgrids
papers.abstract: Continuous deployment of moving target defense in modern power grids is often limited to intermittent use in practice because deliberately perturbing the network to expose stealthy cyber attacks pushes the dispatch away from its economic optimum and inflicts an operating-cost penalty that is paid with certainty in every hour of operation, whereas the attacks it prevents are sporadic. In the cluster studied here this penalty amounts to about 298 dollars per hour, roughly 1.4 percent of the base operating cost and 6.2 percent in the most congested microgrid, or about 2.6 million dollars per year. This paper proposes a unified cyber-physical architecture that absorbs most of this penalty while enforcing a minimum subspace-separation margin for attack exposure and preserving the data sovereignty of every participant. The defense layer selects each reactance reconfiguration through a decision-based multi-objective optimizer that simultaneously maximizes the geometric separation needed to expose hidden attacks, minimizes the induced operating cost, and minimizes the physical actuation effort of the flexible-transmission devices. The cost penalty created by the reconfiguration is then absorbed by mobilizing the bidirectional flexibility of electric vehicle fleets, which are dispatched precisely at the buses where the defense creates artificial congestion. Detection of the exposed attacks is delegated to a federated detector that is trained collaboratively across the cluster by exchanging only model parameters, so that raw measurements never leave a local microgrid. The framework is evaluated on a cluster of five interconnected IEEE 30-bus microgrids, each hosting five charging stations with one hundred electric vehicles. The results show that full participation of the vehicle fleet reduces the cluster defense penalty from about 298 to roughly 16 dollars per hour, a reduction close to 95 percent that leaves a small residual cost, while the federated detector reaches a detection area under the curve of about 0.92 and outperforms an isolated, data-scarce local detector. The exposed attacks raise the detection statistic far above its alarm threshold, supporting reliable and economically sustainable protection.

papers.title: Activated platelets release extracellular vesicles with a distinct thromboinflammatory protein signature
papers.abstract: Platelet-derived extracellular vesicles (PDEVs) from activated platelets possess a shifted biomolecular profile and enhanced procoagulant activity. However, the specific EV proteome and surface antigens characterizing these vesicles in acute thrombotic events remain poorly defined. We aimed to identify a thromboinflammatory PDEV surface signature and evaluate its diagnostic potential in deep vein thrombosis (DVT). PDEVs from control or TRAP6-activated washed platelets were analysed by mass spectrometry (MS). Candidate protein markers were validated on the surface of washed platelets PDEVs and plasma EVs from DVT patients, symptomatic non-DVT patients, and healthy controls using an in-house immunocapture bead-based flow cytometry assay. Platelet activation enriched 129 proteins in the PDEV proteome, primarily mediators of coagulation and inflammation. While MS identified high levels of vWF and Factor V, flow cytometry confirmed that CD41, CD62P, CCL5, and CD9 are specifically enriched on the PDEV surface. An integrated multi-marker panel (CD41, CD9, CD151, PF4, FV, CD62P) successfully discriminated DVT patients from healthy controls, but not between DVT and symptomatic non-DVT patients. In conclusion, activation reconfigures the EV proteome and surface into a distinct thromboinflammatory signature. While this signature captures systemic platelet activation in symptomatic patients, further refinement is required to achieve clot-specific diagnostic utility.

papers.title: Multimodal Sentiment-Symptom Disentanglement network for interpretable mental health classification from text and visual data
papers.abstract: Mental health disorders manifest through intertwined affective and symptomatic signals that are difficult to separate using unimodal or naively fused multimodal models, often producing classifiers that conflate general sentiment polarity with clinically meaningful symptom markers and offer little insight into their own decision process. This paper proposes a Multimodal Sentiment-Symptom Disentanglement Network (MSSD-Net) that explicitly decomposes textual and visual representations into two orthogonal latent subspaces — a sentiment-affect subspace capturing general emotional tone and a symptom-specific subspace capturing clinically relevant behavioral and linguistic markers (e.g., psychomotor cues, facial action units, negation and rumination patterns in text). Modality-specific transformer encoders first extract joint text and visual embeddings, which are passed through a disentanglement module trained with a combination of mutual-information minimization, orthogonality regularization, and adversarial subspace classifiers to enforce separation between the two latent streams. A cross-modal attention fusion layer then recombines the disentangled symptom subspaces from both modalities for downstream mental health classification (e.g., depression, anxiety severity levels). At the same time, the sentiment subspace is retained only as an auxiliary, interpretability-supporting signal. To ensure clinical transparency, the framework incorporates a post-hoc and intrinsic explainability layer that projects attention weights and subspace activations back onto input tokens and facial regions, yielding symptom-attributed saliency maps rather than sentiment-confounded heatmaps. Experiments on benchmark multimodal mental health datasets demonstrate that MSSD-Net achieves 89.4% F1-score over E-DAIC and state-of-the-art multimodal baselines, while substantially improving the faithfulness and clinician-rated interpretability of the generated explanations. Ablation studies reveal that disentangling sentiment and symptom is responsible for the performance gain and improved interpretability in joint entangled fusion. The findings indicate that disentangled multimodal architectures can serve as promising, clinically sound methods for automated mental health screening from naturalistic, real-world data.

papers.title: Neuronal cell line expressing full-length mutant huntingtin displays alteration of proteasome activity
papers.abstract: Polyglutamine diseases are incurable genetic neurodegenerative disorders characterized by the accumulation of extended polyglutamine fragments-containing mutant proteins, which are prone to the formation of poorly soluble aggregates. The adequate cellular model is crucial in uncovering the pathological mechanisms responsible for neurotoxicity in Huntington’s disease (HD), screening for therapeutic molecules and elucidation of the molecular mechanisms impacted by particular compound. In the present study, genetic constructs based on the Sleeping Beauty system were created for the stable inducible expression of full-length normal and mutant huntingtin (HTT) in eukaryotic cells. These constructs were then employed to develop model neuronal cells using Neuro-2a cell line. The expression of HTT as well as the accumulation of HTT-immunopositive intracellular aggregates (most characteristic features of HD) was demonstrated, and these aggregates showed colocalization with the proteasome. The activation of the proteasome, as well as changes in the expression of proteasome regulators, components of the autophagy system, and the neuronal proteases cathepsins B and D, reflect the versatility of cellular responses to the mutant pathological forms of HTT.

papers.title: Optimization of ultrasound-assisted enzymatic extraction of volatile oil from Gardenia jasminoides flowers and evaluation of antioxidant activity
papers.abstract: This study developed and optimized an integrated enzymatic pretreatment and ultrasound-assisted extraction (EPUAE) process for volatile oil recovery from Gardenia jasminoides flowers. Pectinase was selected over cellulase through enzyme-type screening. Flower powder underwent enzymatic hydrolysis, enzyme inactivation, and ultrasonic treatment prior to steam distillation. Using Box-Behnkel response surface methodology, hydrolysis temperature, pH, and ultrasound time were optimized at 55 °C, pH 4.6, and 29 min, respectively. The optimized process yielded 0.85% ± 0.03%, representing a significant improvement over steam distillation (0.52%), ultrasound-assisted steam distillation (0.68%), and enzymatic extraction alone (0.63%). The volatile oil demonstrated concentration-dependent radical scavenging activity, with IC50 values of 0.44 mg/mL for DPPH and 0.50 mg/mL for ABTS•+. These findings demonstrate the technical feasibility of the combined EPUAE approach and provide preliminary evidence for the oil’s antioxidant potential. This study provides experimental evidence and technical support for the efficient preparation and application of volatile oil from Gardenia jasminoides flowers.

papers.title: Implementation challenges of eliminating preferential currency in Iran’s pharmaceutical sector
papers.abstract: Before the implementation of Darooyar, Iran’s pharmaceutical sector relied heavily on preferential foreign-exchange allocation for imported medicines and pharmaceutical inputs, while the system faced broader challenges related to financing, affordability, and medicine supply. In this context, the Darooyar plan was introduced to eliminate preferential currency and replace it with a targeted pharmaceutical subsidy mechanism intended to improve the sustainability and transparency of pharmaceutical financing. This study aimed to explore the challenges associated with eliminating preferential currency in Iran’s pharmaceutical sector, with particular attention to financing, governance, stakeholder relationships, and pharmaceutical supply-chain pressures. A qualitative study employing descriptive content analysis was conducted in 2025 to explore the challenges associated with eliminating preferential currency in Iran’s pharmaceutical sector, with particular attention to financing, governance, stakeholder relationships, and pharmaceutical supply-chain pressures. Participants included policymakers, executive managers, insurance specialists, pharmacy technical officers, and pharmaceutical manufacturers. Purposive sampling with a snowball approach was applied, yielding 27 participants. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews using an interview guide. Data collection and analysis were performed concurrently using Atlas.ti software. Five overarching themes, 21 subthemes, and 73 codes were identified regarding the challenges of implementing the policy. The main themes comprised: (1) Weaknesses in policy design, management, planning, and implementation; (2) Reported irregularities, misconduct, and inadequate oversight within the pharmaceutical system; (3) stakeholder dissatisfaction and constraints; (4) financial problems across the pharmaceutical supply chain; and (5) Macroeconomic and policy pressures on pharmaceutical system sustainability. Recommendations include strengthening technological infrastructure (integrated insurance systems and reliable internet), targeted education and communication, establishing independent expert oversight, ensuring sustainable budget allocation with timely online payments, and conducting pilot implementations with continuous evaluation prior to nationwide rollout.

papers.title: Lon protease modulates bacterial morphology, stress tolerance, and virulence in Riemerella anatipestifer
papers.abstract: Riemerella anatipestifer (R. anatipestifer) is an important avian pathogen that causes severe economic losses in the poultry industry, yet its molecular pathogenic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Lon protease has been reported to regulate virulence in several bacterial pathogens, but its role in R. anatipestifer has not yet been defined. In this study, a R. anatipestifer lon deletion mutant was constructed by natural transformation and homologous recombination to investigate the role of lon. Phenotypic analyses showed that deletion of lon did not affect bacterial growth but resulted in a shorter cell length and reduced tolerance to heat, acidic, and oxidative stresses. Adhesion and invasion assays using RAW264.7 murine macrophages revealed that the lon mutant exhibited significantly reduced adhesion and invasion abilities compared with the parental strain. In vivo infection experiments further demonstrated attenuated virulence of the mutant, with an LD50 approximately 50-fold higher than that of the parental strain and less severe pathological lesions in ducklings. RNA-seq analysis identified 54 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the lon mutant, including 29 upregulated and 25 downregulated genes. These DEGs were mainly enriched in metabolic pathways, including nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism, pyrimidine metabolism, ribosome-related pathways, and microbial metabolism in diverse environments. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that lon contributes to the stress tolerance and virulence of R. anatipestifer and provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying its pathogenicity.

papers.title: Real-time embedded control and performance evaluation of BLDC motors for electric vehicle applications
papers.abstract: Brushless DC (BLDC) motors are central to modern electric vehicle (EV) drivetrains, yet achieving high efficiency and stable torque under dynamic conditions remains a significant engineering challenge. This study presents the design and real-time embedded implementation of a motor control system realised on the STM32F103C8T6 microcontroller, together with a hardware-parameterised performance characterisation used to evaluate and cross-validate its behaviour. Two established control strategies—Trapezoidal Commutation and Field-Oriented Control (FOC)—were implemented independently on the same hardware platform under identical load conditions to enable a direct, unbiased comparison. The system incorporates Hall-effect sensor-based rotor position detection, closed-loop PI control (speed for Trapezoidal, d/q current for FOC), Direct Memory Access (DMA) for high-speed data acquisition, and a Controller Area Network (CAN) / Universal Asynchronous Receiver-Transmitter (UART) framework for real-time parameter transmission to a driver-facing display. Characterised performance results, derived from the implemented hardware's own rated parameters, show that FOC achieves a peak efficiency of 92% versus 86% under Trapezoidal Control, with torque ripple reduced by approximately 40% and peak current lowered from 50 to 44 A. The characterised thermal behaviour indicates that FOC maintains motor temperatures below 70 °C at full load, whereas Trapezoidal Control approaches critical thresholds under equivalent conditions. The modular architecture supports scalability across microcontroller tiers and EV configurations, providing a validated and deployable reference for energy-efficient BLDC drive systems.

papers.title: User interaction, perceived narrative quality and perceived spatiotemporal organization are associated with user experience in virtual reality museums
papers.abstract: This study examined associations among user interaction (UE), perceived narrative quality (PNQ), perceived spatiotemporal organization (PSO), sensory experience (SA), and user experience (UX) in virtual reality (VR) museum exhibitions. The stimulus–organism–response framework and embodied cognition informed a model positioning UE, PNQ, and PSO as perceived exhibition attributes, SA as a multisensory organismic state, and UX as an overall evaluation. Cross-sectional survey data from 398 respondents with prior VR museum experience were analyzed using second-order structural equation modeling. The model showed acceptable overall fit (χ²/df = 1.592, CFI = 0.945, RMSEA = 0.039). UE, PNQ, and PSO were positively associated with both SA and UX, and SA was positively associated with UX. UE had the largest standardized direct coefficient for UX (β = 0.658), while PSO had the largest coefficient for SA (β = 0.400). The indirect estimates through SA were 0.116, 0.131, and 0.136, respectively; all bootstrap confidence intervals excluded zero. This study refines the application of the stimulus–organism–response framework to VR museums by distinguishing sensory experience from overall UX. The findings provide an empirical basis for evaluating interaction, narrative quality, spatiotemporal organization, and multisensory presentation as related aspects of exhibition design.

papers.title: First application of a ball-pen probe for direct measurements of plasma potential and nonlinear fluctuation dynamics in a linear helicon plasma
papers.abstract: Direct measurements of the plasma space potential and electron temperature are essential for characterizing plasma dynamics and fluctuations, particularly in magnetized plasma systems. Here, a ball-pen probe (BPP) is assembled and installed for the first time on a linear helicon plasma device, enabling direct and fast measurements of the plasma space potential and, in combination with a Langmuir probe, estimation of the electron temperature. A comparative study between BPP and Langmuir probe measurements demonstrates the success of the BPP in simultaneously resolving radial profiles and temporal fluctuations of the plasma potential and electron temperature. The BPP floating potential approximates the plasma potential directly in the edge and peripheral regions, whereas a finite correction is required in the core. Preliminary measurements further reveal low-frequency instabilities and nonlinear plasma potential dynamics that are not directly accessible through Langmuir probe measurements. These results demonstrate for the first time the potential of BPPs for direct investigation of plasma potential dynamics and turbulence in linear helicon plasmas.

papers.title: Chitosan-intercalated FePS 3 as novel and efficient adsorbent for Congo-red dye removal from aqueous solution
papers.abstract: This study investigates surface adsorption of Congo red dye (CR) by iron phosphorus trisulphide (FePS3) before and after chitosan (CS) intercalation. The novel intercalation of CS into the layered nanomaterial FePS3 was processed to obtain FePS3-CS. The materials of FePS3 and FePS3-CS were characterized by XRD, FTIR, SEM–EDX, and BET techniques. These tests verified the effective intercalation of the chitosan into the layered nanomaterial FePS3 with improved characteristics for applications involving adsorption. XRD measurements show a slight shift and partial intercalation of CS into FePS3 layers, and some diffraction peaks have disappeared. This behavior may be due to CS as a polymer interacting with FePS3 through electrostatic interactions between the amino/hydroxyl groups of CS and S-containing FePS3, surfaces, and hydrogen bonding. IR and SEM–EDX confirm the presence of CS functional groups and main elements after intercalation with FePS3. FePS3 and FePS3-CS exhibited notable removal of Congo-Red from artificial aqueous solutions. The best adsorption circumstances of FePS3 and FePS3-CS were found in the presence of a dye concentration of 50 mg/L, a dose of (0.05 g and 0.025 g), and pH 5 and 6, respectively, and a contact time of 90 min. Under these conditions, the maximum adsorption efficiencies of FePS3 and FePS3-CS are 91.4 and 99%, respectively. The results of the kinetic study indicated that a pseudo-second-order kinetic model described the adsorption process with a high degree of agreement between the experimental data and the kinetic model. Moreover, the best kinetic model describing the equilibrium data is the Freundlich isotherm, and this model demonstrates multilayer adsorption behavior. These results highlight the proper effectiveness and promise of FePS3 and FePS3-CS as novel adsorbents for CR dye removal applications.

papers.title: Federated dual-attention temporal convolutional networks for privacy-preserving intrusion detection in EV charging infrastructure
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure has increased exposure to cyberattacks, while conventional centralized intrusion detection remains poorly suited to distributed and privacy-sensitive EVSE environments. This study proposes a federated learning framework based on a Dual-Attention Temporal Convolutional Network (DA-TCN) for collaborative cyberattack detection without centralized data sharing. The model combines dilated causal convolutions with channel and temporal attention to capture complex dependencies in multimodal EVSE telemetry. To improve federated optimization, we introduce Federated Stochastic Weight Averaging (FedSWA) and client-local mixup augmentation, which together enhance generalization and robustness across distributed clients. Evaluated on the CICEVSE2024 dataset, the proposed framework achieved 99.29% accuracy and 99.10% macro F1-score, outperforming a centralized baseline (98.79% accuracy) while maintaining perfect recall for benign and cryptojacking traffic. With an inference latency of 8.26 ms per batch and a model size of 4.07 MB, the framework is well suited for real-time edge deployment. A complementary Isolation Forest module provides unsupervised zero-day anomaly detection. These results demonstrate that federated learning can deliver accurate, lightweight, and deployment-ready intrusion detection for privacy-preserving EV charging infrastructure.

papers.title: His-tag-directed, stable conjugation of proteins via [Co III (NTA/IDA)(CO 3 )] 2−/− reagents
papers.abstract: Site-selective conjugation of proteins remains an important tool in biological research, medical engineering as well as the production of biopharmaceutical products and biosensors. However, current methodologies still suffer from one or more drawbacks such as a potential reduced protein functionality, lack of stability, or laboratory simplicity and versatility. Here we report a stable, His-tag-directed and physiological system for the conjugation of His-tagged proteins or an antibody by cobalt(III)-carbonate-mediated functionalization with nitrilotriacetic acid (NTA)-based or iminodiacetic acid (IDA)-based reagents ([CoIII(NTA/IDA)(CO3)]2−/−). In comparison to the well-established metal(II)-NTA/IDA-mediated interactions, the application of low-spin octahedral dia​magnetic complexes of cobalt(III) results in a stable complex formation that is chemically inert towards various chelators and reduction agents. Thus, the usage of carbonatocobalt(III) complex reagents helps overcome current limitations by obviating the present H2O2-dependent oxidation step and was associated with an increase in coupling efficacy by about 200% and 100% for NTA-reagents and IDA-reagents, respectively. This allows for a simple and His-tag-directed protein or antibody conjugation under physiological conditions within a reasonable time without compromising conjugate stability, function, or protein binding efficacy.

papers.title: Evaluating large language models for quality control in research ethics review
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) could streamline research ethics and governance review by automating routine quality control checks. This study assessed Claude 3.5 Sonnet, ChatGPT4o, and Microsoft CoPilot in evaluating participant information sheets against Health Research Authority standards. Six clinical trial applications were processed using 32 standardised queries, with accuracy, processing time, error rates, and response quality assessed by two blinded reviewers. Claude showed the highest accuracy, detected more deviations from guidance, and had the fastest processing time (7.17 ± 0.68 min vs. ChatGPT 13.58 ± 2.2 min, CoPilot 23.25 ± 6.21 min). Hallucination rates were lowest in Claude, followed by ChatGPT and CoPilot. Claude also received the highest response quality ratings (77.6% “very good” vs. ChatGPT 56.7%, CoPilot 45.2%). While all three models were capable, Claude consistently outperformed the others, demonstrating the potential of LLM-assisted quality control while emphasizing the need for human oversight.

papers.title: Environmental conditions associated with the occurrence of Haematococcus pluvialis in agricultural landscapes affected by intensive livestock production farming
papers.abstract: Intensive livestock production is associated with increased pressure on aquatic environments in agricultural landscapes. The occurrence of Haematococcus pluvialis in waters exposed to intensive livestock production was analysed in relation to selected physicochemical parameters. The study was conducted at two locations characterized by high livestock density and included precipitation, surface, groundwater, and well waters. The alga was detected in surface and precipitation waters, but was absent from groundwater. The occurrence of H. pluvialis was associated with moderately nutrient-enriched waters characterized by elevated conductivity and slightly alkaline pH. Elevated nutrient concentrations were recorded in waters influenced by intensive livestock production. The results suggest that H. pluvialis may represent a potential candidate indicator of aquatic environments exposed to intensive agricultural pressure. However, the observed relationships are associative rather than direct causal effects, and further studies are required to evaluate the broader indicator potential of this species under different environmental conditions.

papers.title: Nutrients and consumer pressure influence coral and microbiome recovery following sequential marine heatwaves
papers.abstract: Current and projected ocean conditions under climate change necessitate an understanding of coral holobiont resilience, factors contributing to host survival during marine heatwaves (MHWs), and how corals can recover after MHWs subside. It is especially important to understand how MHWs may interact with local stressors such as nutrient pollution and overfishing. Here, we used a five-year field experiment to investigate the effects of nutrient enrichment and consumer exclusion on host mortality (percent dead tissue) and microbiome stochasticity (beta dispersion) of three coral species, Acropora retusa, Porites lobata, and Pocillopora spp., following MHWs in Moorea, French Polynesia. Our experiment tracked resident coral colonies and their microbiomes through time and captured two MHWs. The interaction of nutrient enrichment with consumer pressure played a significant, yet coral-specific role in host and microbiome recovery from sequential MHWs. Specifically, after the MHWs and under reduced consumer pressure, A. retusa and P. lobata experienced lower host mortality when subjected to ambient nutrient levels. Under high consumer pressure, A. retusa had lower host mortality when nutrient levels were elevated. However, under low consumer pressure, corals with a history of elevated nutrient exposure experienced higher mortality and microbiome stochasticity. On the other hand, Pocillopora spp. microbiomes were more homogenous under elevated nutrients and consumer pressure. Additionally, a reduction in a dominant P. lobata bacterial symbiont, Parendozoicomonas haliclonae, was strongly associated with increased host mortality during and after the MHWs. Overall, these results suggest that local nutrient inputs and fishing pressure can significantly alter reef recovery from MHWs, despite heat stress masking the impacts of these local-scale factors during MHWs.

papers.title: Deep generative design and structure-based evaluation of celecoxib-inspired PTGS2/COX-2 ligands: a computational study in the context of adenomyosis-associated inflammation
papers.abstract: Adenomyosis is a chronic inflammatory gynecological disorder in which cyclooxygenase-2 (PTGS2/COX-2)-derived prostaglandin signaling contributes to inflammation. This study asked whether deep learning-based generative modification of the celecoxib scaffold yields compounds with a more favorable predicted interaction profile at PTGS2. A generative platform combining a three-dimensional convolutional neural network with a conditional variational autoencoder returned twelve analogues, all carried forward without post hoc selection and examined by substructure analysis, docking at the experimentally defined ligand-binding site, pharmacophore comparison, ADMET and toxicity prediction, density functional theory, and 200 ns molecular dynamics with MM/GBSA estimation. The benzenesulfonamide group of celecoxib was retained in five of twelve analogues and the trifluoromethyl-pyrazole core in none, so the compounds are better described as scaffold-hopped analogues than as close derivatives. AI Analogue 2 returned the most favorable predicted binding energy (− 10.024 kcal/mol; celecoxib − 7.748 kcal/mol) and formed a persistent complex with an effective binding energy of − 51.89 kcal/mol. Its predicted pose lies along the main cyclooxygenase channel rather than the COX-2 side pocket occupied by celecoxib, so the two energies are not comparable as affinities. Redocking of the co-crystallized ligand gave a deviation of 1.924 Å and the celecoxib trajectory did not converge, indicating a rigid-receptor starting-pose artifact rather than a property of the generated compounds. Predicted blood–brain barrier permeability coincided with an active neurotoxicity call, identifying central exposure as the principal predicted liability. The study does not establish COX-2 inhibition, selectivity over COX-1, improved safety, or therapeutic activity in adenomyosis.

papers.title: Integrating sustainable technological interventions for cleaner fertilizer production and occupational ammonia exposure reduction
papers.abstract: Egypt's fertilizer industry is a major component of the petrochemical sector and relies heavily on ammonia during nitrogenous fertilizer production, creating potential occupational exposure risks for workers. Over the past decade, sustainable technological interventions and pollution-control measures have been implemented to reduce ammonia emissions and improve workplace safety. This study assessed occupational ammonia exposure among workers in a modern nitrogenous fertilizer plant in Alexandria, Egypt, and evaluated the effectiveness of these interventions. Ammonia concentrations were measured at representative operational stations using a MIRAN gas analyzer, and a structured questionnaire was administered to assess workers' occupational characteristics, use of personal protective equipment, health complaints, and awareness of occupational hazards. Ammonia concentrations ranged from 0.70 to 1.06 ppm, remaining approximately 95.8–97.2% below the occupational exposure limit of 25 ppm recommended by the American Conference of Governmental Industrial Hygienists (ACGIH) and the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH). These low exposure levels were completed through the implementation of cleaner production technologies, including the Uhde ammonia synthesis process, replacement of conventional urea melting and prilling with environmentally friendly granulation technology, acidic scrubbing systems, condensate stripping, ammonia recovery and recycling, emission capture systems, and preventive maintenance practices. The findings demonstrate that integrating cleaner production technologies, Best Available Techniques (BAT), continuous environmental monitoring, ammonia detection systems, emergency response measures, and targeted occupational health training can effectively minimize occupational ammonia exposure, enhance worker safety, ensure compliance with international occupational health standards, and promote environmentally sustainable and economically efficient fertilizer production

papers.title: Evaluating large language models for public patient education on levodopa therapy in Parkinson’s disease: accuracy, empathy, reliability, and readability
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based chatbots are increasingly used for health information, but their performance in Parkinson’s disease (PD) patient education remains unclear. This study evaluated five widely used LLM-based chatbots in answering public questions about levodopa therapy. In this cross-sectional comparative study, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, DeepSeek, and Doubao were assessed using a structured set of levodopa-related patient education questions. In the primary analysis, 265 responses were evaluated by five blinded raters for safety, accuracy, empathy, and information quality using predefined criteria, including DISCERN, EQIP, JAMA benchmark criteria, and the Global Quality Score. Readability was assessed using six established indices. An additional 265 responses were generated in an independent repeat-generation analysis using the same question set to assess response stability. Inter-rater agreement was high. Safe-response rates ranged from 86.8% to 94.3%. Accuracy differed significantly, with Copilot and DeepSeek showing the highest median scores, whereas empathy differences were modest and closely clustered. Doubao had the highest DISCERN and EQIP scores, while ChatGPT had the lowest information-quality scores. Gemini showed the best readability profile and Doubao the poorest. Repeat-generation analysis showed generally high stability, with 97.0% exact safety agreement and largely preserved model rankings. Current LLM-based chatbots generated generally informative English-language responses about levodopa therapy, but safety gaps, variable information quality, and poor readability remained. These findings reflect expert-rated output quality rather than demonstrated patient education effectiveness, and patient-centered validation is warranted.

papers.title: Age-dependent effects of titrating anodal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) intensity on motor sequence learning
papers.abstract: Optimising the currently heterogenous efficacy of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) interventions for motor learning requires identifying stimulation parameters facilitating performance while accounting for age-related differences in baseline performance and mechanisms underlying neuroplasticity. We systematically explored anodal tDCS intensity effects on implicit motor sequence learning (IMSL) in young and older adults. The study utilised a randomised, double-blind, counterbalanced crossover design. Ninety-six healthy participants (48 young adults, 48 older adults) completed a serial reaction time task (SRTT) with online sham or anodal tDCS over M1 at intensities of 1, 2, and 3 mA. The next day, memory retention and consolidation were assessed in a recall test. Both age groups demonstrated IMSL across conditions. While 1 mA tDCS improved IMSL in young adults by reducing reaction times, higher intensities had no significant benefit compared to sham. In older adults, anodal tDCS did not affect general task performance compared to sham, but selective sequence learning was lower with 1mA tDCS. Young adults’ performance remained unchanged between learning and recall, indicating motor memory retention, but following anodal tDCS conditions, older adults showed faster reaction times in sequence blocks at recall compared to learning, indicating offline consolidation. The results demonstrate age-dependent and non-linear dose-dependent effects of anodal tDCS on IMSL. This underscores the necessity for age-adapted protocols for experimental and clinical tDCS applications. Future research should explore neurophysiological reasons for altered tDCS efficacy in older adults found in the present study.

papers.title: Secrecy-aware sequential RIS selection for energy efficient user-assisted cooperative NOMA in 6G networks
papers.abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) have emerged as a transformative technology for achieving ultra-reliable and inherently secure connectivity by enabling software-defined control of the electromagnetic environment in sixth-generation (6G) networks. However, most existing RIS-assisted Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) frameworks assume static user positions or rely on simple nearest-RIS selection (NRS) criteria, which fail to account for the security risks posed by spatially distributed eavesdroppers along a mobility path. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a secrecy-aware, RIS-enabled user-cooperative NOMA framework, where a near-user acts as a cooperative relay to assist a mobile far-user in the presence of localized eavesdropping threats. A novel Sequential-Action Secrecy-aware RIS Selection (SA-SRS) algorithm is introduced, utilizing a security-constrained hysteresis margin to optimize handovers and proactively bypass “danger zones” where eavesdropping risk is high. The framework integrates a partitioned RIS architecture with Singular Value Decomposition-based (SVD-U) precoding and artificial noise (AN) injection to maximize the secrecy gap while effectively suppressing inter-user interference without the need for high-complexity iterative phase tuning. Extensive simulations along a dynamic mobility path demonstrate that the proposed SA-SRS scheme maintains a superior and stable secrecy sum-rate by strategically avoiding compromised RIS units, effectively mitigating the rate degradation observed in traditional NRS methods. Furthermore, the analysis of secrecy outage probability (SOP) and energy efficiency (EE) confirms that the proposed framework achieves a robust trade-off between physical layer security and sustainable power consumption, proving its suitability for high-mobility secure 6G communications.

papers.title: Evaluating canine hip analysis: NANet model for norberg angle prediction
papers.abstract: The Norberg angle (NA) plays a crucial role in evaluating hip joint conformation in canines by quantifying femoral head subluxation within the hip joint. It is a key metric for assessing hip joint quality and diagnosing canine hip dysplasia (CHD), a multifactorial orthopedic disease influenced by both genetic and environmental factors. While contemporary tools offer automated NA quantification, they still rely on substantial manual labeling and verification by trained veterinarians. Rather than focusing on workflow efficiency, the objective of this study is to develop a fully automated system capable of predicting the NA directly from radiographs, thereby reducing dependence on manual annotation and enabling consistent and reproducible assessment. To address the limited availability of diverse, high-quality annotated radiographs, our previous work incorporated diffusion-based generative models to augment the training dataset from 1,168 images to 2,693 images. Training with this expanded dataset resulted in substantial performance gains, with an average improvement of 35.3% across evaluation metrics. Our proposed NANet model outperformed state-of-the-art alternatives, demonstrating superior predictive accuracy. In particular, the predicted Norberg angle fell within 5 degrees of the reference measurement in 81.30% of test cases, approaching or surpassing the consistency observed among human annotators.

papers.title: Integrated core-based calibration of the lower Bahariya reservoir in the Shahd and Shahd SE fields, Western Desert, Egypt
papers.abstract: Reliable petrophysical evaluation is essential for reservoir characterization and hydrocarbon resource assessment, particularly in heterogeneous sandstone reservoirs where uncertainties in log interpretation, core measurements, and reservoir cutoffs can affect reservoir-property estimates. This study presents an Integrated Core-Based Calibration (ICC) Workflow for the Lower Bahariya reservoir in the Shahd and Shahd SE fields, Western Desert, Egypt. The workflow integrates conventional wireline logs, routine core analysis, X-ray diffraction (XRD), thin-section petrography, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and reservoir-engineering data through a structured sequential framework comprising wireline-log quality control and normalization, core–log depth matching and overburden correction, core-based petrophysical calibration, geological validation and reservoir-quality rock typing, integrated reservoir characterization, and independent reservoir validation. The calibration established a consistent basis for estimating clay volume, effective porosity, and water saturation from calibrated wireline responses. Integrated reservoir characterization identified 32.0 ft of net pay in Shahd-1, with an average effective porosity of 14.3% and average water saturation of 25.4%, compared with 194.5 ft of net pay in Shahd SE-5, with an average effective porosity of 21.4% and average water saturation of 9.7%. Independent well-scale and reservoir-scale validation using Shahd SE-63 and XPT pressure-gradient data provided supporting evidence for hydraulic differentiation between the interpreted Lower Bahariya intervals and distinct oil–water contact depths. The proposed workflow provides a structured sequential framework for integrating multi-scale geological and petrophysical information and progressively constraining interpretation uncertainty in heterogeneous sandstone reservoir characterization.

papers.title: Priming parallel fiber signals drive plasticity in the in vivo cerebellum
papers.abstract: The cerebellar role in motor adaptation rests – according to the foundational theories of Marr and Albus – on the detection of (near)coincident activity between parallel fiber (PF) and climbing fiber (CF) inputs onto Purkinje cells. Supported by numerous in vitro studies, these theories predict synaptic adaptation based on temporal precision detected in time windows of ≤ 150 ms. These predictions have not been tested in intact animals. Using two-photon imaging from cerebellar Crus I in intact, awake mice, and dendritic calcium signals as a measure of PF response strength, we show here that coincident stimulation of PF and CF inputs does not readily initiate plasticity. Rather, long-term depression (LTD) is reliably evoked by prolonged constant or ramping PF activity that precedes a CF burst by 400 ms. In Crus I, a lobule involved in sensory-prediction tasks, prolonged PF activity may present expected sensory contexts and prime synapses for plasticity supervised by CF signals.

papers.title: InferPloidy enables CNV guided tumor cell stratification and biomarker discovery from single cell RNA sequencing
papers.abstract: Identifying malignant cells in single-cell gene expression data is essential for understanding tumor heterogeneity, but existing computational methods can be slow and perform inconsistently across datasets. Here, we present InferPloidy, a framework that combines graph-based cell grouping with iterative probabilistic modeling to distinguish cells with normal and altered chromosome copy numbers using profiles generated by InferCNV. Across breast, lung, pancreatic, and colorectal cancer datasets, the evaluated workflow reduces computation time by up to two orders of magnitude compared with existing tools and improves agreement with published cell annotations. This classification supports the identification of established therapeutic targets and candidate cell surface markers associated with tumor subtypes. The low proportion of unclassified cells helps preserve information for downstream analyses of gene expression differences and tumor population characteristics. These findings support InferPloidy as an efficient framework for tumor cell stratification and biomarker discovery within the evaluated workflow. Its performance with inputs from other copy number inference methods requires further validation.

papers.title: Transferring active inference to newly encountered prism-shifted environments
papers.abstract: Rapid adaptability to sudden changes in environmental contingencies is a hallmark of biological intelligence. However, how animals flexibly adapt to novel environments remains largely unclear. To investigate the brain’s generalizability, this work focuses on prism adaptation, a classical visuomotor phenomenon reflecting rapid recalibration of perception–action coupling. Modeling is conducted based on canonical neural networks that instantiate active inference at the circuit level. Namely, we develop canonical neural networks equipped with multiple policy matrices in parallel, enabling the reuse of previously acquired sensorimotor knowledge. We demonstrate that the proposed model recapitulates key features of prism adaptation in an arm-reaching task, including rapid error reduction and after-effects following prism removal. Networks employing policies pretrained for different target positions adapt substantially faster than naive networks that relearn policies from scratch. These results suggest a biologically plausible mechanism by which neural circuits flexibly reuse prior knowledge to support rapid adaptation.

papers.title: Flipping the switch on organelle traffic: how cellular stress rewires bidirectional transport
A bowl-shaped nanocarbon incorporating an aromatic cyclopentadienide ring
papers.abstract: Five-membered rings are ubiquitous in non-planar π systems, yet they are typically neutral, non-aromatic or anti-aromatic. Here we report the synthesis and characterization of pentabenzocorannulenide (PBC−), a bowl-shaped nanocarbon incorporating an anionic, aromatic cyclopentadienide (Cp−) ring. The five-membered Cp− ring is generated quantitatively by aromatization-driven nucleophilic dealkylation (C–C bond cleavage) of a pentabenzocorannulene derivative. Through single crystal X-ray diffraction and quantum chemical analyses, we reveal the unique structural features and physicochemical properties of PBC−, demonstrating uncommon bonding pattern and electronic characteristics distinct from corannulene, fullerenes, end caps of carbon nanotubes and other geodesic polyarenes. PBC− has an exceptionally strong conjugate acid, undergoes reversible covalent functionalization and engages in η5-type metal complexation. Incorporating the iconic Cp− ring into a fully conjugated sp2 carbon network opens avenues for exploring non-conventional π systems. Five-membered rings are ubiquitous in non-planar π systems, but are typically neutral, non-aromatic or anti-aromatic. Now a bowl-shaped nanocarbon incorporating an anionic, aromatic cyclopentadienide ring has been prepared and found to exhibit unusual structural and electronic properties, enabling site-selective reactivity on its π surface for both covalent functionalization and metal coordination.

papers.title: Extension of coherence time beyond breakeven point using only drives and dissipation
papers.abstract: Quantum error correction aims to mitigate the loss of quantum information to the environment and is a central requirement for scalable quantum computing. Existing implementations are mainly based on measurement-based feedback, but constraints on read-out fidelity, hardware latency and system complexity can limit performance and scalability. Autonomous quantum error correction offers a complementary route based on engineered drives and dissipation, without repeated measurements or classical feedback. Here we implement an autonomous quantum error correction protocol, derived from quantum channel simulation, that repeatedly restores a photon-loss-corrupted logical qubit by transferring error information to ancilla qubits and resetting them. Unlike earlier demonstrations based on manifold stabilization through code-specific Hamiltonian and dissipation engineering, our approach is, in principle, applicable to arbitrary recovery maps. Using a binomial code encoded in a long-lived bosonic mode, we extend the logical qubit coherence time to 1.04 times that of the best physical qubit in the system. This result shows that drives and dissipation can extend the coherence time of an error-corrected bosonic logical qubit beyond the breakeven point. An autonomous quantum error correction protocol based on engineered drives and dissipation extends the coherence time of a bosonic logical qubit beyond that of the best physical qubit in the same system.

papers.title: Extending qubit lifetime beyond break-even and enhancing quantum sensing by autonomous quantum error correction
papers.abstract: Extending the lifetime of a logical quantum bit (qubit) beyond that of the best physical qubit available within the same system—the break-even point—is a prerequisite for building practical quantum computers. Previous demonstrations have crossed this threshold using active quantum error correction (QEC), which measures an error syndrome and then applies an adaptive correction. Reaching the break-even point with autonomous QEC, which removes the need for resource-intensive measurement and feedback, remains challenging. Here we demonstrate beyond-break-even autonomous error correction in a circuit quantum electrodynamics system. We encode a photonic logical qubit in a superconducting microwave cavity and protect it against photon loss using engineered dissipation. The protected logical qubit achieves a lifetime of about 2.0 ms, 18% longer than that of the best physical qubit available in the system. We then use the protocol to measure a small frequency shift, obtaining a metrological gain of 6.3 dB relative to the most robust Fock-state superposition. These results show that autonomous QEC not only represents a necessary step towards fault-tolerant quantum computation but also offers advantages for robust quantum sensing. A measurement-free quantum error-correction protocol is shown to extend the lifetime of a bosonic logical qubit beyond the best physical qubit in the same system. This also offers prospects for enhanced quantum sensing.

papers.title: 150 years proving fundamental science is worth the wait
papers.abstract: Founded in 1876, the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science created an early space for Indians to pursue science. Its achievements offer valuable lessons for strengthening today’s research landscape in India.

papers.title: Cognitive grounding improves LLM simulation of collective human behavior
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly stand in for human participants, yet a plausible response is not evidence of a human decision process. The gap matters most when agents interact, where locally reasonable choices compound through delays and feedback into collective outcomes. Behavioral models fit decision rules to human data; we ask whether their qualitative content alone can drive LLM agents, an approach we call cognitive grounding. Here we show, across 231 sessions of the Beer Distribution Game, a supply-chain experiment in which players’ orders amplify demand swings, that grounding moves seven LLMs toward human-calibrated behavior. Ungrounded agents reproduce the game’s instability but miss its magnitude, timing and propagation; grounding improves trajectory fit for every model and generally shifts inferred decision parameters toward the human-calibrated reference, although unevenly across roles and models. The effect holds against independent empirical data and under alternative prompting and memory designs. Cognitively grounded LLMs are therefore candidate behavioral surrogates, contingent on task-specific validation. The study shows that guiding AI agents with descriptions of how people make decisions in a supply-chain game helps agents reproduce collective human behavior.

papers.title: Unlocking sustainable thermoelectric generation with zinc antimonide
papers.abstract: Thermoelectric technologies offer a compelling path to sustainable waste-heat recovery, yet their widespread deployment is constrained by the reliance of many high-performing materials on scarce, environmentally problematic, or expensive elements. Beyond maximizing conversion efficiency (η), practical thermoelectrics must reconcile performance with resource availability, environmental impact and economic cost. Here we establish zinc antimonide (ZnSb) as a cost-effective and sustainable thermoelectric material by benchmarking elemental abundance, raw-material cost and device efficiency. By leveraging dynamically activated carrier modulation and intrinsically low thermal conductivity, ZnSb achieves impressive material performance while avoiding reliance on scarce, costly, or environmentally problematic elements. Furthermore, we demonstrate a ZnSb-Mg3Sb1.5Bi0.5 device yielding a maximum η of 8% at ΔT = 400 K. This translates to a high efficiency-to-cost ratio of ~0.2% US$−1 kg, highlighting the unusual combination of performance and resource compatibility. Our findings provide a framework for evaluating thermoelectric materials beyond isolated record efficiencies towards scalable and sustainable energy harvesting. Thermoelectric technologies must balance conversion efficiency with resource sustainability. Here the authors demonstrate that eco-friendly zinc antimonide (ZnSb) is a viable materials choice, delivering ~8% efficiency alongside exceptional cost-effectiveness.

papers.title: Holistic evaluation for deployment
papers.abstract: Thermoelectric technologies can convert waste heat directly into clean electricity, but high laboratory efficiency does not necessarily translate into practical deployment. By revisiting the long-neglected material zinc antimonide, researchers now show that strong thermoelectric performance can go hand in hand with affordability and sustainability.

papers.title: Machine learning-based Taylor cone analysis for electrospinning process-window identification and cell-laden nanofiber scaffold fabrication
papers.abstract: Electrospinning is a powerful biofabrication technique for constructing fibrous scaffolds that mimic extracellular matrix architectures. However, the process is highly nonlinear and involves strongly coupled parameters, making fiber architecture and biological performance difficult to control empirically and limits reproducibility. Most ML studies still focus on static correlations between processing parameters and outcomes rather than on dynamic modeling of electrospinning evolution and regulation, thereby hindering real-time, precise process control. Here, we establish a data-driven framework that links process parameters, Taylor cone geometry, and nanofiber/cell outcomes through high-speed imaging and ML. A custom image-processing pipeline is developed to automatically extract cone angle, height, and width from in situ images with improved accuracy via a rotating-ray–based geometric algorithm. Using datasets collected from three representative polymer systems PVDF, PVB, and PEO, RF models outperform SVM and MDL, achieving moderate-to-good prediction of Taylor cone descriptors (R2 ≈ 0.57-0.83) across varied voltages, flow rates, and needle–collector distances. We further extend this framework to PEO-based cell electrospinning. By correlating predicted cone geometries with experimentally measured viability of 293 T cells and umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells, we identify a Taylor cone ‘safe window’ that simultaneously stabilizes jet formation and preserves cell survival (>95%). Guided by this window, a bilayer cell-laden scaffold comprising a PVB support layer and a PEO–cell layer is fabricated with improved process robustness. This enables stable delivery of high-density, highly viable cells and facilitates the fabrication of three-dimensional cell-laden nanofiber scaffolds. Overall, this ML-guided Taylor cone analysis strategy provides a quantitative framework for process-window identification in polymer and cell electrospinning, and may support future integration with real-time monitoring, online inference, and closed-loop control in intelligent biofabrication.

papers.title: In vitro human arteriole microphysiological system with physiological scale and functional vasoactivity enabled by a dual material fabrication strategy
papers.abstract: Arterioles are the principal regulators of vascular tone, yet their small size and deep tissue location hinder direct investigation of their roles in microvascular disease. To address this, we developed a human microphysiological arteriole distinguished from previous models by simultaneously integrating an arteriole-scale caliber (∼200 μm), continuous perfusion culture, and active vasoactivity. The vessel autonomously forms and matures under flow through a spatially regulated coating strategy that eliminates post-seeding manipulation. The engineered vessels exhibit vasoactivity in response to both biochemical and metabolic cues. In particular, the metabolic response is a physiological form of vasoactivity rarely reproduced in previous in vitro systems. Leveraging the ease of sample harvesting, proteomic profiling and mechanical testing indicated that flow-induced maturation promotes a contractile phenotype consistent with arteriogenesis-like remodeling. This accessible platform provides a versatile tool for studying arteriolar physiology and microvascular remodeling.

papers.title: Microfiber-reinforced GelMA hydrogels with tunable Poisson’s ratio enhance chondrogenesis under dynamic loading
papers.abstract: Hydrogels are widely used in cartilage tissue engineering but fail to replicate key mechanical features of native cartilage, particularly its near-zero Poisson’s ratio, which governs lateral deformation under load. Here, we demonstrate that matching deformation behavior in addition to compressive stiffness may contribute to the enhanced chondrogenic response under physiological mechanical stimulation. Human articular chondrocytes were encapsulated in GelMA hydrogels reinforced with melt electrowritten scaffolds engineered to independently tune the effective compressive modulus and Poisson’s ratio. Reinforcement increased the compressive modulus from 33 kPa (neat GelMA) to 245–345 kPa, while reducing the Poisson’s ratio from 0.42 to 0.12 in hybrid designs, approaching native cartilage values. Under dynamic loading, constructs matching both properties showed significantly higher expression of the chondrogenic markers SOX9 and ACAN compared to both neat GelMA and lattice-reinforced constructs, which exhibited a physiologically relevant compressive modulus but a higher Poisson’s ratio, along with increased COL2A1 expression compared to the latter specifically. Histological analysis confirmed enhanced and more homogeneous extracellular matrix deposition, with up to 76% GAG and 36% collagen type II coverage. These findings suggest that lateral deformation behavior, alongside compressive stiffness, contributes to directing chondrocyte matrix synthesis under mechanical stimulation, establishing Poisson’s ratio as an important and previously underexplored design parameter in cartilage tissue engineering, and providing a framework for engineering mechanically instructive biomaterials for load-bearing tissues.

papers.title: A fibrochondrogenic polymer fibre-reinforced collagen-based scaffold with graded architecture, mechanics and composition for meniscus repair
papers.abstract: Developing biomaterials for meniscal repair that reproduce native tissue biomechanics while providing pro-regenerative bioinstructive cues remains challenging. To address this need, we developed a zonal biomimetic fibre-reinforced collagen-based scaffold designed to recreate key microstructural and mechanical features of the meniscus and support fibrochondrogenesis in vitro. A multilayer scaffold was fabricated with a circumferential electrospun (ES) fibre core composed of polycaprolactone (PCL), polylactic acid (PLA), or a hybrid PCL/polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)/PLA reinforcement, together with radially oriented melt-electrowritten (MEW) PCL intermediate zones and multidirectional MEW PCL superficial zones, followed by integration with a collagen I-chondroitin-6-sulphate matrix. Fibre-reinforced scaffolds combining MEW PCL with the hybrid ES PCL-PVA-PLA reinforcement framework demonstrated the best-balanced biomechanical performance, achieving mechanical properties within the range reported for native meniscus under comparable test conditions, including tensile, compressive and complex moduli of 140.62 ± 26.31 MPa, 723.21 ± 147.09 kPa and 25.91 ± 1.21 kPa, respectively. Moreover, human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells cultured on this scaffold exhibited enhanced sulphated glycosaminoglycan production, balanced type I and type II collagen expression, and fibrocartilage-like extracellular matrix deposition with the reinforced architecture supporting deeper and more uniform matrix formation. Together, these findings support zonal fibre reinforcement as a design strategy to integrate mechanical fidelity with scaffold-dependent modulation of hMSC fibrochondrogenesis in vitro, identifying the hybrid PCL-PVA-PLA-reinforced scaffold as a best-balanced configuration for meniscal repair.

papers.title: Phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover enables rate-matched nitrate-sulfate paired electrolysis for ammonium persulfate synthesis
papers.abstract: Electrochemical conversion of nitrate-rich wastewater to valuable ammonium salts is promising. We report a phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover mechanism that synchronizes nitrate-reduction and sulfate-oxidation kinetics, enabling direct electrosynthesis of ammonium persulfate.

papers.title: Directly visualizing the energy level structure of quantum dot molecules
papers.abstract: Characterizing the energy spectrum of semiconductor quantum dots is essential for spin qubit operation but remains challenging across broad parameter ranges. Here, the authors use molecular spectroscopy to map one and two electron energy levels in a silicon double quantum dot as functions of detuning, tunnel coupling, and magnetic field.

papers.title: Cytotoxic drugs and bispecific T cell engagers synergize to rewire host immunity and elicit polyclonal antitumor T cell responses
papers.abstract: TAA×CD28 costimulatory bispecific antibodies are a class of immunotherapeutics that provide tumor-targeted CD28 costimulation to T cells by crosslinking CD28 on T cells to a tumor-associated antigen (TAA) expressed on tumor cells. Here, the authors show that cytotoxic therapies reprogram the tumor microenvironment and augment the antitumor immunity induced by TAA×CD28 bispecifics.

papers.title: Assembly of a renal countercurrent system in a beetle
papers.abstract: Developmental assembly of a powerful water conservation countercurrent exchange system in a beetle is orchestrated through dynamic crosstalk between its multiple constituent organs mediated by just two fibroblast growth factor signalling pathways.

papers.title: Facet-dependent anion adsorption for electrolyte-Cu interfacial stability in initially anode-free Li-metal batteries
papers.abstract: Initially anode-free lithium-metal batteries are limited by unstable interfacial reactions at Cu current collectors. Here, authors show that preferential anion adsorption can stabilize the copper interface and improve long-term cycling.

papers.title: Site-specific N-glycoproteomic analysis of extracellular vesicles from seminal plasma reveals the molecular typing of azoospermia
papers.abstract: This study presents EVGlyco, a low-input platform for site-specific N-glycoproteomic analysis of biofluid EVs. It identifies site-specific N-glycan signatures in seminal plasma EVs that distinguish azoospermia types and nonobstructive subtypes.

papers.title: Chromatin priming of skeletal stem and progenitor cells governs cell fate during bone repair
papers.abstract: Skeletal stem/progenitor cells in bone and skeletal muscle are diverse populations with distinct roles in bone repair. This study defines their transcriptomic and chromatin-priming signatures that control cell fate during regeneration.

papers.title: Mapping dynamics of subcellular RNA and protein localization and organization using optimal transport
papers.abstract: The authors introduce a computational tool SLOT to map mRNA and protein localization within cells, providing a framework and spatial atlas for studying molecular organization during early development and informing virtual cell models.

papers.title: An optimized PanFlu-IOA-based mRNA vaccine targeting hemagglutinin confers broad-spectrum protection against heterosubtypic influenza viruses in mice
papers.abstract: Researchers developed PanFlu-IOA, a computational approach to design a broad spectrum mRNA influenza vaccine. The vaccine induced broad immune responses and protected mice against multiple influenza subtypes, offering a path to universal vaccines.

papers.title: Rhizospheric pH mediated thermo-signalling coordinates root growth under heat stress
papers.abstract: Plant roots adjust their growth in response to soil temperature, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, the authors show that pH regulates temperature-dependent root growth through ROS-mediated control of cell cycle dynamics in Arabidopsis thaliana .

papers.title: Context-aware forecasting of inter-firm competitive dynamics with graph learning and multi-agent reasoning
papers.abstract: The evolution of competitive dominance in technology-intensive industries is shaped by complex interactions among research activity, media visibility, strategic disclosures, public attention, and market signals. Understanding these dynamics is critical for strategic intelligence, yet existing predictive models often treat firms as isolated entities and provide limited support for contextualizing long-horizon firm-to-firm competitive forecasts. Here, we introduce an integrated framework that captures the relational nature of market competition by extending our prior Bayesian Multivariate Time-series Graph Neural Network with a newly designed, post hoc, lookahead-free multi-agent reasoning layer. The framework infers inter-firm relational dependencies endogenously from multimodal signals to forecast latent firm competitiveness and pairwise competitive gap trajectories with quantified predictive uncertainty. To evaluate strategic plausibility, specialized persona-driven language model agents critique the forecasted trajectories across technological, financial, and regulatory lenses using retrieved evidence. Evaluated under a rigorous date-based temporal protocol with strictly withheld test horizons, the framework consistently outperforms competitive structural baselines and yields well-calibrated prediction intervals. When applied to thirty leading AI-oriented technology firms, the framework uncovers asymmetric competitive momentum, contested market leadership, and emerging challenger dynamics. By bridging relational time-series forecasting with structured multi-agent deliberation, this study advances competitive dynamics analysis from purely accuracy-centric prediction toward context-aware, uncertainty-informed strategic intelligence.

papers.title: The Cdh23 tm2a mouse allele causes progressive hearing loss that is not improved by postnatal Cdh23 gene expression
papers.abstract: Cdh23 encodes cadherin related 23, a cadherin which is an essential component of the tip link of stereocilia on the sensory hair cells of the inner ear. Mutations in human CDH23 lead to either non-syndromic deafness or Usher syndrome, while mutations in mouse Cdh23 lead to hearing impairment with or without balance defects. Here we characterise the Cdh23tm2a mouse mutant and show that the mutation causes reduced transcription of Cdh23 and early-onset progressive hearing loss in Cdh23tm2a/tm2a homozygotes. Cdh23+/tm2a heterozygotes also exhibit progressive hearing loss but only at high frequencies, and this was dependent on the presence of the Cdh23ahl allele which is present in the background C57BL/6N strain. Scanning electron microscopy revealed stereocilia bundle defects in homozygous mutants but stereocilia appeared normal in heterozygotes. To investigate whether hearing loss could be reversed by inducing expression of the gene, we removed the transcription disruption cassette within the Cdh23tm2a mutant allele using tamoxifen-inducible Flp recombinase at either 4 days or 21 days old, but no improvements in Auditory Brainstem Response thresholds or stereocilia bundle appearance were detected. These findings suggest that any treatments for Cdh23-associated hearing loss would probably need to applied very early in development, before stereocilia are fully formed.

papers.title: Distributed \(H_\infty \) leader–following control of nonlinear heterogeneous multi-agent systems via an alternating LMI iterative approach
papers.abstract: This paper investigates distributed $$H_{\infty }$$ leader–following control for nonlinear heterogeneous multi-agent systems (HMASs) subject to external disturbances. A compact tracking-error model is formulated by introducing a lumped nonlinear mismatch term, and a detailed derivation of this term is provided to clarify the components induced by heterogeneity and nonlinearity. Sufficient conditions for stability and prescribed $$H_{\infty }$$ disturbance attenuation are derived via Lyapunov stability theory and a structured weighted quadratic constraint on the mismatch. For controller synthesis, a bilinear matrix inequality (BMI) condition is established, and a verification-based alternating linear matrix inequality (LMI) iterative approach is proposed to address it, together with an analysis of its relation to the original BMI problem and of the initialization sensitivity. Numerical examples, including a nonlinear HMAS and a leader–following unmanned ground vehicle (UGV) network, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Cross-sectional study of facial bone wall thickness of maxillary incisors in healthy and periodontitis populations based on CBCT analysis
