papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the differences in facial bone wall thickness (FBT) of maxillary incisors between healthy and periodontitis populations and to explore potential influencing factors, providing a theoretical basis for immediate implant placement. A retrospective study was conducted using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) to analyze the facial bone wall thickness of 300 patients. According to the alveolar bone loss (ABL) level, patients were classified into healthy, mild, moderate, and severe groups. FBT was measured at three positions: alveolar crest (FBT1), mid-root (FBT2), and root apex (FBT3). The sagittal root position was classified into three types. Multiple linear regression analysis was performed to identify influencing factors. A total of 300 patients were enrolled, including 177 males (59.0%) and 123 females (41.0%). The median FBT1 values for the healthy, mild, moderate, and severe groups were 1.03 mm, 0.93 mm, 0.63 mm, and 0.55 mm, respectively (P < 0.001); the median FBT3 values were 1.88 mm, 1.54 mm, 1.38 mm, and 1.24 mm, respectively (P = 0.002). For root positions, the median FBT3 values for Type 1 (palatal/central), Type 2 (slightly labial), and Type 3 (obviously labial) were 2.47 mm, 1.81 mm, and 1.00 mm, respectively (P < 0.001). Multiple linear regression showed that ABL had a significant negative effect on FBT1 (beta=−0.165, P = 0.004), root angle alpha had a significant negative effect on FBT3 (beta=−0.426, P < 0.001), and gender had a significant effect on FBT3 (beta = 0.198, P < 0.001). Significant differences exist in facial bone wall thickness of maxillary incisors between healthy and periodontitis populations. Periodontitis patients generally have thinner facial bone walls than healthy populations, and bone wall thickness is significantly affected by the level of alveolar bone loss. Higher alveolar bone loss is associated with thinner bone walls. Gender, age, and root position also influence bone wall thickness to a certain extent.

papers.title: Elucidating the dielectric, magnetic, and optical properties of PVA/PVP/CS-MWCNTs/NiFe₂O₄ nanocomposite for nanoelectronics applications
papers.abstract: The effect of multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs)/nickel ferrite (NiFe₂O₄) hybrid nanofiller loading on the electrical transport characteristics and dielectric relaxation behaviour of poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)/poly(vinyl pyrrolidone) (PVP)/chitosan (CS) polymer nanocomposite films was investigated. The films were prepared using the solution-casting method. X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis revealed changes in the structural characteristics of the polymer blend, with an increase in its amorphous character up to a nanofiller concentration of 2.0 wt%. Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy indicated possible interactions between the nanofillers and the functional groups of the polymer blend. Ultraviolet–visible (UV–Vis) spectroscopy was used to evaluate the optical properties. Increasing the nanofiller concentration from 0 to 2.0 wt% reduced the indirect optical band gap from approximately 4.8 to 2.8 eV, while the estimated refractive index increased from 1.108 to 2.348. Electrical conductivity and dielectric properties were investigated using alternating-current (AC) impedance spectroscopy. The frequency dependence of AC conductivity followed Jonscher’s power law for all prepared films. At ambient temperature, the film containing 2.0 wt% nanofiller exhibited the highest AC conductivity of 1.54 × 10⁻⁶ S cm⁻¹. The complex dielectric permittivity and loss tangent were analysed to investigate the dielectric response and relaxation behaviour, while the electric modulus spectra indicated non-Debye relaxation. These findings demonstrate that incorporating hybrid nanofillers can modify the optical, dielectric, and electrical properties of the polymer blend, suggesting potential for nanoelectronic and dielectric applications. Further electrochemical evaluation is required to establish its suitability for energy-storage applications.

papers.title: Machine-learning-assisted prediction and optimization of tensile strength in particulate-filled polymer composites
papers.abstract: Particulate-filled polymer composites (PFPCs) are characterized by high specific strength, good formability, and considerable design flexibility, making them key materials for rapid tooling in aerospace equipment manufacturing. In this study, metal-powder/resin composites were investigated, and a tensile-strength dataset comprising 45 independent experimental conditions was established. Three machine-learning regression algorithms, namely linear least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and support vector regression (SVR), were employed to develop tensile-strength prediction models. A fixed outer five-fold cross-validation procedure was used to obtain out-of-fold (OOF) predictions, while hyperparameters were selected through inner five-fold cross-validation within each outer training fold; a genetic algorithm (GA) was subsequently used to further optimize the SVR hyperparameters. The OOF RMSE, MAE, and R² values of SVR were 1.67 MPa, 1.32 MPa, and 0.882, respectively, and those of GA-SVR were 1.54 MPa, 1.21 MPa, and 0.901. With increasing particle volume fraction and particle size, the tensile strength initially increased and then decreased, whereas ball-milling time had a relatively limited effect. Single-parameter analysis yielded predicted peak positions of approximately 34.80%, 30.92 μm, and 2.68 h for particle volume fraction, particle size, and ball-milling time, respectively. Continuous searching within the experimental domain identified a high-strength parameter combination of f = 34.63%, D = 30.67 μm, and t = 2.65 h, corresponding to a predicted tensile strength of 61.33 MPa. The measured strengths of three independent validation specimens prepared using a nominal particle size of 31 μm were 61.12, 60.93, and 60.56 MPa, with a mean of 60.87 ± 0.28 MPa, a coefficient of variation of 0.47%, and a relative deviation of 0.75% between the experimental mean and model prediction. Within the current experimental domain, the proposed framework can provide a quantitative reference for PFPC tensile-strength prediction and formulation/process-parameter screening, and offers an efficient strategy for accelerating formulation design and optimization while reducing experimental cost. Its implementation also provided students with practical experience in applying machine-learning algorithms to material-strength prediction and parameter design.

papers.title: Digital literacy and teaching innovative behavior among physical education teachers: a cross-sectional moderated mediation study
papers.abstract: Although digital literacy is critical for physical education teachers, the indirect pathways linking it to teaching innovative behavior remain unclear. Guided by Social Cognitive Theory and Conservation of Resources Theory, this study tested a moderated mediation model in which teaching self-efficacy mediates the digital literacy–teaching innovative behavior association, and perceived organizational support moderates the teaching self-efficacy–teaching innovative behavior association. A cross-sectional survey included 984 primary and secondary physical education teachers in Jiangsu, Hubei, and Sichuan, China. Digital literacy was positively associated with teaching innovative behavior (c = 0.351, p < 0.001). Teaching self-efficacy partially mediated this association (indirect effect = 0.056, 95% bootstrap CI [0.030, 0.084]). Perceived organizational support moderated the teaching self-efficacy–teaching innovative behavior association (B = 0.057, p < 0.001). The index of moderated mediation was significant (0.042, 95% bootstrap CI [0.019, 0.065]). Conditional indirect effects were significant at mean and high support but not low support. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested the moderated mediation pathway was significant in primary and junior secondary teachers but not senior secondary teachers, although most between-group differences were not statistically significant. The moderation model explained 14.9% and the full model explained 18.6% of variance in teaching innovative behavior. Findings are correlational, not causal.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal analysis of shoreline changes in Mobile Bay, U.S.A.
papers.abstract: Shoreline changes affect coastal communities by altering ecosystems and storm buffers. With the growth of coastal populations, the societal impact of shoreline change is expected to increase. Understanding the past and present shoreline positions is thus essential for managing coastal hazards and supporting population as well as ecosystem services. This study quantifies shoreline change rates and evaluates the persistence and variability of shoreline behavior in Mobile Bay, U.S., over the past 25 years (2000​–2024 inclusive). CoastSat, an open-source Python software toolkit built on the cloud computing platform Google Earth Engine (GEE), is used to detect shoreline positions and analyze change rates. Furthermore, the Hurst exponent analysis is applied to the shoreline change rate of 396 shore-normal transects to assess the persistence or randomness of shoreline change behavior. The findings reveal substantial spatial heterogeneity in shoreline dynamics across Mobile Bay, with Dauphin Island exhibiting the highest erosion rate (−5.4 m/yr), the greatest shoreline variability between the northern and southern shore, and the strongest responses to major hurricane events. In contrast, the more sheltered estuarine shorelines towards the riverine delta experienced smaller shoreline displacements and more localized variability. The integration of persistence analysis with conventional erosion-accretion assessments enabled the distinction between persistently erosional, persistently accretional, and highly variable shoreline segments, providing additional insight into long-term and short-term shoreline behavior. The findings contribute to a more comprehensive understanding of shoreline dynamics and support site-specific coastal management, hazard mitigation, and the implementation of nature-based solutions.

papers.title: Monomer extraction and compressive responses of contemporary resin-based composites under distinct exposure conditions
papers.abstract: Resin-based composites (RBCs) may change mechanically during prolonged aqueous storage, while residual monomers and related low-molecular-weight compounds can be released from their polymer networks. This study evaluated four conventional and four bulk-fill RBCs. Engineering compressive modulus, maximum engineering compressive stress, and engineering strain at maximum engineering compressive stress were determined after 24 h and after 20 weeks of storage in physiological saline. Extraction of selected compounds was quantified by HPLC after 1, 2, 4, 8, and 20 weeks in 75% ethanol/water. Compressive properties changed in a strongly material-dependent manner between the 24-h and 20-week saline-storage conditions, ranging from reductions to stable behavior or increases in selected parameters, particularly among bulk-fill RBCs. Material composition, extraction time, and their interaction significantly affected cumulative monomer extraction. These findings show marked material-dependent variation in both outcomes and indicate that conventional and bulk-fill classification alone does not predict compressive-property changes after prolonged saline storage.

papers.title: Development of flax/kenaf hybrid epoxy composites incorporating sugarcane biochar with enhanced fire performance for potential electrical conduit applications
papers.abstract: This study examines the effect of sugarcane biochar on the structural, mechanical, thermal, and fire-related behaviour of flax/kenaf/flax hybrid epoxy composites with different weight contents of biochar (0–6 wt%). FTIR analysis shows that chemical structure changes may occur and that there might be interactions between the biochar and the epoxy matrix. Mechanical characterisation revealed that the measured mechanical properties improved with biochar contents up to 4.5 wt%, but decreased at 6 wt% biochar loading, where changes in filler distribution may have occurred. At 4.5 wt% biochar, the composite exhibited a tensile strength of 38.01 ± 0.55 MPa, flexural strength of 76.12 ± 0.90 MPa, impact strength of 9.62 ± 0.45 kJ/m2, hardness of 86 ± 1 Shore D, and ILSS of 13.24 ± 0.35 MPa. Additionally, TGA/DTG results revealed that the thermal degradation resistance was enhanced, as the onset degradation temperature rose to 317 °C and the residual char content was 28% at 4.5 wt% biochar. The fire-performance evaluation revealed that the LOI of neat epoxy increased from 19.5 ± 0.5% to 28.4 ± 0.8% at 4.5 wt% biochar. The same formulation showed a lower PHRR of 300.10 ± 9.28 kW/m2 and THR of 54.03 ± 1.74 MJ/m2, with delayed ignition and a lower horizontal burning rate. Morphological support for the proposed condensed-phase protective mechanism was obtained from SEM analysis of the post-flammability residues. A cylindrical prototype was fabricated as a proof-of-concept demonstration of the feasibility of forming the composite into a conduit-like geometry, with a length of 300 mm and a wall thickness of 3 mm.

papers.title: Integrating UAV-assisted blow sampling and photo-identification in common bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus )
papers.abstract: Non-invasive genetic sampling can improve the study and conservation of cetaceans by reducing disturbance while providinsg information on population structure, connectivity, and other parameters. In this study, we evaluated the feasibility of UAV-assisted blow sampling for obtaining DNA from free-ranging common bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops truncatus) in two Mediterranean areas: The Gulf of Ambracia (Greece) and the Gulf of Trieste (off Piran, Slovenia). Blow samples were linked to photo-identified individuals and assessed through UAV video review. Mitochondrial DNA amplification was successful for at least one mitochondrial locus in 78% of Greek and 100% of Slovenian samples, whereas a nuclear marker amplified only in samples of animals under human care, used as a control, indicating that the mitochondrial assays used here performed more consistently than the single nuclear assay tested for blow-derived low-template DNA. Fifteen individuals were sequenced for up to six mitochondrial loci, and 13 were retained in the final concatenated dataset. Phylogenetic, haplotype network, and multivariate analyses showed that the recovered mitochondrial sequences could be used for genetic comparisons between the two study areas. Video-assessment categories were associated with molecular success, suggesting that UAV video assessment is particularly useful for identifying sampling attempts with a low likelihood of molecular success. Overall, our results support UAV-assisted blow sampling integrated with photo-ID as a promising approach for individual-based molecular monitoring of small cetaceans.

papers.title: Scale-dependent associations between urban landscape characteristics and PM 2.5 concentrations across contrasting landscape backgrounds in Beijing
papers.abstract: Associations between urban landscape characteristics and PM2.5 concentrations may vary with spatial scale and landscape background, yet these variations remain insufficiently understood. We examined these relationships using annual mean PM2.5 concentrations from 13 monitoring stations in Beijing during 2021–2025 and high-resolution urban landscape data. We fitted XGBoost models using eight predictors, including five two-dimensional landscape indicators and three three-dimensional morphological indicators, within 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 km buffers. SHAP analysis was then used to assess the relative importance of these predictors in model predictions. A dominance-ratio approach was used to classify the surroundings of each station into blue-, green-, or grey-space backgrounds. The highest-ranked predictor changed across scales, from frontal area index (FAI) at 1.0 km (mean absolute SHAP = 0.824 µg m−2) to building height (BH) at 1.5 km (0.813 µg m−2) and street canyon height-to-width ratio (HW) at 2.0 km (0.756 µg m−2). At each scale, the single station classified as blue-space had the lowest PM2.5 concentration, whereas grey-space backgrounds generally showed the highest. Under the 1.0 km classification, the 2023 increase was 1.1 µg m−2 at the blue-space site, compared with mean increases of 3.3 and 3.5 at green- and grey-space stations, respectively.

papers.title: Quantification and micro-costing analysis of healthcare waste generated in a pre-clinical simulation laboratory
papers.abstract: This study aims to evaluate the comprehensive environmental and financial burden—specifically, the amount, type, per-student waste load, and micro-costs—of medical, sharps, and packaging waste generated during the practical examination process for first-year midwifery students. In this descriptive, cross-sectional study, the clinical skills practical examination (including parenteral applications, catheterization, and venipuncture) of 67 students was audited. Waste generated during examination stations was audited and classified in accordance with World Health Organization guidelines and national health waste management standards, adapted for a non-biological simulation environment. Waste was segregated at the source, weighed using precision scales, and inventoried. A micro-costing approach was used to calculate consumable procurement and waste-disposal costs, which were converted to US Dollars (USD) based on June 2026 market rates. The examination generated a total of 28,450 g of non-hazardous medical consumables, 597 g of sharps waste, and 2,621 g of packaging waste, consuming 1,521 needles, 536 ampoules, and 1,675 gloves. On average, each student produced 120.5 waste items, including 40.7 sharps materials. Financially, the total institutional expenditure for the single examination session was 18,301.85 TRY ($396.83 USD), which includes both consumable procurement costs ($368.01 USD) and waste disposal/management fees ($28.82 USD), translating to an overall operational expense of $5.92 USD per student. Pre-clinical laboratory training imposes a substantial, hidden eco-financial burden on institutions while exposing students to high occupational safety risks due to the density of sharps. Integrating waste minimization strategies and green curriculum protocols could significantly lower institutional procurement and disposal costs while minimizing injury risks. University administrations are urged to adopt sustainable laboratory infrastructures to achieve both fiscal efficiency and environmental stewardship.

papers.title: Real-time predictive control of fusion plasmas with an adaptive digital twin
papers.abstract: Fusion plasma control requires real-time coordination of multiple actuators under partial observations and model uncertainty. Here we demonstrate predictive control of a fusion plasma on the Large Helical Device using an adaptive digital-twin system that combines data assimilation with physics-based integrated modeling. The digital twin was dynamically synchronized with experimental observations, while heating and fueling inputs were optimized from its predictions to drive the plasma toward target states. Real-time adaptation and control estimation were performed on a remote supercomputer located approximately 1,000 km from the experimental device, using up to 10,000 CPU cores. Multivariate control of electron density, electron temperature, and ion temperature was demonstrated in five representative target cases. These results establish a closed loop between an adaptive digital twin and a physical fusion plasma. They provide a route toward digital-twin-based control of fusion reactors and other partially observed complex systems.

papers.title: Multilayer feed-forward neural network-based mobile app for photovoltaic module parameter estimation
papers.abstract: Accurate parameter estimation of photovoltaic (PV) cells and modules is essential for the modeling, simulation, and optimization of PV systems. However, this task involves solving a complex nonlinear optimization problem, which often suffers from slow convergence and entrapment in local minima. The objective of this research is to contribute finding an efficient and software-independent approach to predict the parameters of the single diode model for polycrystalline and monocrystalline PV cells and modules from only the datasheet parameters at Standard Test Conditions (STC). To accomplish this task, an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) approach is used, which resulted in the ability to estimate instantly without the need of commercial software. The developed model is additionally implemented in an Android application, which offers a user friendly and accessible instrument for PV system designers. The model was further evaluated through comparisons of reconstructed I–V and P–V characteristics with available reference characteristics, Simulink library modules, manufacturer datasheet values, and recently published algorithms. The results demonstrate high reliability, with RMSE, MAE and U95 values of 1.3610e−04, 6.8160e−05 and 2.659820e−04 respectively. Furthermore, the model reliably reproduced P–V and I–V characteristics under varying environmental conditions, closely aligning with the datasheet specifications of the four modules.

papers.title: A unified aperture-based framework for modeling fracture capillary pressure and relative permeability in multiphase flow
papers.abstract: Fracture capillary pressure and relative permeability strongly influence multiphase flow in fractured porous media, yet fracture-flow representations commonly assume zero capillary pressure and linear relative permeability. This study develops a unified aperture-based constitutive framework for fracture capillary pressure and relative permeability from statistical fracture-aperture characteristics. Fracture aperture is represented by a lognormal distribution parameterized by its mean and log-space standard deviation. Capillary pressure is formulated using a local Young–Laplace capillary-equilibrium relationship and an aperture-based phase-occupancy criterion, while relative permeability is obtained by integrating aperture-dependent phase flow with a saturation-dependent tortuosity closure. The framework is intended primarily for quasi-static and capillary-dominated conditions and does not explicitly resolve dynamic capillary effects, fracture deformation, network topology, disconnected pathways, or directional/tensorial network-scale behavior. Model assessment distinguishes cases with independently specified aperture-distribution parameters from calibration cases in which the aperture parameter is inferred from target data. Comparisons with published analytical and experimental datasets reproduce the principal trends of the investigated capillary-pressure and relative-permeability relationships. The framework provides a compact aperture-based constitutive representation, while its applicability beyond the investigated conditions requires further independent experimental assessment.

papers.title: The brain tumor sequence registration (BraTS-Reg) challenge for establishing correspondence between pre-operative and follow-up MRI scans of diffuse glioma patients
papers.abstract: Registration of longitudinal brain MRI scans containing pathologies remains a challenging problem, due to substantial changes in tissue appearance. While medical image registration methods have advanced considerably, they often lack the required precision and robustness. To address this gap, we introduced the brain tumor sequence registration (BraTS-Reg) challenge, the first public benchmark specifically designed for deformable registration between pre-operative and follow-up scans of patients with adult-type diffuse gliomas. Conducted in conjunction with ISBI-2022 and MICCAI-2022, BraTS-Reg provides de-identified, multi-institutional, multi-parametric MRI data accompanied by expert-annotated landmark points across time. Training data with ground truth annotations were publicly released for algorithm development, while validation data without annotations enabled pre-testing. Submitted containerized algorithms were evaluated on hidden testing cases. Quantitative evaluation was based on median Euclidean error (MEE), Robustness, and the determinant of Jacobian of the displacement field. Top-ranked methods demonstrated comparable performance and shared key features, including pre-alignment of scans, deep neural networks, inverse consistency analysis, and per-case test-time optimization. The best method achieved MEE comparable to inter-rater variability for 63% of landmarks, underscoring the need for further improvements in accuracy and robustness relative to human experts. BraTS-Reg serves as a three-fold active resource for research on image registration, providing a publicly available dataset, a framework for a community benchmark, and online evaluation tools, accessible at https://bratsreg.github.io/.

papers.title: Robust low-light object detection and classification via hybrid feature fusion and synthetic data augmentation
papers.abstract: Robust visual navigation in low-light environments remains a fundamental challenge for autonomous systems due to severe illumination degradation, low signal-to-noise ratio, reduced texture information, and loss of discriminative visual cues. These primary conditions significantly impact the reliability of conventional handcrafted descriptors to detect objects on training on well-illuminated datasets through deep learning models. To improve low-light image object detection and classification by overcoming above limitation, we proposed a low-light visual recognition framework that combines image enhancement, complementary handcrafted and pretrained deep feature representations, dimensionality reduction, and synthetic low-light data augmentation. In the pre-processing stage, we had applied Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE), followed by gamma correction, to enhance local contrast while preserving structural information. To improve generalization across varying illumination levels, a pseudo low-light image synthesis pipeline was introduced, combining gamma-based exposure reduction, Poisson photon noise modeling, and intensity bias simulation. The resulting pseudo low-light images provide realistic illumination degradations for data augmentation. Feature extraction was done using Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG), which captures local edge and gradient structures that are comparatively robust to intensity variations, followed by deep convolutional embeddings that provide high-level semantic representations. For image classification, HOG descriptors and pre-trained features of ResNet-18 model was evaluated both individually and as a fused representation with PCA-based dimensionality reduction, using Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) classifiers. Separately, for object detection, synthetic low-light images generated from COCO images were used to augment ExDark training images, and their effect is evaluated with YOLOv8 and YOLOv11 object detection models. Extensive experiments were performed on the ExDark benchmark dataset to evaluate the proposed hybrid feature fusion strategy in terms of feature discriminability, detection accuracy, recall, and robustness across varying illumination conditions, in comparison with conventional handcrafted and deep feature baselines. The results show that complementary feature representations and synthetic low-light augmentation improve classification and detection performance under challenging low-light conditions, supporting improved robustness to illumination variation of low-light images.

papers.title: Behavioural and physiological responses of sheep, laying hens and horses to a total solar eclipse: a multi-site biologging study
papers.abstract: The sudden reduction in daylight during a total solar eclipse provides a unique natural setting to investigate how animals respond to an unexpected transition towards darkness. We investigated behavioural and physiological responses to the total solar eclipse of 12 August 2026 in sheep, laying hens and equids monitored at three locations in Spain. Locomotor activity (LA) was continuously recorded in 10 sheep, 22 hens and five mares, while body temperature (T) and heart rate (HR) were monitored in five additional sheep and six hens. Responses differed markedly among species and populations. Sheep exhibited a pronounced but transient reduction in LA around totality, followed by a rapid recovery. Activity during the early post-totality period was lower than on reference days (P = 0.039), although this difference was not consistently supported by broader statistical analyses. In laying hens, the eclipse coincided with changes in evening activity, including an earlier transition towards sustained inactivity in Zaragoza and pronounced activity suppression in Burgos. In contrast, free-ranging mares showed no consistent group-level response. Physiological measurements revealed no uniform changes in body T or HR associated with the eclipse. These findings indicate that a late-day total solar eclipse can coincide with short-lived changes in livestock behaviour, particularly in species exhibiting pronounced evening activity transitions. However, the diversity of responses and the proximity of the eclipse to natural sunset suggest that its behavioural effects cannot be separated entirely from normal dusk-related processes.

papers.title: Associations of anti-carbamylated protein antibodies with systemic inflammation and osteoporosis in rheumatoid arthritis: a cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Anti-carbamylated protein (anti-CarP) antibodies are part of the anti-modified protein antibody repertoire in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but their relationship with systemic inflammatory burden and osteoporosis (OP) remains insufficiently defined. This retrospective cross-sectional study investigated the complementary serological value of anti-CarP antibodies and their associations with systemic inflammation, osteoarticular damage, and OP in RA. A total of 182 patients with RA and 100 age- and sex-matched healthy controls were included. Serum anti-CarP antibodies were measured by ELISA. Associations with conventional autoantibodies, inflammatory markers, disease activity indices, radiographic damage, bone mineral density and OP were evaluated using non-parametric tests, correlation analyses and multivariable regression models. Nested logistic models assessed the incremental value of anti-CarP for OP-associated model performance. Anti-CarP levels were higher in RA patients than in controls (P < 0.0001), with positivity rates of 41.2% and 4.0%, respectively. Anti-CarP correlated more strongly with RF than with anti-CCP antibodies and was detected in 12.5% of double-seronegative RA patients. After multivariable adjustment, anti-CarP remained significantly associated with ESR, CRP, and OP, but not with structural joint damage. Adding anti-CarP significantly improved model fit, but the improvement in overall discrimination was minimal. Anti-CarP antibody concentrations remained associated with systemic inflammatory markers and OP after multivariable adjustment in this Chinese RA cohort. These findings suggest that anti-CarP antibodies may provide complementary serological information regarding inflammatory and skeletal manifestations of RA. However, given the cross-sectional design, these associations do not establish causality or the ability of anti-CarP to predict future outcomes. Further longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal and prognostic significance of these associations and their potential clinical applications.

papers.title: Resting-state aperiodic EEG activity exhibits regional differences and behavioral associations in mild-to-moderate age-related hearing loss
papers.abstract: Age-related hearing loss is associated with cognitive decline, yet its underlying neural changes remain poorly understood. Resting-state EEG offers a clinically feasible approach to investigating these changes. Eighty adults aged 50–70 years were classified by pure-tone average (PTA) into normal-hearing (NH; n = 40) and hearing-impaired (HI; n = 40) groups. Resting-state 128-channel EEG was recorded during eyes-closed (EC) and eyes-open (EO) conditions. Power spectra were parameterized using FOOOF to characterize the aperiodic spectral background. Alpha-band functional connectivity was quantified using the weighted phase lag index, with regional analyses conducted across six electrode-based regions of interest (ROIs). No significant between-group differences in alpha-band total power were detected in either condition. During EC rest, the HI group showed a lower aperiodic exponent in the Frontal ROI at nominal significance (p = 0.032, Cliff’s δ = 0.280). During EO rest, lower exponents were observed in the TemporalCore, TemporalExtended, Occipital, and Parietal ROIs. Exponent–alpha power correlations were numerically weaker in the HI group in several ROIs. During EC rest, the Frontal exponent was positively correlated with Frontal connectivity strength in the NH group (Spearman’s ρ = 0.53, p < 0.001), whereas the HI correlation was not significant (ρ = −0.19, p = 0.24). Within the HI group, the Frontal exponent during EO rest was negatively associated with speech-in-noise threshold after adjustment for PTA, age, sex, and education (partial ρ = −0.386, p = 0.020). PTA remained positively associated with speech-in-noise threshold after adjustment for the Frontal exponent and the same demographic covariates (partial ρ = 0.691, p < 0.001). These exploratory findings suggest that aperiodic spectral measures may complement conventional alpha-power analysis in characterizing hearing-related EEG differences. The cross-sectional, sensor-level findings require replication and do not establish underlying physiological mechanisms.

papers.title: Culturomics complements 16S rRNA gene sequencing in the characterization of the urogenital microbiome of asymptomatic reproductive-age women
papers.abstract: Culturomics and 16S rRNA gene sequencing offer complementary views of the genitourinary microbiome (GUM) but are rarely compared in well-phenotyped cohorts. Here, we characterized the GUM of 100 prospectively enrolled asymptomatic, non-pregnant, premenopausal women (18–45 years). Community structure types (CSTs) were defined by hierarchical clustering of genus-level relative abundances identified by culturomics and 16S V3-V4 sequencing. Correlations with clinical and behavioural host metadata collected were assessed based on sequencing. Culturomics and sequencing respectively identified 139 species from 59 genera, and 138 species from 144 genera. Per-sample richness at the genus level was higher by sequencing, but mean Shannon diversity was similar. Lactobacillus-dominated communities were common (37% by culturomics; 53% by sequencing), followed by Gardnerella-dominated and mixed Lactobacillus–Gardnerella profiles. Seven CSTs were defined from culturomics and six from 16S rRNA gene sequencing, which were concordant in only 31 of 98 samples (31.6%). Regarding metadata, none correlated with CST profiles, and only the menstrual cycle was significantly associated with variation in the beta diversity indices. This study revealed a well-structured and diverse GUM in asymptomatic women of reproductive age. However, longitudinal studies involving larger cohorts are needed to further our understanding of the host factors potentially associated with GUM.

papers.title: A highly reliable, self-healing photovoltaic cell-level dynamic reconfigurable architecture based on software-defined energy flow management
papers.abstract: Traditional crystalline silicon photovoltaic modules employ irreversible laminated packaging. Once individual cells fail or become obstructed, the entire string’s output power declines significantly, and repairs cannot be made without damaging the module—this constitutes a fundamental limitation of “static packaging.” This paper proposes a cell-level dynamic reconfigurable photovoltaic architecture that encapsulates each cell as a standardized “power generation cell,” integrating chip-level power optimizers, microfluidic active cooling systems, and high-speed industrial communication networks. Through a matrix backplate, the system enables online hot-swapping of cells and millisecond-scale electrical reconfiguration. This architecture redefines photovoltaic systems from static “power panels” into self-healing energy networks with physically maintainable components and software-defined energy pathways. A joint electrical-informatics-reliability simulation model was developed, comparing the proposed architecture with traditional modules under local failures, non-uniform shading, and long-term degradation conditions using Python simulations. Results demonstrate that during single-cell failure, the proposed architecture isolates the faulty cell and switches to backup cells within 5 ms, achieving power loss below 2%; over a 25-year lifecycle, the system’s rated output availability approaches 100%, whereas traditional modules show annual declines to approximately 82%. Active liquid cooling maintains cell temperatures at 45 ± 2 °C, thereby substantially reducing thermal hotspot risks under the simulated conditions. This study establishes a novel system paradigm and quantitative benchmark for next-generation high-reliability, intelligent photovoltaic power systems. The reported performance metrics are derived from numerical simulation; experimental validation through hardware-in-the-loop testing and outdoor prototyping remains necessary and is outlined as future work.

papers.title: Polygenic associations with COVID-19 severity across two danish cohorts: relationships with pre-infection health
papers.abstract: COVID-19 severity varies widely between individuals, reflecting a combination of demographic, clinical, and genetic risk factors. Although polygenic scores (PGS’s) are increasingly used to study susceptibility to infectious disease, it remains unclear to what extent these associations are sensitive to health characteristics present before infection. We examined PGS associations across four disease domains with COVID-19 severity outcomes in two complementary Danish cohorts: 14,364 participants from the Danish Blood Donor Study (DBDS), with self-reported bedridden COVID-19, and 115,515 participants from the Copenhagen Hospital Biobank (CHB), with register-defined COVID-19 severity among individuals with documented SARS-CoV-2 infection. PGSs surviving false-discovery-rate correction were examined across sequential models adjusting for pandemic period, measured pre-infection health and vaccination status at infection. Associations were quantified using population-standardised risk differences with 5,000 bootstrap iterations used to generate 95% CIs for risk estimates. Eight PGSs were associated with bedridden COVID-19 in DBDS and nine with register-defined COVID-19 severity in CHB, with seven associations shared across cohorts and showing concordant directions. In our nested sequential adjustment models adjustment for pre-infection health resulted in heterogeneous changes across PGSs. In DBDS, the risk difference per 1-SD higher ADHD PGS decreased from 1.75% points after adjustment for pandemic period to 1.31 after additional adjustment for pre-infection BMI and physical and mental health, whereas the corresponding influenza PGS association changed from 2.00 to 1.83% points. In CHB, ADHD PGS decreased from 0.49 to 0.40% points following adjustment for pre-pandemic comorbidity, while the COVID-19 severity PGS remained stable (0.19 to 0.19% points). Vaccination adjustment generally produced comparatively little additional attenuation. In our study, polygenic liabilities across multiple disease domains were associated with COVID-19 severity outcomes, but their associations showed varying sensitivity to adjustment for measured pre-infection health across two distinct cohort settings and two distinct pre-infection health measures. These findings suggest that cross-trait polygenic associations with COVID-19 differ in their relationships with pre-existing health highlighting the importance of pre-existing health when interpreting genetic associations with infectious disease outcomes.

papers.title: A generative approach for synthetic image-response in surface plasmon resonance sensors
papers.abstract: A generative approach for the automatic generation of surface plasmon resonance (SPR) image-responses is presented. The modern development of SPR sensors is driven by machine learning (ML) interventions that require data related to the sensors’ operation, with the intention of anticipating behaviors, predicting responses, and accelerating the design, optimization, and utilization of this type of sensor. The cost to produce SPR data in terms of time, material consumption, and experimental complexity associated with the absence of a public dataset of SPR images, makes it difficult to develop effective intelligent solutions for SPR sensors. The methodological proposition is based on a generative adversarial network (GAN) model to generate​ synthetic SPR images, reducing experimental data dependence, accelerating research workflows, and supporting intelligent biosensor advancement through complementary synthetic data. Manual​ creation of Fresnel images based on Kretschmann-configuration experimental SPR images of aqueous solutions was employed as training data. The results of synthetic images were quantitatively and qualitatively evaluated, in particular for a deep-convolutional GAN (DCGAN), indicating the feasibility of the model to generate two-dimensional SPR images. The latent space generated by DCGAN was explored in different scenarios of image generation, and the utility of the generative approach is attested in the substance classification task, leading to a model improvement of the main performance metrics.

papers.title: Region-guided cross-attention and view-GCN for interpretable multi-view echocardiographic classification of common left-to-right shunt lesions
papers.abstract: Echocardiography is the primary imaging modality for screening common congenital left-to-right shunt lesions; however, accurate diagnosis requires systematic integration of multiple standard views by experienced sonographers. Existing deep learning approaches typically analyze single views or rely on simple concatenation of multi-view features, which fail to capture anatomical relationships across imaging planes. Moreover, echocardiographic models are prone to shortcut learning, attending to background artifacts rather than clinically meaningful cardiac structures. We developed an interpretable end-to-end multi-view fusion framework integrating spatial region-guided cross-attention (RG-CA) and a view graph convolutional network (View-GCN). The framework was developed using a retrospective single-center cohort comprising 2,205 patients and 27,535 cine clips across four diagnostic categories: normal, atrial septal defect (ASD), ventricular septal defect (VSD), and patent ductus arteriosus (PDA). All dataset partitioning was performed at the patient level. The cohort was stratified into a development cohort of 1,764 patients (564 Normal, 576 ASD, 360 VSD, and 264 PDA) and an independent test cohort of 441 patients (141 Normal, 144 ASD, 90 VSD, and 66 PDA). All cine clips, sampled frames, and echocardiographic views from the same patient were retained within the same partition, and five-fold cross-validation was conducted exclusively within the development cohort. Five standard echocardiographic views were included: subcostal, apical four-chamber, parasternal short-axis, parasternal long-axis, and suprasternal long-axis. Cine clips were processed as frame-based multi-view image sets: representative frames were sampled from each clip, frame-level features were aggregated within each cine clip to obtain clip-level representations, clip-level representations belonging to the same echocardiographic view were further aggregated into a single view-level representation, and missing views were handled using zero-padding together with a view-availability mask. Zero-padding and the availability mask specify how the model processes missing views, but this architectural mechanism is not itself an empirical demonstration of missing-view robustness. The retained analysis did not include a controlled stress test in which one or more of the five views were systematically removed. View-GCN generated one final patient-level prediction per patient. No explicit temporal sequence model was used in the current implementation. Physician-annotated lesion masks were used only during model training as anatomical supervision for the mask-guided attention penalty (MGAP); no manually annotated mask is required during validation, testing, or clinical inference. Stratified five-fold cross-validation within the 1,764-patient development cohort yielded a reported mean patient-level AUC of 0.976 ± 0.015 for distinguishing normal cases from common left-to-right shunt lesions. In the independent test cohort, the model correctly classified 428 of 441 patients, yielding an overall multiclass diagnostic accuracy of 97.05%. The test cohort comprised 141 Normal, 144 ASD, 90 VSD, and 66 PDA patients. No ASD, VSD, or PDA cases were misclassified as normal, and the normal class achieved a precision of 1.0000. All reported test-set diagnostic-performance analyses were based on one aggregated patient-level prediction per patient rather than frame- or clip-level observations. Quantitative t-SNE/clustering and ablation performance claims are not made because the corresponding data partition, evaluation subset, denominator, and unit of analysis could not be verified. Attention maps are presented as qualitative illustrations only; quantitative Dice, IoU, and attention-mass measures are not reported. An exploratory L1-regularized analysis of 13 handcrafted grayscale intensity and texture descriptors ranked GLCM dissimilarity, homogeneity, and energy highest. This post hoc analysis was not based on a separately locked training-only subset and was not used as an input to the deep-learning classifier. The fold-specific configurations underlying the reported AUC could not be linked to a single defined training setup, and the exact configuration associated with the checkpoint used for the independent test predictions could not be verified. The proposed framework combines lesion-aware attention and graph-based multi-view reasoning to support automated diagnosis of common left-to-right shunt lesions using echocardiography. By using physician-defined anatomical regions as training-stage supervision rather than inference-stage inputs and integrating diagnostic evidence across multiple views, the training strategy was designed to encourage attention toward clinically relevant anatomical regions while supporting clinically oriented interpretability. The present results do not establish that reliance on non-anatomical artifacts or shortcut learning was quantitatively reduced. The model demonstrated high internal diagnostic accuracy, perfect normal-class precision, and qualitative attention visualizations and exploratory handcrafted intensity/texture-feature findings, suggesting its potential as an AI-assisted screening tool for common left-to-right shunt lesions.

papers.title: Theoretical study on the in-plane vertical and rotational coupled vibration of a shield cutter head
papers.abstract: During shield tunnelling, cutter head vibration not only affects face stability but also accelerates structural fatigue and cutter wear. To address the coupled vibration effect induced by the combined action of gravity and drive torque, this paper presents a comprehensive theoretical method for analysing the in-plane vertical-rotational coupled vibration response of the shield cutter head. First, the cutter head is modelled as a thin elastic circular plate with clamped edges, which is discretised using the localized radial basis function (LRBF) method, and its free vibration characteristics are obtained via the modified QR algorithm. Second, a two-degree-of-freedom mass-spring-damper model is established to simulate the cutter head system, and a coupling stiffness is introduced to account for the interaction between vertical displacement and rotational angle. Subsequently, the multi-scale perturbation method is applied to separate fast and slow time scales and eliminate secular terms, thereby enabling a reduced-order solution of the coupled vibration equations and yielding the amplitude and phase evolution equations as well as the frequency response functions. Finally, a case study indicates that the vertical-rotational coupling causes a shift in the natural frequencies of the cutter head, resulting in two new coupled frequencies. This frequency splitting is attributed to energy exchange between the vertical and rotational modes: the low-frequency mode is dominated by rotational vibration, whereas the high-frequency mode exhibits stronger modal coupling. Within the assumptions of harmonic excitation and linear coupling, the frequency splitting amount ΔΩ increases nonlinearly with increasing coupling stiffness and cutter head diameter, suggesting that the modal coupling becomes more intensive. Thus, the vertical-rotational coupling effect should be carefully considered for ultra-large diameter shields. Design should prioritise cutter layout optimisation to reduce coupling stiffness, or increase rotational stiffness to separate the natural frequencies, thereby weakening the risk of coupled vibration. This paper elucidates the energy transfer mechanism between the two modes and provides a theoretical basis for vibration control.

papers.title: Multi-step-ahead forecasting of highway slope displacement using adaptive feature decoupling and an attention-enhanced Bi-LSTM ensemble
papers.abstract: GNSS monitoring data for highway slopes exhibit strong non-stationarity and high-frequency noise, making traditional deep learning models prone to error accumulation in long-sequence forecasting. This paper proposes a highway slope displacement forecasting model based on Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN) and a weighted ensemble of Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) networks. OC-SVM and Simple Moving Average (SMA) are employed for outlier removal and noise reduction, while CEEMDAN decomposes the displacement sequence into a multi-channel feature matrix to suppress environmental interference. A Bi-LSTM incorporating a self-attention mechanism and Global Average Pooling (GAP) is then developed, and an inverse-error-based homogeneous weighted ensemble strategy is adopted for prediction. The model is validated using three-dimensional GNSS displacement data from a highway slope in Qingxiu District, Nanning, Guangxi. A total of 9000 E-W displacement samples (2-min interval) are used for evaluation. As the forecasting horizon increases from 1 to 12 h, prediction accuracy gradually decreases (R2 = 0.9577, 0.9122, and 0.8717) but consistently outperforms baseline models. When applied without retraining to the N-S and U displacement components recorded at the same GNSS monitoring station, the model also achieved R² values above 0.86. The proposed model effectively mitigates long-sequence forecasting divergence and provides technical support for dynamic highway slope monitoring.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of antioxidant, antibacterial activity of methanol solvent extract and ZnO nanoparticle synthesized using Hydrolea zeylanica (L.) Vahl
papers.abstract: In the present study, the whole plant of Hydrolea zeylanica was used to prepare a crude methanolic extract, which was then used as a bioactive capping agent for the synthesis of nanoparticles using zinc oxide metal ions. Formation of nanoparticles was confirmed using an UV–Vis spectrophotometer at the absorption peak of 320 nm, FESEM revealed the nanoparticles form aggregation after long storage; EDX confirmed ZnO elemental composition of the nanoparticles, XRD analysis revealed hexagonal crystalline nanoparticles with size 35.4 nm ±17.31, DLS analysis showed single peak at 420.6 nm with PDI 0.384 and FT-IR data revealed presence of functional groups like phenols and flavonoids. After characterisation, the bioactivity of both the methanolic extract and nanoparticle sample was evaluated for comparative bioactivity assessment using DPPH and H2O2 free radical scavenging tests in vitro. The DPPH test revealed IC50 value of 86.11 mg/mL for the methanolic extract and 29.34 mg/mL for the ZnO nanoparticle solution and  80.07 mg/mL for the plant extract. The antibacterial assessment was performed against two bacterial strains, Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus and the nanoparticle solution showed better activity in both disc diffusion and MIC tests. A viable colony count assay has also been performed to determine the antibacterial efficiency of the nanoparticles. Overall, the results show that nanoparticle synthesis is an effective way to enhance the bioactivity potential of the plant’s natural metabolites compared with raw plant extracts.

papers.title: Antifungal bioprotective effect of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum against Aspergillus niger and Penicillium notatum in set yogurt during refrigerated storage
papers.abstract: This study investigated the antifungal bioprotective potential of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum PTCC 1058 in set yogurt during 28 days of refrigerated storage (4 ± 1 °C). Four distinct formulations were evaluated: regular yogurt (Y1), yogurt containing L. plantarum (Y2), pre-acidified yogurt with L. plantarum (Y3), and chemically acidified milk prepared with glucono-δ-lactone (GDL) without cultures (Y4). Samples were monitored for mold counts (Aspergillus niger and Penicillium notatum), viable counts of L. plantarum, physicochemical properties, and sensory attributes. Viable cell counts of L. plantarum changed during storage (P < 0.05), but reached approximately 9 log CFU/g by day 28. In fungal challenge assays, L. plantarum-containing yogurts (Y2 and Y3) demonstrated pronounced antifungal activity, whereas regular yogurt (Y1) and chemically acidified milk (Y4) showed no noticeable fungal suppression. Specifically, viable counts of P. notatum decreased significantly by ~ 1.8 log CFU/g from day 14, and A. niger was reduced by ~ 1.67 log CFU/g from day 21 through day 28 (P < 0.05). This indicates that the antifungal effect was biologically mediated by the active culture rather than non-specific bulk acidity. Concurrently, post-acidification in formulations containing L. plantarum contributed to a pH decline to 3.94, which significantly lowered flavor and overall acceptability scores by day 28, whereas color, texture, total solids, and syneresis remained technologically stable. Overall, L. plantarum PTCC 1058 exhibits strong potential as a clean-label bioprotective adjunct against post-processing mold spoilage in set yogurt, although formulation optimization is required to balance bioprotection with long-term sensory quality.

papers.title: An experimental study on enhancing learning motivation and academic performance through AI literacy training
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in higher education, creating opportunities to support personalized learning. However, the educational value of AI depends not only on access to AI tools but also on students’ motivation, academic self-efficacy, and learning progress. This study presents the Motivation–Performance Adaptive AI Literacy Optimization Framework (MP-AILOF), a conceptual framework designed to integrate AI literacy instruction with learner-related indicators to inform adaptive instructional decisions. The framework combines learner profiling, motivational assessment, academic performance monitoring, and a proposed feedback-based instructional optimization process. Its empirical evaluation used a two-group pre-test–post-test dataset comprising 80 undergraduate students, with 40 students in the experimental group and 40 in the control group, from one higher-education institution. The experimental group received MP-AILOF-supported AI literacy instruction, whereas the control group received conventional classroom instruction. Academic self-efficacy, learning motivation, and grade point average (GPA) were assessed before and after the intervention. Paired-sample t-tests were used to examine within-group changes, and analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) was used to compare post-test outcomes while adjusting for baseline scores. In the supplied dataset, the experimental group showed statistically significant increases in all three outcomes. The ANCOVA analyses also indicated higher adjusted post-test scores for the experimental group than for the control group. These findings describe the observed results in the available sample and should be interpreted in light of the study design and the need to verify the recorded GPA values against the institutional grading scale. The implementation package reproduces the principal descriptive and inferential analyses; it does not independently validate the framework’s proposed GBR prediction and adaptive optimization components. Further research using verified data, documented allocation procedures, validated measurement instruments, and follow-up assessments is required to evaluate generalizability and the persistence of any observed changes.

papers.title: Crop-specific vegetation indices and phenological windows for spectral separability of 46 United States crops
papers.abstract: Vegetation indices designed for greenness are routinely applied to crop discrimination, yet searches for better indices rarely control for redundant candidates, selection bias or spatial dependence. We quantified one-versus-rest spectral separability for 46 crops on 16,647 parcels across the contiguous United States in 2019, 2021 and 2023, using 36 dekadal Sentinel-2 composites. A generative grammar produced 985 index expressions, of which 563 were distinguishable to rank-based methods; each was scored at every dekad against spatially matched neighboring parcels, and leading candidates were re-evaluated with selection confined to training folds. Optima were largely crop-specific (38 different best indices for 46 crops), with median held-out separability of 0.846 across years. Once candidate-family size was equalized, no index family dominated. Held-out separability fell from 0.872 in training to 0.835 when years were withheld and to 0.734 when spatial blocks were withheld, a gap that persisted after removing test parcels near training parcels. Thinning clear observations left a fixed index essentially unchanged but degraded re-selection; nevertheless, re-selection within a withheld region outperformed, on average, indices transferred from other regions at every observation density tested. Index atlases should therefore report sets of near-equivalent indices, calendar windows and the domain over which separability was validated.

papers.title: Human milk composition data for healthy growing, breastfed infants: analysis from 9 countries in Europe and Asia
papers.abstract: Human milk (HM) is the gold standard for infant nutrition, but, currently – beyond the macronutrients – there is limited knowledge on the composition of milk fed to infants growing within the WHO growth reference standards. This study aims to provide HM composition values for energy, macronutrients, fatty acids, and gangliosides for breastfed infants growing within the WHO growth reference standards. A pooled analysis of previously collected HM data from the mothers of healthy growing infants from 9 countries across Europe and Asia was performed using meta-analysis techniques to identify average values for energy, protein, lactose, total fat, fatty acids, and gangliosides. Healthy infant growth was defined according to the WHO growth standards. The pooled mean for energy in HM was 71.2 (95% confidence interval 66.27–76.22) kcal/100 mL, total fat was 4.21 (3.73–4.69) g/100 mL, protein was 1.26 (1.12–1.40) g/100 mL and lactose was 7.18 (6.91–7.44) g/100 mL. Pooled means for saturated​ and monounsaturated fatty acids were similar to previously reported values (mean, 95% CI: 42.2%, 39.12–45.29 and 41.3%, 39–43.66, respectively). Total polyunsaturated fatty acids showed considerable between-country heterogeneity, with the highest country-specific mean of n-3 PUFA in HM from Norway (2.49, 2.04–2.95) %. Pooled mean (95% CI) for HM gangliosides were 0.88 (0.7–1.05) mg/100 mL and 0.24 (0.21–0.27) mg/100 mL for GM3 and GD3 species, respectively. This analysis provides values for HM macronutrients, fatty acids and gangliosides from healthy mothers breastfeeding healthy, term infants from 9 countries across Europe and Asia. These data may be used to inform nutrient intake recommendations and guide nutritional interventions to support infant health and development. Clinical Trial Registry: NCT01894893 (25/04/2013); NCT01805011 (04/03/2013); NCT03387124 (21/12/2017).

papers.title: Process evaluation showing the importance of co-located, high-intensity and person-centred smoking cessation support in a lung cancer screening setting
papers.abstract: Evidence regarding optimal integration of smoking cessation is needed to inform implementation of lung cancer screening (LCS) and reduce smoking-related inequalities. The Yorkshire Enhanced Stop Smoking Randomised Controlled Trial tested opt-out, co-located standard best practice (SBP) smoking cessation support (control) versus SBP enhanced with theory-informed, personalised risk information derived from participants’ lung scan results to boost quit motivation (intervention). The intervention was tailored to degree of lung/heart damage, and designed to optimise self-efficacy and response-efficacy for quitting smoking1. Smoking cessation practitioners (SCPs) received bespoke intervention training in delivering theory-informed behaviour change techniques (BCTs). We conducted a nested process evaluation to evaluate the implementation of optimised smoking cessation support compared to SBP. Semi-structured interviews were carried out with 45 trial participants and eight SCPs at 4-, 12- and 52-weeks after screening (participants) or training (SCPs). Interviews were analysed thematically to assess intervention fidelity, exposure, context, contamination and theory. Observations of SCP consultations on the mobile screening unit (n = 84; 4%) and 4-weeks after screening (n = 132; 13%) were analysed to test fidelity, context and contamination. Intervention context was paramount: participants in both trial arms described benefits of co-located and ongoing high-intensity smoking cessation support, with immediate provision of pharmacotherapy. Tailored, non-judgemental care was considered key to initiating and sustaining quitting, particularly for participants at various points along their quit pathway and awaiting a possible lung cancer diagnosis. Fidelity was high (97%) on the screening unit and moderate (75%) 4-weeks after screening, and moderate for the enhanced intervention (77%) 4-weeks after screening. SBP and the intervention was flexibly delivered according to time constraints, participant motivation to quit, anxiety about screening and screening and/or booklet results. There was variation in how participants used and shared their booklets (exposure). Contamination of SCP intervention training was observed, with SCPs delivering theory-informed BCTs across both trial arms e.g. using the LCS context to boost response-efficacy beliefs. Provision of co-located, high intensity and person-centred smoking cessation support was vital, irrespective of trial arm. Investment in specialist LCS smoking cessation practitioners may harness the benefits of LCS as a teachable moment for cessation. Trial registration: www.clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03750110 (registered 21/11/2018).

papers.title: Identification and mechanistic elucidation of neutrophil migration-related biomarkers in bladder cancer based on single-cell and transcriptomic sequencing data
papers.abstract: This research comprehensively explores the role of neutrophils in bladder cancer (BLCA), aiming to clarify underlying molecular mechanisms, identify key genes and biomarkers, and develop a reliable prognostic prediction model to provide new insights for clinical diagnosis and treatment strategies. Multiple datasets from GEO and TCGA databases were collected. Single-cell RNA sequencing data underwent processing with Seurat, including quality control, cell clustering, and annotation. Differential abundance, expression, and enrichment analyses were performed. WGCNA screened neutrophil migration-related genes. Ten machine-learning algorithms constructed 116 prognostic models; molecular mechanisms were explored via database and network construction. RT-qPCR validated key gene expression. To explore EMP1 roles, overexpression and knockdown experiments were conducted using human peripheral blood neutrophils, with migration assessed via transwell assays. Neutrophil abundance was notably increased in tumor tissue. Among eight neutrophil subtypes, neutro4 showed highest migration-related activation. Through comprehensive analyses, we identified 28 candidate genes associated with neutrophil migration. The stepCox + RSF composite model was selected as optimal (average C-index = 0.7, AUC > 0.7), incorporating EMP1 and RBP7 biomarkers involved in specific biological processes with complex non-coding regulatory networks. These biomarkers correlated with bladder cancer clinical phenotypes. RT-qPCR confirmed RBP7 and EMP1 were significantly downregulated in tumors (p < 0.05). Furthermore, functional experiments revealed that EMP1 overexpression significantly enhanced neutrophil migration. This study provides a better understanding of neutrophil roles in bladder cancer. The identified biomarkers and constructed prognostic model offer potential clinical value for diagnosis and prognosis assessment, which may contribute to more effective treatment strategies. Functional experiments validate EMP1’s biological significance in neutrophil migration, supporting its potential as a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Assessment of potential bias mechanisms in the analysis of large electronic medical record datasets
papers.abstract: Electronic medical records aid general practitioners in the follow-up of their patients. The vast amounts of patient data that are being collected through such electronic medical records offer opportunities to use them for other purposes such as epidemiological and (pre)clinical research. But the use of electronic medical record data for research purposes raises concerns about potential biases, since these data are typically not collected within a study design specifically developed to address a predefined research question, which may instead emerge during or after data collection. In addition, data collection practices and reporting behaviours can vary between general practitioners, while patients themselves differ in their likelihood of seeking care or reporting symptoms. Although a large patient population may mitigate some of these random variations through the law of large numbers, systematic biases related to the non-randomized sample of the participating practices and heterogeneity in patient characteristics may persist. If not appropriately accounted for, these sources of heterogeneity and potential bias can lead to different or potentially conflicting research findings. Using a large electronic medical records dataset from Flanders, Belgium, we assess how simple statistical approaches, such as adding practice-level random effects and changing the analytical entity, can help identify potential bias mechanisms and assess the sensitivity of estimated associations to them.

papers.title: Intraspecific differentiation in metabolite diversity of a monotypic endemic Indianthus in the Western Ghats
papers.abstract: Indianthus virgatus (Marantaceae), a monotypic genus endemic to the Western Ghats–Sri Lanka Biodiversity Hotspot, represents an evolutionarily distinctive lineage for which intraspecific metabolomic variation remains poorly documented. Such variation can provide insights into biochemical differentiation among populations and potential environmental interactions. We used untargeted high-resolution liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (HR-LC-MS) to characterize metabolomic diversity across nine geographically distinct populations of I. virgatus in the Western Ghats. A total of 3,673 metabolite features were detected, of which 214 putative plant-derived metabolites were annotated and retained for downstream analyses following quality filtering. Multivariate analyses revealed differences in metabolomic profiles among the sampled population composites. Principal component analysis showed that the first two components explained 51.2% of the total variation. Variable importance in projection analysis highlighted glutamyl derivatives, amino acid intermediates, and phenolic compounds as important contributors to the observed separation. Distance-based redundancy analysis identified precipitation during the coldest quarter as the only individually significant environmental predictor (P < 0.05), although the overall model was not statistically significant (P > 0.05). KEGG pathway analysis indicated nominal enrichment of pyrimidine metabolism, which did not remain significant after false discovery rate correction (FDR = 0.0539). This preliminary metabolomic characterization provides a biochemical foundation for future multi-omics investigations integrating genomic, transcriptomic, and metabolomic data to elucidate the ecological and evolutionary processes underlying intraspecific diversity in I. virgatus. It also suggests a basis for further research into its phytochemical composition, bioactive compounds, and potential pharmacological applications.

papers.title: Deep learning analysis of echo signals from a single piezoelectric element for breast mass detection: a proof-of-concept study
papers.abstract: A palpable mass is a common presenting symptom of breast cancer, but neither breast self examination nor clinical breast examination is sensitive enough to detect breast masses early. We hypothesized that deep learning analysis of signals from a single-element (A-mode) ultrasound sensor can differentiate breast regions containing a mass from normal breast tissue. A-mode signals were prospectively acquired from 200 patients (192 malignant and 8 benign or borderline lesions). Signals collected during a freehand sweep were stacked into two-dimensional images (reconstructed A-mode images), whose appearance varies with probe motion. Self-supervised pre-training on public B-mode images was compared with ImageNet initialization, and an acquisition-specific augmentation (Variable Speed and Pressure Augmentation, VSPA) with conventional augmentation. The first 131 patients were used for model development and the next 69 for additional validation. On additional validation, ultrasound pre-training gave higher region-level AUCs than ImageNet initialization (ResNet-50, 93.6% versus 91.7%; ViT-B/16, 96.3% versus 93.2%) and more mass-focused Grad-CAM heatmaps. For ViT-B/16, the advantage grew as training data decreased. Conventional spatial augmentation gave most of the gain (ViT-B/16, 96.8% versus 93.2%), and VSPA added little. Further validation in women without known breast lesions is needed before this approach can be considered for screening.

papers.title: Prognostic value of triglyceride-glucose glycemic variability index in critically ill unstable angina patients via machine learning with independent hospital validation
papers.abstract: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is associated with outcomes in critical illness, but the prognostic value of combining it with glycemic variability, the TyG-glycemic variability index (TyG-GVI), has not been evaluated in critically ill patients with unstable angina. In this study we examined the association between TyG-GVI and ICU and in-hospital mortality and developed an interpretable machine-learning model for mortality risk. We retrospectively analyzed 1,444 adult patients with unstable angina from the MIMIC-IV 3.1 database (2008–2022) as the development cohort, dichotomized at the median TyG‑GVI. Associations with ICU and in-hospital mortality were estimated using Cox proportional-hazards and logistic regression, and the dose-response relationship was modelled with restricted cubic splines. Random Forest, XGBoost and LightGBM classifiers were developed with Boruta confirmatory importance analysis and SHAP-based interpretation, and the optimal model was externally validated in an independent retrospective cohort of 340 ICU patients with unstable angina from the Quzhou Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University. A total of 108 ICU deaths (7.5%) and 190 in-hospital deaths (13.2%) occurred. Compared with the low TyG-GVI group, high TyG-GVI was associated with ICU mortality in the fully adjusted Cox model (HR 2.29, 95% CI 1.43–3.66) and with in-hospital mortality (HR 1.54, 95% CI 1.11–2.15), although the latter did not reach statistical significance in every model specification. The dose-response relationship was non-linear (P for non-linearity < 0.01 for ICU mortality and < 0.05 for in-hospital mortality), with a data-derived nadir at a TyG-GVI of approximately 3.135. Random Forest achieved the numerically highest discrimination in the development cohort (AUC 0.830) and in the external validation cohort (AUC 0.874). High TyG-GVI was independently associated with ICU mortality and was also associated with in-hospital mortality in critically ill patients with unstable angina. An interpretable machine-learning model incorporating TyG-GVI showed consistent discrimination performance in the development and external validation cohorts and has been deployed as a web-based research prototype. Prospective validation and formal assessment of calibration and clinical utility are required before clinical use.

papers.title: Postoperative evaluation of Achilles tendon using short echo time MRI and artificial intelligence
papers.abstract: The objective was to identify the optimal MRI sequence to evaluate postoperative Achilles tendon (AT) healing. We compared T2 gradient sequence with 4.1ms (TE4) and 16ms (TE16) echo time with PD (proton density-weighted) through signal intensity (SI) measurements and correlated them with tendon-specific biomarkers. Additionally, the study assessed agreement between radiologists and AI in evaluating tendon-specific biomarkers. A total of 45 patients (mean age 36 ± 6 years; 36 men, 9 women) underwent nine consecutive MRI examinations at intervals from 1 to 52 weeks after surgery. SI in all postoperative MRI examinations was measured in AT in TE4, TE16 and PD. SI in the operated AT appears normal in PD and TE16 sequences around week 39. However, TE4 still shows high signals, indicating ongoing remodeling. Significant correlations were found between biomarkers and SI in the TE4 sequence (p < 0.001 for structural changes and tendon edema, and p = 0.002 for tissue edema). High SI values were associated with poor biomarker outcomes. The mean absolute errors (MAE) between AI model scores, obtained using only axial TE4 scans, and radiologist evaluations ranged from 0.12 to 0.63. In conclusion, TE4 demonstrated greater sensitivity to persistent postoperative signal and structural abnormalities and may be useful in postoperative assessment of AT. AI scores showed relatively small absolute differences from the reference radiologist scores.

papers.title: Prediction of flavonoid components and antioxidant activity in tangerine peel based on machine learning
papers.abstract: Tangerine peel is a valuable citrus by-product enriched with flavonoids and antioxidant compounds, possessing considerable potential for applications in the functional food and nutraceutical industries. Conventional analytical techniques for flavonoid determination are often labor-intensive, time-consuming, and unsuitable for high-throughput quality evaluation. This study developed a machine learning-based prediction framework for the rapid assessment of major flavonoid components and antioxidant activity in tangerine peel using physicochemical characteristics and near-infrared spectral information. A total of 320 tangerine peel samples were analyzed, incorporating moisture content, soluble solids, color parameters, total phenolic content, and spectral variables as predictors. Hesperidin, nobiletin, and tangeretin concentrations were quantified by high-performance liquid chromatography, while antioxidant activity was determined using the DPPH radical scavenging assay. Three machine learning algorithms, including Support Vector Regression (SVR), Random Forest (RF), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), were evaluated and compared. The results demonstrated that XGBoost exhibited the highest predictive accuracy, achieving coefficient of determination (R²) values of 0.945, 0.921, and 0.907 for hesperidin, nobiletin, and tangeretin, respectively. Antioxidant activity prediction achieved an R² of 0.959, with a root mean square error (RMSE) of 2.73%, which demonstrates the reliability and generalization capability of the model. Feature importance analysis revealed that total phenolic content (24.8%), absorbance at 1450 nm (18.6%), and peel color parameter a* (12.9%) were the most influential predictors. Compared with conventional laboratory analysis, the proposed framework reduced analytical time from approximately 51.6 min per sample to less than 2.5 s while maintaining prediction accuracy above 95%. These findings confirm that machine learning integrated with spectral sensing technologies provides an efficient, accurate, and non-destructive strategy for predicting flavonoid composition and antioxidant capacity, offering substantial potential for intelligent quality control and high-value utilization of citrus processing by-products.

papers.title: College students’ perceived course usefulness and ease of engagement in an aesthetic education course in Shanxi, China
papers.abstract: Despite increasing policy attention to aesthetic education, college students’ responses to aesthetic education courses remain a concern in China. This study examined students’ perceived course usefulness and ease of engagement and its associations with creativity and attitude in an optimised course integrating Chinese literati painting. A quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design involved 793 students from six intact classes across three higher education institutions in Shanxi Province, China. Individual-level analyses indicated both a pre-post increase in perceived course usefulness and ease of engagement in the experimental group and higher baseline-adjusted post-test scores than in the control group. Neither finding was statistically supported after accounting for class-level clustering. Within the experimental group, primary and baseline-adjusted structural equation models used individual-level and class-clustered inference.
