The positive associations of creativity with attitude and of attitude with perceived course usefulness and ease of engagement retained statistical support across these analyses. Statistical support for the direct creativity-outcome association and the indirect association through attitude was less consistent. Based on the findings, the proposed model offers a framework for further investigation of the relationships among creativity, attitude, and perceived course usefulness and ease of engagement rather than an established causal explanation.

papers.title: GRACE-AI: a governance-centric MLOps framework for risk-tiered control, continuous assurance, and explainability in high-stakes AI systems
papers.abstract: The recent successful adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in several important applications has made it imperative to integrate operational machine learning with governance frameworks to facilitate regulatory alignment, structured accountability mechanisms, and risk-based decision-making. Current MLOps frameworks are good at controlling the technical lifecycle of AI models, but are less likely to support governance needs in regulated environments. This paper introduces a governance-oriented MLOps framework to support healthcare and financial AI systems, namely GRACE-AI (Governance, Risk, Assurance, Compliance, and Explainability for Artificial Intelligence). The proposed framework is composed of four interconnected layers, (i) Regulatory Alignment Layer: mapping regulatory requirements into pipeline constraints that incorporate information about governance; the Regulatory Alignment Layer is presented as a proposed architectural component for automated obligation extraction; its clause-level classification performance was not independently benchmarked in this study (ii) Dynamic Risk-Tiering Engine: assigning adaptive governance risk levels based on composite risk scores; (iii) Continuous Assurance Pipeline: drift detection, monitoring, automated recalibration, and anomaly tracking; and (iv) Explainability-by-Design Module: generation of stakeholder-oriented and interpretable explanations. The proposed framework was evaluated using three benchmark datasets supporting four prediction tasks across the healthcare and financial domains, achieving an average accuracy of 96.38% and an unweighted cross-task mean AUC of 0.973; this is 2.78 percentage points above the strongest evaluated standalone baseline (Transformer, 93.60%) and 6.06 percentage points above the mean of the five evaluated standalone baselines. In addition, GRACE-AI could cover 94.7% of the risk, reduce compliance overhead by 38.6%, and detect drift with an average latency of 1.8 s. The findings suggest that the proposed governance model is effective in a controlled experimental setting and could be used to enable trustworthy, governance-aware deployment of AI in regulated environments. In the future, the framework will be validated under operational, real-world conditions with human involvement and at production scale.

papers.title: Broadband sensor-level EEG power dynamics differentiate anticipation, observation, imitation, and execution of hand actions
papers.abstract: To understand how perceived actions translate to neural processes relevant for learning, planning, and adaptation, it is important to study how sensory inputs and intentions are interpreted within the mirror neuron system (MNS) framework. Although execution, observation, and imitation are commonly studied within the MNS framework, prior reports on cortical activity differences—particularly hemispheric lateralization between left- and right-hand actions and the temporal progression of activity across perceptual, cognitive, and motor cortical regions—remain unclear. Here, we analyzed electroencephalography data from 15 right-handed adults as they anticipated, executed, imitated, and observed right- and left-hand squeezes to characterize task-, hand-, and phase-specific temporal, spectral, and spatial patterns of sensor-level EEG oscillatory power, and to evaluate the within-sample reliability of these patterns. We found that low- and high-frequency EEG power differed by task and hand. EEG oscillatory power patterns were predominantly bilateral, whereas contralateral power modulations emerged during anticipation. Differences in the temporal profile of sensor-level EEG activity were consistent with top-down organization during observation (early frontal EEG power modulation) and bottom-up organization during cue-driven execution and imitation (early visuoparietal EEG power modulation). These findings demonstrate that a single within-subject EEG design can resolve task-, hand-, and phase-specific sensor-level dynamics within MNS-related action paradigms with adequate within-sample reliability, establishing an empirical basis for future hypothesis-driven investigations of sensorimotor integration and perception–action mapping.

papers.title: A stabilized abdominal imaging platform for intravital interrogation of preclinical omental metastatic niche models
papers.abstract: The omentum is a highly specialized immunological and metabolic tissue that frequently acts as a permissive niche for metastatic dissemination within the peritoneal cavity. Despite its central role in metastatic progression and therapeutic response, real-time interrogation of the omental microenvironment in preclinical in vivo models remains technically challenging because of respiratory motion, tissue drift, and the fragility of abdominal tissues. Current methodologies largely rely on endpoint analyses or invasive tissue externalization procedures that disrupt physiological tissue dynamics and limit longitudinal investigation. Here, we present a mechanically stabilized abdominal imaging platform that enables high-resolution longitudinal intravital imaging of the omentum in live mice. The system combines a custom abdominal imaging window with a lift-support stabilization structure that mechanically isolates the omentum from respiratory motion while preserving tissue architecture and physiological immune cell behavior. Using fluorescent reporters, we demonstrate stable, long-term visualization of tumor progression, immune cell recruitment, and adoptive cell transfer targeting within the omental niche. As a proof-of-concept application, the platform was validated using an omentum-tropic model of peritoneal ovarian cancer dissemination, enabling longitudinal monitoring of metastatic engraftment and spatiotemporal immune dynamics during locoregional immunotherapy. Importantly, imaging through the stabilized window preserved lymphocyte motility significantly better than conventional tissue externalization approaches, thereby supporting the physiological relevance of the system. Overall, this platform provides a robust, adaptable framework for studying immune and metastatic processes in the peritoneal cavity and may facilitate preclinical evaluation of intraperitoneal therapies, cell-based immunotherapies, and microenvironment-targeted interventions.

papers.title: Long-term trends and COVID-19 pandemic–era changes in the incidence of cancers with established screening strategies in the United States: a population-based SEER study
papers.abstract: Cancer screening and prevention constitute essential components of cancer control, although their influence on population-level incidence varies across cancer types and is shaped by patterns of healthcare access and utilization. Large-scale public health emergencies can disrupt the delivery of routine preventive, diagnostic, and oncologic services. The present study examines long-term incidence trends and evaluates changes in cancer incidence patterns during the COVID-19 pandemic. Data were sourced from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) 21 registries database. Age-adjusted incidence rates for lung and bronchus, colon and rectum, breast, and cervix uteri cancers among adults aged 40 years and older were analyzed separately from 2000 to 2022. Joinpoint regression analysis was conducted to assess long-term incidence trends. Pre-pandemic trends from 2000 to 2019 were extrapolated to estimate expected incidence rates for 2020–2022, which were compared with observed rates. Long-term incidence declined significantly for lung and bronchus (AAPC, − 1.81%), colorectal (AAPC, − 1.94%), and cervical cancers (AAPC, − 1.48%) from 2000 to 2022, whereas breast cancer incidence showed no significant overall change (AAPC, − 0.32%). Descriptive subgroup analyses demonstrated heterogeneous patterns across age, sex, race/ethnicity, and stage. Stage distribution among diagnosed cases showed only modest year-to-year variation across the four cancer sites. Over the past two decades, lung and bronchus, colorectal, and cervical cancer incidence declined, whereas breast cancer incidence remained relatively stable among adults aged ≥ 40 years. During 2020–2022, observed incidence rates for several cancer types deviated from those expected based on pre-pandemic trends, with the largest reductions generally observed in 2020 and variable patterns thereafter. These findings highlight the importance of maintaining accessible and resilient cancer screening and diagnostic services during future public health emergencies to minimize potential disruptions in timely cancer detection and care.

papers.title: Neurophysiological correlates of interoceptive compassion training for depression
papers.abstract: Depression is often linked to interoceptive dysfunction and self-critical thinking. The Heart-Smile Training-Intensive Introduction Program (HST-IIP) integrates interoceptive attention training with compassion-based practices to support emotional well-being. This pilot study randomized 23 individuals with depression to either HST-IIP or a waitlist control group. Participants completed EEG recordings and clinical assessments before and after a 4-week intervention. The primary outcome was heartbeat-evoked potentials (HEPs), while depression severity was our main clinical outcome, assessed using the Computerized Adaptive Test-Mental Health (CAT-MH). Exploratory outcomes included Delta power spectral density (PSD) during guided meditation, as well as psychological measures of interoceptive awareness (MAIA-2) and self-compassion (SCS). Compared to the control group, participants assigned to HST-IIP showed greater improvements in depression scores (Hedges’g = –1.422, p = 0.028) and increases in interoceptive awareness. EEG analyses revealed attenuated (less negative) HEP amplitude in right frontal electrodes during attention-focused meditation and reduced Delta power during compassion-focused meditation. Changes in these neural markers were associated with improvements in depression outcomes. This exploratory pilot study provides preliminary evidence that HST-IIP is associated with improvements in depressive symptoms together with changes in HEP and Delta activity. These findings suggest that interoceptive compassion training may influence neurophysiological processes relevant to depression and support further research into interoceptive compassion training as a treatment for depression.

papers.title: Age- and stage-specific competing mortality after colorectal cancer resection
papers.abstract: Mortality after colorectal cancer (CRC) resection reflects cancer and competing health risks. We analysed 231,248 resected stage I–III adenocarcinomas diagnosed during 2004–2017 in SEER using cumulative-incidence functions, Fine-Gray models and separate survivor landmark cohorts. Exploratory stable crossover times were estimated on a monthly grid with 2,000 bootstrap replicates. In stage I, other-cause mortality predominated within 1–5 months; among patients aged ≥ 90 years, the estimate was 5 months (95% CI, 1–12; n = 1,091). In stage II, crossover occurred at 7.0 years (6.3–7.5) at ages 65–74 and 2.6–2.9 years at ages ≥ 75; no crossover was observed below age 65. No stage III age group crossed within 10 years under recorded cause-of-death classifications. Age-by-stage interactions were significant for both outcomes (P < 0.001). Among separate 5-year survivor cohorts, subsequent 5-year CRC/other-cause incidences were 4.1%/17.6%, 8.1%/19.6% and 12.8%/13.0% in stages I–III. Cause-of-death reallocation changed some crossover conclusions. These population-level descriptions require external validation and do not define individual treatment or surveillance thresholds.

papers.title: Systematic identification of bedaquiline-anchored regimens with cross-species efficacy for nontuberculous mycobacterial pulmonary disease
papers.abstract: Nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM), particularly Mycobacterium avium and Mycobacterium abscessus, are increasingly recognized causes of chronic pulmonary disease, yet current therapies remain prolonged treatment, are frequently associated with adverse effects, and often achieve suboptimal clinical outcomes. To identify therapeutic regimens active against both slow- and rapidly growing NTM species, we systematically evaluated 11 tuberculosis (TB) standard-of-care drugs using a tiered preclinical screening framework comprising minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) testing, intracellular macrophage infection assays, and species-matched murine lung infection models. Initial susceptibility screening demonstrated substantial differences in drug activity between M. avium and M. abscessus, with cell wall-directed agents generally exhibiting limited cross-species activity. Bedaquiline (BDQ), an FDA-approved antimycobacterial agent, demonstrated the greatest activity among the compounds evaluated in our screening panel and was therefore selected as the foundation for subsequent combination studies. Azithromycin (AZI), clarithromycin (CLA), and ofloxacin (OFL) also emerged as promising agents for further evaluation. Following extended incubation, CLA and AZI MICs increased 2- to 4-fold in M. abscessus, consistent with inducible erm(41)-mediated macrolide resistance, whereas BDQ and OFL retained unchanged activity, supporting BDQ as a candidate therapeutic anchor. Intracellular macrophage studies confirmed BDQ as the most consistently active single agent and demonstrated enhanced bacterial clearance with BDQ + AZI; BDQ + OFL was advanced based on complementary mechanisms and favorable cross-species activity. Subsequent murine lung infection studies confirmed BDQ as the principal driver of antibacterial efficacy against both species. The BDQ + AZI and BDQ + OFL combinations emerged as two-drug therapeutic backbones with activity in both species-matched models, while optimizing the dose and schedule of the three-drug BDQ + AZI+OFL regimen produced cross-species efficacy and the greatest bacterial clearance observed in the M. abscessus model. Treatment performance was examined using complementary measures with distinct purposes: Δlog10 CFU quantified absolute bacterial clearance, Hedges’ g described standardized effect magnitude, quartile classification provided relative within-model ranking, and MACI provided secondary normalization for species-specific in vitro susceptibility. Collectively, these studies establish a systematic translational framework that down-selected 11 TB standard-of-care drugs to 3 prioritized therapeutic agents (BDQ, AZI, and OFL) and ultimately to three BDQ-anchored regimens with activity across both species-matched models. Further, these findings identify BDQ as a candidate therapeutic anchor whose activity is maintained despite inducible erm(41)-mediated macrolide resistance and support the development of modular BDQ-anchored therapeutic platforms that can be optimized for species-specific susceptibility while maintaining a common therapeutic architecture across clinically important NTM species.

papers.title: Heterogeneous genetic sharing between inflammatory bowel disease and allergic phenotypes: genome-wide and targeted regional analyses
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and allergic diseases share genetic liability, but subtype and regional patterns remain uncertain. We analysed European-ancestry summary statistics for Crohn’s disease (CD), ulcerative colitis (UC), combined IBD, and four allergic phenotypes using genetic correlation, Mendelian randomization (MR), Causal Analysis Using Summary Effect estimates (CAUSE), targeted colocalization, fine-mapping, and gene and functional follow-up; UK Biobank analyses served as cross-dataset consistency checks. Genetic sharing was detected more consistently for CD than for UC, without a formal subtype difference. Reference inverse-variance-weighted MR associations of genetically predicted CD log odds with atopic dermatitis, allergic rhinitis, and allergic conjunctivitis passed within-family false-discovery-rate correction; CD–asthma did not, whereas secondary discovery-only combined-IBD associations passed correction for all four outcomes. Three CAUSE comparisons had nominal model-comparison P values, but none survived within-family correction. Regional architectures were heterogeneous: targeted 5q31 CD–asthma colocalization support was high but specification dependent; 2q12 remained unresolved, and 17q12–21 supported distinct IBD and asthma signals. Regulatory and functional follow-up did not establish a stable target-specific mechanism, and SLC22A5 remained a 5q31 regional candidate. Resolving these signals requires ancestry- and linkage-disequilibrium (LD)-matched fine-mapping with estimable regulatory data and direct perturbation in disease-relevant models.

papers.title: A causal decision framework for selecting industry 4.0 technologies to overcome open innovation barriers in construction
papers.abstract: The construction industry has long struggled to embrace open innovation, not for lack of intent, but because of deeply embedded financial, organizational, and cultural barriers that resist change. This study responds to that challenge by building an integrated decision-support framework that identifies which Industry 4.0 technologies are best positioned to address these barriers. The research followed a three-stage design. Following a systematic literature review and expert content validation, 11 open innovation barriers and 7 technologies were retained. Then, a two-method analytical sequence combining Pythagorean Fuzzy DEMATEL (PF-DEMATEL) with Grey MABAC applied. PF-DEMATEL mapped the causal structure among the barriers, identifying inadequate support from top management and their risk attitude (C2; weight = 0.1119, D + R = 4.566) as the central systemic mediator, while difficulty in finding suitable human resources for R&D (C6; D − R = 1.730) and market uncertainty regarding innovative products (C4; D − R = 1.023) emerged as the dominant root causes driving the broader barrier network. Grey MABAC then ranked the seven technologies by their weighted mitigation potential, placing Building Information Modelling well ahead of the field, followed by the Internet of Things and Artificial Intelligence. The findings offer construction practitioners a sequenced, evidence-based roadmap for digital transformation that targets the most influential barriers first and builds collaborative innovation capacity from the ground up.

papers.title: LLM-agent-based cross-modal retrieval method for detecting clues of ecological environment damage
papers.abstract: Within Ecological Conservation Redline zones, ecological environmental damage caused by non-compliant production and construction activities has become increasingly severe. Existing methods typically leverage remote sensing imagery and deep learning techniques to automatically identify unauthorized construction, or retrieve clues of ecological environmental damage from textual information such as public complaints and official circulars. The former often relies on professional experiential knowledge, while the latter remains at the level of passive retrieval; both rely on predefined rules and professional experience and suffer from a time lag. Recently emerging Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents, which possess both natural language understanding and multi-step task execution capabilities, make it possible to acquire and fulfill users’ retrieval demands in a fast and flexible manner through human–machine dialogue. Inspired by this, this paper constructs a multimodal clue retrieval agent for ecological environmental damage based on a multi-agent framework. The agent interacts with users who lack computer professional and technical backgrounds through natural language via LLMs to clarify their retrieval demands regarding specified regions, time periods, and damage types. It then orchestrates different sub-agents to automatically retrieve textual clues and remote sensing image clues within the corresponding spatiotemporal scope in a cross-modal manner, and aggregates and presents textual and image evidence to users to support the review and analysis of problem clues. Testing and evaluation conducted by researchers in the field of procuratorial case handling show that the proposed method achieves satisfactory retrieval performance and usability, and is simple and easy to learn. It can provide technical support for the screening and assessment of ecological environmental damage issues.

papers.title: Study on similar materials for the asphalt concrete impervious layer of the pumped-storage upper reservoir in a karst area
papers.abstract: Groundwater–air pressure may break the full-basin impervious systems in pumped-storage reservoirs built in karst depressions. This study developed polyurethane-based similar materials for asphalt concrete impervious layers. An L9(34) orthogonal design was used to evaluate the formulation factors. Mechanical and permeability tests, weighted grey relational analysis, uplift loading, and SEM–EDS were used for formulation screening and validation. Across the nine formulations, elastic modulus, flexural modulus, flexural strength, and maximum flexural tensile strain ranged from 1.47 to 5.07 MPa, 2.10 to 12.42 MPa, 0.11 to 1.02 MPa, and 4.12% to 13.69%, respectively. Results showed that the curing ratio had the greatest effect on flexural modulus and maximum flexural tensile strain, whereas talc powder increased stiffness and DOP enhanced deformation capacity. The novel mechanical uplift tests were carried out, and result showed that the deformation and cracking processes broadly similar to those of the asphalt concrete prototype. The material group X5 also exhibited more uniform talc dispersion and matrix encapsulation than material groups X1 and X9. This study provides a method for preparing similar materials with adjustable deformation and strength properties for physical model studies of asphalt concrete impervious structures.

papers.title: Short term effects of ambient air pollution exposure on influenza: a multi-city study in Shandong, China
papers.abstract: Ambient air pollution is a recognized risk factor for influenza-like illness (ILI). However, it remains unclear how city-specific characteristics modify these associations. This study evaluated the short-term associations between six major air pollutants and ILI incidence in Shandong Province, China, and investigated the modifying effects of seasonal, spatial, and socioeconomic factors. Daily air pollutant concentrations and ILI surveillance data from 16 cities in Shandong Province (2015–2019) were analyzed using a two-stage approach. City-specific associations were estimated using quasi-Poisson distributed lag non-linear models (DLNM), followed by a multivariate random-effects meta-analysis to calculate pooled cumulative relative risks (CRRs). Meta-regression and stratified analyses were used to assess effect modification by demographic, geographic, and macroeconomic indicators. A total of 2,145,543 ILI cases were included. Except for O3, short-term exposure to all evaluated air pollutants was significantly associated with increased ILI incidence. NO2 (CRR: 1.041, 95% CI: 1.031–1.052) and SO2 (CRR: 1.040, 95% CI: 1.023–1.058) exhibited the strongest positive associations, whereas O3 was inversely associated with ILI. The risks were higher in children aged 5–14 years, during transition seasons (spring and autumn), and in coastal areas. Meta-regression indicated that higher gross domestic product and healthcare resource density mitigated the adverse impacts of particulate matter and carbon monoxide, whereas basin. Basin topography exacerbated pollution-induced ILI risks during severe pollution episodes. Short-term exposure to major air pollutants increases ILI risk, but the magnitude of this risk is significantly modified by city-level socioeconomic and geographic characteristics. These findings highlight the need to develop localized, resource-adjusted air quality early warning systems to protect vulnerable populations.

papers.title: Coupled exposure–response assessment and regulation of multi-source ecological risks in coastal wetlands of Guangxi
papers.abstract: Coastal wetlands serve as ecological security barriers and provide important ecosystem services. They are now under combined pressure from multiple human activities. To address the diverse risk types, complex impact pathways and heterogeneous ecological responses in the wetlands of the Beibu Gulf, Guangxi, this study extended the conventional Relative Risk Model (RRM) by incorporating an explicit exposure–response pathway framework linking risk sources, habitat receptors and ecological endpoints. The extended framework integrates four indicators: relative risk density, habitat abundance, exposure coefficient and response coefficient. The model integrates four indica-tors, namely relative risk density, habitat abundance, exposure coefficient and response coefficient. Remote sensing interpretation, field investigation and AHP-based weighting were combined to support quantitative, pathway-based and zoning-oriented assessment of coastal ecological risks. The results show clear spatial differences among the five assessment subregions. The Maowei Sea and Qinzhou Bay region (Q4) had the highest comprehensive risk value, reaching 7.58. This was mainly driven by the combined effects of port expansion, pollutant discharge and waterway construction. Tieshan Port (Q1) and Pearl Bay (Q5) had risk values of 4.14 and 3.90, respectively. These two areas were classified as medium-high risk zones. The Nanliu River Estuary (Q2) and Sanniang Bay (Q3) showed lower risk values, at 2.24 and 2.73, respectively. Among all ecological receptors, mangrove wetlands had the highest exposure and response coefficients. They therefore represented the most sensitive areas with concentrated ecological risks. The model identified the pathway from urban construction to mangrove wetlands and then to biodiversity degradation as an important risk transmission pathway. Based on the assessment results, differentiated ecological regulation strategies are proposed for different zones. High-risk zones should implement ecological red-line protection and risk monitoring and management mechanisms. Medium-risk zones should strengthen pollution control and industrial restructuring. Low-risk zones should promote green ecological use and preventive management. The proposed model can jointly represent multiple risks, multiple receptors and multiple endpoints. It provides spatially precise and regulation-oriented decision support for coastal wetland conservation. It also extends the application boundary of the relative risk model (RRM) in complex ecosystems. The results showed clear spatial differences among the five assessment subregions, mainly associated with differences in port and urban construction, waterway disturbance, aquaculture intensity and pollution pressure.

papers.title: Machine learning maps multiplanar spinal surface alignment and patterns of change across heterogeneous cohorts
papers.abstract: Surface-derived thoracolumbar-pelvic alignment measures span sagittal, frontal, and transverse planes, but their multivariate organization remains incompletely characterized. This retrospective pooled analysis comprised a baseline cross-sectional sample of 468 participants from four cohorts (CGH, n = 200; FMS, n = 120; LSR, n = 80; AIS, n = 68) and a separate paired sample of 268 participants from the three intervention cohorts (FMS, n = 120; LSR, n = 80; AIS, n = 68). The CGH cohort was a matched cross-sectional study with one baseline assessment and was excluded from all post-treatment, change-score, and multiplanar change-magnitude analyses. In the primary cohort-centered baseline analysis, the first two PCA components explained 83.3% of variance, and CCA yielded Rc = 0.926 (95% cohort-stratified bootstrap CI 0.915–0.939; within-cohort permutation p < 0.001). In the cohort-centered paired analysis, PCA of post-minus-baseline changes explained 81.2% and 6.7% of variance in PC1 and PC2, respectively (87.9% cumulative), and CCA yielded Rc = 0.917 (95% cohort-stratified bootstrap CI 0.898–0.935; within-cohort permutation p < 0.001; repeated cohort-stratified cross-validated Rc = 0.912 ± 0.022). Exploratory K-means clustering yielded two partially overlapping descriptive profiles; an alternative Gaussian mixture analysis did not support two discrete latent subgroups. The profiles were not validated against independent clinical outcomes. Three-class classification using change scores alone was modest (balanced accuracy 0.418 ± 0.072; macro-AUC 0.610 ± 0.035). The paired findings describe multiplanar covariance of observed within-participant change across different interventions and follow-up intervals. They do not establish a shared adaptive mechanism or a common treatment effect, and they do not apply to the baseline-only CGH cohort.

papers.title: GKB202 suppresses malignant phenotypes of circulating tumor cells in non-small cell lung cancer by modulating adaptive oxidative stress responses
papers.abstract: Antrodia cinnamomea is a Taiwan-endemic medicinal fungus with reported anti-inflammatory and anticancer activities. Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) contribute to metastasis and therapy resistance in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This study investigated whether stress-adaptive programs supporting CTC survival can be pharmacologically disrupted by GKB202, a purified derivative of A. cinnamomea. Patient-derived NSCLC CTCs were isolated and treated with GKB202 followed by RNA sequencing. Differential expression, pathway enrichment, and rank-rank hypergeometric overlap (RRHO) analyses were performed using a public NSCLC bone metastasis dataset (GSE175601). Functional assays in A549 cells assessed proliferation, migration, and invasion. MT1E protein expression was examined by Western blotting, and metabolomic profiling was conducted using UPLC-QTOF/MS. Untreated CTCs showed enrichment of migration- and lipid metabolism-related programs, whereas GKB202 treatment was associated with enrichment of stress-adaptive and detoxification pathways. Metallothionein-1E (MT1E) expression increased following GKB202 treatment. GKB202 reduced CTC viability and its combination with cisplatin produced a greater reduction in viability than either treatment alone in patient-derived CTC cultures. In A549 cells, GKB202 reduced proliferation and migration, accompanied with time-dependent changes in MT1E protein expression. Exploratory metabolomic profiling showed alterations in lipid-associated metabolic pathways consistent with stress-responsive regulation. These findings suggest that GKB202 is associated with changes in stress-adaptive molecular and metabolic programs in NSCLC models, together with reductions in selected malignant phenotypes and modulation of MT1E-associated responses. By potentially modulating compensatory stress responses in CTCs, GKB202 may increase their vulnerability to therapeutic stress, a possibility that warrants further investigation in the context of CTC-associated metastatic progression in NSCLC.

papers.title: Association between ultrasonographic diaphragm thickness and pulmonary function in children with pectus excavatum
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between ultrasonographic diaphragm thickness and pulmonary function in children with pectus excavatum compared with healthy controls. In this prospective study, 32 children with pectus excavatum and 29 healthy controls were included. Diaphragm thickness was measured ultrasonographically at functional residual capacity (FRC) and total lung capacity (TLC). Spirometry assessed forced vital capacity (FVC), forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1), and FEV1/FVC ratio. Correlations between diaphragm thickness and spirometric parameters were analyzed using Pearson’s test, with significance set at p < 0.05. In the pectus group, inspiratory diaphragm thickness at TLC showed a modest positive correlation with FVC % predicted (r = 0.421, p = 0.016), while no correlation in the controls (r = 0.070, p = 0.719). In the pectus group, inspiratory diaphragm thickness at TLC showed a modest positive correlation with FEV1 % predicted (r = 0.421, p = 0.016), whereas no significant correlation between these parameters was observed in controls (r = 0.070, p = 0.719). Mean expiratory thickness at FRC was 1.60 ± 0.38 mm versus 1.64 ± 0.47 mm, respectively (p = 0.709). Regarding spirometric values, mean FVC % predicted was 82.62 ± 9.00 vs. 87.10 ± 10.58 (p = 0.079), mean FEV1 % predicted was 83.31 ± 11.16 vs. 88.72 ± 11.64 (p = 0.069), and mean FEV1/FVC ratio was 88.28 ± 8.52 versus 91.34 ± 6.42, respectively (p = 0.121). Inspiratory diaphragm thickness at TLC showed a modest positive association with FEV1 % predicted in children with pectus excavatum. Given the cross-sectional design, small sample size, and multiple exploratory comparisons, this finding requires confirmation in larger studies. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06392984 (Registration Date [01052024]).

papers.title: Deep learning-based computer-aided detection of cerebral microbleeds achieves high sensitivity with a low false-positive rate in a confirmatory clinical trial
papers.abstract: Cerebral microbleeds (CMBs) are small, focal brain lesions recognized as critical biomarkers of cerebrovascular disease and cognitive decline. Despite advances in MRI technology, detecting CMBs remains challenging, highlighting the need for automated tools. This study aimed to evaluate the standalone performance of Neurophet SCALE MRI for automated CMB detection. The model was trained on 201 SWI and phase examinations. Neurophet SCALE MRI employs a two-stage deep learning pipeline with preprocessing steps, including reorientation, resampling, and data augmentation. In the first stage, CMB candidates are generated using a multiscale backbone and bidirectional convolutional Long Short-Term Memory. The second stage reduces false positives through a Squeeze-and-Excitation ResNet-based classifier and brain tissue segmentation. In this retrospective, single-center clinical trial, the model was tested on 457 MRI examinations. The primary endpoints were lesion-wise sensitivity (> 85.7%) and false positive rate (< 2.35 per patient). In addition, patient-wise and group-wise analyses were conducted. A total of 456 participants (224 CMB-positive, 232 CMB-negative) with 515 CMB lesions were included for the statistical analysis. The device exceeded all predefined performance criteria, demonstrating a lesion-wise sensitivity of 88.35% (95% CI: 86.61–90.17) and a false positive rate of 0.95 per patient (95% CI: 0.83–1.07). Patient-wise sensitivity and specificity were 1.0 (95% CI: 0.98–1.0) and 0.86 (95% CI: 0.81–0.90), respectively. For group-wise classification (0–4 vs. ≥5 CMBs), sensitivity and specificity were 0.91 (95% CI: 0.88–0.93) and 0.95 (95% CI: 0.74–1.0). Neurophet SCALE MRI demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity along with a low false-positive rate, supporting its potential clinical utility. Further validation by expert readers in a broader population is warranted.

papers.title: Detection and classification of failed fiber reinforced polymer composite samples under mechanical loading using YOLO11 on microscopic SEM images
papers.abstract: The fracture surfaces of fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites have multiple scale failure features that are hard to interpret manually by scanning electron microscope (SEM) and are slow to conduct. The fracture surfaces of FRP composites have multiple scale failure features that are hard to interpret manually by scanning electron microscope (SEM) and slow to conduct. This proof-of-concept study compares an anchor-free single-stage detector, YOLO11n, to localize and classify six fractographic features: fiber breakage, fiber pull-out, fiber–matrix debonding, delamination, voids and matrix debris, in SEM images of carbon- and glass-fiber/epoxy specimens failed in tension, three-point bending and short-beam shear. The data consists of 125 images with 37 specimens, with 1318 labelled boxes following written labelling criteria. The weights for the model were initialized from COCO and were updated using the Adam optimizer. YOLO11n was able to obtain mAP@0.5 = 0.821 with 6.5 ms per image on a preliminary image-level split, but the number of images per subset is not consistent with 125 images and the results may be optimistic due to the fact that images from one specimen can be split into multiple subsets. Multiple seeds, a controlled comparison between it and YOLOv5n, YOLOv8n and YOLOv9t, per-class ablations and an error analysis were performed at the level of the specimen and the groups. The study shows that it is possible to apply the method of detector-assisted laboratory fractography. It does not provide any structural-health-monitoring or safety-critical capability, and is not tested on other material systems or imaging conditions.

papers.title: The joint association of glycated haemoglobin and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol with type 2 diabetic neuropathy
papers.abstract: Neuropathy is highly prevalent and has a poor prognosis in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) patients. T2DM is accompanied by abnormal glucose and lipid metabolism. Glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) is a risk factor with a limited regulatory role. The role of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) also remains unclear. Here, we analysed the effects of HbA1c and LDL-C on type 2 diabetic neuropathy. Patients with T2DM with no baseline neuropathy were selected from the UK Biobank (UKB) database; 1,484 patients were enrolled based on a 12-year follow-up period. Patients were grouped according to their HbA1c levels(< 7%, 7–9%, and ≥ 9%) and their LDL-C levels (< 2.6 mmol/L and ≥ 2.6 mmol/L). Cox regression analysis revealed associations between HbA1c and LDL-C levels and the risk of type 2 diabetic neuropathy. Next, logistic regression was performed using clinical data from 611 patients with T2DM. We also analysed the interaction between LDL-C and HbA1c. After adjustment for confounding factors, compared with HbA1c < 7%, both HbA1c 7–9% and ≥ 9% were associated with an increased risk of type 2 diabetic neuropathy [HR = 1.62 (1.31–2.01); P < 0.001; HR = 2.44 (1.76–3.38); P < 0.001] in the UKB; compared with LDL-C < 2.6 mmol/L, LDL-C ≥ 2.6 mmol/L did not increase the risk of type 2 diabetic neuropathy [HR = 1.06(0.81–1.40); P = 0.675]. Compared with LDL-C ≥ 2.6 mmol/L combined with HbA1c < 7%, LDL-C ≥ 2.6 mmol/L combined with HbA1c ≥ 9% increased the risk of type 2 diabetic neuropathy [HR = 2.80 (1.76–4.48); P < 0.001]. Consistent findings were observed in the logistic regression analysis of clinical data and in sex-stratified analyses. HbA1c is an independent risk factor for neuropathy in patients with T2DM. LDL-C is not associated with type 2 diabetic neuropathy. However, in the context of suboptimal LDL-C control, extremely poor HbA1c control is closely associated with diabetic neuropathy than well controlled HbA1c.

papers.title: Salt chemistry regulates liquid environments and microsphere distribution in brinicles
papers.abstract: Brinicles are dynamic ice structures that have been proposed as chemically active systems on Ocean Worlds, potentially serving as habitable niches for life. However, experimental studies of their internal microstructures and implications for habitability remain limited. This study examined how brine composition influences the formation of liquid habitats within brinicles and how differences in liquid fraction distribution impact the transport and location of fluorescent microspheres representing cellular proxies. Flow cytometry and cryo-Raman spectroscopy were used to quantify the spatial distribution of cellular proxies, liquid brine, and hydrated salts across the radial and vertical axes of brinicles grown under two salt compositions (NaCl and CaCl2). Our findings demonstrate fundamental differences in brinicle microstructure between the two salt compositions. CaCl2 grown brinicles exhibited confined localization of liquid brine towards the inner channel, whereas NaCl brinicles showed a more homogeneous distribution of the liquid fraction.​ Ultimately, these differences in liquid fraction and microstructure provide a physical mechanism for cellular surrogate localization in the ice. CaCl2 brinicles resulted in the entrapment of microspheres near the brine channel while the NaCl brinicles produced uniform distribution of microspheres throughout the ice. These results demonstrate that brine chemistry can control habitat structure and the entrapment of cellular proxies within brinicles, highlighting the importance of ocean composition when assessing habitability on Ocean Worlds.

papers.title: Social jetlag, sleep duration and clinically significant fatigue among Chinese college students from health-related majors
papers.abstract: Evidence on the relationship between social jetlag (SJL) and fatigue is limited among college students from health-related majors. This study aimed to examine the association between SJL and clinically significant fatigue among Chinese college students from health-related majors and assess the extent to which sleep duration mediates this association. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 1764 Chinese college students from 10 health-related majors. Fatigue was assessed using the shortened fatigue questionnaire, with scores ≥ 18 indicating clinically significant fatigue. SJL was calculated as the absolute difference between mid-sleep on weekdays and weekends. Logistic regression and restricted cubic spline were used to assess the relationship between SJL and fatigue. Mediation analysis was used to explore the potential mediating role of sleep duration. Among participants, 8.3% met criteria for clinically significant fatigue. A non-linear association between SJL and fatigue was observed, with odds of fatigue increasing sharply when SJL exceeded 1.1 h. In the fully adjusted model, participants with higher SJL (≥ 1.1 h) had elevated odds of fatigue (OR = 1.51, 95%CI: 1.05–2.17). Similar results were found using literature-based SJL categories, with the highest risk in those with SJL > 2 h (OR = 2.01, 95%CI: 1.24–3.27). Subgroup analyses showed that elevated SJL was associated with higher odds of fatigue among females and freshmen, although no significant interactions were observed between SJL and sex or academic grade. Exploratory mediation analysis suggested that sleep duration may partially account for the observed association between SJL and fatigue ( -18.1% of the total effect). Higher SJL was associated with greater odds of clinically significant fatigue among Chinese college students from health-related majors. Sleep duration may play a potential mediating role in this association. Further longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationships and underlying mechanisms.

papers.title: Industrially promising probiotic candidates, Lacticaseibacillus paracasei strains from artisanal fermented camel milk, with no detected antibiotic-resistance genes
papers.abstract: Antibiotic resistance (AR) in industrial strains of lactic acid bacteria (LAB) poses a critical safety concern, as these microorganisms can serve as reservoirs and vectors for AR within the food chain. LAB isolates obtained from human or animal samples may harbor AR genes as a result of selective pressure from antibiotics. Traditional products derived from pasture-raised animals that do not receive feed additives serve as a possible source of AR-free LAB. We isolated six strains of Lacticaseibacillus paracasei from shubat — a traditional Asian fermented camel milk beverage, obtained from free-grazing camels in the high-altitude pastures of the Altai Mountains — and evaluated their probiotic potential, antimicrobial features and some technological characteristics. Whole-genome sequencing did not reveal any known AR genes in novel LAB. The strains exhibited variable tolerance to gastrointestinal stressors in vitro, grew in the presence of up to 6–8% NaCl, and efficiently fermented milk, reaching final counts of ≥ 10⁶–10⁹ CFU/mL, supporting their technological suitability as potential starter or adjunct cultures. Several biosynthetic gene clusters encoding putative secondary metabolites, including bacteriocins, were identified, suggesting the potential for bacteriocin production. The strains also exhibited in vitro antagonistic activity against the tested pathogenic and opportunistic bacteria, supporting their further evaluation as probiotic candidates.

papers.title: Optimization of gum arabic powder content in Kenaf fiber-reinforced epoxy hybrid composites for enhanced mechanical, thermal, dielectric, and moisture-related performance
papers.abstract: The use of sustainable multifunctional composites made from renewable sources is gaining momentum in the field of advanced engineering. A constant kenaf fiber content of 20 wt% was maintained, while gum Arabic powder loading was varied from 0 to 20 wt% (KEG0–KEG20) in the proposed in kenaf fiber-reinforced epoxy hybrid composites. The effects of gum Arabic incorporation on mechanical, thermo-mechanical thermal dielectric, and moisture absorption properties were systematically investigated. The addition of fillers increased the composites’ performance and the effects were the highest at 15 wt%. The enhancement of mechanical properties may be attributed to the improved filler dispersion, improved interfacial interaction, improved stress-transfer conditions and lower microstructural defects in the composite. KEG15 composite demonstrated the best tensile strength of 55.3 MPa, Young’s modulus of 3.12 GPa, flexural strength of 88.9 MPa, flexural modulus of 4.48 GPa, impact strength of 28.6 kJ m⁻², Shore D hardness of 83.2, dielectric strength of 29.8 kV mm, storage modulus (~ 4500 MPa), glass transition temperatures of around 105 °C and residual char content of 23.7%. Despite the individual properties showed different responses to the gum Arabic powder loading, KEG15 was found to be the optimum formulation based on the highest overall multifunctional performance index representing the most balanced combination of the selected mechanical, thermo-mechanical, thermal, dielectric, and moisture-related properties. One-way ANOVA based on independent specimen level observations revealed statistically significant differences between the formulations (p < 0.001). FTIR and SEM observations supported the corresponding interfacial and morphological changes. This study has effectively combined the synergistic action of kenaf fiber and gum Arabic powder to make multifunctional epoxy composites with excellent mechanical, thermal, electrical insulation, and environmental durability properties being achieved. 15 wt% gum Arabic powder was the optimum filler level.

papers.title: Prevalence, awareness, treatment, and control of hypertension among older adults in China
papers.abstract: China contributes to approximately 20% of the global burden of hypertension; however, a nationwide epidemiological survey on the prevalence of hypertension among older adults is lacking. This study aimed to assess the prevalence, awareness, treatment, and control of hypertension among older adults in China. The data were derived from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) in 2015. We included 7,733 participants aged 60 years and older. The prevalence of hypertension was 53.1% (95% CI 51.7–54.6%), which is equivalent to 140 million adults aged 60 years or older with hypertension in China. Among the participants with hypertension, 74.1% (95% CI 72.5–75.8%) were aware of their condition, 54.5% (95% CI 52.5–56.5%) were treated, and only 33.7% (95% CI 31.8–35.6%) were controlled. Systolic blood pressure increased with age (r = 0.504, P < 0.001), whereas diastolic blood pressure decreased with age (r = − 0.175, P < 0.001). The prevalence of hypertension increased with age (P for trend < 0.001). The prevalence of hypertension was observed to be higher in urban areas (57.0%, 95% CI 53.7–60.3%) than in rural areas (51.2%, 95% CI 49.8–52.6%) (P = 0.002), along with the prevalence being higher in northern areas (56.8%, 95% CI 54.7–58.8%) than in southern areas (50.7%, 95% CI 48.8–52.7%) (P < 0.001). Spanning from the western provinces to the central provinces to the eastern areas, the prevalence of hypertension was 50.8% (95% CI 48.6–53.1%), 52.6% (95% CI 50.4–54.8%), and 55.6% (95% CI 52.7–58.5%) (P for trend < 0.001), respectively. Multivariable analysis revealed that older age (65–69 years group: OR = 1.292, 95% CI 1.105–1.512; 70–74 years group: OR = 1.482, 95% CI 1.235–1.779; 75–79 years group: OR = 1.922, 95% CI 1.569–2.355; ≥ 80 years group: OR = 2.192, 95% CI 1.739–2.764), living in northern areas (OR = 1.197, 95% CI 1.054–1.360), drinking more than once a month (OR = 1.187, 95% CI 1.000–1.410), obesity (OR = 2.568, 95% CI 1.977–3.336), diabetes (OR = 1.694, 95% CI 1.443–1.989), and dyslipidaemia (OR = 1.378, 95% CI 1.218–1.559) were positively correlated with hypertension, whereas being married (or cohabitating) (OR = 0.772, 95% CI 0.668–0.892) was negatively correlated with hypertension. The prevalence of hypertension was high in people aged 60 years or older in China; however, the rates of control of hypertension remain low. Efforts are needed to prevent hypertension and improve the treatment and control of hypertension.

papers.title: RCE-YOLO: receptive-field attention and content-aware feature enhancement for aerospace transparent-component defect detection
papers.abstract: Aerospace transparent components are safety-critical optical structures whose surface integrity directly affects visual quality, environmental isolation and maintenance reliability. Single-image detection is particularly difficult when defects are weak, small or elongated and when reflections and illumination changes produce strong background responses. This study develops RCE-YOLO, a compact YOLOv11n-based detector organized around three staged operations: receptive-field-aware feature extraction, content-aware feature reconstruction and multi-scale feature recalibration. RFCBAMConv and C3k2_RFCBAMConv strengthen channel-selective and receptive-field spatial responses; CARAFE replaces fixed top-down interpolation with content-dependent feature reassembly; and efficient multi-scale attention (EMA) recalibrates the final P3, P4 and P5 features before prediction. Experiments use the Aircraft Glass Defect Dataset (AGDD) as a representative aerospace glazing benchmark. The 219 selected single-view source images are split into 197 training and 22 validation images before offline augmentation, yielding 1,379 training and 154 validation images under the current protocol. RCE-YOLO achieves 89.77% precision, 88.29% recall, 93.80% mAP@0.5, 77.27% mAP@0.75 and 71.60% mAP@0.5:0.95. Relative to YOLOv11n, mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.75 improve by 1.47 and 2.11 percentage points, respectively, with 2.80 M parameters and 7.40 GFLOPs. The eight-configuration ablation includes the three pairwise variants $$A+B$$, $$A+C$$ and $$B+C$$ (A = C3k2_RFCBAMConv, B = CARAFE, C = EMA). The $$A+B$$ configuration attains the highest mAP@0.5 (93.96%) and mAP@0.5:0.95 (73.53%), whereas the full $$A+B+C$$ model yields the highest mAP@0.75 (77.27%). Pairwise interaction contrasts are 0.00 percentage points at the reported precision for these three mAP metrics; the three-way contrast varies by metric. These point estimates do not demonstrate reproducible synergy or establish that all three stages are necessary. At the class level, contusion AP@0.5:0.95 declines by 3.44 percentage points despite a 0.42-point gain at IoU 0.5; the full model therefore does not improve every defect class or IoU criterion. All performance figures are single-run point estimates, without multi-seed standard deviations, confidence intervals or significance tests. Because the 154 augmented validation images originate from only 22 source images, the small numerical differences must not be interpreted as statistically established improvements. No independent external dataset or untouched real-image test set was evaluated; therefore cross-material and cross-acquisition generalization remains unverified.

papers.title: Development of an anti-GM1 antibody-specific glycomimetic for Guillain-Barré syndrome and multifocal motor neuropathy
papers.abstract: Multifocal motor neuropathy (MMN) is a chronic autoimmune neuropathy predominately affecting motor neurons, caused by IgM antibodies that target the ganglioside GM1. These pathogenic autoantibodies trigger complement-mediated nodal disruption and axonal injury at paranodes and neuromuscular junctions. Similar anti-GM1 antibodies also drive acute forms of peripheral neuropathy, such as Guillain-Barré-Syndrome (GBS), in which molecular mimicry following infection induces cross-reactive immune responses. Antibodies generated against microbial GM1-like glycans bind endogenous GM1, leading to severe neurological symptoms which requires intensive care. Current therapies, such as plasmapheresis and intravenous immunoglobulins (IVIG), can be effective, however, they lack selectivity and can cause adverse effects. We hypothesize that selective depletion of autoreactive anti-GM1 antibodies could provide a targeted therapeutic strategy. This antibody removal can be achieved through multivalent presentation of carbohydrate mimetics of pentasaccharide on a biodegradable poly-l-lysine scaffold. Here we report the development of a lead compound that successfully inhibits binding of anti-GM1 antibodies from patients’ sera to GM1 and effectively prevents binding of anti-GM1 antibodies on terminal axonal networks in vitro and ex vivo.

papers.title: From media to meals: intergenerational transmission of food-based media literacy and its association with food security in Iran
papers.abstract: Food insecurity remains a major global challenge, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. In this context, food-based media literacy has emerged as an important skill that enables individuals and families to critically evaluate food-related media messages and make healthier dietary decisions. This study examined the intergenerational dynamics of food-based media literacy and its associations with food choices, dietary habits, and household food insecurity among Iranian families. Using a cross-sectional parent–young adult dyadic model, data was collected from 250 dyads (n = 500) and analyzed using Dyadic PLS-SEM. The findings showed that food-based media literacy operates as a shared family resource rather than an individual competency. Both parents and young adults significantly influenced each other’s food choices and dietary habits, highlighting the importance of intergenerational dialogue. Critical thinking, self-efficacy, and food heritage preservation emerged as significant predictors of healthier dietary behaviors. Food choices and dietary habits also mediated the relationship between media literacy constructs and household food insecurity. Higher levels of food-based media literacy were associated with lower food insecurity, particularly through healthier dietary practices. Young adults’ constructs showed stronger overall associations than those of parents, emphasizing the importance of youth empowerment in strengthening household food security. The findings suggest that family-centered interventions promoting critical thinking, self-efficacy, and cultural food heritage may contribute to reducing food insecurity and improving dietary resilience.

papers.title: Severity-stratified peripheral immune response and interleukin-6 dynamics in severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome
papers.abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), caused by Dabie bandavirus, carries a case fatality rate of 12–30%. In a retrospective cohort of 120 SFTS patients (4 asymptomatic, 70 mild, 26 moderate, 20 severe), 17 (14.2%) had critical illness, of whom 11 died in-hospital (9.2%). Admission interleukin-6 (IL-6) rose across severity grades (mild 9.1, moderate 12.6, severe 61.4 pg/mL; p < 0.001) and was higher in critical illness than non-critical illness (99.4 vs. 10.0 pg/mL; p < 0.001). Critical illness patients had lower initial CD4 + T-cell counts (167 vs. 420 cells/µL; n = 63; p = 0.036) and a lower one-week CD4/CD8 ratio (0.5 vs. 1.6; n = 24; p = 0.0004). Initial viral load was higher in critical illness (143,948 vs. 40,059 copies/mL; p = 0.047) but not at one week (p = 0.167), suggesting that initial viral burden, rather than delayed clearance, is associated with critical illness. Mixed-effects models showed different lymphocyte-fraction and platelet trajectories by outcome. Admission IL-6 (cutoff 18.9 pg/mL) discriminated severe disease (AUC 0.890; cross-validated) and improved an exploratory multivariable model (p = 0.004), although its adjusted odds ratio was not significant (p = 0.22). These confirmatory findings are integrated into a two-axis model that is hypothesis-generating pending external validation.

papers.title: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy across acute and post-acute phases after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a multi-cohort randomized controlled pilot study (HOT-RESUS 1)
papers.abstract: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains untested in humans despite promising preclinical evidence. We thus evaluated feasibility, tolerability, observed treatment-related adverse events, and early biological signals of HBOT across three distinct clinical cohorts and exposure subgroups. This prospective, single-centre, randomized, controlled, open-label pilot study enrolled (i) Intensive Care Unit (ICU) patients with sustained return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) within the preceding 24 h, (ii) long-term OHCA survivors, and (iii) healthy volunteers. Within each cohort, participants were randomized to no HBOT, one HBOT session, or five HBOT sessions. Assessments included serial laboratory biomarkers, vascular function, neurocognitive testing, and patient-reported outcomes. Analyses were primarily descriptive, with additional between-group comparisons considered exploratory. The prespecified recruitment target was achieved (45/45 participants), all assigned HBOT sessions were completed (90/90; 100%), and all scheduled blood samples were obtained. No HBOT-related adverse events occurred. In ICU patients, serial biomarkers demonstrated pronounced temporal changes during the acute post-cardiac-arrest phase across inflammatory, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, neuronal injury, and myocardial injury domains, whereas direct comparison of trajectories between HBOT groups were generally inconclusive. In long-term OHCA survivors and healthy volunteers, exploratory analyses suggested reductions in arterial stiffness and, particularly among survivors, favourable changes in neurocognitive and patient-reported outcomes, with several favourable numerical patterns observed in HBOT-exposed groups. Given the small subgroup sizes, extensive multiplicity, and generally inconclusive direct between-group comparisons, these findings remain exploratory. HOT-RESUS 1 demonstrated that the prespecified recruitment and HBOT procedures could be completed as planned, including treatment of selected acute post-ROSC ICU patients in a specialised hyperbaric centre, with no HBOT-related adverse events observed. Exploratory analyses showed dynamics of inflammatory and oxidative stress markers, arterial stiffness, and neurocognitive and patient-reported outcomes, with several favourable numerical patterns observed in HBOT-exposed groups. Although the small pilot sample, extensive multiplicity, and largely inconclusive direct between-group comparisons preclude attribution of these changes to HBOT or conclusions regarding biological or clinical efficacy, the findings identify possible biological and functional outcomes for further investigation in adequately powered randomized trials.

papers.title: Application of Raman spectroscopy to the first actual fuel debris retrieved from the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station Unit 2
papers.abstract: Following the successful first trial retrieval of fuel debris from Unit 2 of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station (FDNPS), a Raman spectroscopic assessment was conducted to investigate the chemical states of the debris. The powdered fuel debris sample, prepared via a vibratory mill, was analyzed using micro-Raman spectroscopy and was compared with simulated debris synthesized under controlled conditions. The average Raman spectrum revealed characteristic bands corresponding to tetragonal ZrO₂, spinel-type oxides originating from stainless-steel structural components, and a cubic (U, Zr)O₂ solid solution. The Raman spectrum of the retrieved fuel debris differed significantly from that of uranium-containing particles (UP1) previously sampled from stagnant water at torus room of Unit 2 of the FDNPS, indicating that further sampling and analysis are required to fully understand the overall chemical complexity of the fuel debris. Raman spectroscopy proved effective for identifying oxidative products in the fuel debris, requiring only minimal sample amounts and no vacuum or coating pretreatments. This study highlights the method’s potential as a valuable tool in nuclear decommissioning efforts, especially for the characterization of uranium bearing compounds in fuel debris.

papers.title: Decoding MMP9 allosteric inhibition by ​​ Ocimum sanctum bioactives via network pharmacology and molecular dynamics for treating diabetic foot ulcers
papers.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFU) represent a global health crisis characterized by chronic inflammation and a failure to transition into the proliferative phase of wound healing. This delay is mostly caused by the abnormal overexpression of matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9), leading to indiscriminate destruction of the extracellular matrix (ECM) and essential growth factors. Conventional orthosteric inhibitors often fail due to lack of specificity and dose-limiting toxicities. This study aims to identify potential allosteric inhibitors of MMP-9 derived from Ocimum sanctum using a systemic computational framework. We employed an integrated approach combining GC–MS profiling and database mining of O. sanctum phytocompounds with transcriptomic analysis of the GSE199939 dataset. Network pharmacology was used to identify hub genes and shared targets between O. sanctum and DFU. High-precision molecular docking and 100 ns multivariate molecular dynamics (MD) simulations including RMSD, RMSF, radius of gyration (Rg), and SASA were performed to evaluate the stability of the phytocompound binding at the allosteric hemopexin-like (PEX) domain of MMP-9. Binding free energies were quantified using MM/GBSA calculations. GC–MS and database mining collectively identified 19 lead bioactive compounds with favourable ADME/drug-likeness profiles, including retinal and eugenol. Transcriptomic integration revealed 11,570 DFU-associated genes, with 52 common targets shared with O. sanctum. MMP-9 was identified as a critical structural hub (degree = 29) within the interactome, closely linked to inflammatory nodes like STAT3 and BCL2. MD simulations and FEL analysis confirmed that O. sanctum bioactives establish stable and energetically favourable interactions within the MMP-9 allosteric PEX domain. This study highlights the potential of the O. sanctum-derived phytocompounds as selective allosteric modulators of MMP-9, offering a focused, multi-target, multi-pathway approach to restore the wound microenvironment and presenting a cost-effective and safe therapeutic solution for chronic diabetic wound management.

papers.title: Association between social determinants of health, lifestyle behaviors, and health outcomes in Saudi Arabia: An exploratory cross-sectional online survey study
papers.abstract: Social determinants of health (SDH) and lifestyle factors significantly influence chronic disease burden and healthcare access. We conducted a cross-sectional online survey of 411 adults residing in Saudi Arabia (January–April 2024) to examine associations between SDH (education, income, financial strain), lifestyle behaviors (diet, physical activity, smoking), chronic conditions, and healthcare access. The sample (mean age 29.4 ± 11.2 years, 60.1% female, 38.2% Saudi nationals) showed prevalences of obesity (10.2%), asthma (7.5%), diabetes (7.1%), hypertension (6.6%), and dyslipidemia (6.1%). In adjusted models, age (β = 0.21, partial η²=0.042, p < 0.001) and financial strain (β = 0.14, partial η²=0.018, p < 0.01) were statistically associated with multimorbidity (associational findings; causal inferences cannot be drawn). Food insecurity was associated with higher chronic disease burden (OR = 1.45, 95% CI 1.12–1.88), while higher education was associated with increased healthcare access (OR = 1.67, 95% CI 1.23–2.27). Financial hardship was associated with reduced healthcare access odds (OR = 0.61, 95% CI 0.42–0.88). In this exploratory sample of adults residing in Saudi Arabia (predominantly young, female, and non-Saudi nationals), socioeconomic factors and lifestyle behaviors were associated with health outcomes and healthcare access. Financial strain and food insecurity showed unfavorable associations (higher chronic disease burden), while higher education showed favorable associations (better healthcare access). Addressing financial strain and promoting education may help reduce chronic disease burden and improve healthcare equity; however, given the cross-sectional design and sample limitations, causal inferences cannot be drawn, and findings should be considered hypothesis-generating.

papers.title: Traumatic PVR prevention and treatment via composite drug film
papers.abstract: This study aimed to develop a composite sustained-release drug film by incorporating triamcinolone acetonide (TA) and daunorubicin (DNR) into a poly-L-lactide caprolactone (P(LLA-CL)) matrix, and to evaluate its in vitro release characteristics, in vivo biocompatibility, and therapeutic efficacy in the treatment of traumatic proliferative vitreoretinopathy (TPVR). P(LLA-CL) was dissolved in hexafluoroisopropanol, weighed TA and DNR powder, and added it to the P(LLA-CL) solution, and then electrospinning was performed on these materials to prepare P(LLA-CL)-TA, P(LLA-CL)-DNR, and P(LLA-CL)-TA-DNR composite drug films. In vitro release experiments were performed on drug films (4 × 8 mm) and corresponding drug powders placed in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS). At fixed time points, samples were collected and drug content was calculated by HPLC to record the cumulative drug release curve. The in vivo safety of the drug films was evaluated by suturing the drug films onto the rabbit eyes sclera, 5 mm away from the limbus, and then observing slit-lamp biomicroscopy, intraocular pressure (IOP), and histopathological changes at fixed time points from 1 week to 6 months after suturing. TPVR was constructed by scleral injury and autologous blood injection, and the rabbits were randomly divided into model, control, P(LLA-CL)-TA, P(LLA-CL)-DNR, and composite drug film groups. The observation indices were fundus photography, HE staining, and immunohistochemistry (IHC) analysis of inflammatory factors TNF-α and TGF-β. In vitro release experiment results showed that the P(LLA-CL)-TA and P(LLA-CL)-DNR drug films released the drugs for 156 and 135 days, and the cumulative drug release rates reached 88.41% and 92.68%, respectively. The composite P(LLA-CL)-TA-DNR drug film released TA and DNR for 141 days (91.54%) and 129 days (89.31%) respectively, which were greatly prolonged compared with the release time of the drugs powders (48 days and 4 days for TA and DNR, respectively). In vivo experiment results showed that no ocular toxicity or IOP elevation was induced by the drug films. The gradual degradation of drug films was observed during the six-month observation period. In therapeutic application, the composite drug film reduced the retinal folding, preretinal membrane formation and TNF-α mean optical density at 2 weeks [(0.426 ± 0.036) vs. (0.518 ± 0.043) in the model group, P < 0.0001] and at 4 weeks [(0.460 ± 0.040) vs. (0.537 ± 0.029), P = 0.0003], and improved the vitreous hemorrhage (P = 0.0402). P(LLA-CL)-TA-DNR composite drug film can achieve sustained release of therapeutic agents for up to five months. The drug film exhibits a good safety profile, and showed preliminary therapeutic potential to attenuate TPVR progression via suppressing inflammatory response and cellular proliferation. Compared with single-drug films, the composite film showed marginal improvement of vitreous hemorrhage absorption and reduced retinal proliferation.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal analysis and machine learning prediction of road traffic crash hotspots: a case of Amhara region, Ethiopia
papers.abstract: Road traffic crashes remain a major public health and development challenge in Ethiopia. While previous studies in the Amhara region have examined crash trends, contributing factors, or specific road corridors, there is limited evidence on spatiotemporal hotspots and on predicting population-adjusted crash rates. This study aimed to investigate the spatial and temporal distribution of road traffic crashes in the Amhara region and to build machine learning models to estimate crash rates across administrative zones. The dataset comprised police-reported crash records from 2013 to 2022 along with spatial, demographic, traffic exposure, and school-related variables. Spatial clustering was assessed using the Getis-Ord Gi* statistic. Machine learning approaches were evaluated using repeated five-fold cross-validation. The North Shewa zone consistently emerged as a statistically significant cluster of reported crash burden, and the East Gojam zone appeared as an emerging hotspot during the later years of the study period. Of the models evaluated, Random Forest achieved the strongest cross-validated performance (RMSE = 0.866 ± 0.205; R2 = 0.678 ± 0.266). The GIS and machine learning findings are complementary: GIS identifies geographic clustering of reported crashes, whereas machine learning estimates population-normalized crash rates. These results can support regional road safety planning by helping prioritize zones for enhanced monitoring, enforcement strategies, data quality improvements, and targeted corridor-level assessment. Future work should incorporate geocoded crash records and road segment-level data to enable the design of site-specific interventions.

papers.title: Environmental DNA captures ecological communities' dynamics along natural and anthropogenic gradients in a mediterranean lagoon ecosystem
papers.abstract: Mediterranean lagoons are vital ecosystems that provide essential services such as water filtration, carbon sequestration, and habitat support. Despite their high ecological and socio-economic value, transitional waters naturally experience strong environmental variability, including atmospheric phenomena like sea level rise and temperature fluctuations, and are vulnerable to human pressures such as invasive species, pollution, and human activities, emphasising the need for effective conservation strategies. In this study, we employed multiple marker genes and eDNA metabarcoding to characterise the micro-eukaryotic and zoobenthic community structure of lagoon ecosystems and to assess its variation in relation to natural and anthropogenic gradients. Our research focused on a large Albanian lagoon, which, like other Mediterranean lagoon systems, plays a significant role in mitigating climate change. Given the importance of effective management and conservation strategies for these ecosystems, our findings highlight the potential of eDNA metabarcoding as an innovative tool for monitoring biodiversity and informing sustainable practices in Mediterranean lagoon environments. Furthermore, this study demonstrated that analysis through eDNA, simultaneously investigating multiple marker genes and targeting benthic and micro-eukaryotic communities, indirectly highlights the potential influence of an urbanised area on their structure, opening up possibilities for the use of this approach in monitoring and prevention activities.

papers.title: Alzheimer’s disease fMRI image classification and hippocampal region detection using faster R-CNN deep learning algorithm
papers.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is characterized by early hippocampal degeneration and microvascular alterations preceding overt neocortical atrophy. Accessible, automated, and interpretable screening from non-invasive neuroimaging remains a clinical challenge. To develop and benchmark a multi-task Faster R-CNN framework for simultaneous AD classification and bilateral hippocampal localization on resting-state fMRI. This retrospective study analyzed 200 participants (100 AD, 100 cognitively normal [CN]) from institutional and public (ADNI, OASIS-3) cohorts. The cohort was partitioned at the participant level into training (70%, n = 140), validation (15%, n = 30), and held-out test (15%, n = 30; 15 AD, 15 CN) sets. Crucially, to preserve steady-state T2* susceptibility contrast and structural hippocampal boundaries without zero-frequency signal loss, voxel-wise temporal-mean functional volumes were calculated from realigned and spatially normalized resting-state fMRI data prior to nuisance regression and band-pass filtering. ComBat harmonization was fitted exclusively on training data. Six contiguous axial slices spanning the bilateral hippocampi (1,200 slices total; 2,400 expert-adjudicated bounding boxes) were extracted. A multi-task Faster R-CNN with ResNet-50 backbone was trained under a unified loss combining proposal regression, objectness, and a dual-hippocampal disease classification head. Subject diagnosis was determined via probability averaging across slices. On the independent held-out test cohort (N = 30), the model achieved 93.3% accuracy (28/30; 95% CI 78.7–98.2%), 93.3% sensitivity (14/15; 95% CI 70.2–98.8%), 93.3% specificity (14/15; 95% CI 70.2–98.8%), and an AUC of 0.95 (95% CI 0.87–0.99). In exploratory subgroup evaluations, test accuracy was 91.3% in mild AD (n = 8 AD, n = 15 CN; 95% CI 72.0–98.9%) and 95.5% in moderate AD (n = 7 AD, n = 15 CN; 95% CI 77.2–99.9%). Accounting for within-subject clustering across the 360 test bounding boxes, a Linear Mixed-Effects Model confirmed that hippocampal localization significantly surpassed fixed Harvard–Oxford atlas templates (IoU 0.87 ± 0.04 vs. 0.72 ± 0.06; beta = + 0.155, SE = 0.0034, Wald z = 45.18, p < 0.001; subject-level paired t(29) = 45.15, p < 0.001). On non-hippocampal axial slices (n = 60), the detector yielded 59 true negatives and 1 false positive, demonstrating 98.3% slice specificity (95% CI 91.1–99.7%). The framework surpassed baseline CNN (80.0%, p = 0.046), SVM (76.7%, p = 0.031), and Random Forest (76.7%, p = 0.031) classifiers. The multi-task Faster R-CNN provides accurate AD classification and interpretable hippocampal detection on temporal-mean resting-state fMRI, demonstrating encouraging preliminary feasibility for automated computer-aided screening. However, given the broad confidence intervals inherent to the small independent test sample (N = 30), prospective validation in larger, multi-center prodromal cohorts is required prior to clinical translation.

papers.title: BALANCE-ST: distilling deep reinforcement learning policies into PLC logic for multi-VFD load balancing
papers.abstract: Industrial multi-VFD load balancing on programmable logic controllers (PLCs) requires control policies that are accurate, transparent, and fast enough for deterministic scan cycles. Deep reinforcement learning can learn effective balancing strategies, but neural policies are difficult to inspect and deploy as IEC 61131-3 Structured Text (ST). We propose BALANCE-ST, a simulation-to-PLC pipeline that trains a deep Q-network (DQN) teacher, distils it into a depth-2 decision tree selected by held-out validation parsimony, renders the tree as PLC-oriented ST, and wraps the resulting policy with a deterministic guard enforcing command-bound, ramp-rate, dwell-time, and overload checks. In an in-distribution post-training evaluation across eight demand families and ten seeds, BALANCE-ST achieves mean load-imbalance coefficient of variation 0.0697 versus 0.0696 for the ten-teacher DQN aggregate, while reducing imbalance by $$34.4\%$$, $$52.6\%$$, and $$15.0\%$$ relative to equal-share, threshold-staging, and PI baselines, respectively. On the interquartile mean, the reduction versus threshold staging is $$43.2\%$$. A guard ablation and hard-stress evaluation show that the runtime guard reduces realised violations at the cost of higher imbalance under actuator dropout. Compared with beam-search model predictive control, BALANCE-ST yields higher imbalance but much lower online decision cost and a compact policy with four leaves and three effective actions. These results support BALANCE-ST as a practical trade-off between control performance, inspectability, and deployment-oriented simplicity for PLC-based multi-VFD control.

papers.title: Cortical activation during hand grasping in Parkinson’s disease with different motor onset sides: an fNIRS study
papers.abstract: Motor symptom asymmetry is a key feature of Parkinson’s disease (PD), but how onset side affects cortical activation during motor tasks remains unclear. This study used functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) to investigate cortical activation and task-related lateralization during hand grasping in left-onset PD (LPD, n = 29), right-onset PD (RPD, n = 35), and healthy controls (HC, n = 14). During the left-hand task, both PD groups showed lower mean ΔHbO in the right primary somatosensory cortex than HC (LPD vs. HC: pFDR = 0.027; RPD vs. HC: pFDR = 0.022), with altered peak timing in the right frontal eye field (pFDR = 0.004 and 0.011). During the right-hand task, the RPD group showed lower activation in the right somatosensory association cortex (vs. HC pFDR = 0.039; vs. LPD pFDR = 0.024) and reduced peak activation (pFDR = 0.021), with shortened full width at half maximum in bilateral S1, M1, and SMA (all pFDR < 0.05). Lateralization analysis showed reversed task-related lateralization in the right primary somatosensory cortex in LPD (deltapeak: pFDR = 0.047) and altered task-related lateralization of timing in the right frontal eye field in both PD groups (pFDR = 0.034).
