In an exploratory analysis, longer disease duration was associated with shorter R-SAC time-to-peak in RPD but not LPD (p = 1.1 × 10⁻⁵, q = 2.4 × 10⁻³ globally). Motor onset side is associated with distinct sensorimotor cortical dysfunction, with RPD showing more widespread deficits, whereas delayed FEF timing is a shared alteration independent of onset side. Temporal-domain metrics were more consistently affected than amplitude-based measures and may capture cortical changes missed by intensity indices.

papers.title: Molecular epidemiology of tuberculosis in Tétouan, Morocco: insights into strain diversity and genetic clustering
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major public health challenge in Morocco. We investigated the diversity, lineage distribution, and clustering of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) isolates from pulmonary TB patients in Tétouan (2020–2023). In a prospective cross-sectional study, 103 MTBC isolates were characterized using 24-locus MIRU-VNTR genotyping. Genetic diversity was assessed using the Hunter–Gaston discriminatory index, while UPGMA and minimum spanning tree analyses evaluated genetic relatedness. Associations between demographic characteristics and double-locus-variant clonal complex membership were assessed using binary logistic regression. The 24-locus scheme showed high discriminatory power (HGDI = 0.9896). Among genotyped isolates, LAM was predominant (29.1%), followed by Beijing (9.7%), Ghana (3.9%), S (2.9%), Haarlem (1.9%), West African 1 (1.9%), and West African 2 (1​%); 49.5% of isolates were unassigned. UPGMA identified five identical-profile clusters comprising 17 isolates (16.5%), corresponding to an estimated recent transmission rate of 11.6%. Ten double-locus-variant clonal complexes included 40 isolates (38.8%). Old Medina residence was independently associated with clonal complex membership (AOR = 6.020, 95% CI 2.158–16.683; p = 0.001). The findings indicate high MTBC diversity and substantial genotypic heterogeneity, with greater likelihood of clonal-complex membership in a socioeconomically vulnerable urban area. Whole-genome sequencing and broader epidemiological sampling are needed to resolve transmission pathways and clarify the significance of genetically related isolates.

papers.title: Computational exploration of Hemidesmus indicus phytochemicals targeting HSP90 in ovarian cancer through molecular docking, structural dynamics and free energy landscape
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer is a leading cause of death in all gynecological cancers, as recurrence, drug resistance, and limited therapeutic options remain critical clinical challenges despite advances. Heat Shock Protein 90 (HSP90) is a molecular chaperone and validated as an attractive therapeutic target in cancer drug discovery, as it supports many oncoproteins that act as critical regulators of the cell cycle, apoptosis, and signalling pathways. In this current study, a computational pipeline was used to evaluate bioactive phytochemicals from Hemidesmus indicus (L.) R. Br. ex-Schult as potential HSP90 inhibitors relevant to ovarian cancer. Among 87 phytochemicals screened, rutin, isoquercetin, and indicine were prioritized based on receptor-based molecular docking, exhibiting favorable docking scores of −14.99, −13.17, and −11.73 kcal/mol, respectively, compared with −5.07 kcal/mol for the reference HSP90 inhibitor geldanamycin. The corresponding MM-GBSA binding free energies were −80.93, −74.61, and −77.47 kcal/mol for rutin, isoquercetin, and indicine, respectively, compared with −80.02 kcal/mol for geldanamycin. In silico ADMET analysis predicted comparatively favorable pharmacokinetic characteristics for isoquercetin and indicine, whereas rutin showed predicted physicochemical limitations that may require further optimization. The stability of the HSP90-ligand complexes was investigated by performing 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations (MDS) with stable and persistent behavior in RMSD, RMSF, radius of gyration, and hydrogen bond parameters across the entire simulation trajectory. Principal component analysis (PCA)-based free energy landscape (FEL) mapping demonstrated well-defined low-energy conformational states, and MM-PBSA calculations affirmed strong interactions with active-site residues. Together, these in silico findings suggest that rutin, isoquercetin, and indicine may represent promising candidate HSP90-targeting compounds from H. indicus for further experimental validation to evaluate their anticancer potential. In vitro studies targeting HSP90 binding and ATPase activity together with ovarian cancer cell line testing, followed by in vivo experiments, are needed to confirm their therapeutic efficacy and anticancer effects.

papers.title: An integrated machining performance framework considering tool wear and hole integrity attributes during drilling via indexable drilling inserts using entropy-weights and TOPSIS
papers.abstract: Quantification of machinability is challenging, especially with the development of new materials like DC 53 steel and new tooling, such as the fabrication of indexable inserts. In this context, an integrated machining performance framework named the Integrated Hole Integrity Index (IHII) is proposed. An indexable drilling setup with peripheral wiper inserts and central stepped carbide inserts was employed. The drilling tests were conducted at 20 m/min and 30 m/min cutting speeds while employing feed rates of 0.05 mm/rev, 0.075 mm/rev, and 0.10 mm/rev to assess the effect of microstructure on tool wear, surface integrity, diametric error, machining temperature, and burr formation. The microstructural examination revealed that D2 steel contained large carbides that were not evenly distributed, but DC53 steel displayed a martensitic structure with small carbides that were evenly spaced. The D2 steel performed better than DC53 steel such that the minimum flank wear value of 49 μm was recorded when drilling the former material at 20 m/min and 0.05 mm/rev, with surface roughness values being in the range of 1.0–4.8 μm. However, tool wear was almost in the same vicinity, but roughness values were substantially higher, ranging from 1.9 to 5.4 μm with the latter material at the same machining parameters. The SEM analysis revealed that surface damage occurred through three main mechanisms, which included adhesion, material side flow, and plastic deformation. For a more holistic drilling performance assessment, an IHII model/performance metric is calculated using entropy weights and subsequently TOPSIS analysis was conducted to overcome the limitations of individual output responses. Hereafter, the best drilling condition is suggested, which indicates the best compromise among all output responses. A value of 0.743 for IHII was calculated for Test 4, performed on D2 material, showing a better performance index, while a 23% lower IHII was determined for DC53 steel.

papers.title: Rasch analysis of the physical activity questionnaire for children in Spain supports a candidate three-item short form
papers.abstract: The Physical Activity Questionnaire for Children (PAQ-C) is widely used to assess habitual physical activity in youth, although its psychometric properties have shown variability across cultural contexts. This study aimed to examine the internal structure and measurement properties of the PAQ-C in Spanish primary-school children using Rasch analysis, explore a candidate short-form version, and derive sample-based percentile thresholds for describing physical activity scores. A cross-sectional exploratory study was conducted involving 259 children aged 6–12 years from two schools in Navarra, Spain. Parents or guardians completed the questionnaire for children in Grades 1–3, whereas children in Grades 4–6 completed it themselves. Item-level analyses and Rasch modeling were used to examine response functioning, scale structure, reliability, and differential item functioning (DIF) by sex and school grade. The original nine-item PAQ-C showed significant overall Rasch model misfit, disordered response thresholds in several items, and evidence of multidimensionality. An exploratory three-item version comprising Items 7–9 demonstrated improved Rasch model fit (χ² = 12.76, df = 9, p = 0.173), ordered thresholds, and acceptable person separation reliability (PSI = 0.76). No statistically significant DIF was detected by sex or school grade. Sample-based percentile thresholds were derived to describe the distribution of three-item scores, without establishing clinical or health-related cut-off values. Overall, the findings suggest that the candidate three-item short form shows more favorable Rasch measurement properties than the original questionnaire in this sample, although independent validation, assessment of temporal reliability, and comparison with external physical activity measures are needed before broader application.

papers.title: Geotechnical characterization and foundation competence evaluation using shallow seismic refraction: a case study from Ain Sokhna, Gulf of Suez, Egypt
papers.abstract: The evaluation of subsurface conditions and foundation competence is essential for sustainable infrastructure development in the Ain Sokhna area along the Gulf of Suez, Egypt. This study applies shallow seismic refraction surveys to characterize the geotechnical properties of near-surface materials and assess their suitability for engineering and construction. Seismic P-wave (Vp) velocities obtained from twenty survey sites were integrated with measured S-wave (Vs) velocities and density values to derive a comprehensive set of dynamic geotechnical parameters, including Poisson’s ratio, shear modulus, Young’s modulus, bulk modulus, material index, concentration index, stress ratio, ultimate bearing capacity, and allowable bearing capacity. Results reveal pronounced spatial variations in subsurface engineering characteristics. P-wave velocities range from 677 to 2330 m/s, while S-wave velocities vary between 376 and 1355 m/s. Velocity distributions show a systematic decrease from the northeastern to the southwestern sector, reflecting reduced density, stiffness, and rock-mass competence. This trend is corroborated by elastic parameters: shear modulus ranges from 224 to 3954 MPa, Young’s modulus from 571 to 9842 MPa, and bulk modulus from 427 to 6420 MPa. The northeastern sector exhibits higher velocities and moduli, indicating compacted, mechanically competent foundation materials, whereas the southwest shows lower values, suggesting increased fracturing, weathering, and diminished geotechnical quality. Bearing-capacity analyses are consistent with this zonation, with ultimate values between 2.0 and 85.4 kg/cm2 and allowable values from 0.7 to 28.5 kg/cm2. The highest capacities occur in the northeast, while progressively weaker conditions dominate toward the southwest. The integrated results delineate two broad geotechnical zones, with comparatively competent materials in the northeastern, eastern, and central sectors and moderately competent materials toward the southwest.

papers.title: Distribution and genetic relatedness of multidrug-resistant E. coli in poultry farms: a One Health perspective
papers.abstract: The prevalence of pathogens, including multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, especially extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing E. coli (ESBL-EC), in poultry farms is a matter of public health and One Health significance. This cross-sectional study aimed to investigate the distribution and genetic relatedness of MDR and ESBL-producing E. coli from different reservoirs in poultry farms. A total of 90 samples were collected from five poultry farms: 60 chicken samples (66.7%), 15 farm-worker stool samples (16.7%), and 15 pooled environmental samples (16.7%), comprising five pooled litter samples, five pooled farm-soil samples, and five pooled agricultural-soil samples. Chickens were selected using a simple random technique (12 samples from each of the five farms), and all available farm workers were included. E. coli was isolated and identified, and the antimicrobial susceptibility profile of the isolates was determined. All isolates were genotyped using Enterobacterial Repetitive Intergenic Consensus polymerase chain reaction (ERIC-PCR) to assess similarity and genetic relatedness among isolates from the different compartments. Out of the total 90 samples, 52.2% (n = 47) were MDR and 40.0% (n = 36) were ESBL-producing E. coli. Among the 60 chicken samples, 63.3% (n = 38) were MDR and 50.0% (n = 30) were ESBL producers. Among the 15 pooled environmental samples, 46.7% (n = 7) were MDR-positive and 26.7% (n = 4) were ESBL-positive. Relatively lower ESBL positivity was observed among farm workers (2/15; 13.3%). Similar ERIC-PCR fingerprint patterns were observed among isolates from chickens, workers, and environmental compartments. Chicken isolates showed higher observed MDR and ESBL positivity than isolates from the pooled environmental samples and farm workers. Similar ERIC-PCR profiles across sources suggest genetic relatedness and potential epidemiological connectivity. These findings underscore the value of integrated One Health surveillance strategies.

papers.title: Nano-curcumin-mediated antibacterial photodynamic therapy activated by blue diode laser or blue LED against Enterococcus faecalis biofilms in infected root canals
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the antibacterial efficacy of nano-curcumin activated by a 450-nm diode laser or a blue light-emitting diode (LED) against Enterococcus faecalis biofilms in infected root canals. Sixty-six extracted human single-rooted teeth were prepared, sterilized, inoculated with Enterococcus faecalis, and incubated at 37 °C for three weeks. Six specimens were used to confirm biofilm formation by scanning electron microscopy (SEM; n = 3) and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM; n = 3). The remaining 60 specimens were randomly allocated into six experimental groups (n = 10 per group): Group 1, 2.5% sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl); Group 2, diode laser alone; Group 3, LED alone; Group 4, nano-curcumin; Group 5, nano-curcumin + diode laser; and Group 6, nano-curcumin + LED. Antibacterial efficacy was evaluated by colony-forming unit (CFU) counts and CLSM-based live/dead biofilm assessment. Data were analyzed using one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) followed by Tukey’s post hoc test (p < 0.05). Significant reductions in Enterococcus faecalis CFU counts were observed in all treatment groups compared with baseline (p < 0.05), except for Groups 2 and 3. Group 1 exhibited the greatest antibacterial efficacy (99% CFU reduction), followed by Group 5 (70.02%) and Group 6 (68.29%), whereas Group 4 demonstrated a modest antibacterial effect (27.86% CFU reduction). CLSM findings were consistent with the CFU results, with Group 1 exhibiting the greatest reduction in biofilm viability, followed by Groups 5 and 6. Within the limitations of this in vitro study, activation of nano-curcumin with either a 450-nm diode laser or a blue LED enhanced its antibacterial activity and may have potential as an adjunctive approach to conventional root canal disinfection.

papers.title: Aversive conditioning prevents perceptual habituation, but not cortical adaptation to odors
papers.abstract: To save attentional resources, the human brain learns to decrease its response to non-threatening stimuli. The decreased behavioral response is known as habituation, while the decreased peripheral and central neural response is called adaptation. In this investigation, we were interested in whether initially non-threatening olfactory stimuli, when paired with aversive shock, may become less prone to habituation and adaptation. To this end, in 46 individuals (24 females; Mage=24.8 ± 5.7 years), we examined changes in cortical response and perceptual assessments of three odors, of which one was conditioned (i.e. paired with electric shock) and the remaining two were unconditioned. The conditioned odor was randomized across the participants. We report that aversive conditioning can prevent odor habituation, but we did not find support for the hypothesis that aversive conditioning prevents odor adaptation. We propose that aversive conditioning can be a method of maintaining olfactory alertness in those, who remain at risk of malodor exposure and may unintentionally get used to it, inflating the risk of negative consequences of this exposure.

papers.title: A cue-locality audit framework for attributing spurious temporal shortcuts in deep sequence models
papers.abstract: High accuracy on independent and identically distributed (IID) test data does not reveal which temporal cue a sequence model uses. A directional process can leave a cue in individual frames, so out-of-distribution (OOD) failure alone does not establish temporal-order use. We propose a six-gate audit that attributes failure to a nuisance and distinguishes frame-local, order-invariant multi-frame, and order-encoded cues. A companion controlled benchmark provides the factor-level probes and interventions the audit requires. Applied to this benchmark, the audit revealed that a variant designed to encode temporal order was instead solvable from individual frames. In the strict order-encoded variant (OE-Strict), direction is readable only from interior frame order. With nuisance direction aligned with the label with probability 0.97 during training, a gated recurrent unit (GRU) trained by empirical risk minimization (ERM) selects the shortcut in thirty of thirty seeds (0.970 IID and 0.030 OOD accuracy). Channel-selective interventions attribute the collapse to nuisance frame ordering. The audit distinguishes which process supports a prediction and whether using that process requires temporal order.

papers.title: Micron-precision depth control in automated volumetric laser ablation with ultrashort laser pulses
papers.abstract: Achieving “first time right” depth precision in volumetric laser ablation – particularly for deep features exceeding 50 μm – is challenging due to dynamic effects such as incubation-induced changes in ablation efficiency and altered laser-material coupling caused by the formation of Laser-Induced Periodic Surface Structures (LIPSS). This work presents an industrial-grade setup for closed-loop volumetric ablation that integrates an ultrafast laser, a galvanometer scanner, and coaxial Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) for real-time depth control. To overcome measurement artifacts arising from the evolving surface morphology and local fluctuations of the OCT depth signal, two complementary correction strategies were implemented. First, a morphology-dependent initial OCT depth offset is determined by extrapolating the stabilized depth progression and subsequently compensated. Second, a pixel-wise moving average of the OCT depth measurements provides a robust termination criterion for local laser processing. The developed processing system with the advanced control software enabled precise and reproducible laser ablation of volumetric structures in AISI 304 stainless steel with a depth accuracy of 1 μm to 2 μm regardless of the investigated initial surface states and process parameters for target depths ranging from 50 μm to 500 μm.

papers.title: Exercise-induced 3-oxoLCA promotes antitumor immunity with CD8⁺ T-cell involvement in colorectal cancer
papers.abstract: Exercise is associated with reduced colorectal cancer risk, but the circulating factors linking exercise to antitumor immunity remain unclear. Here we show that plasma collected within one hour after exercise suppresses colorectal tumor growth in mice. Metabolic profiling identifies 3-oxolithocholic acid, a bile acid metabolite that increases after acute exercise in mice and humans. Oral administration of this metabolite suppresses tumor growth and is associated with increased tumor infiltration by CD8+T cells, which can kill cancer cells, and altered immune-response markers. Exploratory single-cell analysis reveals differences in gene activity related to immune function and metabolism in these cells. Depletion of CD8+T cells attenuates, but does not eliminate, tumor suppression. These findings identify an exercise-responsive metabolite that promotes antitumor immunity in a mouse model of colorectal cancer and support a contribution from CD8+T cells, while leaving additional mechanisms unresolved.

papers.title: Maternal polystyrene nanoplastics exposure compromises ovarian reserve by disrupting oocyte adhesion and granulosa cell homeostasis
papers.abstract: Polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs), as an emerging environmental contaminant, have attracted growing concern owing to their widespread distribution and bioaccumulation capacity. This study investigated the effects of maternal PS-NPs exposure on primordial follicle (PF) assembly in offspring, a process critical for lifelong ovarian reserve establishment. Using a mouse model combined with single-cell RNA sequencing, we characterized the impact of PS-NPs on oocytes and granulosa cells during early folliculogenesis. We demonstrate that PS-NPs undergo intergenerational transfer, crossing the placental barrier to accumulate preferentially in the ovarian cortex of offspring. PS-NPs exposure significantly impaired cyst breakdown and PF assembly, resulting in a marked reduction in ovarian reserve. Mechanistically, PS-NPs enhanced intercellular adhesion within germline cysts by activating the JNK/WNT-β-catenin signaling, causing cyst dissociation defects. Also, PS-NPs suppressed the FAK/PI3K signaling, inhibiting granulosa cell proliferation and inducing apoptosis, ultimately impeding PF formation. This work provides a scientific basis for understanding nanoplastic-associated ovarian disorders, including premature ovarian insufficiency.

papers.title: Chirality-locked low-dimensional bound states in the continuum lasers
papers.abstract: Bound states in the continuum are intrinsically delocalized. Here, the authors realize localized bound state-in-the-continuum lasers at one-dimensional interfaces and zero-dimensional junctions by interfacing domains of opposite chirality.

papers.title: Boosting reinforcement learning for critical node detection with multi-topology training strategies
papers.abstract: Critical node detection helps identify network elements whose removal most disrupts connectivity. Here, the authors develop a reinforcement-learning approach that trains on diverse graph topologies to improve generalization to both synthetic and real networks.

papers.title: Field-angle-resolved heat transport in UTe 2 : determination of nodal positions in the superconducting order parameter
papers.abstract: Determining the gap symmetry of superconducting phases in UTe2 remains a central challenge. Here, the authors use field-angle-dependent thermal conductivity and theoretical analysis to identify b-axis point nodes in the low-field state, consistent with a B2u order parameter.

papers.title: Geophysical conditions favoring precursory slip before major earthquakes
papers.abstract: Laboratory experiments show that precursory slow slip before earthquakes is controlled by fault roughness and stress. On smooth faults, it is most pronounced at low stress, explaining why smooth, fluid-rich megathrust faults often host precursors.

papers.title: TRIM47 drives cardiac ischemia/reperfusion injury by impairing mitochondrial function and fatty acid metabolism in male mice
papers.abstract: Cardiac I/R injury is a prevalent and intractable clinical complication. Here, the authors show that TRIM47 facilitates ubiquitination-dependent nuclear translocation of FOXO1 and the subsequent inhibition of HNF4α, thereby aggravating mitochondrial dysfunction, FAO defects and cardiac I/R injury.

papers.title: Multi-ancestry genetic analysis reveals 29 novel rheumatoid arthritis loci, effector genes and drug repurposing opportunities
papers.abstract: Integrated genetic, functional, and network-level analyses reveal how population-specific and shared genetic signals contribute to rheumatoid arthritis and provide new insights into disease mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities.

papers.title: Emergent mesoscale nanoparticle patterns from a non-equilibrium liquid lens
papers.abstract: Nanoparticle assembly at fluid interfaces is often viewed as unpredictable and dominated by uncontrolled non-equilibrium effects. Here, the authors show that evaporation-driven nanoparticle assembly reveals predictable morphologies through multiscale modeling, linking transport dynamics and kinetic arrest.

papers.title: DPI-score: a deep learning-based metric for assessing protein-protein interfaces in cryoEM derived assemblies
papers.abstract: The study introduces deep learning-based protein-protein interfaces’ quality score- DPI-score, that uses only structural coordinates, without engineered interface features. It provides complementary validation and detects errors at interfaces.

papers.title: Tuning methanol-CO selectivity in CO 2 hydrogenation by Ga coordination engineering in ZnGa 2 O 4
papers.abstract: Controlling whether carbon dioxide hydrogenation yields methanol or carbon monoxide remains challenging. This study shows that tuning gallium coordination in ZnGa₂O₄ directs distinct reaction pathways and product selectivity.

papers.title: A subspecialty diagnostic system powered by self-supervised learning for cervical histopathology
papers.abstract: Foundation models could be promising for cervical cancer screening, but have important limitations for their clinical deployment. Here, the authors introduce the Cervical Subspecialty Pathology (CerS-Path) diagnostic system, a self-supervised learning framework for cervical cancer pathology that outperforms state-of-the-art foundation models across multiple diagnostic tasks.

papers.title: Sunflower pollen microgels enable sonication-free dispersion of carbon nanotubes for bio-based conductive inks
papers.abstract: Dispersing carbon nanotubes in conductive inks often requires energy-intensive sonication. Here, the authors use sunflower pollen microgels and alginate to create sonication-free conductive inks for printing, sensing, and electromagnetic shielding applications.

papers.title: A split RNA-guided Cas9 system for PAM-independent and cis -cleavage-free nucleic acid detection
papers.abstract: CRISPR-Cas9 lacks collateral cleavage for nucleic acid diagnostics. Here, authors show that splitting the guide RNA into scaffold and spacer converts Cas9 into SCas9, enabling rapid, single-nucleotide-specific DNA/RNA sensing, PAM-independent dsDNA detection, and attomolar clinical assays.

papers.title: Bright and stable near-infrared tin-perovskite LEDs enabled by efficient optical and thermal management
papers.abstract: Invisible near-infrared light sources are vital for imaging and sensing, but planar emitters struggle to achieve high optical power. Zhou et al. developed stable, lead-free perovskite light-emitting diodes with record radiance for night vision and biomedical uses.

papers.title: A Miniaturized Electrostatic Field Sensor Based on MOS Depletion-Layer Capacitance Modulation
papers.abstract: Static and low-frequency electric fields are important in power systems and insulating materials, but compact non-perturbing sensors remain challenging to build. Here, the authors show a miniaturized MOS-capacitance sensor that measures electric fields with high linearity and enables monitoring of surface charge and device electric fields.

papers.title: Enhancer-driven gene regulatory network of human forebrain development provides insights into autism
papers.abstract: The authors construct a gene regulatory network showing the potential role of specific enhancer elements in driving lineage imbalance in autism, explaining why forebrain organoids from autism probands show heterogeneity in the generation of excitatory neurons.

papers.title: Glutamine binding and sodium coordination reveal the transport mechanism of y⁺LAT1/CD98hc
papers.abstract: Here, cryo-EM, functional and computational studies reveal how the lysinuric protein intolerance transporter y⁺LAT1/CD98hc integrates Na⁺ and substrate recognition to mediate selective exchange of neutral and cationic amino acids.

papers.title: Single cell RNA sequencing reveals unexpected heterogeneity and identifies AP2XI-6 as a mature bradyzoite specific cell cycle regulator
papers.abstract: Authors show mature chronic-stage T. gondii adopt cell-cycle-controlled cyst-wall protein expression and two cell-cycle architectures in vivo. AP2XI-6 is required for the mature architecture; without it, parasites form cysts in vitro but fail in vivo.

papers.title: Global patterns of radial growth-structural heterogeneity relationships in forests
papers.abstract: Climate change can reshape forest size structure. Using tree rings from > 900 sites, the authors found warming and wetter conditions reduce tree-size inequality in high-stress regions but have little effect in low-stress forests.

papers.title: Kinetic balancing for near-equilibrium growth of defect-suppressed lead bromide perovskite single crystals
papers.abstract: A ligand-regulated crystallization strategy achieves near-equilibrium growth of lead bromide perovskite single crystals, suppressing defects and improving quality. The resulting CsPbBr 3 crystals enable stable, sensitive ionizing-radiation detection.

papers.title: Light-driven oxidative coupling of methane via charge-symmetry-breaking
papers.abstract: The successful construction of multiple CuO/ZnO interfaces with charge symmetry breaking achieves a high POCM performance with a C2H6 yield of 30.87 mmol g − 1 h − 1 and C 2+ selectivity of 97.8% under ambient conditions in flowing reactor.

papers.title: An electrically driven multimodal soft robot enabled by a monolithic heterolayer elastomer
papers.abstract: Soft robots are promising for complex applications, though typical robots rely on a single active material limiting applications. Here the authors design artificial muscle using dielectric elastomers and liquid crystal elastomers for multimodal locomotion.

papers.title: Photocatalytic radical hydrogenation of unactivated alkenes via an intermolecular hydrogen-atom-transfer relay
papers.abstract: Cross-electrophile coupling between unactivated alkyl halides and alkynyl halides has long been challenged by reactivity mismatch and poor chemoselectivity. Here the authors report nickel-catalyzed crosselectrophile coupling enabled by a tridentate ligand that controls the sequence of electrophile activation, allowing direct construction of alkynyl–alkyl bonds.

papers.title: Chemogenetic dissection of the H 2 O 2 –salicylic acid feedback loop in PTI and ETI evolutionary conservation
papers.abstract: Interaction between hydrogen peroxide and salicylic acid is important for plant stress responses. Here, the authors develop a dual-responsive fluorescent probe that simultaneously resolves the two signals in living plants.

papers.title: Sensory cortical disinhibition underlies long-term fear memory in humans
papers.abstract: The study demonstrates that human sensory cortex plays a causal role in transforming fleeting fearful experiences into lasting memories and that non-invasive brain stimulation can intercept this process, opening possibilities for treating anxiety- and trauma-related disorders.

papers.title: Taming crystallization to achieve superior soft magnetic performance via fine nanocrystallines
papers.abstract: Researchers demonstrate that rotational magnetic field annealing controls crystallization to produce ultrafine nanocrystals, enabling soft magnetic alloys with both high magnetic flux density and low coercivity for next-generation energy-efficient power electronics.

papers.title: Built-in electric field driven MXene/perovskite Schottky heterojunction for photo-electro-thermal energy redistribution in thermochromic smart windows
papers.abstract: A MXene and chloride-doped perovskite Schottky junction uses a built-in electric field to route ultraviolet and visible light into charge separation and interfacial heating, enabling room-temperature switching with 5.2 degrees Celsius hysteresis, 20.5% solar modulation, and 55% higher photocurrent.

papers.title: Agricultural economic responses to ecoclimate teleconnections induced by forest loss
papers.abstract: Forest loss across 14 U.S. regions can affect distant climates. Linking these teleconnections to crop yields and agricultural markets reveals soybean losses, wheat gains, 1–3% higher total production, lower crop prices, and small net gains in agricultural welfare.

papers.title: Theoretical frameworks for credit assignment via behavioral timescale synaptic plasticity
papers.abstract: Hippocampal neurons can learn in one shot via BTSP (Behavioral Timescale Synaptic Plasticity), triggered by dendritic plateau events. The authors derive when and where these events should occur to optimize learning and identify architectural limits on rapid learning in recurrent circuits.

papers.title: Phenotypic variation in Drosophila complex traits is influenced more by genotype and environmental interactions than by mitonuclear coevolutionary history
papers.abstract: Complex traits depend on energy produced by proteins encoded in both mitochondrial and nuclear genomes. By mixing and matching Drosophila variants of these genomes, this study finds that recent mtDNA mutations have more impact on traits than divergent mtDNAs revealing the influence of purifying selection.

papers.title: Molecular profiling of repeated self-sampled blood reveals dynamic immune phenotypes in young adults
papers.abstract: In this study, the authors used repeated at-home blood sampling to track changes in the immune-related protein during the recent pandemic. The study reveals shorter-lived shifts alongside stable proteins, providing insights missed by standard one-time blood tests

papers.title: Functional diversity of GPCR–Gustducin complexes controls signaling output and suppresses alternative pathways
papers.abstract: Gustducin mediates taste signaling but is also found throughout the body. Here, the authors show that non-taste GPCRs can activate or suppress gustducin signaling, revealing a mechanism that balances concurrent signaling pathways within cells.

papers.title: Mechanisms of β ↔ γ transformations in tin induce asymmetric kinetics
papers.abstract: Solid-solid phase transformation mechanisms need to be understood to establish suitable kinetic laws. Here, the β-Sn  ↔ γ-Sn phase transformations are investigated at different strain rates at 300 K. On one side, single crystals have been statically compressed and characterized using in situ x-ray diffraction. Multiple transformation cycles were performed in diamond anvil cells to measure their conditions and the associated microstructures. (101)β∣∣(110)γ and $${[10\bar{1}]}_{\beta }| | {[1\bar{1}1]}_{\gamma }$$ orientation relationships (OR) between β-Sn and γ-Sn are observed in most cases, for both direct and reverse transformations. An atomic martensitic transformation mechanism, associated with self-accommodation, is proposed to account for these OR and variant selection. However, γ-Sn  → β-Sn reversion also presents features that are consistent with recrystallization in β-Sn or a massive transformation. On the other side, time-resolved (22 μ s scale) dynamic diamond anvil cell experiments have been carried out. They show that while β-Sn  → γ-Sn transformation is fast (Pβ→γ=10.9  ± 0.2, insensitive to strain rate), reversion pressure Pγ→β varies with strain rate, from 9.4 ± 0.8 GPa to 6.35 ± 0.7 GPa. Moreover, timescales of β-Sn formation and subsequent recrystallization/growth in this phase can be distinguished. A different kinetic description needs to be used for direct and reverse transitions. Solid-solid phase transformation mechanisms need to be understood to establish suitable kinetic laws. Here, the beta-phase Sn  ↔ gamma-phase Sn phase transformation is investigated at different strain rates at 300 K.

papers.title: Global weight deep equilibrium attention for numerical simulations on unstructured meshes
papers.abstract: Graph-based neural networks have emerged as efficient and versatile surrogates for mesh-based numerical simulations. However, achieving high predictive accuracy remains challenging due to over-smoothing, under-reaching during message passing, and disregard for mesh connectivity. To address this, we propose Global Weight Deep Equilibrium Attention (GDEA). GDEA constructs a sparse global weight matrix from mesh connectivity via the direct stiffness method, introducing an inductive bias toward diagonal dominance. We apply the resulting matrix iteratively until convergence, allowing information to propagate globally without adding extra message-passing layers. We formulate the iterative process as a Deep Equilibrium Model (DEQ) to reduce memory consumption, and we use Anderson acceleration to speed convergence. Extensive experiments across multiple numerical simulation datasets, including the newly introduced Deformed ABC dataset with diverse geometries, materials, and boundary conditions, demonstrate that GDEA outperforms other methods on Deformed ABC while remaining competitive on established benchmarks. An accurate surrogate model that can handle diverse design configurations can facilitate efficient early-stage design exploration. Junghun Lee and Conrad Tucker present Global Weight Deep Equilibrium Attention, which builds a global weight matrix from mesh connectivity and propagates information via equilibrium iterations, reducing over-smoothing and under-reaching. Their model outperforms existing surrogates on Deformed ABC, a new diverse dataset, and stays competitive on established benchmarks.

papers.title: Low-frequency phase in early visual cortex gates prefrontal influence on perception
papers.abstract: Perceptual experience depends on interactions between sensory inputs and top-down predictions, yet how intrinsic cortical rhythms shape this interaction remains unclear. Here, we use rare human intracranial recordings from the prefrontal and early visual cortices during bistable motion perception, including two patients with simultaneous coverage of both regions, to investigate how oscillatory phase shapes perceptual outcomes. We show that prestimulus low-frequency phase in early visual cortex and prestimulus theta phase in prefrontal cortex are each associated with subsequent perceptual reports. Crucially, directed connectivity and cross-frequency coupling analyses, conducted in the two patients with simultaneous prefrontal and early visual cortex coverage, show that prefrontal theta phase modulates visual high-frequency activity preferentially at specific phases of early visual low-frequency activity, consistent with a probabilistic, phase-dependent gating of top-down influence. A computational model implementing low-frequency-phase–dependent gating successfully reproduces these empirical dynamics, suggesting a unifying mechanism by which cortical state constrains top-down modulation. Together, these findings provide preliminary human intracranial evidence that ongoing low-frequency phase in early visual cortex is associated with the efficacy of top-down influence from prefrontal cortex, and thereby with perceptual interpretation under ambiguity.

papers.title: ADAMTS7 impairs endothelial angiogenic function via suppressing POSTN-mediated VEGFR2 activation in pre-eclampsia
papers.abstract: Angiogenic imbalance-induced endothelial dysfunction is central to pre-eclampsia (PE) pathogenesis. A disintegrin and metalloprotease with thrombospondin motif, member 7 (ADAMTS7) is upregulated in PE placentas and suppresses trophoblast function; however, its role in systemic endothelial dysfunction during PE remains unclear. Here we show a higher placental secretion and plasma level of ADAMTS7 in PE patients. ADAMTS7 circulating levels are positively correlated with systolic and diastolic blood pressure of pregnant women. Besides, hypoxia stimulates ADAMTS7 expression in human trophoblast and vascular cells by a HIF1α-dependent way. Pregnant rats with ADAMTS7 overexpression by adenovirus injection exhibits PE-like symptoms and impaired placental development. Functionally, ADAMTS7 significantly inhibits endothelial angiogenic activity and suppresses vessel formation as evidenced by proliferation, migration, angiogenic assays. Mechanistically, ADAMTS7 binds to and decreases periostin (POSTN), reducing VEGFR2 expression and phosphorylation. This study identifies ADAMTS7 as a pathogenic factor in PE that impaired endothelial angiogenic function, suggesting that targeting ADAMTS7/POSTN/VEGFR2 axis may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for PE. Angiogenic imbalance drives endothelial dysfunction in pre-eclampsia (PE). Here, the authors show the metalloprotease ADAMTS7 is elevated in the circulation of PE patients and impairs endothelial angiogenic function, suggesting the ADAMTS7/POSTN/VEGFR2 axis as a therapeutic target for PE.

papers.title: Artificial skyglow at night disrupts chronobiology and physiology in Crassostrea gigas
papers.abstract: Artificial skyglow at night (ASAN) is widespread in coastal environments, with consequences beginning to be highlighted but still understudied. Long-term ASAN field studies are needed to better understand the real challenge that nocturnal light poses to coastal organisms. To fill this gap, we investigated during one year in Arcachon Bay (France), ASAN’s impact on the oysters’ biological rhythms and major physiological parameters: behavior, growth, and gametogenesis. Results show that ASAN affects oysters’ behavioral valve activity rhythms, whether they are directly driven by light cycles (daily, lunar, and annual) or not (tidal and semi-lunar), suggesting a disruption of the oyster’s internal clock functioning. Our study also reveals that ASAN affects oyster physiology at the annual scale by inducing a phase advance in body weight and shell length growth, and gametogenetic cycle. These chronobiological and physiological effects of ASAN could lead to a disruption of the oyster’s fitness.

papers.title: Circulating HSPCs enhance their self-renewal by augmenting the endocytosis and lysosomal acidity via MIF-(CXCR4_CD74)-ATP6V1A axis
papers.abstract: Human circulating hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (cHSPCs) in steady-state blood are a rare, underutilized resource limited by poor ex vivo expansion and unclear regulation. Using an immune-cell screening platform, we found that monocytes most effectively promote cHSPC expansion while preserving long-term hematopoietic reconstitution in serial transplantation. Mechanistically, cHSPCs engage the MIF-(CXCR4_CD74)-ATP6V1A axis to enhance endocytosis and lysosomal acidification, which upregulates CD34+CXCR4+ cells, reduces ROS, stabilizes HIF-1α, and maintains glycolytic activity and stemness. Monocyte co-culture or pathway agonizts (MIF, EN6) also expanded HSPCs from cord blood, bone marrow, and poor-graft-function patient samples. Thus, cHSPC self-renewal is driven by an MIF-(CXCR4_CD74)-ATP6V1A-dependent mechanism modulating endocytosis, lysosomal function, and metabolism. This offers a universal expansion strategy for diverse clinical sources, including steady-state peripheral blood, cord blood, and functionally compromised hematopoietic cells.

papers.title: In planta -specific transcriptional regulatory circuit regulates expression of MoHTR1 , a nuclear effector gene of Magnaporthe oryzae
papers.abstract: During host-pathogen interactions, fungal pathogens secrete effectors into host cells to manipulate the host immune system and facilitate infection. Although many effector genes are highly expressed during infection stages, there is limited information on the mechanisms regulating their in planta expression. Here, we characterize the promoter of MoHTR1, a nuclear effector gene of the rice blast pathogen, to elucidate its in planta-specific expression. Using promoter deletion and mutation analyses, we identified a core cis-element (TATTTCGT) within the MoHTR1 promoter, designated the in planta inducible (IPI) element, which is crucial for in planta-specific expression. The IPI element is responsible for the expression of not only MoHTR1, but also Slp1, a known effector gene. Furthermore, the IPI element enables the in planta expression of MobZIP14, a gene specifically expressed during vegetative growth. The IPI element plays a critical role in fungal virulence by enabling MoHTR1 expression. Bioinformatic and DNA-protein interaction analyses revealed that RGS1, a transcription factor containing a winged-helix binding domain, acts as a transcriptional regulator of MoHTR1 by directly binding to the IPI element. Our findings provide insights into the regulatory mechanisms driving the in planta-specific expression of fungal effector genes.

papers.title: Amyloid pathology compresses dynamic range and degrades spatial coding in an Alzheimer’s mouse model
papers.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) disrupts neural circuits vital for memory and cognition. Using two-photon calcium imaging in behaving 5xFAD mice, we examined how amyloid pathology alters hippocampal CA1 activity and spatial coding. We found elevated baseline activity but reduced locomotion-driven firing, leading to a diminished neuronal dynamic range. To our knowledge, this is the first direct experimental evidence for reduced dynamic range in an AD model. These abnormalities were strongest near amyloid plaques and became more widespread with age. We also observed altered network synchrony, degraded spatial coding, and increased neuronal response variability. Furthermore, place fields emerged more slowly in both familiar and novel environments, indicating impaired recall and learning. By showing a link between local plaque pathology and impaired flexible modulation of CA1 activity and progressive deficits in spatial memory coding, our study offers new insights into the circuit basis of cognitive decline in AD.

papers.title: Volitional stopping is preceded by a transient motor cortex EEG beta oscillation
papers.abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG) beta (15-30 Hz) oscillations undergo power modulations during volitional movements. The prevailing view is that beta oscillations are involved in inhibitory control, but their timing relative to movement cancellation is highly variable across studies. This variability has hindered understanding the function of beta oscillations in movement. The variability arises from use of the stop-signal task, in which movement cancellation time is covert. We recorded 32-electrode cortex-wide EEG along with the velocity of a treadmill while head-fixed rats stopped in-progress running. We show that a single beta oscillation cycle occurred in the left motor cortex around 200 msec before movement cancellation with consistent across-trial timing. Using information theory, we show that beta power was informative about velocity 200 msec in the future, but only during planning to stop. By introducing artificial temporal jitter to mimic the estimation of a covert stopping time used in prior work, we show that this brain-action relationship fails with even small jitter. Finally, we use machine learning methods to show that, despite EEG beta oscillations being a clear neural correlate of stopping, it has limited utility for real-time action decoding. Our work suggests a new conceptual model for neural control of overt action stopping.

papers.title: Dual HDAC6 and HDAC8 inhibition enhances STING mediated innate immune responses
papers.abstract: Despite the critical role of Stimulator of Interferon Genes (STING) in innate immune regulation, the isoform-specific epigenetic mechanisms that regulate its activation remain poorly understood because of the lack of suitable chemical tools. Here, we identify SEH002, a mechanistically informative dual HDAC6 and HDAC8 inhibitor that amplifies STING activation and reveals the complementary roles of HDAC6 and HDAC8 in innate immune signaling. STING-induced innate immunity proceeds through an intrinsic cell-autonomous phase, followed by a non-cell-autonomous paracrine phase. HDAC6 inhibition promotes the early cell-autonomous phase by increasing α-tubulin acetylation and facilitating endoplasmic reticulum-to-Golgi trafficking, thereby enhancing STING signaling. In contrast, HDAC8 inhibition sustains the later non-cell-autonomous phase by limiting STAT1 dephosphorylation and prolonging interferon signaling. These findings establish HDAC6 and HDAC8 as regulators of distinct phases of STING-mediated immune response. SEH002 provides an isoform-aware chemical handle to probe this cross-talk and suggests a general strategy for defining how epigenetic mechanisms orchestrate the magnitude and duration of STING-mediated innate immune responses.

papers.title: Nanobody mimicry of a GPCR recognition site disrupts human C5a-C5aR1 signaling
papers.abstract: The human anaphylatoxin C5a is a potent proinflammatory mediator generated during complement activation. C5a acts through the G-protein-coupled receptors C5aR1 and C5aR2, which are implicated in many immune-inflammatory diseases, and blocking C5a-C5aR1 signaling is a promising therapeutic strategy. Here we generate and characterize nanobodies, single-domain antibody fragments, that bind human and mouse C5a with high affinity and fall into two families recognizing non-overlapping epitopes. In cell assays, these nanobodies block C5a-induced receptor activation and downstream signaling. Crystallography shows that the antigen-binding loop of the highest-affinity nanobody mimics a turn in the extracellular amino-terminal region of C5aR1 and C5aR2, so that the nanobody competes with the receptor for the same surface of C5a. An antibody loop and a cell-surface receptor thus converge on analogous solutions for engaging the same ligand. These results inform our understanding of antibody-mediated inhibition of receptor agonists and identify nanobody-based C5a inhibitors as candidates to modulate C5a-driven inflammation.

papers.title: Critical dynamics govern the evolution of political regimes
papers.abstract: Political regimes lack a stable endpoint: they shift between more and less democratic configurations over time, as illustrated by historical democratic waves and recent backsliding. We analyse the historical trajectories of countries within a two-dimensional regime space derived from the principal components of the Varieties of Democracy dataset. We observe dynamics consistent with weak non-ergodicity, unfolding in an effective landscape of sparse and shifting basins of stability. Step sizes and sojourn times follow heavy-tailed distributions near the critical regime where mean values diverge, pointing to intermittent and heterogeneous regime change. A continuous time random walk model reproduces the average dynamics and trajectory-to-trajectory variability of the last three decades. The temporal evolution of the ergodicity breaking parameter recovers waves of democratisation and periods of heightened global political divergence, demonstrating the framework’s diagnostic potential. These results suggest that political regime evolution follows universal stochastic principles while remaining punctuated by unique historical pathways.

papers.title: Author Correction: Shear-induced Fickian yet non-Gaussian diffusion in athermal jammed matter
Trait absorption association with ketamine’s benefits and drug-context interactions in treatment-resistant depression: exploratory results from the MUSIK randomized clinical trial
papers.abstract: Ketamine exerts rapid antidepressant effects in treatment-resistant depression (TRD) but therapeutic predictors remain elusive. The personality trait absorption – tendencies for immersive sensory, imaginative, and emotional experiences – influences responses to serotonergic psychedelics, like psilocybin, but has not been studied for ketamine. This study explores trait absorption’s influences on ketamine-therapy for TRD, including interactions with music- versus mindfulness-based support. This exploratory analysis draws on the MUSIK trial (NCT04701866), a multi-site, parallel, single-blind RCT at two Montreal hospitals, whose primary outcome examined hemodynamic effects of pairing ketamine with music. Thirty-two adults (aged 18-75 years) with severe TRD, receiving a structured psychedelic ketamine-therapy intervention, were randomized 1:1 to receive either music (n = 15) or matched non-music support (n = 17) during their six infusions (0.5 mg/kg over 40 min) over four weeks. Outcome assessors but not participants were blinded. Across 181 infusions, this exploratory outcome examined associations between baseline absorption and (1) changes in depression, anxiety, and suicidality; and (2) mystical/emotional experiences using linear correlations and multilevel models. Baseline trait absorption is associated (p ≤ .002) with pre-post improvements in depression (r = .721), anxiety (r = .546), and mean/peak Mystical Experience Questionnaire scores (r = .528-.637). In multilevel models, higher absorption is associated with steeper declines in depression and suicidality. Three-way interactions with timepoint and group suggest that music, versus matched non-music support, is associated with greater depression improvements in higher-absorption individuals (p <.001). Although confirmation in larger studies is required, this exploratory study suggests that trait absorption relates to ketamine’s benefits for TRD. Observed drug-context interactions highlight possible strategies for individuallytailoring ketamine-therapy. Low-dose ketamine can be very beneficial for severe depression even when other treatments have not helped. However, much remains unknown about how ketamine works and who might most benefit. This study explored how a personality trait called absorption may influence the benefits of a series of ketamine doses, paired with either music- or mindfulness-based support, for adults with severe depression. Trait absorption reflects an individual’s tendencies to become deeply immersed in sensory, imaginative, and emotional experiences. The results suggest that higher trait absorption is associated with greater benefits from ketamine, especially when administered with music. This may be because high-absorption individuals tend to have more significant ketamine experiences – indeed, the study found that higher trait absorption was associated with more mystical-like ketamine experiences. If confirmed, these results may help guide patient selection and the personalized use of mindfulness or music in ketamine therapy for depression. Garel et al. explore the influence of the personality trait absorption in the MUSIK trial which administered 181 doses of ketamine, with either music or mindfulness, for treatment-resistant depression. Higher absorption is associated with larger antidepressant effects, reduced suicidality, and more mystical experiences, especially with music-based support.

papers.title: Learning uncertainty fields for joint brain stroke diagnosis and intrinsic lesion localization in CT and MRI
papers.abstract: Early stroke changes can be difficult to detect and localize on neuroimaging, particularly when lesion boundaries are indistinct. We developed the Dynamic Fuzzy Encoder Network (DFE-Net), which uses learnable fuzzy membership fields to represent spatial uncertainty and jointly classify stroke and localize lesions. We evaluated the model on a multicentre computed tomography (CT) cohort comprising 6650 patients and 8873 images and a separate magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) cohort comprising 67 patients and 615 images. Training and testing were performed separately within each modality. DFE-Net achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.974 and an F1 score of 0.897 on CT, and corresponding values of 0.978 and 0.879 on MRI. In the CT cohort, lesion localization against expert annotations yielded a Dice score of 0.70. MRI localization was assessed using gradient-derived pseudo-targets because expert lesion masks were unavailable. Expected calibration error was ~0.022 in both cohorts, and the model contained 0.20 million parameters. These results support joint diagnosis and spatial localization with a compact model, while prospective validation and expert-annotated MRI evaluation remain necessary.

papers.title: Learning health system frameworks and the integration of artificial intelligence and data science in United States health care: a scoping review
papers.abstract: Learning Health Systems (LHSs) use routinely collected data to generate evidence that informs practice through continuous learning cycles. Artificial intelligence (AI) and data science may strengthen this model, but how LHS frameworks and AI applications relate remains unclear. We mapped LHS frameworks and their components and examined how AI and data science are integrated. Searches identified U.S.-based, English-language studies published January 2007–August 2025; two reviewers independently screened and extracted data, resolving disagreements by consensus. We included 54 framework studies (24 [44%] conceptual adaptations; 30 [56%] real-world implementations) and 30 AI/data science studies. Five components recurred across the frameworks: data infrastructure and interoperability, governance and stakeholder engagement, learning and improvement cycles, evidence generation and translation, and equity and ethics. Relative to framework studies, AI studies less often addressed governance and stakeholder engagement (17% vs 35%) or equity (13% vs 22%), emphasizing computational over organizational functions. Most AI studies (27/30) focused on the data-to-knowledge phase; only three extended to knowledge-to-practice, and none described practice-to-data feedback with post-deployment outcomes informing model updating. AI applications capture only part of the LHS vision, concentrating on knowledge generation with less attention to the organizational and feedback mechanisms needed to translate insights into practice and sustain learning.

papers.title: Measurement fidelity and external validation of automated breast DCE-MRI segmentation
papers.abstract: Automated breast dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) segmentation could facilitate quantitative tumor measurement, but geometric overlap alone does not establish the fidelity of mask-derived measurements. We developed an enhancement-aware three-dimensional MedNeXt framework with gated skip fusion and boundary supervision and evaluated it in a retrospective multi-cohort design spanning locked internal testing, source-held-out assessment, retrospective external validation, and radiologist review. Measurement fidelity was the primary endpoint. Across 521 paired internal-test and DUKE cases, median errors were 9.7% for tumor volume, 1.8 mm for 3D maximum surface diameter, and 10.2% for operational enhancement-defined volume, with corresponding ICCs of 0.97, 0.80, and 0.97. Median Dice was 0.831 internally and 0.823 in the DUKE source-held-out stratum, and was 0.812 and 0.806 in the BC-MRI-SEG and public BreastDCEDL_AMBL retrospective external-validation cohorts, respectively, using the frozen checkpoint without external-label tuning. No major correction was required for 78 of 80 masks in the blinded two-reader review. In 276 paired response-analysis cases, AUROC was 0.732 with automatic geometry and 0.757 with expert geometry (difference, −0.025; 95% CI, −0.095 to 0.045); discrimination non-inferiority was not demonstrated. These findings support automated segmentation as a starting point for radiologist-supervised retrospective quantitative research within the evaluated cohorts, while distinguishing measurement fidelity from downstream predictive equivalence.

papers.title: Beyond skin deep: physiologic oral pigmentation as an overlooked validation gap in AI-assisted oral cancer screening
papers.abstract: AI-assisted oral cancer screening tools, exemplified by MeMoSA, have been validated almost exclusively in Asian populations. We propose a testable hypothesis: physiologic oral pigmentation, which varies by race independent of pathology, may cause classifiers to misclassify normal variation as suspicious or miss camouflaged lesions. Following precedent from pulse oximetry and dermatology AI, we call for pigmentation-stratified validation before deployment in racially diverse settings such as the United States.
