papers.title: Photonic-assisted ingenious agile non-periodic oscillator (PIANO)
papers.abstract: The study presents PIANO, a microwave photonic oscillator that generates frequency-agile microwave signals with rapid switching and ultra-low phase noise, while overcoming the cavity-delay constraint of conventional delay-based oscillators.

papers.title: Room-temperature continuous-wave lasing-like emission from solution-processed bulk monolayer MoS 2 thin films
papers.abstract: Scaling up atomically thin light emitters remains challenging. Here, authors develop solution-processable bulk-monolayer MoS 2 films that preserve monolayer optical properties and exhibit room-temperature lasing-like emission under continuous optical pumping at just a few nW.

papers.title: Selective aromatization of polyolefins by temporal decoupling from cracking
papers.abstract: Turning plastic waste into useful chemicals is limited because breaking polymer chains and controlling products need conflicting conditions. This study separates these steps in time, enabling fast, durable aromatic production with lower emissions.

papers.title: Depth-enhanced molecular imaging with two-photon oblique plane microscopy
papers.abstract: Two-photon oblique plane microscopy combines high-numerical-aperture single-objective detection with two-photon light-sheet illumination, resolving subcellular and single-molecule dynamics deep in multicellular systems through standard glass-based mounting.

papers.title: Signatures of a Kondo insulator in a multilayer moiré Superlattice
papers.abstract: Kondo insulator phases are traditionally found in materials with f-electrons. Here, the authors present evidence towards the realization of a tunable Kondo insulator in a monolayer WS 2 /bilayer WSe 2 moiré superlattice.

papers.title: Vagal afferent activation induces a dissociated NREM sleep-like state with wake-related locus coeruleus activity
papers.abstract: The role of peripheral signals in sleep state regulation is not well understood. Here authors show that vagal sensory afferent activation induces a NREMS-like state with low-frequency EEG, slowed heart rate, and cooling, while elevating locus coeruleus noradrenergic activity, revealing brain arousal within a sleep-like state.

papers.title: Failure of TSPO-dependent metabolic compensation marks the loss of mitochondrial bioenergetic adaptation in parkin- deficient neurons
papers.abstract: Neurons initially adapt to mitochondrial damage, but why this defence fails is unclear. Here, the authors show that TSPO maintains glutamate-supported mitochondrial energy production in parkin-deficient neurons, and loss of this defence marks the transition from adaptation to neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Percolation and site energy distribution jointly control Li + transport in disordered rocksalt positive electrodes
papers.abstract: Ion transport limits the capacity and rate performance of disordered rocksalt positive electrodes. Here, the authors show that percolation connectivity and Li-site energy distributions jointly govern Li transport and provide a framework for composition and structural design.

papers.title: Non-equilibrium resonance scattering in intramolecular charge transport drives conformational changes
papers.abstract: Charge transport through molecules can couple to current-induced nuclear dynamics, but its microscopic details remain unclear. Park et al. study this process in alkanethiolate-based molecular junctions and show that the strength of the coupling can be quantitatively linked to microscopic parameters.

papers.title: LRH-1 coordinates metabolic and epigenetic programs that establish luteal cell identity
papers.abstract: Gagnon et al. show that LRH-1 coordinates metabolic and epigenetic programs that establish large luteal cell identity, progesterone production and fertility.

papers.title: Sex differences in the genetic basis of human recombination within 190,000 parent-child pairs
papers.abstract: A meta-analysis of 190,797 human meioses across four countries maps 24 recombination loci, seven novel and mostly female-specific. Between-sex genetic correlation is 0.37, and a polygenic predictor links female recombination to reproduction and aging.

papers.title: The posterior paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus to nucleus accumbens medial shell circuit mediates an anti-pruritic response
papers.abstract: Neural mechanisms underlying itch are not fully understood. Here authors show that the pPVT-NAcMed (posterior paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus to nucleus accumbens medial shell) circuit oppositely responds to histamine-dependent vs -independent itch, with LH inputs buffering the former, but chronic itch reduces postsynaptic efficacy, promoting sensitization and revealing differential processing.

papers.title: Dynamic chlorine vacancies enable X-ray-specific afterglow
papers.abstract: Afterglow is thought to arise from permanent charge-trapping defects, yet radiation-specific responses defy this model. Liu et al. reveal that X-rays create transient chlorine vacancies and control their formation for prolonged, high-resolution flexible imaging.

papers.title: Thermodynamic-guided tailoring of single-atom coordination environments via oxygen chemical potential for efficient C-N coupling
papers.abstract: Precise control of single-atom coordination is hindered by thermodynamic and kinetic constraints. Here, the authors report tuning Fe-O coordination on CoWO 4 via oxygen chemical potential control. Optimal Fe 1 O 4 boosts hexamethylenetetramine electrosynthesis with high yield, efficiency and stability.

papers.title: A microfluidic fluorescence lifetime screening platform bridges in vitro and in vivo formats and enables discovery of Amyloid β aggregation inhibitors
papers.abstract: Alzheimer’s drug discovery is hindered by unreliable tests for Amyloid β aggregation. Here, the authors develop nanoFLIM, a microfluidic screening tool to identify and validate aggregation inhibitors in vitro, in cellulo and in vivo.

papers.title: Directional motility of crystallizing cholesterol on supported lipid bilayers
papers.abstract: Cholesterol crystallizing inside a lipid membrane reshapes the membrane around it. Here, authors show that cholesterol crystallites travel in directed paths across model membranes, and map how lipid composition tunes that motion.

papers.title: A hierarchical metabolic flux orchestrates cell cycle transitions in bacteria
papers.abstract: How cells coordinate growth and division with their metabolic state is poorly understood. Here, Agrawal et al. describe changes in glucose uptake and central metabolism that alter cytosolic redox balance and drive cell cycle progression in the bacterial model Caulobacter crescentus .

papers.title: Post-pandemic immunity debt and environmental decoupling reshape urban influenza transmission
papers.abstract: Using 1.88 million clinical records from Macau and regional and global surveillance, in this study, the authors show how reduced population immunity and renewed travel reshaped post-pandemic influenza transmission and weakened its usual links with climate.

papers.title: Chirality inversion in DNA-assembled nanorod superlattices via site-specific asymmetric anchoring of single nanospheres
papers.abstract: Chiral 2D plasmonic superlattices are hard to tune without global redesign. Here, the authors use DNA-origami-templated 4-arm pinwheel lattices of gold nanorods to demonstrate that site-specifically adding one gold nanosphere per unit inverts handedness while preserving long-range order.

papers.title: CCR8-depleting antibodies restore response to radiotherapy plus anti-PD1 therapy in head and neck cancer by targeting intratumoral CCR8+ regulatory T cells
papers.abstract: Previous evidence has implicated regulatory T cells (Tregs) in treatment resistance in head and neck cancer. Here the authors report that radiotherapy and anti-PD1 therapy drive the accumulation and activation of intratumoral CCR8+ Tregs, promoting tumor growth and recurrence, which can be reversed with administration of CCR8 depleting antibodies.

papers.title: Sugar rationing during the first 1000 days of life and biological aging and age-related diseases
papers.abstract: Exposure to sugar rationing during the first 1,000 days of life was associated with slower biological aging in adulthood, with stronger associations after longer exposure. It was also associated with lower risks of several age-related diseases.

papers.title: miProbe: microbial peptide repository of biological embeddings
papers.abstract: Authors present miProbe, a platform aimed to consolidate peptide data and functional characterisation, and presenting a resource to accelerate AI-driven exploration of microbial dark matter.

papers.title: Comparative genomics analysis of luminescent and non-luminescent fireflies reveals mechanisms underlying adult light organs development
papers.abstract: Not all fireflies emit light. Here they perform comparative genomics between luminous and non-luminous fireflies to reveal that light organ loss stems from simplified gene networks. They show that Laccase2 is essential for light organ integrity, offering insights into bioluminescence trait evolution.

papers.title: Co-administration of the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 and bivalent Ancestral/BA.1 vaccination is well-tolerated in immunosuppressed patients highly vulnerable to infection with SARS-CoV-2 virus: the results of the multicentre, open-label, phase II randomised controlled, RAPID-PROTECTION trial
papers.abstract: In this clinical trial, authors found that administering the COVID-19 antibody AZD7442 before vaccination was safe in immunocompromised adults and boosted immune responses. The findings support combining antibodies and vaccines to protect vulnerable people.

papers.title: Anion manipulation for breaking through 3.0 V of aluminium–graphite batteries
papers.abstract: Aluminium–graphite batteries are limited by electrolyte decomposition above 2.5 V. Here, authors regulate chloroaluminate anions with a fluorine-rich, framework-confined quasi-solid-state electrolyte, enabling stable 3.0 V operation for Al | |Graphite cells.

papers.title: Sublevel-selective electron spin hyperpolarization of triplet radical pairs in metal–organic frameworks
papers.abstract: While molecular spin systems are promising platforms for spin-based technologies, previous studies have mainly focused on isolated molecular systems embedded in dense solid matrices. Here, the authors report a metal-organic framework approach for regulating the generation of spin-polarized radical pairs within a well-defined donor-acceptor arrangement.

papers.title: Strain-induced correlated metallic phase in 1T-TaS 2
papers.abstract: The nature of the insulating state in the layered transition-metal dichalcogenide 1T-TaS 2 remains under debate. Here, the authors show that uniaxial strain alters the stacking of charge‑density‑wave layers, driving an insulator‑to‑metal transition and yielding a correlated metallic state.

papers.title: Humanized yeast ORC drives R-loop dependent transcription-replication conflicts and global gene dysregulation
papers.abstract: ORC binds specific sites in yeast but broad promoter regions in humans, and whether origins and promoters share functions is unclear. Here, the authors use a humanized yeast model to show that ORC-bound origins trigger transcription-replication conflicts and can themselves act as promoters.

papers.title: AS01 E -adjuvanted RSV pre-F protein vaccine in adults with lung or kidney transplant: a phase 2b randomized trial
papers.abstract: The authors report results from a randomized phase 2 trial showing that the adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine was immunogenic and had an acceptable safety profile in lung and kidney transplant recipients, supporting a favorable benefit-risk profile.

papers.title: Epithelium stratifies via nucleation and growth induced by foam-geometric instability
papers.abstract: Researchers show that epithelial stratification, the shift from monolayer to multilayers, occurs via a nucleation-and-growth process. Combining cell cultures and 3D modeling, this study reveals how local cell delaminations drive tissue-wide changes.

papers.title: Intrinsic neural dynamics reveal a body-part-specific topography in mouse secondary motor cortex
papers.abstract: This presents a body-part-specific topography in mouse secondary motor cortex by analyzing intrinsic brain dynamics. The map is structurally and functionally linked to homologous sensory regions, and is selectively engaged during multi-part actions.

papers.title: The patient in the conversation
papers.abstract: The translational promise of biomedical technologies often becomes clearer when viewed from the perspective of the intended patient.

papers.title: A unified and practical taxonomy for false discovery rate control in omics research
papers.abstract: False discovery rate (FDR) control is central to omics research, yet the diverse procedures used rely on different assumptions. This Comment proposes a 2 × 2 matrix that helps sequencing-based and mass-spectrometry-based omics researchers choose the appropriate family of FDR procedures, or alternative methods that may be more rigorous, depending on data and study design.

papers.title: Immersive and wearable bi-directional thermal rendering for physical and virtual interaction in augmented reality
papers.abstract: Augmented reality blends virtual content with the physical world, creating a challenge for thermal feedback: users must feel virtual temperature cues without losing dexterity or access to real-world thermal information. Here we show that a palm-mounted warm/cool thermal feedback prototype can address this challenge through three design considerations: indirect feedback that leaves the fingertips unobstructed, active thermal passthrough that senses and reproduces the temperature of contacted physical surfaces, and spatially and temporally varying thermal stimulation. Human-subject experiments show that indirect feedback preserves immersion and comfort despite reduced realism when visual contact occurs at the fingertips; thermal passthrough supports discrimination between real and rendered temperatures; and moving thermal patterns increase immersion and realism compared with static stimulation. These findings suggest that our design considerations are viable design strategies for AR thermal haptics, while also clarifying tradeoffs for applications that require precise realism versus broader immersive thermal experience.

papers.title: Multiplexed node-pore sensing for high-throughput, label-free single-cell detection
papers.abstract: We present a multiplexed four-channel Node-Pore Sensing (NPS) platform in which each channel is encoded with a unique Manchester-coded sequence selected by combinatorial optimization for minimum aperiodic cross-correlation. A structural classifier based on the node-pore structure of each Gold code sequence achieves 99.3% single-channel identification accuracy on 1480 labeled experimental transit events, without template alignment or velocity correction. A linear support vector machine successfully distinguishes single-channel events from multi-channel coincidences, enabling label-free, high-throughput single-cell detection across all four channels. This multiplexed architecture provides a route to measuring cell mechanical properties, such as stiffness and recovery time, across parallel channels, extending NPS mechanophenotyping of primary human mammary epithelial cells toward the throughput needed for clinical study.

papers.title: Hippocampal somatostatin neurons gate context generalization during fear memory updating
papers.abstract: Freezing is used as a readout of fear memory in rodents, but it remains unclear how distinct freezing features reflect discrimination and generalization of threatening and neutral contexts. Using pose-tracking and unsupervised analysis in male and female mice undergoing contextual fear conditioning, we show that fear in neutral a context is expressed through fragmented freezing that resist experience-dependent updating, in contrast with more sustained, uninterrupted, and adaptable freezing in a threatening context. Neuronal recordings revealed that recalling neutral context fear is associated with increased activity of dentate gyrus somatostatin inhibitory neurons (SST INs). Chemogenetic suppression of SST INs during fear memory updating selectively facilitated neutral context freezing adaptation while activation prevented generalization of contextual information by restricting long-term fear reduction in contexts that differed from the updating context. These findings identify DG SST INs as context-specific modulators of fear memory updating and suggest that freezing dynamics serve as a behavioral signature of generalization.

papers.title: Pesticide-exposed bees fail to thermoregulate leading to cold colonies with consequences for offspring development
papers.abstract: For many organisms, effective thermoregulation is needed to cope with changing environmental temperatures. But if exposure to pesticides in the environment were to impair this homoeostatic process, reproduction and population viability could be at risk. Focusing on an important insect pollinator, we conducted three complementary experiments exposing bumblebees to a pesticide under different temperature challenges and measuring the impacts on thermoregulatory ability and brood development. First, we reveal that pesticide-exposed individuals (food spiked with a neonicotinoid insecticide) cannot maintain a stable thorax temperature, especially at lower temperatures. Second, that reductions in body temperature are accompanied by behavioural changes with pesticide-exposed colonies failing to maintain the brood temperatures that control bees achieved. Third, that such collective impairment of brood thermoregulation (not the pesticide toxicity to offspring per se) leads to delayed pupal development and reduced adult population growth. Our study provides a plausible mechanistic pathway for why terrestrial insects requiring brood thermoregulation may be vulnerable to decline. With frequent extreme weather events forecasted, our findings have concerning implications for how populations will adequately persist and grow under current pesticide-use regimes with ramifications for pollination services.

papers.title: E2F7 and E2F8 attenuate diabetic kidney disease by suppressing E2F1-induced tubular senescence
papers.abstract: Resveratrol reduces kidney fibrosis and cellular senescence in diabetic kidney disease by suppressing E2F1 through induction of E2F7/8 repressors. Targeting this E2F1-E2F7/8 regulatory axis may offer a promising strategy to slow DKD progression.

papers.title: End-to-end mapping of membrane transport from chemical structure to microorganisms
papers.abstract: Membrane transport is a fundamental biological process with profound implications for pharmacology, biotechnology, and microbiology. While computational approaches have largely adopted a protein-centric perspective to annotate transportomes, inferring transport function directly from the intrinsic properties of substrates remains a major challenge. Addressing transport at the compound level enables the systematic evaluation of whether molecules undergo active transport and by which mechanisms, independent of prior transporter annotation. Here, we introduce ChemProFlow, a comprehensive computational framework that redefines transport analysis from a substrate-centric perspective. By integrating geometric deep learning with orthology-based genomic mapping, ChemProFlow predicts molecular transportability, assigns transport mechanisms according to the Transporter Classification Database, and identifies the microorganisms encoding the corresponding transport systems. We show that this integrated pipeline enables scalable, end-to-end mapping of substrate-transporter-organism relationships, with broad applications in pharmacology for anticipating drug transport, in biotechnology for guiding strain engineering, and in microbiology for dissecting substrate utilization across diverse taxa. By capturing the chemical determinants of transportability, ChemProFlow generalizes to previously unseen substrates and provides a high-throughput framework for systematic exploration of molecular transport across diverse biological contexts. Membrane transport is crucial for pharmacology, biotechnology, and microbiology, yet predicting transport function from substrate properties remains challenging. Here, the authors introduce ChemProFlow, a substrate-centric computational framework that integrates geometric deep learning and genomic mapping to predict molecular transportability.

papers.title: Boundary-controlled imbibition reveals liquid-structure coupling in soft jammed systems
papers.abstract: Transport in soft jammed materials is often described as liquid flow through a fixed structure, yet foam imbibition frequently deviates from classical Lucas–Washburn scaling. Here, we investigate liquid imbibition in foams while directly visualizing both liquid penetration and foam motion under controlled boundary conditions. When foam motion is allowed, liquid uptake is accompanied by collective translation of the unimbibed foam, while the penetration relative to the foam matrix follows approximately xrel ∝ t1/2. When foam motion is suppressed, compression accumulates ahead of the imbibition front and the apparent propagation becomes slower than t1/2. We interpret these behaviors using an effective osmotic driving pressure reduced by a counterpressure generated by foam compression. When the matrix can move, this compression does not accumulate substantially; under a closed boundary, it progressively increases and suppresses further imbibition. These results demonstrate that foam imbibition is governed by coupling between capillary transport and the mechanical response of the foam matrix.

papers.title: Rosette formations as symmetry breaking events
papers.abstract: Multicellular rosettes are ubiquitous structures in biological systems, observed in contexts ranging from morphogenesis to wound healing and cancer progression. Although some molecular insights have been gained to explain the presence of these assemblies of cells around a common center, the tunable global features that favor/hinder their formation are still largely undefined. Here, we use a Voronoi dynamical model in combination with fluorescence microscopy experiments on neural cell populations derived from induced pluripotent stem cells to investigate the ingredients driving the emergence of rosettes. We find that (i) breaking the local spatial symmetry of the system by introducing local curvature-inducing defects allows for the emergence of rosette-like structures, (ii) whose probability of formation depends on the characteristics of the cellular layer. A trade-off between tissue fluidity and single-cell deformability controls the assembly of transient rosettes, which are stabilized in the presence of cell self-alignment interactions. This work provides a physical framework for interpreting the organization of the rosette in developing tissues.

papers.title: Development and validation of a machine learning model to predict the daily risk of febrile neutropenia in patients with AML undergoing chemotherapy
papers.abstract: Infections are among the main complications in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) undergoing intensive chemotherapy, increasing morbidity and mortality. However, no established tools exist to detect early signs of infection. Here, we develop and validate a machine learning model to predict the daily risk of febrile neutropenia (FN). We conducted a retrospective observational study using registry data from two university hospital districts in Finland. We included adult patients with newly diagnosed AML undergoing intensive chemotherapy (n = 271, 48-hour FN outcomes=540), excluding acute promyelocytic leukemia. The model used a 48-hour prediction window and 1.2 M clinical data points to generate daily FN risk estimates. We built the model using the Extreme Gradient Boosting algorithm, explained variable importance with Shapley Additive Explanations, and evaluated and validated performance using measures of discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility. We show how seven variables predict daily FN risk: white blood cell count, temperature, time since cycle start, C-reactive protein trend, absolute neutrophil count, treatment phase, and prior antibiotic treatment. We achieve an AUROC of 0.91 (95% CI, 0.89–0.93) and a calibration slope of 0.95 (95% CI, 0.73–1.16) in the development cohort’s test set (n = 55, 48-hour FN outcomes=109) and validate performance in the external cohort (n = 136, 48-hour FN outcomes=124, AUROC 0.79 (95% CI, 0.75–0.82), calibration slope 0.65 (95% CI, 0.51–0.79)). While prospective validation is warranted, this study suggests that routinely collected clinical data may be useful for daily prediction of FN and that further development of such screening tools could potentially support personalized infection prevention. Infections can be a life-threatening complication of chemotherapy in patients with acute myeloid leukemia. Here, we developed a screening tool to help physicians detect these infections early. Using registry data from two Finnish university hospital districts, we trained an AI model to predict early infection onset over the next 48 hours. The model required seven variables, including routine laboratory tests, temperature measurements, time since each chemotherapy cycle started, and information on the treatment phase and antibiotic use. Such a screening tool could potentially support more personalized supportive care. However, the results must be confirmed prospectively before clinical adoption.

papers.title: Analyses of plasma protein levels in relation to body composition in the UK Biobank
papers.abstract: Excess fat mass is causally linked to multiple diseases, but the use of existing therapies, such as glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, is limited by varying effects and common side effects, including loss of fat-free mass. We aimed to identify proteins associated with fat mass, but ideally not also associated with fat-free mass, as potential drug targets for alternative therapeutic strategies. We used UK Biobank data on plasma levels of 3K proteins (n = 35K) and fat and fat-free mass (n = 368K). We applied a machine learning procedure to select proteins for downstream cis Mendelian randomisation analyses, which estimated associations of genetically predicted protein levels with fat mass. These were followed by colocalisation analyses to assess shared causal genetic variants and further cis Mendelian randomisation analyses to assess associations with fat-free mass. Here we present evidence on the associations of genetically predicted levels of 21 proteins with fat mass, including five which also colocalise with the trait (AGER, CRIM1, DNER, NEFL, and PRRT3). Seven of the 21 proteins have no clear association with fat-free mass, and ADM has an association with fat-free mass opposite in direction to its association with fat mass, suggesting that modulating these proteins may be less likely to also lower fat-free mass. Two proteins, AGER and ADM, have been investigated in advanced-stage clinical trials for indications unrelated to adiposity. These findings support prioritising several proteins for further research as potential drug targets for fat mass reduction. They highlight proteins that may help diversify therapy options beyond glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and suggest possible repurposing opportunities. High levels of body fat can increase risk of several diseases, but existing treatments do not work equally well for everyone and can have side effects. Some treatments may reduce fat-free mass, which includes muscle and other non-fat tissue. We aimed to identify proteins that may be useful targets for alternative therapeutic strategies to reduce fat mass. We used data from UK Biobank, including on blood protein levels, body composition measures, and genetic information. We found evidence linking 21 proteins with fat mass, some of which also appeared not to have a relation with fat-free mass. These findings highlight proteins to prioritise in further studies as possible treatment targets, which may ultimately help develop more options for people who could benefit from reducing body fat, ideally without also reducing fat-free mass. Orešković et al. use UK Biobank proteomic and body composition data, applying machine learning, cis Mendelian randomisation, and colocalisation to prioritise targets for lowering fat mass without lowering fat-free mass. MR analyses yield 21 proteins related to fat mass, five of which also colocalised with the trait; seven proteins had no, and one had an opposite-direction association with fat-free mass.

papers.title: Contextualizing biological heterogeneity in brain structural normativity assessments across the aging continuum with the nearest neighbor normativity framework
papers.abstract: Despite established consensus about the individuality of brain physiology and structural changes, current neuroimaging biomarker paradigms heavily rely on population averages. Here, we define normativity not as a single reference point but as a landscape of permissible configurations arising from diverse physiological manifestations. We introduce the Nearest Neighbor Normativity (N3) framework, designed to parse the natural heterogeneity in brain structural measurements into a diversity-aware biomarker of brain structural decline. Through repeated comparisons within different demographic subgroups, N3 contextualizes an individual’s measurements from several viewpoints along the aging continuum. Relying on local density estimation, it accommodates multiple, shared normative configurations within and across age groups. We use T1-weighted MRI data from 29,883 individuals for training and 7,013 individuals for validation, and benchmark our framework against Brain Age models and Normative Modeling. We evaluate each biomarker’s ability to detect neurodegenerative diseases, using them as representative models of atypical brain structural decline. In group-level analyses, the N3 biomarker shows the largest effect sizes in the detection of Mild Cognitive Impairment, Alzheimer’s Disease, and Frontotemporal Dementia. Similarly, the N3 biomarker achieves the highest predictive performance in the classification of neurodegenerative diseases on a single subject level. Notably, the N3 estimates remain stable across age and robust to compositional changes in the reference sample. Finally, correlation analyses indicate that it captures distinct and complementary aspects of brain structural variation compared to existing approaches. Our findings underscore that rethinking normativity assessments to explicitly accommodate natural inter-individual variability can advance our collective efforts toward truly personalized patient care. Brain aging varies greatly between individuals, yet standard medical tools rely on population averages that may miss important individual differences. We developed a method called Nearest Neighbor Normativity (N3) that assesses brain health by searching for similar configurations along the aging spectrum and their likelihood, rather than to a single average. Using MRI scans from nearly 37,000 people, we tested whether this framework could detect brain changes associated with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer’s disease and frontotemporal dementia. The N3 method outperformed existing approaches, distinguishing disease-related brain changes from natural aging effects more accurately. This work suggests that personalized medical assessments accounting for natural human diversity may improve our ability to detect brain diseases early and support more targeted interventions. Leenings et al. methodologically reformulate neuroimaging standards to explicitly account for natural inter-individual variability of brain physiology. Applied to brain structural decline, the result is a diversity-aware biomarker which improves the detection of disease signals in both statistical and machine learning analyses.

papers.title: Just publish it
High-harmonic generation during ultrafast melting of a Mott insulating state
papers.abstract: High-harmonic generation in solids exposed to an intense laser field can provide information on carrier dynamics and band structures in weakly correlated systems. In strongly correlated systems, a laser field can induce a transition between the various electronic phases formed by the entanglement of charge, spin and orbital degrees of freedom via carrier generation. The high-harmonic generation accompanying this process can carry information on the non-equilibrium electronic-state dynamics along the oscillating field, an aspect that remains unresolved. Here we show that an intense mid-infrared pulse induces melting of a Mott insulating state in a one-dimensional cuprate, Sr2CuO3, the evolution of which leaves a trace in the high-harmonic spectra. Carriers are efficiently generated when the electric field amplitude exceeds 6 MV cm−1, and each harmonic frequency decreases from odd multiples of the mid-infrared frequency. Dynamical mean-field theory suggests that these redshifts originate from a series of electronic-structure reconstructions in each electric field cycle during the melting of the Mott insulating state, which modifies the radiation phase from carrier recombination cycle by cycle. This phenomenon is negligible in rigid-band systems. This study suggests that high-harmonic spectroscopy could obtain information on the cycle-by-cycle dynamics of non-equilibrium transitions in correlated materials. High-harmonic spectroscopy under an intense mid-infrared field reveals redshifts of high-harmonic peaks during the ultrafast melting of a Mott insulating state, while dynamical mean-field theory links them to cycle-by-cycle electronic-state changes.

papers.title: Synthetic interfaces in perovskite photovoltaics
papers.abstract: Synthetic interfaces, created in situ through physical and chemical processes that facilitate structural interlocking, chemical bridging and surface restructuring, offer a scalable pathway to commercially viable perovskite photovoltaics.

papers.title: Training reservoirs without looking back
papers.abstract: By training a reservoir computing system without access to its intermediate states and by eliminating the coupling between its nodes, a physical learning framework achieves efficient learning both in simulation and on optoelectronic hardware.

papers.title: Vaccines could be a new frontier in KRAS targeting
papers.abstract: A convergence of therapeutic and technological advances reveals KRAS-targeting vaccination as a potential new approach to preventing the recurrence of pancreatic cancer, but many hurdles remain.

papers.title: Gut and urogenital microbiomes influence menopausal hormone therapy outcomes
papers.abstract: A 6-month study shows that menopausal hormone therapy induces multi-site microbiome remodeling, including rejuvenation of the vaginal microbial community toward a reproductive-age-like state. In turn, baseline gut and vaginal community types affect the clinical response to therapy. Integrating clinical and gut microbiome features predicts rapid symptom remission, providing a blueprint for precision menopausal care.

papers.title: Antenatal inflammation drives postpartum cardiac dysfunction in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
papers.abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs), including preeclampsia and gestational hypertension, are strongly associated with maternal cardiac dysfunction during and after pregnancy. We hypothesized that maternal inflammation drives persistent postpartum cardiac maladaptation after HDPs. We conducted a prospective longitudinal study assessing cardiac function and circulating inflammatory profiles during pregnancy and 3–6 months postpartum, complemented by a preclinical mechanistic mouse model recapitulating key antenatal and postpartum immune and cardiac features of HDPs. Here we show that distinct antenatal inflammatory signatures, including elevated chemokines, correlated with adverse left ventricular structure and function 3–6 months postpartum, despite resolution of systemic inflammation. Mechanistically, our preclinical HDP mouse model demonstrates that reduced antenatal progesterone, also observed in patients with HDPs, drives inflammation and postpartum cardiac dysfunction. Antenatal (embryonic day 14.5), but not postpartum (postpartum day 28), progesterone treatment prevented postpartum cardiac dysfunction, identifying both a potential mechanistic and therapeutic strategy to reduce long-term maternal cardiovascular morbidity. Bert et al. show that inflammatory alterations associated with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy are linked to persistent postpartum cardiac dysfunction. Combining clinical and mechanistic studies, they identify reduced progesterone as a key driver and suggest antenatal progesterone supplementation as a potential strategy to mitigate long-term maternal cardiovascular risk.

papers.title: Multiparametric assessment of TNNI3 variant phenotypes in human iPSC-cardiomyocytes correlates with disease severity in patients
papers.abstract: Routine genetic testing of patients with cardiomyopathy has identified many causative genetic variants. However, in most instances, the impact of these variants on physiological function and clinical outcomes remains unclear. Here we develop a high-throughput human induced pluripotent stem-cell-based platform to measure the effects of variants in cardiac troponin I (encoded by TNNI3) on systolic and diastolic force generation and calcium handling. By integrating contractility and calcium signaling, we accurately distinguish pathogenic from nonpathogenic TNNI3 variants and characterize the pathogenic effects of variants of uncertain significance. Further, by evaluating the clinical presentations of patients with TNNI3 cardiomyopathy from a single site, we demonstrate that diastolic function in vitro correlates with age at onset (R2 = 0.6), a measure of disease severity. The ability to comprehensively characterize in vitro variant effects that correlate with clinical outcomes should help identify mechanisms underlying variable disease severity and enhance the discovery of class-targeted treatments. Staudt et al. introduce a high-throughput human induced pluripotent stem cell-cardiomyocyte platform that links TNNI3 genetic variants to contractile and calcium-handling phenotypes. The approach identifies pathogenic variants, provides evidence of pathogenicity for variants of uncertain significance and correlates functional defects with disease onset.

papers.title: Mechanisms of cardiac dysfunction in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
papers.abstract: Our study combines human clinical and mouse preclinical data to investigate the induction and persistence of cardiac dysfunction during and after pregnancy complicated by hypertensive disorders. We hypothesize that antenatal maternal inflammation drives cardiac dysfunction during pregnancy and contributes to long-term cardiovascular risk among women affected by these high-risk conditions.

papers.title: ZEUS has spoken: lessons for IL-6 inhibition and the road ahead
papers.abstract: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) signaling has been implicated in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), yet neutralizing IL-6 with ziltivekimab did not cut cardiovascular events in patients with ASCVD and chronic kidney disease in the ZEUS clinical trial. I explore possible explanations and implications for immune-targeting strategies in ASCVD.

papers.title: Decoding genetic cardiomyopathy through functional phenotyping
papers.abstract: Multiparametric phenotyping of TNNI3 variants in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes provides a functional link between genetic variation, cardiac dysfunction, and clinical disease severity.

papers.title: Enhanced skin tone and blood estimation through AI-enabled upscaling of discrete reflectance spectra
papers.abstract: Objective quantification of epidermal melanin content and dermal blood volume is crucial for equitable applications in dermatology and in the evaluation and engineering of  optical devices, such as pulse oximeters, where variable amounts of melanin may introduce inaccuracies. Here, we demonstrate a method leveraging diffuse reflectance spectroscopy and a machine-learning framework using fully connected neural networks (FCNNs) to non-invasively estimate melanin and blood indices from sparse data through spectral upscaling. We validated the algorithm on custom phantoms, porcine skin, and in vivo human participants. In phantoms with variable blood and melanin (0–20%), the model achieved high accuracy (R2 > 0.90) to absolute concentrations. In porcine skin, estimated melanin strongly correlated with histology-derived density scores (Pearson r = 0.95). Across six regions of the human hand, the FCNN accurately estimated pigmentation from sparse wavelengths, even during hand-raise challenges that induce confounding blood volume changes. After upscaling, sparse-wavelength estimates strongly correlated with a model using over 450 wavelengths (Pearson r = 0.96), reducing data requirements ~ 150-fold without compromising accuracy. These findings highlight the importance of high-spectral information for disentangling melanin and blood contributions in reflectance spectra and the capacity of machine-learning to restore predictive performance from sparse inputs. These findings demonstrate that artificial-intelligence -driven spectral upscaling can enhance objective skin tone quantification in wearable optical devices.

papers.title: Multicenter benchmarking of large language models for bladder cancer management recommendations from mpMRI reports
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can interpret radiology reports, but their ability to generate guideline-concordant recommendations from bladder cancer multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) reports remains uncertain. Following TRIPOD-LLM, we retrospectively evaluated nine API-accessed LLMs using 590 mpMRI reports from three hospitals under two input conditions: original Chinese reports and clinician-translated, quality-controlled English reports. Two physicians independently rated each model-generated recommendation on a 1–5 ordinal scale. We analyzed 21,240 ratings using patient-level random-intercept cumulative link mixed models, with paired Wilcoxon tests as secondary exploratory analyses. The association between input condition and physician rating differed across LLMs (likelihood-ratio chi-square = 683.05, df = 8, P < 0.001). Compared with original Chinese input, clinician-translated English input was associated with higher ratings for chatgpt-o3-pro (OR 2.79, 95% CI 2.29–3.41), deepseek-v4-flash (OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.19–1.81), claude-opus-4-7 (OR 3.07, 95% CI 2.47–3.82), and gpt-5.5 (OR 1.88, 95% CI 1.53–2.32), but with lower ratings for claude-sonnet-4-5 (OR 0.29, 95% CI 0.23–0.36; all Holm-adjusted P < 0.001). Four LLMs showed no clear input-condition difference. Center-specific contrasts also depended on input condition and were materially unchanged after adjustment for age, sex, pathological T stage, tumor grade, tumor number, and maximum lesion diameter. Inter-rater agreement was substantial (quadratic weighted kappa range, 0.621–0.743). Readability did not track physician-rated recommendation quality. These findings argue against clinician-translated English as a universal optimization strategy and support model-specific validation of input conditions before clinical deployment. LLM-generated recommendations from mpMRI reports are best positioned as clinician-supervised, imaging-based decision support rather than standalone treatment advice.

papers.title: Challenges for human oversight in detecting system malfunctions in AI-assisted medical diagnostics
papers.abstract: Increasingly, physicians must oversee AI systems to detect system malfunctions. We studied 48 physicians in a randomized controlled study using an increasingly malfunctioning AI for cardiac auscultation. Diagnostic performance declined alongside AI reliability, even when physicians were cognitively forced to make an initial classification, and when human performance exceeded AI reliability. Physicians’ confidence declined faster than their trust in AI. Results call for specification of oversight goals and processes ensuring patient safety.
