papers.title: Granular hydrogel bioink for macroporous pancreatic spheroid scaffolds
papers.abstract: Cells positioned more than several hundred microns away from a vascular network experience insufficient oxygen and nutrient supply due to diffusion limitations, leading to compromised viability and impaired function. This challenge is especially relevant in large, engineered 3D constructs which exceed the diffusion limitation of 100–200 µm, resulting in necrotic cores. Granular hydrogels have emerged as a promising approach for tissue engineering due to their inherent porosity. Their interconnected pores can facilitate mass transport of oxygen and nutrients, and therefore support cellular function. In this work, we developed a facile method to prepare bioprintable granular hydrogel bioink containing microparticles with tunable diameters, that can form porous scaffolds with different pore sizes and porosities. The bioink remained shelf-stable for at least 60 d when stored at 4 °C, as determined by the melt temperature. The macroporous granular hydrogel scaffold has inherent void spaces between the hydrogel microparticles, in which spheroids can be embedded. Pancreatic spheroids incorporated into the scaffold showed improved viability compared to free spheroids, indicating the granular microenvironment supports spheroid survival. Furthermore, functional studies of embedded pancreatic spheroids with glucose-stimulated insulin secretion demonstrated preserved insulin secretion functionality. Our approach thus serves as a tunable platform for supporting the culture of functional spheroids and organoids, that has potential regenerative medicine applications in restoration of physiological functions when implanted.

papers.title: Found: a protein that drives ageing without unleashing inflammation
papers.abstract: Aged mice engineered to lack granzyme K have improved heart and liver function and less kidney damage.

papers.title: This little brown mushroom is laced with a hallucinogen — and lethal toxins
papers.abstract: A Florida fungus might combine the psychedelic compound psilocybin with deadly chemicals to defend itself against hungry animals.

papers.title: Who needs sex? Kelp reproduce asexually when no mate is nearby
papers.abstract: Insights into the reproductive modes of brown algae could help in the fight to protect them in warming climate.

papers.title: Author Correction: SLAMF6 as a drug-targetable suppressor of T cell immunity against cancer
Record-breaking Ebola outbreak: phone data reconstruct first weeks of spread
papers.abstract: The Bundibugyo virus strain was circulating for weeks before its detection in May, but was missed owing to surveillance failures, testing gaps and funding cuts, researchers say.

papers.title: Massive atlas of brain region linked to a host of diseases is the most detailed yet
papers.abstract: A global team profiled nearly 26 million brain cells from the basal ganglia to build a cross-species reference database that will help to understand conditions from Parkinson’s disease to addiction.

papers.title: RSV vaccines slash infections: data show jabs’ staggering success against dangerous virus
papers.abstract: Vaccines and monoclonal-antibody injections are cutting hospitalizations linked to the respiratory virus.

papers.title: Daily briefing: Are one-person firms the future of biotech?
papers.abstract: Researchers are debating whether small, AI-enabled biotech companies are the future of drug discovery. Plus, even microplastics still reach the wildlife furthest from humanity and an upgrade to AlphaGenome.

papers.title: Novel CRISPR therapy is poised to gain first FDA approval to alter genes inside the body
papers.abstract: Current gene-editing treatments require removal of a participant’s cells, a complex and costly approach.

papers.title: Scaling medical imaging report generation with multimodal reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: Researchers developed UniRG, a reinforcement learning framework that optimizes clinically aligned composite rewards for medical imaging report generation. UniRG outperforms prior models and demonstrates strong generalization across unseen hospitals and datasets

papers.title: A single NLS directs AGO1 import shaping small RNA loading and silencing outputs in Arabidopsis
papers.abstract: Small RNAs guide ARGONAUTE proteins to their targets. Here the authors identify a pathway controlling AGO1 nuclear import and show that AGO1 subcellular localization shapes small RNA loading and silencing outputs in plants.

papers.title: Autapse-inspired neuromorphic hardware with synapse–neuron integration for bidirectional feedback control
papers.abstract: Inspired by autapses in the nervous system, researchers integrated artificial synapses and neurons to enhance or suppress signals through self-feedback, opening a new path toward autonomous, self-regulating hardware.

papers.title: Thin-film lithium niobate waveguide-integrated p-i-n Tungsten selenide photodiodes with 10Gbit/s data reception
papers.abstract: Thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) is a promising photonic platform, but its integration with 2D materials remains challenging. Here, the authors report the realization of TFLN-based waveguide-integrated WSe 2 photodetectors, showing a 3-dB bandwidth up to 1.12 GHz, up to 10 Gbit/s data rates and responsivity up to 492 mA/W in the visible range.

papers.title: Structural basis of ligand-mediated transition to higher-order rubisco assemblies
papers.abstract: Proteins often assemble into complexes, and while binding partners typically drive this, ligand binding can too. Here the authors show ligand binding drives distinct rubisco assemblies, revealing an evolutionary path to greater structural complexity.

papers.title: Latitude modulates climate-driven maize yield gains across the central U.S. “warming hole”
papers.abstract: Climate change affects crop yield variation across regions and seasons. This study suggests that climate impacts on maize yields shift from losses in the southern U.S. Corn Belt to gains in the north, driven by climate trends, thermal matching, and hybrid selection.

papers.title: Evolution of the molybdenum and vanadium cycles through time and their impact on ancient nitrogen fixation
papers.abstract: Partitioning experiments and Fe-rich sediments show V was removed from Archean– Paleoproterozoic seawater more efficiently than Mo, enriching seawater in Mo relative to V and helping explain the early evolution of Mo-based nitrogenase.

papers.title: Constructing exclusive Pt@WO x interfacial sites enables selective C–O bond activation
papers.abstract: Precisely constructing metal–oxide catalysts with exclusively interfacial active sites remains challenging. Here, glycerol is selectively converted to 1,3-propanediol over catalysts in which Pt exists solely as isolated Pt@WO x interfacial sites.

papers.title: A prefrontal microcircuit computes trial-wise discount of reinforcement during threat learning in male mice
papers.abstract: Neural mechanisms underlying threat learning are not fully understood. Here authors identify a prefrontal circuit that constrains early threat learning in male mice. Local inhibitory neurons may release this constraint, providing a mechanism for regulating how strongly each experience shapes memory.

papers.title: Engineering CAR-Vδ2 T cells to boost persistence and anti-tumor function
papers.abstract: CAR-Vδ2 T cells show promise for cancer immunotherapy, but their efficacy is limited by poor persistence and activation induced cell death. Here, this group propose an engineered CAR-Vδ2 T design that leverages IL18 signaling inducing a durable expansion in vivo.

papers.title: Phylogeographic and functional assembly of population-level bacterial immunity
papers.abstract: In this study, the authors use comparative genomics and cross-infection assays to show a spatially and evolutionarily structured bacterial immune reservoir in which interactions among defense systems can reinforce or undermine phage resistance, refining the pan-immunity framework.

papers.title: Cobalt based anode for highly stable alkaline water electrolysis under operation conditions beyond industrial requirements
papers.abstract: Hydrogen production by alkaline water electrolysis is limited by anode durability under industrial conditions. Here, the authors demonstrate a cobalt–nickel layered double hydroxide anode that sustains operation for over 8,000 h at 1 A cm⁻² in 6 M NaOH at 80 °C, enabling durable hydrogen production.

papers.title: ISG15 promotes PARP inhibitor resistance in BRCA1-deficient cells by facilitating DNA replication and repair
papers.abstract: Despite promising initial responses, BRCA1/2 -mutated cancers treated with PARP inhibitors (PARPi) often develop resistance. Here, the authors show that PARPi-resistant BRCA1-deficient models lose TP53BP1 expression and upregulate factors of the ISGylation machinery, including ISG15, which supports replication fork progression/restart and facilitates homologous recombination-mediated DNA repair, driving PARPi resistance.

papers.title: Emergent stoichiometric host-guest recognition on ligated colloidal surfaces via dynamic ligand reorientation
papers.abstract: Physical adsorption on ligand-protected colloidal nanoparticles is central to their properties and applications, yet adsorption events on dynamic ligand shells are rarely characterized with molecular precision. Here the authors show that molecular adsorption can trigger stoichiometric host-guest recognition through dynamic ligand reorientation.

papers.title: scMomer: a pretraining framework for inferring robust cellular representations from single-cell transcriptomes
papers.abstract: Here, the authors develop scMomer, a pretraining framework that infers multimodal-aware cellular representations from scRNA-seq data alone. By distilling chromatin accessibility knowledge, the authors show that this method can be applied to different downstream single-cell tasks.

papers.title: SIP-enabled multi-omics reveals soil microbiome responses to drought and rehydration
papers.abstract: This study demonstrates that soil microbial growth rates are extremely slow under dry conditions, with rehydration causing a rapid increase in anabolic activity within days. These findings refine our understanding of microbial contributions to soil carbon cycling with a warming climate.

papers.title: Extinction risks in deep-sea populations revealed by genomic data and ecological niche modeling
papers.abstract: Here authors use genomic data to reveal indicators of elevated extinction risk in Gulf of Mexico mesopelagic species. Together with projected declines in habitat suitability, these findings raise the possibility of a broader, unnoticed crisis.

papers.title: Epigenetic gatekeeping enables genome-scale horizontal gene transfer in eukaryotic cells
papers.abstract: Aoki et al . show that mammalian cells can acquire and retain chromosome-scale DNA from algae. The study reveals that host DNA methylation helps establish and maintain foreign DNA, offering insight into gene transfer between distant species.

papers.title: Proximal redox coupling enables oxidation damping for stable water electrolysis
papers.abstract: The design of atomically precise catalysts requires strategies that regulate their electronic and structural dynamics under operating conditions. While conventional doping can effectively tune bulk materials, it translates poorly to single-atom catalysts (SACs), in which isolated atoms lack extended coordination and are prone to oxidative instability. Here we design atomically dispersed Ru−O−Cr motifs that enable oxidation damping during acidic oxygen evolution. In situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy shows attenuated Ru oxidation synchronized with anticorrelated and partially reversible Cr redox evolution, consistent with proximity-dependent redox coupling. This buffered redox response is accompanied by bounded and partially reversible changes in the local metal−oxygen coordination environment. These coupled dynamics support proximity-coupled Ru−O−Cr redox units, enabling a 55.7-fold increased resistance against oxidation-induced Ru dissolution compared with conventional SACs. In proton exchange membrane water electrolysis, catalysts incorporating proximal Ru−O−Cr configurations exhibit degradation rates that are 6.8-fold and 14.4-fold lower than those of Ru SACs and commercial RuO2, respectively, at 1 A cm−2. These results suggest proximal oxidation damping as a potential design principle for stabilizing atomically precise electrocatalysts. Single-atom catalysts can mitigate reliance on scarce noble metals, but isolated sites can be fragile. Here a catalyst with proximal Ru−O−Cr motifs is fabricated that demonstrates proximal oxidation damping where the Cr neighbour buffers Ru overoxidation, improving stability for acidic oxygen evolution.

papers.title: A smart display woven on your sleeve
PANGEA: an integrated cell atlas across diverse biological contexts enables systematic profiling of multicellular responses in human diseases
papers.abstract: Diseases affect multiple cell types within tissues, but the overall landscape of the multicellular responses in human diseases remains largely unexplored. Here we categorize the multicellular responses of human diseases based on a remapped atlas of human cells, PANGEA, incorporating 12.6 million cells acquired from a pipeline that automatically processes raw sequence files from public repositories. We constructed a hierarchical cell classification framework comprising 32 major cell types and 165 cellular subtypes. On the basis of this annotation framework, we explored an extensive atlas of human cells containing 46.5 million cells from 160 diseases across 48 organs and revealed core archetypes of human diseases repeatedly found across organs. We show that this cell atlas could also serve as a reference for unbiased analysis in spatial transcriptomics, revealing spatial features associated with immunotherapy responses. Collectively, our study provides foundational resources for cell ontologies, enabling cross-tissue comparisons of cellular features in human diseases. PANGEA is a comprehensive single-cell transcriptomic atlas of 160 human diseases across 48 organs.

papers.title: A comprehensive analysis of CBER experience with AAV gene therapy IND submissions
papers.abstract: An analysis of Investigational New Drug (IND) submissions to the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) from 1995 to 2025 reveals a rapid growth in adeno-associated virus (AAV) development over three decades and highlights common reasons for regulatory holds that should be considered for successful product development.

papers.title: High-pressure phase transitions, electrical conductivity and recoverability of uranium polyhydrides
papers.abstract: The uranium-hydrogen system has been predicted to form numerous polyhydride compounds, exhibiting diverse physical properties. However, experiments report starkly conflicting results regarding synthesis pressures, stoichiometries, and stability, leaving their fundamental properties and even their existence uncertain. Through a series of laser-heated diamond anvil cell experiments, we systematically investigate the high-pressure phase diagram of the uranium-hydrogen system up to 99(3) GPa using synchrotron powder X-ray diffraction. Compression and laser heating of β-UH3 at pressures of 41(1) and 91(3) GPa result in the formation of hcp-UH7 and fcc-UH8, respectively. Upon decompression of hcp-UH7 below 27(1) GPa, we observe decomposition into hcp-UH5, which subsequently further dehydrogenates to U4H15 below 12(1) GPa. The U4H15 compound, analogous to the well-known Th4H15, is recoverable to ambient pressure and temperature, and slowly oxidizes over the timescale of hours. Whilst all compounds are metallic, electrical resistance measurements demonstrate an absence of superconductivity upon cooling to 3 K in U4H15, hcp-UH5, and hcp-UH7, and to 7 K in fcc-UH8. The uranium-hydrogen system has the potential to host numerous polyhydride compounds with diverse properties, but there are conflicting experimental data on their synthesis and stability. Here, the authors use laser-heated diamond anvil cell experiments and synchrotron X-ray diffraction to map the uranium-hydrogen high-pressure phase diagram, revealing new phases and their properties, with implications for understanding hydrogen-rich materials.

papers.title: Membrane-coupled conformational switching of VISTA regulates CC′ loop accessibility and immune checkpoint signaling
papers.abstract: V-domain immunoglobulin suppressor of T-cell activation (VISTA) is an immune checkpoint that suppresses T-cell responses and has emerged as a promising target for cancer immunotherapy. Here we show, using atomistic molecular dynamics simulations of both truncated glycan-free and full-length glycosylated membrane-bound human VISTA, that the extracellular and transmembrane domains remain structurally stable, while the unusually long CC′ loop is stabilized by extensive hydrogen-bonding interactions. Principal component analysis and conformational clustering reveal a recurrent rotational motion of the extracellular domain relative to the membrane, producing two conformational states: an “Up” state with a solvent-exposed CC′ loop and a “Down” state in which the loop transiently associates with the membrane. These transitions are coupled to proline-mediated bending of the transmembrane helix. We propose that this membrane-coupled Up/Down switching regulates CC′ loop accessibility, providing a structural mechanism that may influence VISTA-mediated immune checkpoint signaling.

papers.title: Isofalcarintriol ameliorates gestational diabetes mellitus-induced β-cell dysfunction by targeting MIF to enhance mitophagy
papers.abstract: Insulin resistance and pancreatic β-cell dysfunction are closely associated with impaired mitophagy, forming a core pathological mechanism in gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). This study investigates the role of isofalcarintriol (IFT), a carrot-derived polyacetylene, in regulating mitochondrial function in GDM-related β-cells. Here, we use a high-fat diet-induced C57BL/6 J pregnant mouse model and high-glucose/palmitic acid (HG/PA)-treated MIN6 β-cells; IFT ameliorates hyperglycemia and insulin resistance, promotes β-cell maturation and proliferation, induces mitophagy, and enhances β-cell antioxidant capacity. Mechanistically, IFT promotes the dissociation of macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) from ubiquitin-specific protease 7 (USP7) through its C224 residue, and induces MIF ubiquitination through F50/L59 residues, thereby driving the phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN)-induced kinase 1 (PINK1)/Parkin-mediated mitophagy and pancreatic injury recovery. A mitophagy inhibitor eliminates the beneficial effects of IFT, while PINK1 knockdown reverses the mitophagy-promoting effect induced by MIF knockdown. This study reveals IFT as a potent antioxidant protecting β-cells against GDM-induced injury through MIF, highlighting its potential value in GDM treatment.

papers.title: A covariance-aware variational generative model preserving gene correlation structure in single-cell transcriptomic data
papers.abstract: Measuring gene activity in individual cells reveals the diversity within tumors but is costly, technically noisy, and often captures too few rare cells. Computer-generated cells could fill these gaps. Here we show, across two independent groups of pancreatic cancer patients, that a deep generative model produces realistic synthetic cells. Explicitly modeling correlations within the model’s compressed description of each cell does not improve preservation of gene-gene relationships over a simpler matched model, which appears to capture this structure implicitly. Nevertheless, the model’s sampling strategy yields cells that faithfully reproduce gene activity patterns, cell-type markers, and cellular organization and compare favorably with established methods. The model trains 100 to 1,000 times faster than a diffusion-based alternative. Synthetic cells blend with real data and support standard analyses, including reconstruction of a precancerous transition. These findings support using synthetic cells to enrich rare populations, benchmark methods, and simulate transitional states in tumors.

papers.title: Salvage of host-derived geranylgeraniol limits fosmidomycin efficacy in murine Plasmodium berghei malaria
papers.abstract: Despite promising preclinical activity, fosmidomycin has shown limited clinical efficacy against malaria. It inhibits the methylerythritol 4-phosphate (MEP) pathway, which supplies precursors for farnesyl and geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (FPP, GGPP) synthesis and protein prenylation. In vitro, fosmidomycin toxicity is transiently rescued by exogenous prenols such as geranylgeraniol (GGOH) via a Plasmodium prenol kinase (PolK)-dependent salvage pathway, suggesting that host-derived isoprenoid salvage limits drug efficacy. Here we show that PolK-deficient Plasmodium berghei (ΔPbPolK) parasites remain viable but cannot use exogenous prenols, rendering murine infections more responsive to fosmidomycin. In P. falciparum, PolK loss caused metabolic remodeling, including altered glycolysis and increased isoprenoid biosynthesis. Accordingly, pharmacological inhibition of PolK by geraniol blocked GGOH utilization and potentiated fosmidomycin in vitro and in vivo. These findings identify prenol salvage as a mechanism by which malaria parasites exploit host-derived prenols, link it to glycolytic and isoprenoid regulation, and reveal it as a constraint on fosmidomycin efficacy, with implications for antiparasitic strategies targeting isoprenoid-dependent pathways.

papers.title: Multi-omics analyses reveal dynamic interactions between DNA methylation and transcriptional regulation during black raspberry ripening
papers.abstract: Fruit ripening is a complex developmental process involving coordinated changes in gene expression, metabolism, and epigenetic regulation. How DNA methylation dynamics influence gene transcription and metabolite accumulation during black raspberry (Rubus occidentalis) fruit ripening remains poorly understood. Here, we performed developmental-series transcriptome, methylome, and metabolome analysis; the results from this analysis reveal extensive epigenetic reprogramming during black raspberry fruit ripening. Fruit tissues exhibit globally higher DNA methylation than leaves, particularly in CHG and CHH contexts. Local methylation in all cytosine contexts progressively decreases in promoter regions during ripening, whereas CHG and CHH methylation increase in transposon-rich regions. Two primary methylation transitions—promoter hypomethylation and CHH hypermethylation—govern transcriptional shifts in genes involved in ripening processes. Methyl-binding transcription factors with activation potential likely promote CHH hypermethylation-linked transcriptional activation. Multi-omics integration reveals that coordinated anthocyanin accumulation parallels expression of biosynthetic and regulatory genes within coherent networks. Elevated non-CG methylation in heterochromatin coincides with increased transcription of histone variants mediating chromatin compaction, suggesting chromatin remodelers fine-tune accessibility for methyltransferases. Our study highlights both genome-wide and locus-specific epigenetic reprogramming and demonstrates a coordinated interplay between DNA methylation and transcriptional regulation during black raspberry fruit ripening.

papers.title: Author Correction: Diversification of the 10th core atom of 9-cyanopyronins expands the resonance Raman vibrational palette
Crystallinity control of spin torque efficiency in CuNi alloys
papers.abstract: Light metals are gaining increasing attention in spintronics due to their advantageous properties over traditional heavy metals. This work investigates the origin of large spin torque efficiency (ξSOT) in CuNi alloys using spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance in FeNi/CuNi bilayers. Polycrystalline CuNi shows a ξSOT comparable to heavy metal Pt. By controlling crystallinity, we observe a significant modulation of ξSOT, as epitaxial CuNi (001) and (111) films exhibit similar but markedly lower values than their polycrystalline counterparts. This suggests that the charge-spin conversion in CuNi is strongly influenced by crystallinity and primarily dominated by extrinsic scattering. Temperature-dependent studies further support a dominant contribution from extrinsic scattering in both paramagnetic and ferromagnetic phases, with minimal contribution from spin fluctuations across the Curie temperature. Our findings deepen the understanding of charge-spin interconversion in light metals and highlight their potential for spintronic applications.

papers.title: Towards high-capacity and robust free-space optical communications
papers.abstract: Free-space optical communication is emerging as a cornerstone technology for next-generation wireless networks, driven by the escalating demand for fiber-optic-level data rates in applications ranging from data center interconnects to satellite and deep-space communications. Despite its substantial theoretical capacity advantage, reliable long-distance optical links remain challenging because of atmospheric turbulence, pointing and tracking inaccuracies, and stringent power budgets. These impairments are becoming increasingly intertwined with advanced modulation formats and various multiplexing techniques aimed at boosting throughput. In this Review, we examine the interplay between increasing capacity and maintaining reliability under turbulence in long-distance, high-capacity optical systems. We trace the evolution of the field from carrying more information on a single optical carrier to fully integrated, multi-dimensional multiplexing architectures. Key strategies for mitigating atmospheric impairments are analyzed, and we conclude by highlighting the major challenges and future opportunities. Free-space optical communication promises fiber-like data rates for next-generation wireless networks. This Review examines the interplay between capacity and reliability, covering advanced modulation, multidimensional multiplexing and strategies for robust long-distance transmission, and highlights challenges and future opportunities.

papers.title: Discovery and development of antimicrobial polymers
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is among the most pressing healthcare challenges of our time. Multidrug-resistant ‘superbugs’ continue to emerge at an alarming rate, while antibiotic development has stalled in recent decades. Antimicrobial peptides have attracted interest for their potent bactericidal activity and lower propensity to spur resistance; however, translation into clinical practice has been hampered by poor bioavailability, challenging syntheses and limited stability. By contrast, synthetic copolymers mimicking antimicrobial peptides have received attention for their efficacy and synthetic tractability. Here we highlight recent advances in antimicrobial polymer development and discuss future directions for their design and implementation. We also outline future research directions, including the use of machine learning to guide polymer design and the development of scalable production methods that ensure the worldwide accessibility of these materials. Antimicrobial polymers offer an attractive tool for combating the crisis of antimicrobial resistance. This Review highlights recent advances in antimicrobial polymer development and discusses future directions, including the use of machine learning to guide polymer design and the development of scalable production methods to ensure global accessibility of these materials.

papers.title: Optimal learning of quantum channels in diamond distance
papers.abstract: The evolution of quantum states can be described by quantum channels. The task of estimating an unknown quantum channel, known as process tomography, is a central problem in quantum information theory. A long-standing open question is how many uses of an unknown channel are required to learn it to a precision quantified by the standard metric for distinguishing quantum processes, known as the diamond distance. Here we address this by establishing the query complexity of channel tomography with optimal dependence on the dimensions of the input and output spaces and the channel’s Kraus rank at any fixed constant accuracy in diamond distance. We design an algorithm that establishes an upper bound and prove a matching lower bound for learning a channel to the given accuracy. Our algorithm follows the strategy of performing optimal tomography on the Choi-state representation of the process, and we show that channel tomography can be reduced to the well-studied problem of pure-state tomography. As channels subsume states, unitaries and measurements as special cases, our protocol provides a unified framework for tomography of these tasks. Quantum channels can be used to describe the evolution of quantum states, including both unitary evolution and measurement. Now the optimal number of uses needed to learn an unknown channel to any fixed accuracy has been found.

papers.title: Climate risk management must move from hazards to impacts
papers.abstract: The next frontier in climate risk management is not just better hazard detection, but better impact prediction. A five-layer framework could help transform physical observations into forecasts of real-world consequences and more effective responses.

papers.title: Open foundation models for clinical AI
Robust hydrogel ion channels for osmotic energy harvesting and environmental sensing
papers.abstract: Harvesting blue energy from salinity gradients offers a sustainable route to reducing fossil fuel use and expanding clean energy supplies. However, current nanofluidic membranes struggle to balance strength, self-repair and high efficiency simultaneously. Here we report ultratough, self-healing hydrogel ionic channels (HICs) engineered through multicomponent synergy to address these limitations. Featuring continuous nanofluidic networks with over 60% water content, these HICs facilitate rapid ion transport while suppressing concentration polarization. Consequently, they achieve a record power density of 48.57 W m−2 under a standard 0.5 M/0.01 M NaCl gradient—the highest reported for homogeneous membranes—and up to 54.62 W m−2 in natural seawater. The HICs exhibit high mechanical robustness (6.18 MPa tensile strength and 545% elongation) and intrinsic self-healing, enabling >91% recovery of energy efficiency and structural integrity after severe mechanical damage. By integrating HICs into self-powered environmental monitors for real-time air quality and climate tracking, this work provides a battery-free platform that aligns renewable power generation with sustainable ionic technologies. Salinity gradient blue energy offers a promising alternative to fossil fuels. Here the authors develop ultrarough, self-healing hydrogel ionic conductors that achieve an excellent power density while maintaining over 91% of their performance after damage and enable autonomous environmental sensing.

papers.title: Towards practical photosynthetic biohybrid systems
papers.abstract: The transition to a sustainable future has intensified interest in technologies that can convert sunlight into useful fuels and chemicals. Photosynthetic biohybrid systems combine light-harvesting materials with biological catalysts, bringing together the strengths of both abiotic and biological approaches to solar-to-chemical conversion. Although they offer several advantages, their performance remains limited by challenges in charge transfer, mass transport, stability and system integration. Here we examine the working principles governing photosynthetic biohybrid systems, analyse the sources of energy loss and discuss the design strategies and sustainability considerations needed to advance the field towards practical solar-driven chemical manufacturing. Photosynthetic biohybrid systems can convert sunlight to chemicals and fuels. This Perspective explores how to better design photosynthetic biohybrid systems to achieve practical sustainable solar-driven biomanufacturing.

papers.title: Effect of two common GVHD prophylaxis regimens on the gut microbiome in a randomized phase 3 trial
papers.abstract: Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation can cure certain hematological disorders but has many complications. In retrospective studies, low gut microbiome diversity is associated with adverse clinical outcomes. In 2023, the Blood and Marrow Transplant Clinical Trials Network 1703 randomized phase 3 trial demonstrated the superiority of post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy) and mycophenolate mofetil to tacrolimus and methotrexate (Tac/MTX) for graft-versus-host disease prophylaxis in participants with hematological malignancies undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation. Here we report on the microbiome-focused companion study to 1703, Blood and Marrow Transplant Clinical Trials Network 1801, which coenrolled participants and shared trial registration. The primary endpoint was association between microbiome diversity at neutrophil engraftment and non-relapse mortality after 1 year; secondary endpoints included associations with other clinical outcomes and with baseline microbiome diversity. Based on 2575 longitudinally collected stool samples from 304 participants (Tac/MTX n = 147, PTCy n = 157), no association between engraftment microbiome diversity and non-relapse mortality was observed (P = 0.314), not meeting the primary endpoint. Lower baseline microbiome diversity was associated with shorter overall survival (P = 0.007). Safety data were reported in the original 1703 publication. In exploratory analyses, microbiome diversity and absolute microbial load were lower in PTCy compared to Tac/MTX on days 14–28 following HCT, independent of non-prophylaxis antibiotics exposure. Microbial domination events, when a single species exceeds 30% relative abundance, did not differ significantly between study arms and reflected both pathogen blooms and less severe disruptions of the microbial community. Clostridium scindens and secondary bile-acid metabolism pathways were less prevalent in PTCy than in Tac/MTX following HCT. In summary, we find prophylaxis regimens likely exert independent effects on both the microbiome and immune compartments and can also impact their interaction. Understanding whether and how microbiome-targeted interventions might improve transplant outcomes will therefore require careful disentangling of these effects within each specific treatment context. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03959241 . In a prespecified companion study (BMT CTN 1801) of the randomized phase 3 BMT CTN 1703 trial comparing two common GVHD prophylaxis regimens, microbiome diversity at engraftment did not associate with non-relapse mortality, but secondary analyses found baseline microbiome diversity was associated with clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Young people with obesity deserve better care
papers.abstract: The evidence available to support the treatment of obesity in children and adolescents is insufficient and requires rapid improvement.

papers.title: DeepTNR: predicting tumor drug sensitivity from spatial transcriptomics with deep graph contrastive and transfer learning
papers.abstract: Heterogeneity within the tumor microenvironment remains a major obstacle to precision oncology. Although existing drug-sensitivity models can capture transcriptional heterogeneity, they generally do not account for the spatial organization of predicted drug responses. Here, we developed DeepTNR, a spatially resolved framework that integrates tumor-stroma interface features, spatial autocorrelation, and distance-dependent associations between local cellular composition and predicted drug sensitivity. Across nine tumor types, with colorectal cancer (CRC) as a representative example, DeepTNR identified irinotecan as the most sensitive drug and revealed significant spatial autocorrelation in its predicted response patterns. Spatial proximity effect analysis further showed that local enrichment of immune and proliferative programs positively was associated with increased irinotecan sensitivity. Together, these findings demonstrate the potential of DeepTNR to resolve intratumoral therapeutic heterogeneity and identify niche-specific vulnerabilities.
