papers.title: A high-polarity molecular-anchor design for stable high-mobility perovskite transistors
papers.abstract: Perovskite transistors have recently achieved field-effect mobilities comparable with commercial polycrystalline silicon devices, but their practical applications remain limited because of poor operational stability and current–voltage hysteresis caused by ion migration. Unlike in optoelectronic devices, transistors have high gate electric fields that exert strong Coulombic forces on mobile ions, making robust ion-anchoring interactions essential for suppressing field-induced ionic motion. Here we report a data-driven additive design strategy that uses molecular polarity to strengthen binding to mobile ions. We perform the high-throughput screening of fluorinated ammonium-based molecules with dual hydrogen-bonding capability across a compound chemical space comprising >108 molecules and identify 14 candidates that combine high molecular polarity with suitable size. Three of these additives allow us to fabricate transistors with field-effect mobilities exceeding 25 cm2 V−1 s−1, with 4-(trifluoromethyl)-phenethylammonium performing the best, having a mobility of 41.3 cm2 V−1 s−1 and stability over 9,000 on/off switching cycles. Molecular polarity can be used to guide the rational and targeted design of additives that suppress ion migration in metal halide perovskite transistors, leading to mobilities of over 40 cm2 V−1 s−1 and stabilities of over 9,000 on/off cycles.

papers.title: Making van der Waals heterostructures through substitution
Designing additives for perovskite transistors using molecular polarity as a guide
papers.abstract: Molecular polarity can be used as a predictive descriptor to screen potential additives for halide perovskite lattices, allowing robust and high-performance tin-based perovskite transistors to be created.

papers.title: Tensegrity continuum robots enable task-adaptive morphologies for cooperative behaviours
papers.abstract: Robots that can change their morphologies and behaviours for different tasks and environments hold great promise for adaptable, multifunctional systems. Modular reconfigurable robots can achieve such functionalities by docking and rearranging individual units, but most rely on rigid modules that lack structural compliance, resulting in limited capabilities. Continuum robots offer compliance through flexible backbones, yet they cannot self-reconfigure into task-adaptive multi-robot configurations. Here we introduce a modular reconfigurable robot that unifies the advantages of both architectures by combining a tensegrity-based compliant body with claw-based connection mechanisms. Each robot can manipulate and locomote independently, and multiple robots can self-reconfigure into different morphologies (for example, chains, loops, branches) for cooperative manipulation and locomotion. We demonstrate the robots’ capability across diverse tasks and environments, including coordinated object manipulation and transport, multimodal locomotion, and loco-manipulation in real-world scenarios. These results lay a foundation for adaptable and multifunctional robotic collectives, with broad potential applications in manufacturing, space exploration and search-and-rescue operations. Saikot et al. present flexible modular robots that combine locomotion and manipulation in a single unit, then physically connect and collaborate in task-adaptive forms to carry objects, cross gaps and navigate challenging terrain.

papers.title: Advancing multimodal tools to decode organoid complexity
papers.abstract: Organoids are complex, miniaturized three-dimensional structures that replicate key biological features and functions of human tissues and organs. These characteristics make them powerful model systems for investigating tissue and organ development, homeostasis and regeneration; understanding disease mechanisms; and advancing drug development and personalized medicine. To fully harness their potential, it is essential to develop advanced tools capable of comprehensively profiling their intricate composition. In particular, cutting-edge technologies are needed to accurately characterize their genotypic and phenotypic profiles, including DNA, RNA, proteins and physiological functions. In this Review, we examine molecular and functional profiling methods for organoids, providing an overview of emerging techniques, recent advancements, future technologies, key knowledge gaps and challenges, and a framework for multimodal integration of methods. Additionally, we examine current barriers to progress and explore opportunities to refine organoid profiling methods with the aim of deepening our understanding of organoid biology. This Review examines the current state-of-the-art for organoid profiling and existing knowledge gaps in this area.

papers.title: Orientational locking in a turnstile metal–organic framework for cyclohexene/cyclohexane separation
papers.abstract: Efficient separation of benzene, cyclohexene and cyclohexane is industrially critical yet challenging due to their nearly identical physicochemical properties. Discriminating cyclohexene from cyclohexane is particularly formidable, given their almost indistinguishable molecular dimensions. Conventional porous materials relying on static size exclusion or affinity differences fail to efficiently separate this ternary mixture. Here we show that a molecular “turnstile” metal–organic framework featuring –CF3 pairs at pore apertures is capable of the stepwise separation of the ternary mixture through a synergy of thermally controlled pore gating and interaction-induced molecular orientation locking. Temperature-driven rotation of –CF3 enables programmable molecular discrimination: the turnstile admits only benzene at 303 K whereas it opens for cyclohexene at higher temperatures. Electronegative –CF3 groups enforce orientational locking; thus, cyclohexene adopts a planar, diffusion-favorable configuration, whereas cyclohexane is locked in a sterically hindered, eclipsed orientation. This synergy leads to high cyclohexene/cyclohexane selectivity and high-purity products. This work establishes a strategy for adaptive porous materials beyond static sieving, offering a scalable and energy-efficient platform for challenging hydrocarbon purifications. This study presents a metal–organic framework that enables the stepwise ternary separation of benzene, cyclohexene and cyclohexane via two temperature-tuned fixed-bed columns operated at room temperature and higher temperatures, exploiting thermally controlled pore gating and interaction-induced molecular orientational locking for selective discrimination.

papers.title: Turnstile metal–organic framework for the efficient separation of cyclic C<sub>6</sub> hydrocarbons
papers.abstract: The industrial separation of cyclic C6 hydrocarbons is crucial but challenging. Now, a metal–organic framework is developed that features –CF3 pairs at the pore apertures. Through a synergy of thermally controlled pore gating and interaction-induced molecular orientation locking, this ‘turnstile’ metal–organic framework enables the stepwise separation of benzene, cyclohexene and cyclohexane.

papers.title: Using industrial ecology to avoid burden shifting
papers.abstract: Industrial ecology can improve the environmental coherence of low-carbon chemical innovation by avoiding burden shifting across materials, ecosystems, places and time.

papers.title: “Rivet” cations enhance mechanical stability of Ni-rich layered cathode materials for Li-ion batteries
papers.abstract: The Mg2+ and Ni2+ ions at the Li site (A-site) in Ni-rich NMC layered cathode materials improve their cycling stability by reducing intragranular cracking. These cations act as “rivets” due to their ability to suppress gliding of the close-packed layers and associated mechanically-destructive phase transitions. In the present study the impact of the Mg2+ and Ni2+ ions on the mechanical properties of the single-crystal Mg-doped NMC811 materials has been investigated quantitatively with in situ micropillar compression, nanoindentation and pillar splitting in a scanning electron microscope. Here we show that the increase in cumulative occupancy of the “rivet” cations NiA and MgA at the A-site in the layered R$$\bar{3}$$m structure results in an increase of the critical resolved shear stress of the basal {0001} < 11$$\bar{2}$$0> slip system activation, hardness, fracture toughness K1c and Young’s modulus. Density functional theory calculations demonstrate that the Ni/Mg for Li substitution contributes synergistically to the enhancement of mechanical properties in NMC811. Mg²⁺ and Ni²⁺ ions at Li sites enhance Ni-rich NMC stability by acting as structural rivets that suppress layer gliding and cracking. Here, the authors show that Mg²⁺ and Ni²⁺ at Li sites synergistically enhance the mechanical strength and toughness of single-crystal NMC811.

papers.title: Why progress in multi-objective materials design via machine learning depends on integrated data infrastructure
papers.abstract: Machine learning is transforming materials discovery, yet its impact on multi-objective optimisation remains constrained by the structure and quality of input data. Despite the growing use of advanced predictive models, most studies rely on single-property datasets developed for specific purposes and not designed for cross-domain integration. Fragmented descriptors, inconsistent metadata, and missing values prevent models from learning relationships across properties and material classes, limiting effective optimisation. This perspective focuses on data-driven materials informatics (with an emphasis on metal alloys) and contends that progress in multi-objective materials design relies on integrated, reliable data infrastructures that enable cross-domain learning and support practical optimisation. We demonstrate this by unifying fragmented mechanical and corrosion databases into a single resource for multi-objective design of multi-principal element alloys. Machine learning promises accelerated materials discovery, but fragmented and inconsistent datasets continue to limit effective multi-objective optimisation across materials systems. In this Perspective, the authors argue that integrated data infrastructures are essential for cross-domain learning and demonstrate this by unifying mechanical and corrosion databases to enable the multi-objective design of multi-principal element alloys.

papers.title: Oral absorption, bioavailability, and uptake routes of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid derived 17(S)-HDHA, 15(S)-HEPE, RvD1 and RvE1 in healthy rats
papers.abstract: Lipid mediators derived from omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), are critical mediators of inflammation. In contrast to EPA and DHA, the bioavailability of their lipid mediator derivatives remains unstudied. Oral, intravenous (IV), and intraduodenal administration of stable isotope labeled n-3 PUFA, and lipid mediators was used to establish their bioavailability, half-lives, and absorption routes in rats. Blood and lymph were analyzed by liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry. Orally administered 17(S)-HDHA-d5, 15(S)-HEPE-d5, and RvD1-d5 were rapidly absorbed into the unesterified plasma pool, reaching peak concentrations within 15 min to 1 h, with a bioavailability of 3–6%. IV administration revealed rapid plasma clearance of n-3 PUFA and administered lipid mediators (half-life ~30 s). Lymph cannulation reduced plasma appearance of 17(S)-HDHA-d5 and 15(S)-HEPE-d5 but not RvD1-d5, indicating structure-dependent changes in absorption via lymphatic or portal routes. These findings demonstrate n-3 PUFA-derived lipid mediators are absorbed following oral intake, providing a foundation for oral delivery.

papers.title: Lysine 69 deacetylation of NFIC drives autophagy-induced epithelial–mesenchymal transition and chemoresistance in glioblastoma
papers.abstract: Autophagy-induced the deacetylation of NFIC at Lysine 69 site accelerates tumorigenesis by activating FOXK1/HERC3 axis, revealing an acetylation-dependent mechanism that can be targeted by peptide Pe-k69 to overcome TMZ resistance in glioblastoma.

papers.title: Self-paced silent speech brain-computer interface for device control
papers.abstract: Decoding self-paced silent speech via an implanted ECoG BCI enables a participant with ALS to reliably control smart home devices without visual cues.

papers.title: Aging remodels the suprachiasmatic nucleus and weakens ultradian rhythms and activity–temperature coupling
papers.abstract: Aging alters daily physiology, but how these changes relate to remodeling of the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) remains incompletely understood. Here, we examined time-resolved SCN transcriptomic profiles alongside longitudinal recordings of core body temperature and locomotor activity, using separate cohorts for the molecular and physiological analyses. Aging was associated with extensive SCN transcriptomic remodeling, including enrichment of innate immune, interferon-related, complement-associated, and glial programs, while selected canonical clock genes retained detectable rhythmic expression. The composition and temporal profiles of broader rhythmic transcriptional programs also differed between young and aged SCN samples. Aged mice retained detectable circadian rhythms but showed reduced 2–6 h ultradian wavelet power in locomotor activity and body temperature, lower activity–temperature correlations, and altered optimal integration windows and time-of-day-dependent relationships. Histological analyses revealed glial remodeling and reduced neuronal marker-positive cell density in the aged SCN. These findings identify parallel age-associated changes in SCN molecular and cellular organization and in physiological rhythmic power and activity–temperature associations.

papers.title: Dysfunction of hepatic lipid metabolism in mice haploinsufficient for the histone methyltransferase Kmt2c
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction is influenced by various factors including environmental effects and genetic variants, and recent evidence reveals close associations between metabolic dysfunction and neurodevelopmental or neuropsychiatric disorders. However, the mechanistic link between them remains unclear. To clarify these relationships, we utilized mice with haploinsufficiency in the autism spectrum disorder-related gene lysine methyltransferase 2c (Kmt2c) (Kmt2c+/fs mice), in which we previously confirmed significantly less body weight. We characterized body composition, small intestinal transcriptome, fecal metagenome, plasma metabolome, and hepatic mitochondrial morphology and biochemical activity in male Kmt2c+/fs mice and wild-type controls. Hepatic transcriptomic changes and lipid accumulation were also assessed. Group comparisons were performed using two-sided Mann-Whitney U-tests, two-way repeated measures ANOVA, and enrichment analyses with appropriate multiple-testing correction. Here we show that Kmt2c+/fs mice have decreased body mass index and body fat mass. The small intestine and fecal metagenome show minimal alterations, while plasma metabolomic analysis reveals an increase of metabolites related to glucose and amino acid metabolism. Hepatic mitochondria display altered morphology and biochemical activity. The liver of Kmt2c+/fs mice exhibits decreased lipid accumulation and the downregulation of genes related to lipid metabolism, particularly fatty acid synthesis. These findings indicate that KMT2C deficiency triggers functional defects in lipid metabolism in the liver, accompanied by upregulation of glucose and amino acid metabolism and consequently less body weight. The mechanism of metabolic dysfunction observed in neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders largely remains unclear. Lysine methyltransferase 2c (Kmt2c) is one of autism spectrum disorder (ASD)-related genes, and Kmt2c mutant mice exhibit ASD-like phenotypes and less body weight. We precisely analyzed metabolic profiles of Kmt2c+/fs mice, and discovered lower body mass index and decreased fat mass. While these phenotypes were unlikely to be explained by changes in the intestine or gut bacteria, we found changes in morphology and biochemical activity of hepatic mitochondria. The liver of Kmt2c+/fs mice showed decreased lipid accumulation and downregulation of lipid metabolism-related genes. These results provide insight into the onset mechanism of metabolic dysfunction in neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders, especially associated with epigenetic regulations.

papers.title: Conformationally driven negative chemotaxis in synthetic vesicles
papers.abstract: Chemotaxis—directed movement in response to environmental cues—is fundamental to biological systems but remains rare in artificial systems, where it typically relies on complex catalytic pathways or intricate adaptive designs. The molecular mechanisms underlying artificial chemotaxis are still scarce and poorly understood, posing challenges for the rational design of advanced artificial chemotactic systems. Here we present a minimal polymeric system that achieves negative chemotaxis through intrinsic conformational dynamics, enabling mechanical transduction and directional movement without the need for catalysis or external energy input. Our study uncovers a previously unrecognized molecular mechanism in which hydrophobic membrane domains dynamically reconfigure in response to chemical signals, triggering a cascade of events, from conformational rearrangements to interfacial tension alterations that generate self-sustained motile behaviour. By elucidating the interplay between membrane dynamics, interfacial forces and directional transport, our findings advance the molecular understanding of synthetic systems that emulate cytoskeletal remodelling in biological motility and establish a versatile framework for engineering functional artificial protocells with life-like behaviours. Achieving negative chemotaxis without catalytic designs remains challenging in artificial systems. Now it has been shown that intrinsic membrane conformational dynamics generate interfacial tension gradients, driving polymersomes away from a lactic-acid source without requiring external energy input.

papers.title: Retraction Note: Real-time monitoring of reaction stereochemistry through single-molecule observations of chirality-induced spin selectivity
Altermagnetism in a new light
papers.abstract: Altermagnets host spin-split bands despite zero net magnetization. A photonic crystal now reproduces this symmetry-driven phenomenon using circular polarization as a spin analogue.

papers.title: Catalytic enantioselective dual C–H cross-coupling enabled by a radical-buffering strategy
papers.abstract: Enantioselective cross-coupling of two inert C–H bonds represents the pivotal advance long sought in asymmetric synthesis, enabling much more efficient and direct construction of essential chiral molecular scaffolds, including those for therapeutics and agrochemicals. Here, taking advantage of the highly regioselective electrophilic reactivity of arenes, we report an enantioselective formal cross-coupling between aryl C–H and benzylic C–H bonds through a photoredox/copper relay catalysis, enabling efficient access to a diverse array of chiral 1,1-diaryl compounds with excellent enantioselectivity. Mechanistic investigations underscore the critical role of the copper catalyst as a radical buffer. Operating at a higher loading than the chiral ligand, it buffers the transient aryl radical, prolonging its lifetime and suppressing its side reactions, enabling highly efficient asymmetric dual-radical cross-coupling. This protocol exhibits a broad substrate scope and excellent functional-group tolerance, highlighting its practical utility in the streamlined synthesis of bioactive molecules. Photoredox and copper relay catalysis enables enantioselective formal cross-coupling between aryl C–H and benzylic C–H bonds, providing access to a range of chiral 1,1-diaryl compounds. Mechanistic analysis reveals the copper catalyst acts as a buffer for the transient aryl radical intermediate, prolonging its lifetime and suppressing potential side reactions.

papers.title: Aryl radical buffering facilitates asymmetric dual C–H cross-coupling
papers.abstract: A method for the enantioselective cross-coupling of arene and benzylic C–H bonds through photoredox–copper relay catalysis is demonstrated, providing efficient access to diverse chiral 1,1-diaryl compounds with high enantioselectivity. The copper catalyst buffers aryl radicals to prolong their lifetime and suppress side reactions, increasing the efficiency of the method.

papers.title: A non-methylphosphonate process for immediate oxic methane production in stratified freshwaters
papers.abstract: Methane accumulation in oxygenated freshwaters, known as the methane paradox, remains a poorly constrained component of aquatic methane cycling. Although methylphosphonate (MPn) hydrolysis is considered an important pathway for oxic methane production in marine systems, its relevance to freshwaters remains uncertain. Here we identify a rapid oxic methane production process in a seasonally stratified reservoir that occurs within hours and is stimulated by locally derived dissolved organic phosphorus (DOP). Cross-depth incubations showed that DOP-enriched filtrates enhanced methane accumulation, whereas inorganic phosphorus suppressed this response. In contrast, MPn amendments enhanced methane accumulation relative to unamended controls only after a pronounced lag, whereas phosphorus-31 nuclear magnetic resonance (31P-NMR) spectroscopy and metagenomic analyses provided no evidence for abundant MPn or canonical MPn biosynthesis. Together, these results indicate that rapid freshwater oxic methane production is associated with a labile, non-MPn DOP pool, expanding the prevailing MPn-centred view of oxic methane production. Oxic methane production in a freshwater reservoir was rapidly stimulated by a labile dissolved organic phosphorus pool rather than methylphosphonate hydrolysis, indicating an alternative mechanism underlying the methane paradox.

papers.title: Integrating science and transboundary water law when renegotiating The Indus Waters Treaty
papers.abstract: The ongoing conflict between India and Pakistan, heightened by the April 2025 terrorist attack in Pahalgam, Kashmir, has led to an unprecedented abeyance of India’s participation in the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT). Although this treaty has often been described as an example of hydrological cooperation despite regional conflict, it has systemic problems from the perspective of long-term environmental, political and social sustainability. We identify several factors that justify renegotiating and revising the IWT, leveraging multilateral and domestic policy frameworks to formulate a more effective and comprehensive agreement. This includes metrics set forth on transboundary water cooperation under the Sustainable Development Goals (Indicator 6.5.2) as well as a range of international legal guidelines for drafting ecologically viable treaties. We explore the role that nascent regional organizations could play in reducing tensions over the Indus Basin and facilitating new discussions. Ultimately, a reset in the IWT could catalyse broader confidence-building and a lasting peace in a region where two nuclear rivals share a 3,200-km-long contiguous border. The ongoing conflict between India and Pakistan, exacerbated by the April 2025 terrorist attack in Kashmir, has led to India’s unprecedented suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty. A renegotiation of the treaty should leverage international and domestic frameworks to enhance environmental, political and social sustainability, potentially fostering regional peace.

papers.title: Core AI ideas liberate our inquiry into the global water cycle
papers.abstract: The long-term value of artificial intelligence (AI) for water sciences remains the subject of debate. Here we argue that the core ideas underlying AI (rather than specific algorithms) can be integrated with domain knowledge to open new modes of scientific inquiry. We identify eight such core ideas, each offering capabilities difficult to achieve within traditional frameworks. Among these, expressive inductive bias allows architectures to declare what matters most while retaining capacity to learn the unexpected; differentiable programming enables constrained learning of partially known relationships; generative models capture joint distributions supporting conditional inference from fragmented observations; functional mapping learns solution operators providing orders-of-magnitude speedups for simulations; and inference-time computation enables AI to decompose complex problems. These ideas build on AI’s ability to learn useful representations of complex systems. Across many of them, a central mode of inquiry is ‘constrained learning’: posing unknown relationships as learnable components within known physical or conceptual frameworks. Tools built on these ideas can broaden access to reliable water predictions and support important open questions such as land–atmosphere interactions, organizing principles of the waterscape, groundwater sustainability, and human water-use behaviours. Domain insights can also feed back to advance general AI, benefiting the broader sciences. This Perspective argues that AI’s lasting value for water science lies in a number of underlying core ideas, which can be combined with domain knowledge to open new modes of inquiry into the global water cycle.

papers.title: An organic semiconductor-based photocatalyst sheet for overall solar-driven water splitting
papers.abstract: Splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen using sunlight offers a route to renewable fuel, but translating this reaction into systems suitable for industrial implementation remains difficult. Photocatalyst sheets can overcome key limitations of common direct water-splitting approaches (photoelectrochemical devices and photocatalyst dispersions), but existing photocatalyst sheets rely on inorganic semiconductor nanoparticles and processing techniques that can be difficult to scale. Here we show that solution-processed organic semiconductors can form water-splitting photocatalyst sheets by simply tailoring the charge extraction layer beneath the light-absorbing film. A single organic semiconductor active layer (deposited as a bulk heterojunction blend) drives either hydrogen or oxygen evolution depending on its underlying molecular contact, yielding photocathode and photoanode half-cells with well-matched photocurrents. Combining both reactions on one substrate using a microdomain-patterned molecular underlayer affords a photocatalyst sheet that achieves unassisted water splitting under simulated sunlight for over 2 h and generates hydrogen at a stabilized rate of 1.3 µmol h−1 cm−2, which corresponds to a solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency of 0.1%. Solar water splitting offers a route to renewable hydrogen, but developing photocatalyst sheets from scalable, solution-processable materials remains a challenge. Here the authors use underlayer engineering to build an organic semiconductor photocatalyst sheet that enables unassisted overall water splitting under simulated sunlight.

papers.title: Author Correction: Dynamic cycling enhances battery lifetime
Cost-effective climate change mitigation through land sector contributions
papers.abstract: Climate change mitigation from Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) comes with severe sustainability risks and faces major implementation challenges. Yet, the consequences of missing out on AFOLU mitigation potential for the transition of the energy sector and the achievability of climate objectives are not well understood. Here, using the Integrated Assessment Modeling framework REMIND–MAgPIE, we derive future mitigation pathways under different AFOLU policy portfolios. We show that, without AFOLU contributions to mitigation, limiting warming to 1.5 °C is out of reach within the twenty-first century and for keeping peak warming below 1.7 °C consumption loss relative to a current-policy baseline increases from 1.3% to 3.5%. A portfolio of options alleviates the burden of energy sector decarbonization and substantially reduces energy price markups, but puts the AFOLU sector under stress. We show that prudent policy measures, such as limiting total bioenergy use to 100 EJ yr−1 and restricting CH4 and N2O pricing to US$75 per tonne of CO2 equivalent, can largely attenuate this pressure by reducing the need for yield increases and diminishing food price markups without severely compromising the achievability of climate targets. Our findings highlight both the need for effective climate action in the AFOLU sector and the importance of balanced and judicious sectorally aligned policies. Land-based mitigation can substantially lower the cost of climate action and ease energy sector decarbonization. Modelled pathways show that limiting warming to 1.5 °C becomes unattainable without land sector contributions, although sustainability trade-offs require careful policy design.

papers.title: Normalized membrane ratio of TROP2 as a predictor of clinical outcomes with datopotamab deruxtecan in non-small-cell lung cancer
papers.abstract: Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd)—a trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2)-directed antibody–drug conjugate—has demonstrated efficacy in patients with advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) ± actionable genomic alterations. However, TROP2 expression by pathologist assessment using conventional immunohistochemistry with visual scoring does not predict response to TROP2-directed antibody–drug conjugates in NSCLC. We developed TROP2 quantitative continuous scoring (QCS)—a fully supervised computational pathology approach that quantifies TROP2 expression in individual NSCLC cells and subcellular components from immunohistochemistry-stained slides. Using QCS to determine TROP2 expression at the tumor cell membrane and cytoplasm, normalized membrane ratio (NMR) was developed (ratio of membrane relative to membrane + cytoplasmic TROP2) in the biomarker-evaluable population of patients with advanced NSCLC in the TROPION-PanTumor01 study (n = 115). The TROP2 NMR cut-point was optimized and validated in patients with nonsquamous NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations (primary intended-use population, n = 221) in the biomarker-evaluable population (n = 352) of the TROPION-Lung01 trial. Association with clinical outcomes was assessed. Progression-free survival was longer in Dato-DXd-treated (median 7.2 versus 4.0 months; hazard ratio 0.40, 95% confidence interval 0.25–0.64) but not docetaxel-treated (median 4.1 versus 4.4 months; hazard ratio 0.94, 95% confidence interval 0.59–1.49) patients with TROP2 NMR-positive versus TROP2 NMR-negative samples (treatment by biomarker status interaction P = 0.0098), indicating that TROP2 NMR may be a predictive biomarker for Dato-DXd. This work developed and validated a computational pathology biomarker—the TROP2 normalized membrane ratio—that quantifies subcellular TROP2 localization and predicts improved progression-free and overall survival with datopotamab deruxtecan in patients with nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer lacking actionable genomic alterations.

papers.title: Lessons from recent investigator-initiated trials of gene-editing therapies in China
papers.abstract: Several deaths during trials of experimental cell and gene therapies in China appear to reveal gaps in governance and oversight. A new layer of independent external review is needed for clinical supervision of high-risk therapies.

papers.title: Optimizing release dynamics of bone-derived nanoparticles for enhanced in vivo fluorescence monitoring and bone regeneration in craniofacial repair
papers.abstract: Craniofacial bone defects, particularly alveolar clefts, pose significant clinical challenges in pediatric patients due to complex anatomy and the limitations of current grafting options. Although autologous bone grafts remain the clinical gold standard, their use is restricted by donor-site morbidity, limited tissue availability, high cost, and risks such as infection, chronic pain, and functional impairment. Decellularized and demineralized bone matrix (DDBM) offers an attractive alternative but lacks controlled drug-release capability and cannot be monitored in real time in patients. To address these limitations, we developed indocyanine green–encapsulated bone-derived nanoparticles (ICG/BPs) from porcine DDBM, combining the intrinsic osteoinductive and osteoconductive properties of DDBM with near-infrared (NIR) imaging functionality. In this study, we fabricated two ICG/BP formulations, crosslinked (X-ICG/BP) and uncrosslinked (UnX-ICG/BP), and compared their in vitro degradation, release profiles, and in vivo performance in a rat model of cavity-type alveolar defects. Crosslinking improved particle stability and prolonged ICG release, and NIR imaging enabled real-time, non-invasive monitoring of particle degradation and retention within the defect. Additionally, both ICG/BP formulations supported bone regeneration, with X-ICG/BPs demonstrating greater regeneration, tissue organization, and vascularization. Overall, these findings highlight the tunability and theranostic potential of ICG/BPs and support their continued development as an image-guided functional biomaterial for craniofacial bone repair.

papers.title: Pico-X: a 24.9 nanowatt microcontroller for long-duration autonomous operation in flexible landing-pad sensor networks
papers.abstract: Researchers present Pico-X, a programmable microcontroller designed for sparse event-driven sensing. Operating at nanowatt power levels, it enables long-duration autonomous monitoring and reliable event detection in distributed flexible sensor networks.

papers.title: Cryo-EM reveals conserved baseplate-architecture and distinct accessory-protein assemblies in mycobacteriophages Claus, Corndog and Mysterious
papers.abstract: Atomic-resolution structures of three mycobacteriophages reveal a conserved baseplate core decorated by diverse accessory proteins, showing how related siphophages build distinct baseplate architectures from a common structural core.

papers.title: A lactate-fatty acid loop drives prostate cancer bone colonization by mediating metabolic interplay between tumor cells and osteoblasts
papers.abstract: Bone metastases in advanced prostate cancer remain difficult to treat and are associated with poor outcomes. Here, the authors show that bone-colonizing prostate tumor cells exploit lactate uptake via MCT1 to fuel tumor growth and promote osteogenesis, identifying MCT1 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: The representational geometry of cognitive maps under cognitive control
papers.abstract: The brain organizes relationships between entities into cognitive maps. Here, the authors show that complementary stable and context-dependent representational geometries balance stability and behavioral flexibility, with their geometry shaped by cognitive control.

papers.title: Electric vehicle battery materials supply disruptions can be mitigated with chemistry changes and recycling
papers.abstract: This study shows that disruptions in US battery materials supply could cost tens of billions of dollars. However, feasible changes in battery chemistry and increasing recycled lithium supply largely reduce the consequences of the disruptions.

papers.title: Toward personalized deep brain stimulation via white matter stimulation and microstructure in depression
papers.abstract: A study of 51 patients receiving deep brain stimulation for treatment-resistant depression shows that individual white matter stimulation and integrity jointly influence antidepressant response, supporting more personalized neuromodulation strategies.

papers.title: High-entropy alloy aerogels promote selective glycerol oxidation to tartronate at industrial current densities
papers.abstract: The production of tartronate from glycerol electrooxidation is limited by low selectivity at industrial-scale current densities. Here, the authors report a PtCuCoCeSn high-entropy alloy aerogel for regulated glycerol adsorption, enabling 81.4% selectivity and stable operation up to 240 hours.

papers.title: Global environmental genomics reveals vast uncultivated protist diversity and taxonomic blind spots
papers.abstract: In this study, the authors analyze over 30,000 assembled metagenomes across ecosystems to uncover hidden protist diversity, including major novel uncultivated lineages, and reveal their habitats and connections to other microbes.

papers.title: A national baseline for methane sink habitats and methanotroph diversity
papers.abstract: In this study, the authors use metagenomics to map the diverse and previously unknown bacteria responsible for taking up methane across Denmark’s varied environments and highlight the natural habitats and methanotroph species with the potential for methane mitigation.

papers.title: Temporal dynamics of premenstrual dysphoric disorder revealed through predictive symptom networks
papers.abstract: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder causes cyclical mental symptoms, but how these symptoms unfold over time is not yet understood. This study reveals temporal patterns and identifies anxiety as a promising treatment target.

papers.title: Prospective and genetic analyses implicate lower immunosurveillance in the aetiology of prostate cancer
papers.abstract: Role of specific immune and inflammation-related pathways and protein markers in the development of prostate cancer remains to be elucidated. Here the authors show evidence for potential protective role of dendritic cell mediated immunosurveillance, with protective associations with immune and inflammation related proteins measured more than seven years before diagnosis.

papers.title: Conserved molecular properties of dissolved organic matter during Weddell Sea Deep Water formation
papers.abstract: The study reveals that molecular properties of dissolved organic matter are conserved during dense-water formation in the Weddell Sea, showing that Antarctic shelf processes minimally affect the dissolved organics exported into the deep ocean.

papers.title: Soft polymer coatings form hard directional bonding
papers.abstract: Soft polymer coatings spontaneously rearrange on nanosphere surfaces to form directional bonds, unlocking an alternative route to delicate nanoparticle superlattices.

papers.title: In situ profiling of plasma cell clonality with image-based single-cell transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Image-based single-cell transcriptomics can identify diverse cell types in intact tissues. However, in adaptive immunity, V(D)J recombination generates unique immune receptors in cells of the same type, leading to important functional variation that is not yet defined by these methods. Here we introduce B cell receptor multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (BCR-MERFISH), which measures plasma cell clonality based on V gene usage in combination with transcriptome profiling. We demonstrate that BCR-MERFISH accurately identifies V gene usage in cell culture and in mice with restricted or native plasma cell diversity. We then use BCR-MERFISH to elucidate the microbiota-dependent changes in plasma cell abundance, clonal diversity, and public clonotype usage in the mouse gut and the non-uniform distribution of plasma cell clones along the mouse ileum. Given that tissue context is an essential modulator of plasma cell dynamics, we anticipate that BCR-MERFISH may offer new insights into a wide range of immunological questions. BCR-MERFISH enables tracking of plasma cell clones by combining V gene-specific detection with spatial transcriptomics.

Ionic-liquid-assisted room-temperature dry etching of metal–organic frameworks
papers.abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are functional nanoporous materials with high surface areas exhibiting great promise for diverse device applications. However, their beam-sensitive structure renders them highly susceptible to electron and ion beam damage, leading to decomposition during etching and hindering fine patterning. In this study, we developed a simple method for room-temperature dry etching of this fragile class of materials. By infiltrating MOFs with ionic liquids, their mechanical stability is greatly improved, and the damage from electron and ion beams is reduced, achieving harmless ion beam etching. Using this method, fine patterning of MOFs with sub-100-nm precision was successfully accomplished at room temperature. The influence of ionic liquid type on the dry etching properties of MOFs was studied, and possible damage mechanisms were suggested, involving reduction of Cu2+ to Cu+ and cleavage of the Cu–O bond. Metal–organic frameworks are promising nanoporous materials, but their sensitivity to electron and ion beams limits fine patterning. Here, the authors developed a room-temperature dry-etching method for metal–organic frameworks by infiltrating them with ionic liquids, improving beam resistance and enabling sub-100 nm patterning while elucidating possible damage mechanisms.

papers.title: AI-guided human-in-the-loop inverse design of high performance engineering structures
papers.abstract: Inverse design tools such as Topology Optimization (TO) can achieve new levels of improvement for high-performance engineered structures. However, widespread use is hindered by high computational times and a black-box nature that inhibits user interaction. Human-in-the-loop TO approaches are emerging that integrate human intuition into the design generation process. However, these rely on the time-consuming bottleneck of iterative region selection for design modifications. To reduce the number of iterative trials, this contribution presents an AI co-pilot that uses machine learning to predict the synthetic user’s preferred regions. The prediction model is configured as an image segmentation task with a U-Net architecture. It is trained on synthetic datasets where human preferences either identify the longest topological member or the most complex structural connection. The model successfully predicts plausible regions for modification and presents them to the user as AI recommendations. The synthetic human preference model demonstrates generalization across diverse and non-standard TO problems and exhibits emergent behavior outside the single-region selection training data. Demonstration examples show that the new human-in-the-loop TO approach that integrates the AI co-pilot can improve manufacturability or improve the linear buckling load by 39% while only increasing the total design time by 15 sec compared to conventional simplistic TO. Overall, this framework demonstrates how AI co-pilots can eliminate iterative bottlenecks in interactive design, establishing a scalable foundation for real-time, preference-aligned human-AI collaboration in high-performance engineering. Dat Quoc Ha and colleagues develop an AI co-pilot framework integrating machine learning into human-in-the-loop topology optimization to predict user-preferred structural regions for interactive modification. This approach eliminates iterative selection bottlenecks, boosting linear buckling load by 39% or enhancing manufacturability with minimal added computational time.

papers.title: Author Correction: Electronics-free, ultra-low-power, wearable sensor chip for high-frequency electromagnetic field detection
Advances in engineered 3D cardiac tissue for functional biosensing, disease modeling, and regenerative medicine
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) engineered cardiac tissues are miniaturized in vitro cardiac models to recapitulate essential aspects of native heart physiology for applications in drug testing, disease modeling and regenerative therapy. Building on advances in microfabrication, biomaterials, bioelectronics and stem cell biology, these systems reproduce myocardial architecture, mechanical dynamics, electrical conductivity, and disease-specific phenotypes. Existing reviews treat biofabrication, biomaterials, functional biosensing, disease modeling, and cardiac regenerative therapy as separate topics, while few have framed these components within a unified micro- and nanoengineering framework that links tissue architecture, functional biosensing, and application-driven performance. This review addresses this gap by highlighting recent advances in biofabrication strategies for precise control over tissue architecture and cellular microenvironments and discusses the incorporation of microelectronic, optical, and mechanical biosensors for real-time, multiparametric monitoring of tissue contractility and electrophysiological activity. We further summarize representative applications in disease modeling such as cardiomyopathies, ischemic injury, and drug-induced cardiotoxicity, as well as the development of bioengineered cardiac constructs and patches as transplantable grafts to restore myocardial function. Finally, key challenges and future directions toward predictive, scalable, and translational cardiac microphysiological systems are discussed.

papers.title: Trade-offs among selection regimes shape trait evolution and resilience in three-guild networks
papers.abstract: Eco-evolutionary feedbacks can alter species traits and reshape ecological networks, influencing network resilience to disturbance. Here we combine ecological dynamics, trait evolution and interaction rewiring in a three-guild adaptive network to test how biotic (antagonistic and mutualistic) and abiotic (environmental) selection pressures interact to shape community structure and stability. We focus on how different selection regimes affect trait directionality, functional diversity, temporal variability and network resilience. We find that weak trait directionality, high functional turnover and variability, and strong resilience are tightly linked. The greatest trait variability and resilience arise when antagonistic and environmental selection pressures are symmetrical. In species-rich communities, fluctuating selection emerges naturally, while dominance of antagonistic pressure consistently dampens trait directionality. Coupled ecological and evolutionary processes favour trait matching and generate both nested and modular network structures. Compared with bipartite antagonistic networks, network architecture plays a weaker role in shaping trait coevolution in three-guild systems. Together, these results show how trade-offs among antagonistic, mutualistic and environmental selection pressures govern trait evolution and resilience in complex ecological networks.

papers.title: Altered developmental profile of the head-direction signal in a rat model of fragile X syndrome
papers.abstract: Fragile X Syndrome is a common inherited, monogenic cause of intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, but the altered neural mechanisms underlying it remain unclear. Here, we investigate the development of the head-direction system in a rat model of Fragile X Syndrome (Fmr1-/y rats) through electrophysiological recordings in the postsubiculum during exploration and sleep. Surprisingly, juvenile Fmr1-/y rats exhibited enhanced head-direction tuning and increased stability of the head-direction signal in relation to the external environment. Sharper intrinsic head-direction tuning persisted in rapid eye movement sleep.  In contrast, adult Fmr1-/y rats exhibited normal intrinsic head-direction tuning but its stability in relation to the external world was impaired. These findings suggest a transient improvement of head-direction coding in juvenile Fmr1-/y rats, followed by a degradation of tuning stability in adulthood, mirroring the developmental regression often observed in neurodevelopmental conditions including Fragile X Syndrome. Overall, our work reveals systems-level dysfunctions in a rat model of Fragile X Syndrome and their developmental trajectories.

papers.title: Sex-specific disease association and genetic architecture of retinal vascular traits in the UK Biobank
papers.abstract: Sex-stratified analyses of retinal vascular traits in the UK Biobank cohort reveal differences in disease associations, prognostic value, and genetic architecture, including an X-chromosome association for retinal vascular phenotypes.

papers.title: Exceptional preservation reveals the deep-time reproductive ecology and trophic breadth of Early Cretaceous viviparid gastropods
papers.abstract: Direct empirical evidence regarding the reproductive biology and trophic strategies of ancient freshwater invertebrates remains scarce due to the typical loss of internal anatomical and dietary records. Here, we report an exceptionally preserved assemblage of the freshwater snail ‘Viviparus’ sp. from the Lower Cretaceous (c. 120 Ma) Kitadani Formation, central Japan. High-resolution X-ray micro-computed tomography and microfossil extraction reveal key ecological adaptations: obligate ovoviviparity with up to 16 embryonic shells showing an axial developmental size gradient within the maternal body whorl, female-biased sexual size dimorphism, and continuous indeterminate growth. Analyses of gastrointestinal residues and taphonomic associations further indicate trophic flexibility (epilithic microalgal grazing, suspension feeding, and detritivory) alongside opportunistic microhabitat use within articulated unionid bivalves. This high-fidelity preservation—retaining delicate embryonic shells, intact protoconchs, and organic residues—is linked to a distinctive taphonomic window, wherein alkaline ash from palaeo-wildfires is inferred to have buffered ambient freshwater acidity, mitigating post-mortem carbonate dissolution. Our findings demonstrate that modern-type viviparid reproductive and feeding adaptations were already established by the Early Cretaceous, illustrating how wildfire-mediated geochemical buffering can preserve rare biological records in Mesozoic limnic ecosystems.

papers.title: Chain-length-selective cooperative assembly underlies β-glucan recognition by Dectin-1
papers.abstract: Lectin receptors recognize specific glycan features within heterogeneous glycan populations to initiate immune signaling, yet how defined signals are extracted from structurally diverse ligand mixtures remains poorly understood. Here we report the molecular basis by which the innate immune receptor Dectin-1 recognizes the soluble β-glucan laminarin. Native mass spectrometry revealed that laminarin exists as heterogeneous chains spanning a degree of polymerization (DP) of 22–44, while Dectin-1 is strictly monomeric in solution. Isotopic mass tagging with uniformly ¹³C-labeled Dectin-1 established a preferred 3:3 receptor-to-laminarin stoichiometry (~80–85 kDa). Flow-induced dispersion analysis demonstrated cooperative binding with an apparent dissociation constant of 46 μM and a Hill coefficient of ~3, accompanied by a large increase in hydrodynamic radius. Analysis of the bound ligand fraction revealed selective enrichment of chains with DP 25–36, defining a preferred chain-length window. High-speed atomic force microscopy showed that individual Dectin-1 molecules undergo cooperative clustering on both laminarin and the longer β-glucan scleroglucan, while chemical crosslinking provided independent evidence for ligand-induced receptor association. Together, these findings demonstrate that β-glucan recognition by Dectin-1 is governed by chain-length selectivity and cooperative receptor assembly, consistent with a molecular ruler mechanism in which lectin receptors extract specific biological information from heterogeneous glycan populations. Lectin receptors on mammalian cell surfaces recognize specific glycan features within heterogeneous glycan populations to initiate immune signaling, yet how defined signals are extracted from structurally diverse ligand mixtures remains poorly understood. Here the authors report the molecular basis by which the innate immune receptor Dectin-1 recognizes the soluble β-glucan laminarin.

papers.title: Physics-inspired Potts machines of coupled oscillators for low-energy sampling and combinatorial optimization
papers.abstract: Sampling low-energy configurations of the standard q-state Potts model is essential in the study of phase transitions, critical phenomena, complex systems, and combinatorial optimization, but remains challenging. While physics-inspired dynamical sampling has been extensively explored for the Ising case (q = 2) in the form of Ising machines, direct dynamical system frameworks for the standard q-state Potts model have received less attention. We propose a class of physics-inspired dynamical samplers, referred to as oscillator Potts machines (OPMs), that directly target the standard q-state Potts model. We show that the OPM exhibits a systematic low-energy bias with respect to the underlying Potts energy landscape. We demonstrate that the OPM can be realized in a network of self-sustaining oscillators, indicating that it is compatible with standard hardware technologies. We apply OPMs to max-k-cut problems by mapping these instances to the Potts Hamiltonians. These results position the OPM as a physically grounded dynamical system framework for multistate sampling and combinatorial optimization. Many optimization and sampling problems involve variables with more than two states, beyond the binary Ising model. For the standard q-state Potts model, we introduce an oscillator-based dynamical system that favors low-energy states and can be implemented with coupled oscillators.

papers.title: Direct observation of phase-space dynamics during energetic-particle-driven MHD bursts
papers.abstract: The phase space (velocity and real space) dynamics of bulk ions is a critical issue for the heating scenario in magnetically confined plasma. Bulk ions accelerate parallel to the magnetic field, and the velocity distribution function can depart from a Maxwellian due to wave-particle interactions such as Landau and transit-time damping. Here we show flattening in velocity space (a decrease in the velocity gradient) and a rapid increase in ion energy parallel to the magnetic field within 0.1 ms of the onset of the MHD burst, by 30% at the location of the MHD burst in the Large Helical Device. In velocity space, the anisotropy of ion-velocity distribution due to the acceleration of ions parallel to the magnetic field disappears within the ion-ion collision time scale (2  ~ 3 ms). The transient increase in ion energy decays within 6 ms at the plasma periphery but persists much longer in the plasma core, contributing to the rise in core-ion energy. The authors study the phase-space (velocity and real-space) dynamics of bulk ions during an energetic-particle-driven MHD burst in LHD. They find a rapid increase in ion energy parallel to the magnetic field within 0.1 ms of the MHD burst onset, rising by 30% at the MHD burst location and contributing to the rise in core-ion energy.

papers.title: Comparing malaria transmission blocking efficacy of Primaquine and Tafenoquine with in vivo pre-clinical models
papers.abstract: The 8-aminoquinoline primaquine is used as a single low dose with antimalarial treatment to reduce malaria transmission. An alternative 8-aminoquinoline, tafenoquine has a substantially longer half-life and may therefore provide more sustained transmission-blocking activity, but direct comparisons with primaquine are limited. We compare the transmission-blocking activity and pharmacokinetics of these drugs in vivo. We assess primaquine dose response in Plasmodium berghei-infected mice and compare an equimolar dose of tafenoquine in a mouse-to-mosquito-to-mouse transmission model. We also assess both drugs against Plasmodium falciparum gametocytes in humanized immunodeficient mice using bioluminescence and microscopy, and measure plasma drug concentrations. Dose-response relationships are modeled using generalized linear and nonlinear regression, with appropriate statistical tests for transmission and parasite endpoints. Here we show that primaquine produces stronger early transmission-blocking activity, reducing mosquito infection more effectively than tafenoquine 24 hours after treatment. In contrast, tafenoquine retains greater activity at later time points, coinciding with prolonged systemic exposure. Similar temporal differences are observed when the drugs are combined with the schizonticide sulphadiazine. In humanized mice, both drugs reduce gametocyte abundance in a dose-dependent manner, while tafenoquine shows sustained exposure for several days compared with the more rapid decline of parent primaquine. Primaquine and tafenoquine have distinct temporal transmission-blocking profiles in vivo. Sustained activity of tafenoquine is consistent with prolonged exposure rather than greater intrinsic potency. These findings are observed across multiple models, both in the absence or presence of a partner schizonticide and thus demonstrate a potential advantage of the utilization of tafenoquine when compared to primaquine. Malaria is spread when mosquitoes bite people who carry the parasite. Drugs that stop malaria parasites from being passed to mosquitoes could therefore help reduce transmission. We compared two related antimalarial drugs, primaquine and tafenoquine, to understand how well they prevent transmission and how long their effects last. We tested the drugs in mice infected with malaria parasites and in mice carrying human malaria parasites, measuring both drug levels and the ability of parasites to infect mosquitoes. Primaquine worked more strongly soon after treatment, while tafenoquine remained effective for longer, consistent with its longer-lasting presence in the body. These findings support further study of tafenoquine as a possible tool to reduce malaria transmission. Duffey, Zakutansky, et al compare the transmission-blocking activity and drug exposure of primaquine and tafenoquine in two preclinical malaria models. They find that primaquine shows stronger early activity, while tafenoquine maintains activity for longer, supporting further investigation as a transmission-blocking intervention.

papers.title: Multi-sequence MRI-based radiomics model for predicting radiotherapy response in thyroid eye disease
papers.abstract: Radiotherapy is a pivotal treatment for active, moderate-to-severe thyroid eye disease (TED), but responses vary. Conventional indicators such as the clinical activity score (CAS) are subjective and have limited response predictive value. We constructed a multi-sequence predictive model integrating clinical data, conventional imaging, and radiomic features of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to predict radiotherapy response in TED patients. 85 TED subjects treated with standardized radiotherapy (20 Gy) were retrospectively enrolled. Pre-treatment orbital MRI, including fat-suppressed T1-weighted contrast-enhanced (T1CE) and T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), was analyzed. Radiomic features from extraocular muscles (EOMs) were extracted and selected to develop single-sequence and multi-sequence models as well as integrated models incorporating clinical data, imaging metrics, and radiomic features using nine machine learning algorithms. Models were evaluated using DeLong’s test, calibration curves, Brier scores, decision curve analysis, and SHAP analysis. Among 85 patients, 46 were responders and 39 were non-responders. Baseline CAS was the only clinical variable significantly different between groups. Clinical models showed limited predictive performance (AUC = 0.700), whereas radiomic models achieved higher discrimination, with AUCs of 0.850, 0.875, and 0.933 for T1CE, T2WI, and multi-sequence radiomics, respectively. The integrated model combining radiomic features and imaging metrics achieved the highest AUC (0.942) and significantly outperformed the clinical model (P = 0.040), with favorable reliability and clinical utility in calibration and decision curve. Multi-sequence MRI-based radiomics integrated with conventional imaging metrics provides an objective approach for predicting radiotherapy response in TED. The combined model demonstrated superior discrimination, favorable calibration, and clinical utility compared with clinical prediction approaches, supporting individualized risk stratification after prospective validatio/n. Thyroid eye disease is an autoimmune orbital disorder that causes orbital inflammation and visual impairment. Orbital radiotherapy is widely used to treat active disease, but treatment responses vary substantially across patients, leaving many individuals exposed to unnecessary radiation without clinical benefits. Currently, no reliable preoperative tools can accurately predict radiotherapy outcomes. Here, we developed a simple and non-invasive predictive model based on multi-sequence MRI radiomics. By integrating multi-sequence radiomic features, orbital conventional imaging metrics and clinical indicators, our optimized model accurately distinguishes radiotherapy responders from non-responders before treatment. This quantitative tool helps guide individualized decision-making, reduce ineffective radiotherapy, and advance personalized management for thyroid eye disease.

papers.title: Passive and continuous assessment of subjective sleep quality using smartwatches
papers.abstract: Sleep is a fundamental physiological process that directly impacts nearly every aspect of human health. Poor sleep quality has been linked to cardiovascular disease, stress, anxiety, depression, inflammation, impaired cognitive performance, and even increased mortality. When assessing sleep quality, it is important to capture two fundamentally different yet complementary dimensions: objective sleep quality and subjective sleep quality, which are both independent predictors of adverse outcomes. While advances in wearable technology now allow continuous monitoring of objective physiological characteristics of sleep, subjective sleep quality still relies exclusively on self-reported questionnaires, which inherently require active user participation and are limited to specific points in time. In this study, we present a machine learning framework for the passive and continuous assessment of subjective sleep quality, leveraging physiological signals collected from commercial smartwatches, such as sleep data, physical activity, heart rate, and stress inferred from heart rate variability, alongside individual characteristics, including sociodemographic factors, personality traits, and health-related attributes. Our machine learning model was trained using data from the PerMed prospective observational study, which includes 4,794 participants, 759,116 self-reported daily questionnaires and 1,765,264 days of smartwatch recordings collected over a three-year period. We show that the model achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.88 in distinguishing between extreme subjective sleep quality ratings. Our passive and continuous approach to assessing subjective sleep quality represents a conceptual shift in how subjective sleep quality is measured, with the potential to enable timely, personalized interventions that support not only sleep-related conditions but also broader aspects of overall health and well-being. How well people feel they have slept can affect their health and well-being. However, understanding this usually requires people to regularly report their sleep quality themselves. We investigated whether this information could instead be estimated automatically using commercial smartwatches. We analyzed three years of data from 4,794 participants, combining smartwatch measurements of sleep, physical activity, heart rate, and stress with personal characteristics such as age, health, and personality. We developed a machine learning model that could distinguish between nights that participants rated as very good or very poor. Combining smartwatch measurements with personal characteristics performed better than using either type of information alone. These findings suggest that smartwatches may eventually help track how people experience their sleep continuously, with less need for repeated questionnaires. Hausner et al. develop a machine learning framework combining commercial smartwatch data with individual characteristics to assess subjective sleep quality. The model achieves high performance in distinguishing extreme levels of self-reported sleep quality, opening the possibility of passive and continuous assessment of subjective sleep quality.

papers.title: Programming golden triple helices
papers.abstract: Chiral helical superstructures provide a platform to control photon polarization and electron spin, yet they are challenging to construct using inorganic materials. Now, homochiral triple helices that exhibit pronounced circularly polarized luminescence have been assembled from gold by tailoring the steric and stereochemical properties of supporting chiral cyclic ligands.

papers.title: The limits of the water bankruptcy framing call for a water justice response
papers.abstract: Water bankruptcy is being promoted as a framing for escalating water challenges. Yet, it risks obscuring their political roots and reproducing technocratic approaches that leave underlying inequalities and drivers of overuse and depletion unaddressed. A transformative vision for global water action must confront the political economy of depletion, and centre justice, care, and plural ways of knowing water.

papers.title: Stricter wastewater regulations challenge accession to the European Union
papers.abstract: The latest directive from the European Union (EU) on the treatment of urban wastewater brings in stricter regulations intended to drive progress towards the United Nations’ sustainability goals, but also heightens the barriers to EU accession for many candidate countries. However, with the right support, this compliance challenge can be reframed as an opportunity to accelerate progress and strengthen environmental governance, not only for accession candidates but also for the existing EU and its neighbours.

papers.title: Projecting global deployment of interfacial solar evaporation
papers.abstract: Interfacial solar evaporation has emerged as a promising solution to water scarcity, yet its geographic suitability and potential societal benefits remain insufficiently understood. A validated physics-based model paired with global climate and socioeconomic data now maps where interfacial solar evaporation can meet genuine water, resource, and health needs, shifting the field from performance benchmarking to demand-driven development.

Widespread North American pollution and health impacts from early twentieth century copper production
papers.abstract: Rapid expansion of fossil-fuel burning and base-metal production during the Second Industrial Revolution resulted in widespread pollution and potentially important health impacts. Here we used an array of Arctic ice cores, atmospheric modelling and epidemiology to investigate arsenic and other toxic heavy metal pollution. From multiple lines of evidence, we attribute the observed 1884–1918 increases of up to 15-fold in arsenic and other heavy metals primarily to emissions from copper production at Anaconda, Montana—then among the world’s largest copper producers and a well-documented source of arsenic emissions. We estimate emissions from Anaconda of 11 and 4.4 kt yr−1 for arsenic and lead, respectively, during the two decades of peak production that polluted much of North America. Installation of electrostatic precipitators, delayed for a decade by lax regulation, reduced heavy metal emissions by 65%, but not before exposing millions of Americans to cancer risks, cognitive declines and other ailments. Mining and industrial emissions can be substantially reduced by technological interventions. The historical case of copper production in Anaconda, Montana shows the widespread health burdens that can result when lax regulation delays such interventions.

papers.title: Agricultural data source choice as a dominant control on nitrogen surplus uncertainty
papers.abstract: Agricultural nitrogen (N) surplus (the residual of total N inputs after harvest removal, plant-tissue storage, runoff and atmospheric losses) is a leading cause of groundwater and other environmental contamination in intensive food-producing regions, yet N surplus estimates often depend on inconsistent fertilizer, harvest and manure datasets in an N balance. Using California’s Central Valley as a data-rich test case, we propagate expert, survey-based, regulatory and county-level datasets through a fixed crop-specific N surplus framework to generate 24 cases. Holding model structure and land use constant, we quantify the large divergence in estimated N surplus arising from data choice, especially for manure-treated field crops. The uncertainty about N surplus is consequential: it can reorder which crops, regions and pathways receive priority for groundwater protection. The resulting spread among N surplus outcomes is large enough to alter hotspot rankings, mitigation priorities and screening-level estimates of economic burden. Credible nitrogen assessment at farm to global scales therefore requires explicit propagation of agricultural data source uncertainty, which can materially affect resulting N surplus estimates. Absent specific local data, the uncertainty magnitudes reported here may guide N surplus uncertainty assessment in other regional, national and global analyses. Environmental impacts from nitrogen surplus in agricultural regions make it critical to understand the nature and drivers of excess nitrogen. Bhaduri and colleagues show that data source uncertainty must be accounted for to avoid misalignments in management and mitigation decisions.

papers.title: Blood-based RNA biomarker for the early detection of ovarian cancer
papers.abstract: Tested in a cohort of 506 individuals, the RNA-based biomarker of microenvironment fitness Tu-stroma shows high performance in discriminating early-stage ovarian cancer from benign lesions, outperforming CA125.

papers.title: Next-generation KRAS G12C inhibitor improves survival in lung cancer
papers.abstract: Phase 3 trial data show that the next-generation KRAS G12C inhibitor divarasib leads to longer progression-free survival than the first-generation inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib in patients with non–small-cell lung cancer.

papers.title: Author Correction: Innate lymphoid cells in the initiation, regulation and resolution of inflammation
Bioprinting, ten years on: from shape to function
papers.abstract: Bioprinting has moved from building organ-like shapes that keep cells alive to constructs judged by function. However, function only emerges when computational design, printing hardware and instructive bioinks are coupled in one process. Making this coupling routine and reproducible is essential for translating printed tissues into credible therapies and models.

papers.title: TrkA<sup>+</sup> sensory nerves coordinate regeneration through NGF-associated regulation of mitochondrial homeostasis
papers.abstract: Sensory nerves are emerging as critical regulators of musculoskeletal repair through neurotrophic signaling, vascular interactions, and direct communication with bone-resident cells. While their requirement for regeneration is well established, the specific contributions of distinct sensory nerve subtypes and their underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. Mammalian digit tip regeneration provides a unique model to study this process, as it recapitulates complete tissue replacement, including bone, nail organ, and marrow. Previous studies using denervation or altered mechanical loading demonstrate that neural input controls regeneration but do not resolve subtype-specific functions. Here, we identify TrkA/NGF signaling as a dominant sensory nerve-associated pathway during digit regeneration using spatial transcriptomics and functional interrogation in TrkAF592A mice. Selective inhibition of TrkA signaling reduced regeneration, decreasing proliferation while accelerating osteogenic differentiation during the patent blastema phase, resulting in a shortened regenerate. Mechanistically, TrkA/NGF disruption induced a compensatory increase in NGF expression within the blastema, associated with increased mitochondrial fusion and fatty acid oxidation (FAO). This NGF-associated shift in mitochondrial dynamics promoted osteogenic differentiation, linking neurotrophin signaling to cellular metabolism and fate decisions. Together, these findings establish a central role for TrkA+ sensory nerves in coordinating regenerative timing and patterning and identify NGF-mediated regulation of mitochondrial homeostasis as a potential therapeutic target for enhancing bone repair.

papers.title: Synthetic data to lower barriers towards equitable artificial intelligence in rapid diagnostic test interpretation
papers.abstract: Rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) support affordable disease diagnosis. Machine learning (ML) can improve RDT interpretation but often relies on large, proprietary, and costly real-world image libraries. We present SynSight – a ML-enabled RDT segmentation and classification pipeline trained on synthetic data. Validated on HIV (98% sensitivity, 99% specificity) and COVID-19 RDTs (up to 99% accuracy), SynSight enables rapid ML training without real-world training images, keeping pace with new RDT development.

papers.title: CORRIGENDUM: Repairing a bone defect with a three-dimensional cellular construct composed of a multi-layered cell sheet on electrospun mesh (2017 Biofabrication 9 025036)
Engineering the synovial lining–sublining architecture in a human 3D model to study macrophage–fibroblast interactions in arthritis
papers.abstract: The synovial membrane is a key regulator of joint homeostasis, inflammation, and tissue remodeling, yet human in vitro models that reproduce its spatial organization while enabling controlled investigation of macrophage–fibroblast-like stromal cell (FLS) interactions remain limited. Here, we developed a xeno-free, spatially organized 3D synovial membrane model that reconstructs the structural relationship between the macrophage lining and fibroblast-rich sublining compartment. The model was generated by establishing an apically organized macrophage-containing lining-like compartment on a transwell membrane, followed by stepwise assembly of FLS laden hydrogel constructs. Hydrogel screening identified a 1:3 VitroGel® RGD formulation as the most suitable condition to support FLS viability, homogeneous cell distribution, and stable tissue organization. Experimentally induced M1-like and M2-like macrophages were incorporated, and the model was stimulated with TNF-α, TGF-β, or Osteoarthritis (OA) synovial fluid (SF). Cytotoxicity, proliferation, metabolic activity, gene expression, and cytokine secretion were analyzed. Pharmacological responsiveness was evaluated using adalimumab and 4-octyl itaconate (4-OI). The spatially organized construct enabled compartment-specific analysis of macrophage–FLS communication. M1-like macrophages induced inflammatory FLS responses characterized by elevated IL1B, IL6, TNFA, and MMP1 expression, whereas M2-like macrophages promoted matrix-remodeling and myofibroblast-related programs, including increased TGFB and ACTA2 expression. Exposure to OA-SF and cytokine stimulation induced FLS hyperproliferation, metabolic adaptation, and distinct transcriptional responses. Treatment with adalimumab suppressed TNF-driven inflammatory responses, whereas 4-OI reduced selected inflammatory markers and altered remodeling-associated responses. Together, these findings establish a spatially organized, xeno-free 3D synovial membrane model as a defined and experimentally tractable platform for studying macrophage–FLS communication and synovial activation. By combining physiologically inspired tissue organization with compartment-specific analysis, the model provides a human in vitro platform for investigating OA-associated inflammatory and remodeling processes and evaluating pharmacological modulation under defined experimental conditions.

papers.title: Silk-hyaluronic acid bioinks recreate a dynamic chondrogenic niche for stem cell differentiation and matrix-driven maturation in bioprinted cartilage models
papers.abstract: Progress in cartilage engineering requires advanced tissue models capable of replicating the structural and cellular organisation of native tissue whilst supporting extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling and functional tissue maturation. In this study, methacrylated silk fibroin (SFMA) and hyaluronic acid (HAMA) were combined into a dual-component, photopolymerisable biomaterial ink designed to recapitulate aspects of the biochemical composition and mechanical dynamics of the native cartilage ECM in bioprinted constructs. HAMA incorporation produced a denser, structurally stable hydrogel system, maintaining long-term stem cell viability and a rounded, chondrocyte-like cell morphology. Under inductive culture conditions, human mesenchymal stem cells underwent chondrogenic differentiation within SFMA-HAMA hydrogels, characterised by the expression of cartilage-associated markers including SOX9, COL2A1, and ACAN, and the deposition of a cartilaginous matrix containing sulphated glycosaminoglycans, collagen type II, and hyaluronic acid. Time-resolved mechanical analysis revealed progressive stiffening of cell-laden SFMA-HAMA constructs over 28 d, distinct from the intrinsic time-dependent mechanical changes observed in acellular hydrogels and temporally associated with cartilage-like ECM formation. Bioprinted constructs retained chondrogenic potential and construct shape fidelity following fabrication. This work demonstrates that SFMA-HAMA bioinks recreate a dynamic chondrogenic niche that supports stem cell chondrogenesis, cartilage-like ECM formation and construct maturation closely associated with cell-mediated matrix deposition—providing a foundation for the development of advanced bioprinted models for studying cartilage biology, disease modelling, and regenerative strategies.

papers.title: Archival and palaeoenvironmental documentation of extreme climate events reveals generational amnesia in collective memory
papers.abstract: Collective memory shapes how societies respond to climate extremes, but its long-term biases are hard to observe. Here, the authors show that historical severity assessments of droughts and floods in northern China over 430 years are biased toward recent experience, consistent with an agent-based model of generational amnesia.

papers.abstract: TBP fragments activate calpains and disrupt AMOT-YAP1 signalling, revealing a pathway involved in normal neural development and implicated in spinocerebellar ataxia type 17.
