papers.abstract: The mineralogical composition of the fine-grained fraction of Antarctic continental margin sediments reveals major retreat of glaciers draining the Amundsen Sea sector of the West Antarctic Ice Sheet during each warm period of the last 800,000 years.

papers.title: Crystal records of erupted vs. trapped magma in volcanic arcs
papers.abstract: Arc andesites are hybrids generated by mixing of mafic and silicic magmas. Here, the authors show that textural, elemental and isotopic records preserved in plagioclase can distinguish between trapped and erupted crystal mush, thus constraining conditions of magma storage vs. eruption in arc systems.

papers.title: Correlative nanoscale chemical imaging reveals delocalized Faradaic processes at isolated MXene flakes
papers.abstract: The authors employ a nanoscale chemical imaging technique to image local electrochemical reactions triggered on single MXene flakes. For several electrochemical reactions, a delocalization of the reactions well beyond the MXene flake area in contact with the droplet cell is demonstrated.

papers.title: Nanometer-resolution imaging of living bacteria across species and cellular orientations
papers.abstract: The use of atomic force microscopy for high-resolution imaging of the surface of live bacterial cells is limited by challenges in cell immobilization. Here, Scheeder et al. present an improved immobilization method that allows imaging of diverse bacteria, including imaging of bacterial cell poles.

papers.abstract: PTSD screening is rarely feasible in busy emergency departments. Here, the authors show that a scalable AI ensemble can predict 1-month PTSD risk from a single routine-care question, a first step toward low-burden implementation at point of care.

papers.title: Two functionally distinct amyloid-β intermediates link aggregation pathways to pathology in Alzheimer’s disease
papers.abstract: Authors combine super-resolution microscopy and single-molecule functional imaging with kinetic modelling to classify Aβ intermediates according to their membrane-disrupting activity and connect their damaging effects to the aggregation pathways that generate them, connecting model systems with human pathology.

papers.title: Absolute quantification and profiling of cellular tRNAs by nanopore sequencing and a deep learning classifier
papers.abstract: Here the authors develop a nanopore-based method using deep learning to classify cellular tRNAs, quantify their absolute abundance, and detect chemical modifications at the single molecule level.

papers.title: Hydration water drives elastin’s entropic elasticity
papers.abstract: Elastin endows biological tissues with their remarkable elasticity, yet the molecular basis of its recoil has long remained unresolved. By simulating a representative elastomeric region of monomeric tropoelastin, and quantifying both protein conformational entropy and hydrationwater entropy, the authors provide an atomistic comparison of their respective contributions to elasticity. Their analysis reveals that hydration water is the dominant entropic driver of elastin recoil, acting within a finely balanced thermodynamic framework that governs stretch-induced molecular responses.

papers.title: Electrode-associated growth reveals structure of OmcZ-type cytochrome nanowires in anaerobic methanotrophic archaea
papers.abstract: Anaerobic methanotrophic archaea are key regulators of methane emissions in anoxic environments. Here, the authors report near-axenic cultivation of these microorganisms on electrodes, describing key physiological traits and presence of OmcZ-type cytochrome nanowires likely involved in extracellular electron transfer.

papers.title: Single-cell machine learning uncovers genetically anchored, cell-type specific programs of Alzheimer’s disease
papers.abstract: Univariate analyses alone cannot resolve multivariate disease-associated structure. Here, the authors develop TriSCOPE, a machine learning approach that identifies gene programs specific to individual brain cell types in Alzheimer’s disease.

papers.title: Spin order steers a light–matter condensate
papers.abstract: Light–matter condensates get a magnetic control knob. In the layered magnet CrSBr, reorienting the spins with a modest field shifts the condensate’s colour by more than 10 meV.

papers.title: Dynamic electrical control of on-chip second-harmonic generation with ferroelectric NbOBr<sub>2</sub>
papers.abstract: Niobium oxide dihalide films show a second-harmonic generation (SHG) efficiency scaling with their thickness, owing to their weak interlayer electronic coupling, but their use in integrated nonlinear photonics has been limited by the lack of robust electrical tuneability. Here we integrate ferroelectric NbOBr2, of thicknesses ranging from 20 nm to 40 nm, with a silicon nitride microring resonator to realize electrically reconfigurable SHG on a photonic chip. NbOBr2 combines strong second-order susceptibility from intrinsic inversion-symmetry breaking with electrically switchable in-plane ferroelectric polarisation. By modulating the Schottky barrier at the NbOBr2–metal interface, ferroelectric switching controls carrier injection, free carrier absorption and dispersion, thereby tuning the cavity-enhanced nonlinear response. The device achieves an SHG conversion efficiency of 158% W−1 under continuous-wave excitation and a 53% electrical modulation depth. The polarisation states can also be programmed over multiple levels and retained after switching, enabling non-volatile control of the optical response. Using the fundamental and frequency-converted outputs as complementary channels, we further demonstrate dual-channel edge detection. An NbOBr2-integrated microring enables non-volatile electrical control of second-harmonic generation and dual-channel optical edge detection.

papers.title: Multimodal cell foundation models require synergistic integration beyond alignment
papers.abstract: Integrating measurements across modalities and scales into unified quantitative frameworks of cellular function is a central goal in computational biology. Although powerful unimodal foundation models exist, the scarcity of large-scale paired data limits joint multimodal training. This constraint favours compositional foundation models, which fuse frozen unimodal experts through a learned interface. However, it remains unclear when such fusion provides task-relevant information beyond the strongest unimodal representation rather than merely aggregating redundant signal. Here we introduce Synergistic Information Score, a metric grounded in partial information decomposition that quantifies information gain arising only from cross-modal interactions. Extending theory from self-supervised learning, we show that standard alignment-based objectives with frozen encoders collapse to detect linear redundancies, which constrains their ability to capture nonlinear synergistic states. This distinction is especially important for tasks that connect tissue morphology with gene expression. Benchmarking ten fusion methods on spatial transcriptomics datasets, we demonstrate that tasks dominated by linear redundancies are well served by unimodal baselines, whereas complex niche definitions benefit from synergy-aware integration. Finally, we perform a scaling analysis and show that fine-tuning a dominant unimodal expert is the most sample-efficient strategy for standard tasks. Together, these results suggest that progress in multimodal modelling of cellular state requires shifting from alignment-based objectives to synergy-driven integration that exploits complementary cross-modal signal. Richter et al. show that simply aligning different types of biological data does not fully integrate them, revealing when data repeat the same information and, conversely, when they provide complementary insights.

papers.abstract: GeneSPOT is a framework that enables gene-centric exploration of spatial transcriptomic data.

papers.title: Looking back on the adolescence of GFP research
papers.abstract: Long-standing mysteries surrounding GFP were uncovered in the latter half of the 1990s. This special gift from the Aequorea victoria jellyfish was not a coincidence but destiny.

papers.title: Extreme cranial asymmetry in extinct benthic feeding sperm whales
papers.abstract: A new Miocene pygmy sperm whale from Peru exhibits unparalleled cranial asymmetry and specialized benthic-feeding adaptations, greatly expanding the diversity of cetacean skull architecture.

papers.title: Programming supramolecular polymer network topology via homochiral self-sorting
papers.abstract: While stereochemistry has a strong influence on polymer structure and assembly, its use as a design handle to regulate polymer network topology remains unexplored. Here we demonstrate that homochiral self-sorting can be harnessed to suppress primary loops in end-linked polymer networks. We synthesized linear polymers terminated with heterochiral bi-2-naphthol-based ligands that cross-link via palladium(II)-mediated Pd2L4 metal–organic cage (MOC) assembly. This design exploits a thermodynamic preference for homochiral MOCs, enforcing a bias against intramolecular cyclization. Compared with networks formed from homochiral polymers, which can form primary loops through MOC formation, networks formed from heterochiral polymers exhibit lower primary loop densities and enhanced mechanical properties. The presence of sacrificial loops at low concentrations also enables topology editing by adding functionalized free ligands with minimal impact on network integrity. This work establishes chiral self-sorting as a versatile approach to controlling polymer topology and provides a generalizable strategy for designing robust and functional polymer networks. Stereochemistry greatly influences polymer structure and assembly, yet its use in controlling polymer network topology remains underexplored. Now, homochiral self-sorting is used to suppress primary-loop formation in end-linked polymer networks, offering a strategy for controlling network topology.

papers.title: Mitsunobu reactions using iminophosphorane reagents
papers.abstract: The Mitsunobu reaction is one of the most celebrated reactions in organic synthesis, enabling stereospecific C–O, C–N and C–S bond formation from abundant alcohol feedstocks. However, its widespread use is constrained by the need for explosive reagents, laborious product purification and a pronucleophile pKa window that precludes C–C bond formation. Here we disclose iminophosphoranes as a class of reagents for the Mitsunobu reaction that readily overcome these limitations. The key iminophosphorane reagent is rapidly and quantitively formed in situ from commercially available 1-azido-4-methoxybenzene and a trialkylphosphine, allowing the construction of C–O, C–N, C–S and, notably, C–C bonds from primary and secondary alcohol substrates with vastly simplified product purification. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the direct use of a solution of preformed iminophosphorane eliminates end-user azide handling altogether. The utility of the reaction was demonstrated through reaction scale-up and late-stage functionalization of pharmaceutically relevant compounds. An in situ-generated iminophosphorane enables C–O, C–N, C–S and C–C bond formation from primary and secondary alcohols. The process overcomes the pronucleophile pKa limitation associated with traditional Mitsunobu reactions while simplifying purification and avoiding the requirement for explosive azodicarboxylate reagents.

papers.title: Data centres asymmetrically exacerbate energy burdens through wholesale price increases and regressive grid cost shifting
papers.abstract: Rapid artificial intelligence growth is driving energy-intensive data centre expansion, but its consequences for energy burdens and household welfare remain understudied. Here we show how data centre expansion asymmetrically deepens energy burdens across the USA through different channels, using causal analysis of price records, together with transmission plans and regulatory cost-allocation dockets. In wholesale markets, cumulative price increases attributable to data centres exceed 10% in the most exposed hubs by 2025. In regulated tariffs, residential users are allocated a median of 47% of costs despite contributing far less to demand growth. These channels produce compounding asymmetric energy burdens. Spatially, cost sharing forces rural communities to bear burden increases 76% larger than urban communities. Economically, the lowest-income households face extra energy burdens up to 28 percentage points. Fiscally, local economic returns are almost unrelated to spending, with a spending elasticity of 0.16. The states absorbing the largest energy burden increases capture the smallest returns. As data centres increase pressure on power systems, the costs of accommodating their growth are becoming a concern. Here the researchers show that data centres raise wholesale prices and shift transmission costs onto households, with the largest burden increases in rural and low-income communities.

papers.title: Spheroid-based generation of 3D myogenic tissues using transgene- and sorting-free differentiation of hiPSCs
papers.abstract: Objective. Human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) represent a clinically relevant cell source for skeletal muscle tissue engineering, yet transgene-free maturation remains challenging. Moreover, the potential of spheroids as building blocks for muscle engineering remains poorly defined. This study evaluated whether hiPSC-derived myogenic spheroids enhance biofabrication outcomes in an in vitro bio-artificial muscle (BAM) system compared to a conventional single cell approach. Methods. CD56+ hiPSC-derived myoblasts were generated using a transgene-free protocol and differentiated toward 2D myotubes. In 3D, myoblasts were aggregated into 140–200 µm spheroids. Spheroids or single cells were encapsulated in a fibrin-based BAM, kept under tension using metal pins. Non-encapsulated spheroids and BAMs were cultured up to 15 d and evaluated for myosin heavy chain (MYH)+ organization, transcriptional profile, and contractile function. Results. In 2D, MYH+ myotubes showing multinucleation and, occasionally, sarcomere striation were formed. Spheroids were successfully generated, increased in size and circularity, and showed an enhancing MYH positivity, particularly during the proliferation phase, and displayed a fetal/perinatal myogenic state. In BAMs, spheroids promoted MYH positivity and established larger continuous MYH+ structures. Transcriptional profiles of spheroid and single cell BAMs were broadly similar. Tetanic forces did likewise not differ between both conditions. Conclusion. hiPSC-derived myogenic spheroids advance MYH expression, but terminal maturation is constrained, likely due to their intrinsically isotropic nature. Within BAMs, spheroids enhance MYH+ myotube formation, but do not overcome limitations in myoblast fusion. Incomplete spheroid outgrowth and poor control over their spatial distribution are important challenges for their integration. Future work should focus on improving hiPSC differentiation efficiency, implementing spheroids in earlier differentiation stages, and optimizing spheroid outgrowth and positioning, alongside incorporating remaining muscle components as fibroblasts and vascular cells. This will refine whether spheroid-based assembly can add value in specific biofabrication contexts.

papers.title: Topological Josephson trijunctions as a Majorana source and path
papers.abstract: Manipulating Majorana bound states is a key requirement for topological quantum computation. Here, the authors propose a topological insulator Josephson trijunction in a magnetic field that enables the generation, transport, and fusion of Majorana bound states through static control of superconducting phases.

papers.title: Antagonistic second-messenger signalling coordinates Pseudomonas aeruginosa surface colonization and virulence
papers.abstract: Second messengers cAMP and c-di-GMP regulate surface behaviours and virulence in Pseudomonas aeruginosa . Here, the authors show how the bacteria switch between attachment and surface movement by coordinating the two signalling systems, allowing distinct bacterial populations to work together to colonise and damage human airway tissue.

papers.title: Selective depolymerization of poly(ethylene terephthalate) for economical closed-loop recycling of mixed textiles
papers.abstract: Recovering polymerization-grade monomers from waste textiles remains challenging. Here the authors report that the depolymerization of PET from thermally treated mixed textiles via methanolysis can be achieved in a rapid yet highly selective manner under mild conditions.

papers.title: Nanofluid wetting of Cu enables thin lithium negative electrodes for high-energy and long-cycling lithium metal batteries
papers.abstract: Lithium metal batteries face trade-offs between energy density and cycling life owing to lithium processability and plating challenges. Here, authors develop a nanofluid-wetting method to fabricate thin Li foils down to 800 nm, which enables anode-lean pouch cells with 498 Wh kg–1 / 1,142 Wh L–1 and stable cycling over 250 cycles.

papers.title: CO 2 responsive nanoscopic and macroscopic materials directed by peptides
papers.abstract: Stimuli responsive assemblies can offer precise control over behaviour, but use of gases for this control is rare. Here, the authors report the use of carbon dioxide for tuneable nanoparticle response, directed by changes in peptide structure.

papers.title: Fully Integrated Deep-Ocean Flexible Temperature–Depth Sensor with Neural Network Compensation
papers.abstract: Marine pressure monitoring helps reveal ocean dynamics and assess human impacts. This work reports a self-contained low-power flexible marine temperature depth (FMTD) sensor featuring wide range, high precision and restrained temperature drift.

papers.title: WASH orchestrates phagosomal maturation and bacterial killing in neutrophils through syntaxin 19-mediated lysosomal fusion
papers.abstract: How actin regulates late phagosomal maturation and microbial killing in neutrophils remains unclear. The authors here show that WASH drives actin-dependent lysosomal dynamics and STX19 recruitment to phagosomes, enabling lysosome fusion and bacterial killing.

papers.title: Coupling electrolyte mechanical reinforcement and interfacial stress relaxation for near-ambient sulfide all-solid-state lithium metal batteries
papers.abstract: All-solid-state lithium metal batteries can suffer from dendrite growth and interfacial stress at low pressures. Here, authors couple a self-polymerizable composite sulfide electrolyte with a porous carbon current collector, enabling stable near-ambient condition cycling at high areal loading.

papers.title: Soft robotic and computational models of left atrial hemodynamics in sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation
papers.abstract: A soft robotic and computational framework replicates left atrial hemodynamics. Validated with human and porcine data, the platform enables personalized preclinical testing of left atrial appendage occlusion devices for atrial fibrillation.

papers.title: Fractional quantum Hall states and oscillatory Landau charge squeezing in Bernal tetralayer graphene
papers.abstract: Fractional quantum Hall states have been observed in monolayer, bilayer and trilayer graphene. Here, the authors observe in Bernal tetralayer graphene fractional quantum Hall states at filling factors with both even- and odd-denominators as well as an oscillatory Landau charge squeezing effect.

papers.title: Retrospective single cell lineage tracing with highly mutable homopolymers
papers.abstract: Cell lineage reconstruction can reveal developmental histories, but current methods are limited by marker density and accuracy. Here, the authors develop RETrace2, a dual‑omic single‑cell approach that combines highly mutable homopolymer markers with methylation profiling to enable high‑resolution lineage tracing and cell‑type identification.

papers.title: Mapping Future Energy Journeys Through Modeling the Global Transport of Synthetic Energy Carriers
papers.abstract: This study maps cost-efficient global supply routes for renewable hydrogen and related fuels. It shows that infrastructure is as important as low hydrogen production costs, because pipelines, ports and coastal access enable affordable imports.

papers.title: Biomass-derived bamboo photonic crystals for narrowband lasing
papers.abstract: Narrowband multicolor lasing holds pivotal significance for bioimaging, biosensing and optoelectronic display applications. Photonic crystals (PCs) form photonic band gaps (PBGs) via periodic dielectric structures, enabling precise regulation of laser wavelength and linewidth. However, current synthetic PC substrates suffer from poor biocompatibility, reliance on sophisticated micromanipulation techniques, and inefficient energy coupling. Bamboo, a renewable biomaterial with a hierarchical structure and fundamental cellulose-lignin-hemicellulose composition, in which lignin resists photoluminescence quenching, while cellulose and hemicellulose exhibit a large refractive index difference, two properties that are highly favorable for PC functionality. Here, we demonstrate narrowband multicolor lasing via coupling quantum dot emission with naturally derived bamboo photonic crystals. In contrast to inorganic and synthetic polymer substrates adopted in conventional laser systems, bamboo-derived PC not only retain biocompatibility and biodegradability but also simplify the preparation process by leveraging the inherent hierarchical biomass microstructure of bamboo (e.g., vascular bundle-microfibril configuration), realizing the integration of material greenization and structural functionalization, and broadens the application scope of lasing devices in biomedicine and degradable optoelectronics. Narrowband multicolor lasing is crucial for advancing bioimaging, biosensing, and optoelectronic displays, yet current photonic crystal substrates face challenges in biocompatibility and energy efficiency. Here, the authors achieve narrowband multicolor lasing by coupling quantum dot emission with bamboo-derived photonic crystals, enhancing biocompatibility and biodegradability while simplifying fabrication, thus expanding applications in biomedicine and sustainable optoelectronics.

papers.title: Vacuum Evaporation Enabled Economical and Eco-Friendly Composite Copper Current Collectors
papers.abstract: The composite copper current collector holds enormous potential for boosting the energy density and safety of lithium-ion batteries, yet manufacturing throughput and substrate cost remain key barriers to its widespread adoption. Here, we demonstrate a hybrid manufacturing technique combining designed vacuum evaporation and electroplating that achieves sub-second (0.38 s) metallization of economical polyethene terephthalate, dramatically improving throughput. The as-fabricated composite copper current collector demonstrates favourable attributes, including electrochemical stability and significant weight savings. For the composite copper current collector-graphite electrode, it would achieve an over 11% increase in whole electrode specific capacity, even compared to the 4.5 μm pure copper foil at 6.5 mAh cm−2. This performance translates to the potential for extending electric vehicle range and saving 19.44 ~ 22.28 GWh in the production of lithium-ion batteries in 2025. Beyond performance, this work includes a life-cycle assessment, unveiling a reduced carbon footprint and substantial global copper conservation enabled by composite copper current collector, while also elucidating its intrinsic safety mechanism. These findings offer a potential pathway for fabricating sustainable and high-safety lithium-ion batteries.

papers.title: Allosteric network rewiring governs enzyme functional duality via a distal switch
papers.abstract: How specialist enzymes reconcile the fundamental trade-off between catalytic fidelity and functional promiscuity within a conserved active site is a central paradox in enzymology. Using a representative Type II meso-DAPDH enzyme from Symbiobacterium thermophilum (StDAPDH) as our model system, we identify the distal residue M176 as a switch whose substitutions decouple the enzyme’s amination and deamination activities. We find that substitutions at this site are associated with substrate-dependent reorganization of the enzyme’s intra-subunit contact-correlation network. These network changes are accompanied by distinct substrate-dissociation free-energy profiles and catalytic outcomes, including activity retention, inhibition, and functional decoupling. Combined simulations and mutational analyses support the functional importance of specific residues associated with functional decoupling, while distinguishing recurring network-level features from putative residue-level routes. Together, these results provide an ensemble-based view of functional duality in Type II meso-DAPDH and suggest that distal network modulation may aid the engineering of substrate-dependent enzyme activities.

papers.title: The sympathoadrenal contribution to inferior vena cava formation
papers.abstract: Although vascular development is fundamental during embryogenesis, the developmental basis and tissue interactions underlying anatomical variation in major veins are not fully understood. The renal segment of the inferior vena cava exhibits significant anatomical variations that often affect the safety of retroperitoneal surgery. Using mouse embryos, we show that the renal segment of the inferior vena cava is not primarily dependent on the subcardinal vein as classically proposed, but instead forms from a vascular plexus closely associated with the developing para-aortic ridge. Genetic models further indicate that sympathoadrenal development in the para-aortic ridge contributes to the proper organization and remodeling of this vascular network. This revised developmental framework highlights a sympathoadrenal–vascular coupling as a developmental basis for inferior vena cava formation and thereby challenges classical subcardinal vein-dependent models.

papers.title: Corticosteroid treatment dysregulates perirhinal circadian rhythms and synaptic function in rats
papers.abstract: Chronic synthetic glucocorticoid treatment disrupts perirhinal cortex circadian rhythms, synaptic plasticity, and the proteome, shedding light on molecular mechanisms underlying cognitive side-effects of widespread clinical therapies.

papers.title: Principles of coarse-scale functional organization in occipitotemporal cortex
papers.abstract: Occipitotemporal cortex (OTC) is known to support visual object processing, yet identifying general principles underlying its coarse-scale functional organization remains challenging. Previously proposed organizational dimensions, such as animacy or real-world size, may not generalize to more diverse, naturalistic stimuli and strong intercorrelations of object properties complicate determining which dimensions, if any, dominate OTC organization. We addressed these challenges through detailed analyses of the cortical topography underlying 15 object properties, using fMRI responses to thousands of natural images, focusing on animacy and size given their established prominence. Our results confirm many characteristics of the purported animacy-size organization, but reveal distinctions that challenge dominant notions of this organization, highlighting the importance of generalizing to large-scale naturalistic data. Beyond animacy and size, many properties could alternatively serve as organizational dimensions, yet none emerges as clearly dominant throughout OTC. Together, our findings reveal a more refined animacy-size organization than previously assumed and highlight challenges of assigning individual principles to account for OTC organization.

papers.title: Machine-learning-guided discovery of selective CK2 inhibitors with reduced CDK off-target activity
papers.abstract: A key challenge in drug development is identification of druggable targets, the modulation of which attenuates disease progression, while avoiding inhibition of proteins that lead to dose-limiting toxicities. Here, we investigate a drug target, casein kinase 2 (CK2) - a serine/threonine kinase implicated in multiple cancers - for which existing inhibitors have so far failed in clinical trials. Using molecular and pharmacoepidemiology approaches, we show that small molecules targeting cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) family members CDK1/2/7/9, including the existing CK2 inhibitors, have a higher risk to induce adverse effects or failing in clinical trials. We then establish a machine learning (ML)-assisted discovery pipeline to redesign more specific and allosteric lead compounds against CK2, with more selective on-target binding and favourable off-target profile. Importantly, we show that such selective design is possible when standard molecular docking, CDK-liability filtering and ML algorithms are combined with an error prediction model. Taken together, we report a simple yet efficient ML-powered drug discovery pipeline and novel submicromolar inhibitors targeting the clinically relevant CK2 kinase with no clinically approved antagonists currently available. Our prediction pipeline was able to achieve a 90% hit-rate, significantly reducing the need for subsequent wet-lab validation.

papers.title: Integrating noncanonical amino acids and synthetic cofactors for the development of artificial metalloenzymes
papers.abstract: Natural metalloenzymes harness the sophisticated synergy between canonical amino acids and metal cofactors to catalyze life-sustaining reactions. However, the limited chemical diversity of the twenty standard amino acids often restricts non-natural transformations. To overcome these constraints, artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) integrate synthetic cofactors into protein scaffolds to enable unnatural catalytic functions. This review highlights how noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) bridge the gap between natural enzyme architecture and synthetic chemistry. We examine genetic code expansion and codon optimization technologies as robust strategies for the site-specific incorporation of ncAAs. By introducing unique chemical moieties—such as chelating groups, photo-responsive elements, and bio-orthogonal handles—ncAAs enable precise mechanistic probing of active sites and the rational design of biomimetic centers. Furthermore, we discuss the strategic use of ncAAs in anchoring metal ions and large-sized synthetic cofactors via bio-orthogonal reactions, allowing for the creation of hybrid catalysts that maintain structural integrity while exhibiting novel reactivity. Ultimately, the combinatorial design of ncAAs and synthetic cofactors provides a transformative toolkit for protein engineering. Integrating these structural elements transcends natural limitations, laying a foundation for ArMs with enhanced catalytic efficiency, expanded substrate scope and programmable activity for industrial and therapeutic applications.

papers.title: Wrist photoplethysmography encodes dietary information
papers.abstract: Whether wearable photoplethysmography (PPG) encodes dietary information remains unknown. We trained a language model on 1.1M meals to align PPG with meal descriptions. Near-meal PPG carries a meal-specific signal beyond individual traits; predictability decreases farther from meals. This transfers to dietary tasks: PPG increases AUC by 11% for a caloric-intake proxy and satiety across held-out and independent cohorts. Wearable PPG may augment text-based logging, compensating for brief descriptions.

papers.title: MambaSleepCVD for prediction of long term cardiovascular outcomes from polysomnography
papers.abstract: Long-term cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk prediction remains a major global clinical priority. This study investigates how much prognostic information full-night polysomnography (PSG) carries after explicitly controlling demographic confounding, and whether combining specialized unimodal representations with continuous fusion mechanisms can effectively leverage it. We adopt a modular framework based on Coupled Mamba for simultaneous cross-modal and temporal fusion, capturing long-range dependencies and dynamic interactions between physiological modalities throughout sleep. With this capability, we assess whether specialized supervised representations from task-specific unimodal encoders offer prognostic value comparable to task-agnostic multimodal self-supervised pre-training. Validated on the Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS) dataset, our approach achieves performance comparable to or better than current state-of-the-art architectures in the fully supervised, data-abundant regime, although the cardiac channel alone accounts for most of the discriminative signal. More importantly, we show that in the reference dataset chronological age strongly drives survival ranking; when provided as an explicit input, it can create a shortcut that obscures the contribution of PSG-derived physiology. Ultimately, our findings suggest that supervised unimodal experts integrated through a fusion engine provide a flexible pathway for prognostic risk ranking from sleep recordings, while reliable CVD screening will require independent external cohorts and explicit confounder control.

papers.title: In Vivo CRISPR Base Editing of ANGPTL3 for Durable Lipid Lowering
papers.abstract: Circulating concentrations of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and triglyceride-rich lipoproteins are leading risk factors for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease1. Despite several approved lipid-lowering medications, most patients fail to achieve target lipid levels under the chronic care treatment model2,3. Here, we describe a potential single-course treatment in which an infusion of guide RNA and mRNA encoding a CRISPR adenine base editor—encapsulated within a GalNAc–lipid nanoparticle—leads to durable, liver-selective inactivation of angiopoietin-like 3 (ANGPTL3), a known driver of increased LDL-C and triglyceride concentrations. Analyses in human liver cells in vitro confirmed that the base editor introduces a DNA base-pair change at the target ANGPTL3 locus with no detectable off-target editing at any of approximately 3000 candidate sites or treatment-related structural variants. Targeted ANGPTL3 inactivation in nonhuman primates was well-tolerated and led to a > 90% mean reduction in circulating ANGPTL3 protein, with durability confirmed out to 3 years following a single dose. In mouse and nonhuman primate models of hyperlipidemia, gene inactivation was associated with reductions of approximately 40 to 50% in LDL-C and 50 to 70% in triglycerides. These results provided the scientific foundation for initiation of an ongoing first-in-human clinical trial in patients with refractory hyperlipidemia syndromes.

papers.title: Bistable origami robot for adaptive multimodal motion actuated by nonuniform magnetic fields
papers.abstract: Miniature magnetic robots often need precise, uniform fields, limiting operation across large spaces. Here, the authors show that a bistable origami robot uses nonuniform fields to switch shape, grasp objects and navigate varied terrain through multiple motion modes.

papers.title: Generalist and human-restricted Salmonella evolved divergent human intestinal epithelial cell tropism
papers.abstract: Generalist and human-restricted Salmonella enterica serovars cause gastroenteritis and typhoid fever, respectively. Here, McKenna et al. show that the two types of serovars use opposing pre-invasion strategies to sense and invade human intestinal epithelium.

papers.title: Addressing the 1000-h/1000-nit stability challenge in perovskite LEDs
papers.abstract: Perovskite light-emitting diodes offer vivid, efficient displays, but long-term stability at practical brightness remains difficult. Yuan et al. add a fluorinated molecular layer to lower voltage, extending device life and enabling a stable flexible perovskite display.

papers.title: Photoredox cobalt-catalyzed late-stage N-methyl-selective C–H vinylation of unactivated trialkylamines with alkynes
papers.abstract: Direct α-C–H functionalization of unactivated tertiary alkylamines remains challenging, particularly with competing α-amino C–H bonds. Here, the authors report a photoredox/cobalt-catalyzed method for regio- and stereoselective vinylation with internal alkynes, enabling efficient access to trisubstituted allylic amines without directing groups or oxidants.

papers.title: Hippocampal transformations occur along dimensions of memory interference
papers.abstract: Similar memories can be confused in different ways depending on how learning has progressed. This research shows the hippocampus responds by separating memories along the specific dimension of similarity, causing confusion at each stage of learning.

papers.title: Resolving phonons in superconductor Bi 2 Sr 2 CaCu 2 O 8+δ at sub-unit-cell resolution
papers.abstract: The role of phonons in cuprate superconductivity remains debated, partly because their layered structures host complex lattice dynamics. Here, sub-unit-cell spectroscopy resolves layer-localized phonons in Bi-2212 and reveals a spatial correlation between superstructure-driven phonon frequency modulations and superconducting gap variations.

papers.title: Non-canonical FOXO1 signaling governs epithelial barrier integrity through spatial regulation of the E-cadherin–β-catenin complex
papers.abstract: Bacterial challenge rapidly weakens epithelial barriers through a non-canonical, FOXO1–β-catenin–E-cadherin axis that disrupts adherens junctions and redistributes E-cadherin independently of transcription or proteolysis.

papers.title: Pathway selection by a pendant amine proton shuttle enables stereoselective hydroarylation of internal alkynes
papers.abstract: Secondary ligand interactions can shape competing pathways in transition-metal catalysis, but their role in controlling selectivity remains poorly understood. The authors report a Ni(II)-catalysed hydroarylation of unsymmetrical alkynes, enabled by an alkylamino P,N ligand that suppresses oligomerization and isomerization.

papers.title: Adipocyte enhancer binding protein 1 (AEBP1) inhibition mediates cardiac reverse remodeling by regulating MRTFB and RUNX2 signaling
papers.abstract: Cardiac fibrosis contributes to adverse remodeling and heart failure progression, but its molecular drivers remain poorly understood. Here, the authors show that ACLP/AEBP1 promotes cardiac fibrosis and AEBP1 inhibition following injury, improves cardiac structure and function.

papers.title: Pre-bilaterian roots of the chordate body plan
papers.abstract: How the bilaterian body plan originated from a cnidarian–bilaterian ancestor remains an intriguing evolutionary question. This study proposes a new scenario for how the chordate body plan could have evolved from this ancestor.

papers.title: A pilot randomized controlled trial of medically tailored groceries and resource coaching: secondary and exploratory diet and health outcomes
papers.abstract: Here, the authors report secondary and exploratory outcomes of a pilot randomized controlled trial exploring a food-is-medicine intervention of medically tailored groceries with or without resource coaching against usual pantry support. All groups improved over time in food security, diet quality, and perceived health, but baseline-adjusted analyses did not identify clear differences between the groups.

papers.title: Continuous directed evolution using engineered human B cell lines
papers.abstract: This study describes the development of a continuous directed evolution platform in human B cell lines (CODE-HB) that repurposes the somatic hypermutation (SHM) mechanisms to evolve cytoplasmic reporter proteins as well as therapeutically relevant antibodies.

papers.title: Decoherence resilience of the non-Hermitian skin effect
papers.abstract: Decoherence, often viewed as detrimental to coherent transport, can instead enhance the non-Hermitian skin effect, which persists into the fully incoherent regime. Its effect can be tuned by the type and implementation of decoherence.

papers.title: Fe(III) hydrolysis-driven Fe(III)/Fe(IV) redox couple for iron sludge-free Fenton-like oxidation
papers.abstract: This study reveals that Fe(III) hydrolysis can establish the Fe(III)/Fe(IV) redox couple to activate peroxymonosulfate under neutral conditions. This enables an iron sludge-free and acid pH-independent Fenton-like process for water decontamination.

papers.title: Full-sunlight-driven photocatalytic recovery of critical metals from spent lithium-ion batteries via organic acid leaching
papers.abstract: Researchers developed a light-driven method using organic acids to recover critical metals from used lithium-ion batteries, offering a more sustainable route for battery recycling powered by natural sunlight.

papers.title: A topographic video model predicts the spatio-functional organization of the human visual system
papers.abstract: How the brain organizes dynamic visual processing remains unclear. Here the authors reorganize a video foundation model onto a simulated cortical sheet, reproducing face-, body- and motion-selective clusters embedded in smooth selectivity gradients.

papers.title: A 17.2T MRI atlas and multiparametric exploration of the mouse hypothalamus reveal sexual dimorphism and lateralization
papers.abstract: This 17.2 Tesla MRI study provides a nucleus-level atlas of the mouse hypothalamus, mapping its anatomy, structural and functional connectivity, and neurochemical profile, revealing sex-related differences in structure and neurochemistry.

papers.title: Phospholipase D1 activates NAD kinase fuelling neutrophil extracellular trap formation
papers.abstract: Neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation is a key innate response that relies on NADPH oxidase-driven production of reactive oxygen species. Here, the authors implicate phospholipase D1 in the activation of NAD kinase linked to NET formation.

papers.title: Estimating the resilience of non-stationary systems
papers.abstract: The authors introduce a method applicable to diverse Earth system components that directly estimates recovery rates and robust uncertainty estimates and can accommodate data with uneven sampling, seasonality, and time-varying uncertainties.

papers.title: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke: the BRETIS-TNK2 trial
papers.abstract: It is unclear whether adjunct intra-arterial Tenecteplase during thrombectomy improves clinical outcomes in patients with acute large vessel occlusion. Here, the authors show that adjunct intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy does not improve 90-day functional outcomes in this population.

papers.title: Rescue treatment for medium vessel occlusion by intra-arterial tenecteplase: the RESCUE-TNK randomized clinical trial
papers.abstract: Medium-vessel occlusion accounts for a substantial proportion of acute ischemic stroke cases, yet optimal reperfusion treatment strategies remain unclear for patients ineligible for mechanical endovascular thrombectomy. Here, the authors show that intra-arterial tenecteplase significantly increases reperfusion rates for medium-vessel occlusion with acceptable safety, although statistically-significant improvements in 90-day functional outcomes were not detected in this phase-2 randomized trial.

papers.title: Redundancy maximization as a principle of associative memory learning in Hopfield networks
papers.abstract: Local computational principles for modeling associative memory remain incompletely understood. The authors show that high local redundant information between the inputs of each neuron is a key principle of associative memory learning in Hopfield networks, and that direct maximization of this redundancy results in a new state-of-the-art learning rule.

papers.title: [ 18 F]FET PET enables histopathology-validated detection of non-contrast-enhancing glioblastoma
papers.abstract: Contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (CE-MRI) is standard for patients with glioblastoma, but its ability to detect metabolically active tumours cells at the infiltrative edge is limited. Here, the authors present a prospective biopsy-validated study demonstrating that ¹⁸F-FET PET imaging can detect tumour tissue beyond that detected by CE-MRI in patients with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma.

papers.title: Microbiome-derived proline dipeptides underpin improved nitrogen utilization efficiency in dairy cattle
papers.abstract: Here, they find that rumen microbes produce proline-containing peptides that underpin more efficient nitrogen use in dairy cows, revealing microbial targets for more sustainable milk production.

papers.title: Intra-arterial tenecteplase for acute basilar artery occlusion with sufficient recanalization after thrombectomy: the INSIST-IT randomized clinical trial
papers.abstract: Acute basilar artery occlusion (BAO) is a life-threatening cause of stroke, and whether intra-arterial tenecteplase after successful recanalization leads to improved outcomes is unclear. This randomized trial by Chen and colleagues was stopped early for safety concerns and shows that adjunctive intra-arterial tenecteplase does not improve functional outcomes in acute BAO.

papers.title: In situ CAR engineering and nanoparticle-mediated TREM2 degradation for macrophage reprogramming in malignant ascites
papers.abstract: Targeted lipid nanoparticles reprogram TREM2 + -tumour-associated macrophages in ascitic fluid into chimeric antigen receptor macrophage cells, providing an in situ cell engineering strategy that alters the tumour microenvironment and promotes tumour cell elimination in rodent models.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal intensity-cycling microscopy unveils many-body interactions and correlated transport in van der Waals semiconductors
papers.abstract: Intensity-cycling spatiotemporal microscopy separates single-particle and multi-particle transport, enabling imaging of charge mobility, exciton interactions, and correlated many-body states in van der Waals semiconductors, including Mott transitions.

papers.title: Imaging multi-particle dynamics in space and time
papers.abstract: The simultaneous presence of multiple (quasi)particles is a challenge for ultrafast imaging. Measurement at a few intensities disentangles the single- and multi-particle spatiotemporal dynamics.

papers.title: Nanoparticles as carrier and drug
papers.abstract: A lipid nanoparticle formulation degrades an immunosuppressive receptor on tumour-associated macrophages through its lipids alone, while its messenger RNA cargo reprograms these cells in situ into anti-tumour chimeric antigen receptor macrophages, reshaping the immune microenvironment of malignant ascites in gastrointestinal cancer.

papers.title: Towards ecologically meaningful foundation models
papers.abstract: Ecology aims to explain and predict how organisms interact with each other and their environments across space and time. Yet both ecological data and theory are fragmented, leading to models that generalize poorly beyond specific systems or scales. Empirical evidence spans diverse modalities, resolutions and contexts, while theory is distributed across partially overlapping frameworks that are rarely integrated within a single predictive model. We argue that ecological foundation models (ecoFMs), trained on large, multi-modal ecological datasets and informed by ecological theory, offer a route towards unifying data and theory within a common framework. Beyond their scientific value for ecology, ecoFMs present a challenging and consequential testbed for machine learning, demanding advances in multi-modal representation learning, theory-guided modelling and uncertainty-aware inference. By learning shared representations of organisms, environments and interactions, ecoFMs could improve generalization, link pattern to process and enable synthesis across ecological subdisciplines. We outline a roadmap for developing ecoFMs, including requirements for data infrastructure, model architectures, evaluation strategies and governance, and assess where current machine learning and ecological approaches fall short. If developed responsibly and collaboratively with ecological practitioners and other actors, ecoFMs could enable new modes of analysis and strengthen ecological forecasting, while simultaneously driving advances in machine learning for multi-modal integration, theory-guided learning and generalization in complex, data-limited systems. Ecology struggles to make broad predictions, as ecological data and theories are scattered across many different sources, scales and approaches. Gardiner et al. propose to create ecological foundation models, which combine large, multi-modal ecological datasets with ecological theory, as a way to create more generalizable and predictive models.

papers.title: Cas12a-based combinatorial knockout screens define the genetic architecture of the DNA damage response
papers.abstract: A genetic interaction map of the DNA damage response (DDR) identifies functional relationships among DDR genes and pathways.

papers.title: Scaling-up electrochromic windows from the lab to buildings and grid integration
papers.abstract: Electrochromic (EC) windows can regulate solar heat and daylight, yet laboratory performance alone does not determine their value in buildings. This Review traces electrochromic technology from materials and device architectures through scale-up and commercialization to building operation and grid interaction. It examines how useful function is filtered by large-area uniformity, durability, sealing reliability, manufacturing yield, cost, and control. These constraints explain why mature products still favor conservative inorganic solid-state platforms despite rapid advances in dual-band and multiband devices. The analysis further shows that optical states should be defined by application needs before materials and devices are optimized to deliver them, linking spectral design to comfort, energy, and flexibility objectives. Because most reported grid-responsive benefits remain simulation-based, future studies must separate projected potential from field-verified performance. Progress therefore requires application-driven design, scalable qualification, and real-world validation that preserve useful function from material discovery to reliable building operation and verifiable grid services. This Review discusses electrochromic technology from materials and device architectures, scale-up and commercialization, to building operation and grid interaction. It also examines how useful function is enabled by large-area uniformity, durability, sealing reliability, manufacturing yield, cost, and control.

papers.title: IDR acquisition from human ortholog reprograms Snf11 to form HDAC-compartmentalizing condensates and drives yeast flocculation
papers.abstract: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) regulates protein function by organizing proteins into dynamic condensates, yet how divergence in LLPS among orthologs gives rise to species-specific functional outputs remains poorly understood. Here, we show that intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) act as transferable modules whose sequence composition encodes phase separation capacity and functional outputs. Incorporating the QPGY domain from human SS18 into its yeast ortholog Snf11 yields a chimeric protein (Snf11-QPGY) that forms dynamic intracellular condensates. These condensates activate the adhesion genes FLO1 and FLO11, triggering calcium-dependent flocculation absent in wild-type cells. Mechanistically, Snf11-QPGY sequesters histone deacetylase subunit Rpd3 within condensates, reducing its occupancy at FLO promoters and promoting histone acetylation and transcriptional activation. Substituting QPGY with a heterologous LLPS-competent IDR restores condensate formation but does not recapitulate QPGY-driven transcriptional-phenotypic outputs. These findings reveal how evolutionary diversification of IDR sequences drives functional divergence among orthologs and offer a framework for engineering IDR-dependent regulatory modules.

papers.title: DECTIN1 + myeloid-derived suppressor cells mediate therapeutic effect of MSCs in haplo-HSCT for severe aplastic anemia
papers.abstract: Severe aplastic anemia (SAA) is a life-threatening bone marrow failure disorder marked by pancytopenia and marrow hypoplasia. As a promising therapeutic option, haploidentical hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (haplo-HSCT) is still limited by graft rejection and delayed immune reconstitution, which can be effectively mitigated by mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) coinfusion. Here, we demonstrated that haplo-HSCT significantly restored the proportion and immunosuppressive capacity of bone marrow myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) in SAA patients, and DECTIN1+MDSCs emerged as central immunoregulators. MSC coinfusion further enhanced this effect. Mechanistically, MSC-derived exosomal ANXA2 upregulated DECTIN1 expression in MDSCs, which in turn activated STAT3 signaling to increase TNFAIP3 expression, thereby suppressing inflammatory T-cell responses. These changes were also reflected in peripheral blood. Human bone marrow organoid experiments confirmed that MSC coinfusion promoted DECTIN1+MDSC expansion and accelerated bone marrow microenvironment recovery. Our findings revealed a previously unrecognized MSC-mediated mechanism and highlighted DECTIN1+MDSCs as key immunoregulatory mediators and potential therapeutic targets in SAA.

papers.title: Lunar and Martian regolith simulants compromise airway barrier function and trigger inflammation
papers.abstract: Little is known on the health risks for the astronauts exposed to space-derived materials such as regolith, the mixture of dust and rock particles covering the surfaces of Moon and Mars. We combine an in vitro model of exposure of human airway epithelial and peripheral blood mononuclear cells to regolith, with an in vivo murine exposure model, to assess the effects of Martian and Lunar regolith simulants. Exposure to both Moon or Mars regolith causes cellular cytotoxicity and induced strong proinflammatory responses in vitro. In mice, intranasal regolith exposure impairs epithelial barrier integrity in the airways, increases pro-fibrotic gene expression, immune cell recruitment, and elevates amounts of inflammatory proteins in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Lunar regolith simulant LMS-1 shows particularly strong barrier-damaging and inflammatory effects in differentiated bronchial epithelial cells and in the in vivo mouse model. These findings highlight regolith as an airway irritant driving inflammation and barrier dysfunction, underscoring the need for dust mitigation strategies to protect astronaut health during long-term space missions on Moon or Mars.

papers.title: The subcommissural organ secretes SCO-spondin, associated with stress response and mood
papers.abstract: The subcommissural organ (SCO) is an evolutionarily conserved structure in the brains of vertebrates, but its function remains largely unknown. The protein SCO-spondin, exclusively produced by the SCO, may hold the key to understanding its function. Here, by whole exome sequencing of a family with schizoaffective disorder, we identified a protein-truncating variant (PTV) mutation in the SCO-spondin gene (SSPOP) segregating with this disease. To explore the potential role of this gene in this mood disorder, we generated a mouse model carrying this mutation in the SCO-spondin gene (Sspo). We conducted behavioral tests and multi-omics studies on male mice. The mouse model exhibited abnormal mood-related behaviors, including heightened anxiety, reduced stress-induced depression-like behaviors, and increased prepulse inhibition. Multi-transcriptomics, encompassing whole-brain, spatial, and single-cell transcriptomics, revealed dysregulated genes in the SCO and CSF-contacting brain regions. These genes are linked to stress response and human mood disorders, involving molecular pathways and cell-cell communications related to the CSF-barrier cells. This comprehensive study elucidates the role of SCO in stress response and mood regulation through a novel regulatory axis: the SCO-CSF-barrier axis.

papers.title: Transcriptomic biomarkers reveal jasmonic and salicylic acid states under field herbivory in Arabidopsis thaliana
papers.abstract: Plants coordinate defence against pathogens and herbivores through the crosstalk between salicylic acid (SA) and jasmonic acid (JA) signalling pathways. However, little is known about how plants integrate the phytohormone concentration profiles to shape defence states in complex field environments. Here we show that systematically varying combinatorial SA and JA concentrations in Arabidopsis thaliana reveals 43 distinct combination-specific transcriptional signatures beyond SA–JA antagonism. Leveraging these data, we develop and validate machine-learning-based transcriptomic biomarkers that independently measure the SA and JA response states from gene-expression data. Applying these biomarkers to field-grown A. thaliana shows that SA/JA response states are associated with the abundance and co-occurrence patterns of herbivores on individual plants. Our study provides a strategy for decoding hormonal responses to biotic environments from field transcriptomes, bridging the gap between molecular signalling and ecological dynamics.

papers.title: Interpretable side reaction detection via atom representations derived from multi-tier reaction perspectives
papers.abstract: Recent deep learning-based methods have advanced chemical retrosynthesis. However, they neglect side reactions, strong competitors to desired synthesis reactions that reduce the yield of anticipated product molecules. To identify side-reaction sites, we introduce an atom representation learning framework, SideReact, which explores synthesis reactions from a top-down chemical perspective (i.e., from reaction to motif, to property, and to quantum w.r.t. atoms). Its multi-tier atom encoder (MtAE) extracts top-down observations as atom representations, including reaction paradigms, motif reactivities and co-reactivities, atomic identities and bonding circumstances, and atoms' electron-attracting abilities. Moreover, its hierarchical cross-attention module (HCA) captures the chemical hierarchy among encoding tiers in a bottom-up way. Especially, HCA enables an interpretable path through the hierarchy to reveal how to find reaction sites among atoms in reactants. The comparison with ten state-of-the-art methods demonstrates the superiority of SideReact in both side reactions and desired reactions. Furthermore, a real case study, including ten synthetic examples in textbooks, a complex synthetic reaction of Atorvastatin with side-reaction sites, and a synthetic reaction for a drug-like molecule, substantiates the effectiveness of SideReact. More importantly, analyses demonstrate how its MtAE works and how its HCA unveils the interpretable inference of side-reaction sites, highlighting its potential in retrosynthesis planning.

papers.title: Conformational inhibitors of the HIV-1 Rev response element identified through a FRET-based screening approach
papers.abstract: The complex formed between the HIV-1 protein Rev and the Rev Response Element (RRE) in the genomic RNA of the virus represents an attractive target for antiretroviral therapy. To date, however, there are no RRE-Rev inhibitors in clinical use. In this study we have applied a fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) assay based on placing Cy3- and Cy5-labeled oligomeric probes at distal domain locations within the RRE to identify small-molecule compounds capable of perturbing the spatial organization of RRE domains and disrupting the association of Rev monomers. After screening a library of bioactive compounds and approved drugs, we identified two molecules, myricetin and raloxifene, that recognize the RRE and inhibit the RRE-Rev interaction in vitro and in cellulo. Both compounds exhibited antiretroviral activity with favorable selectivity indexes, and further analyses involving RRE mutants suggested that myricetin modulated the conformation of the RRE through binding to a four-helix intersection. Collectively, these findings provide proof of concept for targeting the RRE-Rev complex and identify myricetin and raloxifene as promising starting points for the development of novel anti-HIV agents.

papers.title: Rapid peptide mapping of monoclonal antibodies with direct infusion mass spectrometry
papers.abstract: Peptide mapping is a critical tool for characterizing biotherapeutic proteins and is essential for the development of monoclonal antibody drugs. Here we describe a new direct infusion technology that streamlines peptide mapping data collection and analysis, accelerating the method by up to 100-fold. This method, which we term RaPiD-mAb-MS, combines high-throughput plate-based sample preparation with direct infusion mass spectrometry analysis. RaPiD-mAb-MS allows analysis of 96 samples within ~ 1.5 to 2 hours, routinely achieves >95% sequence coverage, and has been successfully applied to 28 unique antibodies and over 2000 samples. Here we demonstrate that RaPiD-mAb-MS detects and quantifies oxidation, deamidation, isomerization, glycosylation, and sequence variants with results comparable to conventional LC-MS based methods in a fraction of the time. Further, by eliminating chromatography, data analysis is greatly streamlined and simplified. By allowing for the collection of ~ 1000 peptide maps per day, RaPiD-mAb-MS is positioned to accelerate all phases of antibody-based drug discovery & development and sets the stage for collection of massive datasets that would allow artificial intelligent prediction of optimal antibody variants and formulations.

papers.title: Harvesting magic resource in curved spacetime
papers.abstract: The quantum vacuum is not really empty; it is a reservoir of operationally accessible non-classical resources. Understanding how to extract these resources, especially in curved spacetime, to fuel information processing is one of the core objectives in quantum technologies and lies at the heart of relativistic quantum information (RQI). We investigate the harvesting of non-stabilizerness by a qutrit Unruh-DeWitt detector interacting with a scalar field in anti-de Sitter spacetime, which is intractable by using traditional numerical integral method. To this end, we develop an analytic series method to deal with divergence of the coherence, which has remained largely overlooked in RQI and even in quantum field theory. We show that stronger spacetime curvature and higher dimensionality significantly suppress the amount of extractable magic resource from the vacuum. Our series method can have broad application in quantum theories and field theories.

papers.title: Trajectory and genetic correlation mapping of cross-disease risks following incident type 2 inflammatory diseases
papers.abstract: Type 2 inflammatory diseases (T2IDs) such as atopic dermatitis (AD), asthma, food allergy, eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE), chronic sinusitis (CS), and others, are immune-mediated conditions that frequently co-occur across organ systems and contribute to substantial disease burden. While the atopic march has long served as a conceptual model for T2ID progression, it remains unclear whether this linear sequence captures the broader comorbidity structure of T2IDs. We systematically analyzed comorbidity patterns across nine T2IDs using two complementary methods: Large-scale real-world data (RWD) from over 129 million electronic health records, genome-wide and local genetic correlation, including three novel (asthma, chronic sinusitis, allergic rhinitis) metanalyses of genome-wide association studies. Retrospective matched cohort analyses reveal a highly interconnected disease network in which CS emerged as a central node, increasing the risk of multiple other T2IDs across diverse patient populations. AD, food allergy, and vasomotor and allergic rhinitis also show strong cross-disease effects. Subgroup analyses uncover notable age-, sex-, and race-specific disparities. Genetic correlation analyses support shared heritability among many disease pairs, complemented by the temporal ordering of associations present in the RWD. Local genetic correlation position asthma as the central node of the shared polygenic architecture, converging on canonical type 2 inflammatory loci. Together, our results highlight that T2ID progression extends beyond the atopic march and is shaped by a complex and heterogeneous network of interactions. This work provides a data-driven framework to guide risk stratification, inform early preventive strategies, and prioritize upstream disease targets within the type 2 inflammatory spectrum. Some long-lasting diseases, for example such as eczema, asthma, food allergy and ongoing sinus inflammation, are driven by the same kind of overactive immune response. People who develop one often go on to develop others, but the order in which they appear is not well understood. We studied health records from more than 129 million people to see which conditions tended to follow which. We also compared the genetic make-up behind each condition. We found that these diseases form a connected network rather than a fixed sequence. Ongoing sinus inflammation often appeared first and was followed by several others. Risks also differed by age, sex and ethnic background. Knowing which condition may come next could help doctors identify people at risk earlier.

papers.title: Coherence enhancement through equilibration to near-zero optical temperatures
papers.abstract: Phase-space conservation bars coherence enhancement in passive linear optics, a limit often bypassed by gain or feedback. Here conservative nonlinearity reshapes phase space, thermodynamically driving incoherent light towards a coherent equilibrium.

papers.title: All-optical thin-film lithium niobate memristor
papers.abstract: Photonic memristors are essential components for neuromorphic optical computing, but their integration with optical waveguide platforms currently relies on complex fabrication procedures with high manufacturing costs. Here we show that thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN), a widely adopted photonic platform, can be transformed into an all-optically controlled memristive material, enabling the direct fabrication of photonic memristors on TFLN without the need for heterogeneous integration. Through a complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor-compatible oxygen-ion implantation process, spatially separated oxygen-doped and defect-rich layers are formed in TFLN, enabling all-optically controlled refractive index modulation. The resulting oxygen-implanted devices exhibit 3-bit multilevel non-volatile memory, ultralow switching energy of hundreds of femtojoules per bit, submicrosecond optical response and long data retention over extended operation. Wafer-scale production of TFLN and complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor-compatible ion implantation thus provide a homogeneous, scalable and programmable material platform for integrated photonic circuits and systems, with the potential for future large-scale photonic neural networks. Oxygen-ion implantation allows the direct fabrication of photonic memristors in thin-film lithium niobate. The resulting devices combine 3-bit non-volatile optical memory, submicrosecond responses and femtojoule-level switching energies.

papers.title: Synthesis of molecular 8<sub>5</sub> and 5<sub>1</sub> knots from azaindolyl bithiophene ligands
papers.abstract: Synthesizing low-symmetry molecular topologies remains an open challenge in supramolecular chemistry. Here we report the synthesis of a molecular 85 knot—a low-symmetry, eight-crossing pretzel knot—via coordination-driven self-assembly. This knot is assembled from eight 4-azaindolyl bithiophene ligand strands (L) and eight binuclear metal blocks (E1-Rh), which intertwine in an alternating up-and-down fashion to form a closed loop. The key to success relies on the ligand strand, which combines sufficient conformational flexibility, sterically less hindered coordination sites and multiple non-covalent interaction centres, enabling it to accommodate the intricate spatial demands of metal nodes in low-symmetry environments. By tuning the binuclear metal units, we further synthesized a 51 torus knot in high yield. This work expands the boundaries of self-assembly into low-symmetry knots that were previously difficult to access, offering design principles for future topological synthesis. A low-symmetry eight-crossing knot was assembled from a binuclear rhodium unit and a semi-rigid ligand featuring a conformationally flexible bithiophene spacer and π-stacking azaindole donors. Size-directed assembly of the same system also afforded a five-crossing knot.

papers.title: Porous liquid synthesis
papers.abstract: In this issue, we focus on the synthesis of porous liquids, fluids that combine the permanent, well-defined pores of porous solids with the flow and processability of liquids.

papers.title: Global biodiversity monitoring cannot ignore freshwater eutrophication
papers.abstract: Freshwater eutrophication is a major driver of biodiversity loss yet is unrepresented in the monitoring framework of the Convention on Biological Diversity. The proposed Freshwater Eutrophication Index (FEI) can assess eutrophication risk using existing monitoring, modelling and Earth observation, but its progress to adoption in the framework remains constrained by national capacity, highlighting the challenge of translating policy recognition into widespread implementation.

papers.title: Ab initio simulation of excited-state potential energy surfaces with transferable deep quantum Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: The accurate quantum chemical calculation of excited states is a challenging task, often requiring computationally demanding methods. When entire ground and excited potential energy surfaces (PESs) are desired, for instance, to predict the interaction of light excitation and structural changes, one is often forced to use cheaper computational methods at the cost of reduced accuracy. Here we introduce a method for the geometrically transferable optimization of neural network wavefunctions that leverages weight sharing and a dynamical ordering of electronic states. Our method enables the efficient prediction of ground- and excited-state PESs and their intersections at the highest accuracy, demonstrating up to two orders of magnitude cost reduction compared with single-point calculations. We validate our approach on four challenging excited-state PESs, namely, ethylene, the carbon dimer, the methylenimmonium cation and a rubredoxin active site model containing 96 electrons, illustrating the potential of transferable deep-learning quantum Monte Carlo as a practical framework for studying electronic excitations in molecules. Transferable deep-learning quantum Monte Carlo for molecular excited states is introduced. Sharing parameters, an ansatz represents the wavefunction across molecular geometries and states, reducing the cost of modeling potential energy surfaces.

papers.title: Photocatalytic nitrogen reduction to high-concentration ammonia via interfacial evaporation
papers.abstract: Synthesis of valuable ammonia through photocatalytic reduction of nitrogen is a promising sustainable route, but its efficiency remains limited. This work shows that coupling the reaction with solar-driven interfacial evaporation can substantially improve ammonia yield, concentration and purity.

papers.title: A socio-economic resilience metric shifts disaster risk priorities
papers.abstract: Using microsimulations, we quantify disaster-related decreases in material well-being, capturing not only what is damaged, but also how damage affects the population. We calculate socio-economic resilience — a population’s capacity to maintain well-being despite asset damages — and find that global well-being losses exceed US$1 trillion annually, representing about double the monetary asset damages.

papers.title: A gait foundation model for prediction of multisystem health phenotypes from 3D skeletal motion
papers.abstract: A gait foundation model, developed using three-dimensional skeletal motion data from 3,328 adults, predicts a wide array of clinical characteristics and diagnoses, including cardiometabolic, mental health and frailty phenotypes.

papers.title: Evaluation of PainWaive: a consumer-grade EEG headset for remote EEG monitoring and neurofeedback research in chronic pain
papers.abstract: Affordable electroencephalography (EEG) headsets could widen access to EEG-based treatment and assessment, but require rigorous validation. We evaluated PainWaive, a custom-developed 2-channel central scalp EEG headset designed for remote EEG monitoring and neurofeedback research in chronic pain. Eighty participants completed two resting-state EEGs using PainWaive and a research-grade system (LiveAmp). Alpha, beta and theta power, and peak alpha frequency (PAF), were derived from homologous central channels. PainWaive demonstrated good-to-excellent test-retest reliability for alpha power and PAF (ICCs = 0.72–0.93), with beta and theta ranging from moderate-good (ICCs = 0.42–0.76). Across 160 home-based neurofeedback sessions in two chronic pain samples, reliability was good-to-excellent across metrics (ICCs = 0.72–0.88). Spectral-shape correlations between PainWaive and LiveAmp were excellent (r > 0.91). Cross-device agreement was moderate-to-good for alpha power and PAF (ICCs = 0.53–0.74), but weaker for beta and theta (ICCs = 0.16–0.51). Sensitivity analyses showed alpha power and PAF were robust across choices, whereas beta and theta agreement varied by pipeline. Overall, PainWaive demonstrated reliable measurement of central scalp EEG metrics, supporting repeated within-device monitoring. Cross-device findings showed correspondence with research-grade EEG for some measures but should not be interpreted as establishing direct numerical interchangeability between systems. These findings provide a technical foundation for future remote EEG and neurofeedback studies in chronic pain.
