papers.title: Carbon radical generation by irreversible metal-to-ligand charge transfer
papers.abstract: Metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) is a fundamental photoinduced process that underpins a broad range of energy- or electron-transfer events1,2. In the absence of productive substrate engagement, the MLCT excited state typically relaxes to the ground state via photophysical deactivation, reflecting its largely reversible character3,4. Here we report a class of isolable copper–heteroaryl sulfone complexes that, upon visible light irradiation, undergo an irreversible MLCT-driven fragmentation through C–S bond cleavage within the coordinated sulfone ligand, generating carbon-centered radicals. Spectroscopic and computational studies support the formation of MLCT-derived excited states and a low-barrier pathway for C–S bond cleavage. This reactivity is largely independent of the reduction potentials of the corresponding free sulfones, enabling the generation of fluoroalkyl and non-fluorinated tertiary, secondary, and primary (even methyl) alkyl radicals. We demonstrate the utility of this platform in copper-catalyzed C–H fluoroalkylation of arenes and terminal alkynes. Leveraging these MLCT-generated trifluoromethyl radicals to initiate halogen-atom transfer (XAT) from perfluorocyclobutyl iodide (I-FCB), we also achieve radical perfluorocyclobutylation–iodination of alkenes, addressing a longstanding challenge in the incorporation of perfluorocyclobutyl motifs.

papers.title: A two-dimensional reticular triaxial molecularly woven fabric
papers.abstract: A two-dimensional reticular triaxial woven network material is constructed by incorporating C 3 -symmetric macrocycles into a triangular weave pattern, enabling an extra topological dimension to be used for the construction of functional materials.

papers.title: In vivo CAR-T double knockout screen maps synergistic antitumour gene pairs
papers.abstract: Using high-throughput in vivo CAR-T double knockout screening, synergistic gene combinations to improve CAR-T cell therapy are revealed.

papers.title: Observation of prethermal dynamical phase transitions and resonant melting
papers.abstract: A programmable neutral-atom quantum simulator is used to explore quench dynamics in spin models with up to 180 qubits, revealing prethermal dynamical phase transitions and resonant melting.

papers.title: Ecological and social cues orchestrate concerted courtship in Drosophila
papers.abstract: In Drosophila erecta , food odours initiate male sexual arousal, which is subsequently reinforced by the visual motion of other courting flies, creating a multisensory mechanism that synchronizes courtship in groups when conditions are favourable for reproduction.

papers.title: An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular operations
papers.abstract: AutoDNA is an artificial intelligence (AI)-native autonomous biomolecular engineering laboratory targeting multi-objective experiments across diverse instruments, realizing the co-evolution of AI and the automation system within an end-to-end multi-user framework.

papers.title: Multimodal X-ray imaging reveals hierarchical fibre mechanics
papers.abstract: The X-ray visualization platform TomoSAXS, demonstrated here on intervertebral spinal discs, can visualize nanoscale to macroscale mechanics in intact biological organs and fibrous materials.

papers.title: Towards observing interstitial hydrogen in solution in metal lattices
papers.abstract: Using deuterium as a proxy for hydrogen, atom probe tomography provides experimental evidence for interstitial hydrogen in solid solution across different FCC phases, consistent with theoretical predictions of hydrogen affinity, revealing hydrogen partitioning in structural alloys.

papers.title: Decoding the regulatory programs governing glioblastoma plasticity
papers.abstract: Multi-omic analyses of cells from patients with glioblastoma (GB) provide insight into the role of non-genetic cellular plasticity in disease progression, showing that state stability in GB cells is controlled by a network of interacting activators and repressors.

papers.title: Comprehensive mapping of essential-gene interactions in M. tuberculosis
papers.abstract: A high-throughput CRISPR-interference platform allows the mapping of interactions between essential genes in Mycobacterium tuberculosis , revealing many previously unknown genetic interactions and providing insight into gene function and drug–target relationships that could enable the development of new therapies for tuberculosis.

papers.title: Conjugation-regulated self-assembled molecules for tandem solar cells
papers.abstract: Rationally engineered molecular spatial conjugation is used for the formation of highly ordered, conformal self-assembled molecules, enabling the fabrication of high-performance perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells.

papers.title: Hard X-ray attosecond metrology
papers.abstract: Metrology techniques are developed to characterize and control attosecond hard X-ray pulses, directly measuring a 170-attosecond duration and enabling ultrafast studies of electronic dynamics in quantum systems.

papers.title: Cancer-selective gene circuits via intrinsic ribosomal frameshifting
papers.abstract: Codon-pair-dependent ribosomal frameshifting is a feature of translational dysregulation in cancer cells.

papers.title: Tracing the spread of Celtic languages using ancient genomics
papers.abstract: Genome-wide data from 4,587 ancient individuals are analysed, focusing on Bronze and Iron Age Europe, to test the extent to which alternative archaeological and linguistic models for the origin and spread of Celtic fit reconstructed demographic histories.

papers.title: Venousization enables angiogenesis in the absence of VEGFR signalling
papers.abstract: Longitudinal tracking of endothelial cells shows they can adapt to loss of VEGFR2 and form new functional vessels, challenging conventional views of the essential role of VEGF receptors in angiogenesis and providing insight into resistance to anti-VEGF therapies.

papers.title: The neural basis of flavour–nutrient learning
papers.abstract: A dopamine pathway to the basolateral amygdala is necessary for associating nutrients with flavours.

papers.title: Nectin-4 mediates rubella virus entry in airway and placental cells
papers.abstract: Nectin-4 is identified as a pivotal host entry receptor for respiratory transmission and early placental infection of rubella virus.

papers.title: Aggression experience and observation drive shared behavioural and neural changes
papers.abstract: Aggression experience and observation recruit a brain-wide network of excitatory, inhibitory and valence signals, and changes to this activation pattern predict a shared adaptive behaviour-control policy in a new aggression context.

papers.title: Transcriptomic convergence and the female protective effect in autism
papers.abstract: Gene network analysis shows how mutations in diverse genes associated with autism spectrum disorder can converge to exert shared effects, with X-linked transcription factor ZFX emerging as a key protective factor in the female brain.

papers.title: The deep Earth origin of the Great Unconformity
papers.abstract: Continental-scale uplift and subsidence associated with long-wavelength dynamic topography due to mantle convection drove the formation and preservation of the Great Unconformity.

papers.title: Twist-angle-dependent quantum phase diagrams in moiré bilayer MoTe 2
papers.abstract: Twist-angle-dependent studies of moiré bilayer MoTe 2 reveal a transition from fractional topological states to correlated insulators and superconductivity, linking topology, symmetry breaking and magnetism in moiré quantum materials.

papers.title: An open structure-guided RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction
papers.abstract: structRFM, a structure-guided RNA foundation model pre-trained on 21 million sequence–structure pairs, learns multimodal representations that improve secondary and tertiary structure prediction, functional inference and zero-shot generalization across diverse RNA families.

papers.title: Synergy in viral–bacterial co-infection expedites algal bloom demise
papers.abstract: Viral–bacterial synergy accelerates algal bloom collapse by enhancing virus-induced mortality, driven by Alteromonas chemoattraction and co-infection, revealing a previously unrecognized mortality agent that influences oceanic carbon cycling .

papers.title: A conserved flowering-time module underlies double-season cropping
papers.abstract: The genomic footprints of 80 years of modern breeding in China are traced using representative cultivars, demonstrating how precision genome editing can be used to reconstruct adaptive modules for climate-resilient crop design.

papers.title: Microbiome-wide PheWAS links gut microbial SNVs to health and exposures
papers.abstract: Gut microbial single-nucleotide variants across 10,781 individuals reveal 940 associations that link strain-level genetic variation to 69 host traits, with structural analyses pinpointing host phenotype-associated variants, providing a base pair-resolution resource for mechanistic hypothesis generation.

papers.title: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory underlies glioblastoma heterogeneity
papers.abstract: A deep single-cell and spatial multi-omic atlas of human glioblastoma is generated, pairing transcriptomic, epigenomic and genomic profiling, and tracing glioblastoma tumour heterogeneity to a stereotyped and spatially patterned trajectory of cancer cells.

papers.title: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit
papers.abstract: A new physics-based method combining the use of automatic differentiation to optimize millions of model parameters with a flexible physical model is described for starlight subtraction from real, on-sky coronagraphic images to greatly improve sensitivity.

papers.title: Highly efficient and durable Ga-doped Ni/Al 2 O 3 catalyst enhanced by interfacial Ga 3+ for low-temperature ammonia decomposition
papers.abstract: Ammonia could enable carbon-free hydrogen production, but efficient decomposition at low temperatures remains difficult. Trace gallium helps nickel catalysts remove surface hydrogen, markedly boosting low temperature activity.

papers.title: Wt1 splice isoforms bias lineage programmes during formative pluripotency
papers.abstract: Here they uncover an unexpectedly early role for Wt1 in biasing lineage programmes before gastrulation and show that Wt1 isoforms differing only by a three-amino-acid KTS motif encode divergent anterior-posterior lineage biases.

papers.title: Pressure-driven regime shifts in graphitization rewrite carbon fate during metamorphism
papers.abstract: This study demonstrates that pressure, metamorphic duration and organic precursor type are key controls on graphitization. The resulting kinetic framework provides constraints on carbon retention and structural partitioning during metamorphism and subduction.

papers.title: Precision probabilistic mapping reveals personalized functional topography in the early postnatal human brain
papers.abstract: Using resting-state fMRI, this study maps individualized functional topographies in the neonatal brain that encode early maturity, predict neurocognitive outcomes at 18 months, parallel cortical structural maturation, and are altered by preterm birth.

papers.title: Decoding microprotein interactome via a minimal genetically encoded photocatalytic proximity labeling system
papers.abstract: Shi, Yan, and colleagues present FlashID, an ultra-compact light-activated proximity-labeling system that maps microprotein interactions with minimal perturbation across bacteria, mammalian cells, worms and plants.

papers.title: Cross-scale observations of expanding bifurcated current sheets in fast magnetic reconnection
papers.abstract: Magnetic reconnection releases stored magnetic energy in space and laboratory plasmas. Here, the authors show that expanding bifurcated current sheets form during quasi-steady reconnection and help organize plasma outflows across scales.

papers.title: PRMT6 suppresses intestinal inflammation by epigenetically repressing IL-1β in mouse models of colitis
papers.abstract: Epigenetic regulation in immune cells drive their physiological and pathologic development, including establishment of inflammatory states. Here the authors show in mouse colitis models, that genomic deletion of the protein arginine methyltransferase PRMT6 leads to a selective upregulation of IL-1β in macrophages and to exacerbated inflammation.

papers.title: Alpha-aminoadipate in the saccharopine pathway promotes cancer metastasis through sumoylation of transcription machinery
papers.abstract: The role of metabolism in metastasis remains unclear. Here, a metabolic RNAi-based screen for cell invasion and metabolite-protein connectivity mapping reveals a mechanism by which sumoylation driven by alpha-aminoadipate, the intermediate metabolite of aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase, drives metastasis.

papers.title: A sublattice polarimeter to probe the quantum geometry of synthetic photonic lattices
papers.abstract: The authors introduce a sublattice polarimeter to measure the Bloch wavefunctions in bipartite photonic lattices. Using their method, they experimentally access the quantum metric, Berry curvature and band Chern numbers.

papers.title: Driving catalysts to the intrinsic optical selectivity limit for accelerating photothermal catalysis
papers.abstract: Optimizing photothermal conversion and catalytic activity is crucial for developing highly efficient photothermal catalysts. Here, the authors propose an optical-depth strategy to drive catalysts toward their intrinsic optical selectivity limit, thereby enhancing the efficiency of photothermal catalysis.

papers.title: UNMASC: modelling non-monotonic dose responses to cytokine combinations
papers.abstract: The authors present UNMASC, a model that captures non-monotonic cytokine combination effects. Applied to T cell development, UNMASC extends drug interaction surfaces to a broader range of dose-responses.

papers.title: Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) prevents excessive protein aggregation and mediates aggrephagy by modulating the liquidity of p62 condensates
papers.abstract: VHL shows an unexpected HIF-independent role in maintaining protein homeostasis under proteotoxic stress, namely, by increasing the liquidity of p62 condensates and orchestrating aggresome formation and subsequent aggrephagy.

papers.title: In vitro–reconstituted Drosophila Arc capsids deliver gene editors to dystrophic muscle
papers.abstract: Capsid-forming proteins are promising vehicles for macromolecule delivery, but have required cellular assembly or fusogens for entry. Here, authors assemble Drosophila Arc1 capsids cell-free, show entry via the receptor SORCS2, and deliver Cas9 editors that restore dystrophin in mdx mice.

papers.title: Triply convergent carbenylative Suzuki–Miyaura coupling enabled by palladium/copper co-catalysis
papers.abstract: The palladium-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura coupling is indispensable in modern organic synthesis, yet extending its modularity beyond two coupling partners remains challenging. Here the authors report a triply convergent cross-coupling that integrates aryl halides, aryl boronic acids, and N -tosylhydrazones through a palladium/copper co-catalyzed process.

papers.title: Multi-ancestry genome-wide and transcriptome-wide association analyses identify new risk loci and genes for inflammatory bowel disease
papers.abstract: Large-scale meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies and advanced transcriptome-wide association studies identify new inflammatory bowel disease risk variants and genes, including druggable targets with potential for therapeutic repurposing.

papers.title: Nitrene-triggered carbocationic rearrangement of tetrasubstituted alkenes enables divergent access to fused δ-lactams
papers.abstract: Transition-metal-catalyzed nitrene transfer offers powerful alkene functionalization, but sterically congested tetrasubstituted alkenes remain challenging. Here, the authors report an Ir(III)-catalyzed aziridination–rearrangement cascade that converts these alkenes into diverse fused δ-lactams with high yields and diastereoselectivities.

papers.title: Agentic intelligent data engine for scientific large language models
papers.abstract: Here, authors develop AIDE, a multiagent framework that automates scientific data curation, and demonstrate across biomedical and chemical tasks that its automatically curated datasets can match or outperform manually curated data while improving efficiency.

papers.title: Systematic screen of RNA binding proteins that enhance circular RNA translation
papers.abstract: Circular RNAs are promising therapeutics due to their stability. Here, the authors identified 68 RNA-binding proteins that enhance circRNA translation, built a predictive machine learning model, and showed these activators promote IRES-driven translation in a context-dependent manner, expanding tools for circRNA therapeutics.

papers.title: Seagrass sediment organic carbon burial rates are globally significant
papers.abstract: Reassessing global seagrass carbon burial via 332 sediment cores reveals an area-weighted average of 33 ± 9 g OC m -2 yr -1 (6-15 Tg C yr -1 globally). Despite covering <0.1% of the seafloor, seagrasses drive 3-6% of total oceanic organic carbon burial.

papers.title: A nonlinear superinductor in a deep-submicrometre integrated circuit
papers.abstract: Superinductors are circuit elements characterized by an intrinsic impedance in excess of the superconducting resistance quantum (RQ ≈ 6.45 kΩ) and are of use in metrology, sensing and quantum computing. However, they are typically based on bespoke structures with high density inductance such as Josephson junctions, superconducting nanowires or twisted two-dimensional materials. Here we report a superinductor created within a silicon integrated circuit fabricated in a commercial complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor process (GlobalFoundries 22-nm fully depleted silicon-on-insulator process). The superinductor leverages the high kinetic inductance (around 1 nH sq−1) of titanium nitride thin films native to the manufacturing process. By co-integrating a resonator containing the superinductor and a silicon quantum dot formed within the same integrated circuit, we create a radio-frequency single-electron transistor, which is widely used as a sensor in semiconductor-based quantum computers. Our sensor has a small footprint of 18 μm2, and offers low parasitics, which, together with the high impedance and nonlinear response of the resonator, yields a power signal-to-noise ratio of 4,500 in an integration time of 4 ns. Our approach could lead to the development of parametric circuits, kinetic-inductance detectors and quantum simulators based on one-dimensional and two-dimensional resonator arrays using integrated circuits. A superinductor can be created in a silicon integrated circuit fabricated in a commercial complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor process and used to build a radio-frequency single-electron transistor with a compact footprint and high sensitivity.

papers.title: A serendipitous CMOS quantum sensor
papers.abstract: Titanium nitride films native to a commercial complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) process can become high-impedance superconductors at millikelvin temperatures, providing compact, sensitive readout of semiconductor spin qubits from within a chip’s existing gate metallization.

papers.title: RobPicker: a meta-learning framework for robust identification of macromolecules in cryo-electron tomograms
papers.abstract: RobPicker improves cryo-ET particle picking by correcting noisy labels and reweighting rare species, enabling robust detection of small macromolecules across diverse datasets.

papers.title: A closed-loop framework for perovskite precursor additive discovery
papers.abstract: Discovering effective perovskite precursor additives is challenging due to the vast chemical space. Here, the authors present a closed-loop active-learning framework that leverages literature knowledge to accelerate perovskite precursor additive discovery, achieving solar cell efficiencies up to 21.32%.

papers.title: Synthesis, ink formulation, and aerosol jet printing of (Nb 0.5 Ta 0.5 )S 2 ternary alloy for additively manufactured electrochemical supercapacitors
papers.abstract: Alloyed 2D transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) hold promise for advanced energy storage, yet their device integration is hindered by the absence of stable, processable inks. Here, the authors develop a ternary TMD alloy ink for aerosol jet printing, achieving significant supercapacitor performance and paving the way for flexible, miniaturized energy solutions.

papers.title: Optical edge computing for speckle sensing interrogation
papers.abstract: Speckle-based sensing exploits the rich environmental information of its high-dimensional spatial intensity patterns. However, the requirement for camera-based acquisition and subsequent electronic digitization introduces significant latency and bandwidth bottlenecks that forbid real-time operation and higher temporal resolutions. Aiming to bypass this imaging processing pipeline, this manuscript presents an optically reconfigurable edge-computing platform for speckle-based sensors that performs task-specific computation directly in the optical domain. This is achieved by projecting output speckle patterns onto a digital micromirror device, using it as a programmable optical layer whose parameters are trained in situ using an evolutionary optimization strategy solely from detector feedback. We demonstrate the concept with a multi-point optical fiber sensing task, where multiple piezoelectric actuators simultaneously perturb the fiber, modifying the speckle pattern. By optimizing a set of masks to decouple these concurrent signals, the system successfully achieves real-time signal separation, achieving a target signal enhancement exceeding 4 dB while suppressing crosstalk leakage below −10 dB. Operating with bandwidths limited only by the photodetector, this approach paves the way for real-time and ultrafast optical sensing via an optical edge computing solution.

papers.title: CD30 ligand promotes skin wound healing through keratinocyte signaling and Vγ6 + γδ T-cell responses
papers.abstract: Skin wound healing depends on coordinated interactions between skin cells and immune cells. CD30 and its ligand CD30L, as members of the tumor necrosis factor (TNF) superfamily, have been implicated in various immune-related disorders. However, the contribution of CD30L in skin wound healing is unclear. Here we show that Cd30l−/− mice exhibited delayed wound closure, as validated by image tracking, along with reduced infiltration of Vγ6+γδ T cells, lower levels of inflammatory cytokines including interleukin (IL)-17A, and impaired angiogenesis in wound tissues, as demonstrated through flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry, RT-qPCR, and ELISA. Furthermore, CD30L deficiency was associated with reduced keratinocyte proliferation, altered nuclear factor (NF)-κB pathway, and lower CCL20 expression in wound-derived keratinocytes, as evidenced by western blot and bulk RNA-seq analysis. These findings support a contributory CD30L-CCL20/CCR6-Vγ6+γδ T-cell axis within the broader multicellular network during skin wound healing.

papers.title: Evolutionary dynamics of adaptive introgression and balancing selection in domestic and wild Capra species
papers.abstract: Genomic analyses reveal a fertile goat–ibex hybrid, uncover ancient introgression among Capra species, and show that balancing selection can mimic introgression signals, highlighting the complexity of interpreting shared genomic variation.

papers.title: A dichotomous family of Cache domain proteins evolved through c-type heme acquisition
papers.abstract: PAS domains often bind cofactors, whereas related Cache domains are thought to function exclusively as ligand-binding modules. We identify and characterize a large family of Cache domains containing covalently bound c-type heme. Sequence, phylogenetic and structual analysis of the DUF3365/Tll0287 family reveals conservation of a canonical CXXCH heme-binding motif, establishing c-type heme binding as a defining feature of this family. Despite previous annotation as PAS-like, these proteins share a distinct heme-binding insertion into a pre-existing Cache scaffold, representing the first documented recruitment of an intact cofactor-binding motif into a bacterial sensor domain. Domain architecture further divides the family into two subclasses: one exhibiting fusions to signaling domains and another comprised of standalone proteins. Spectroscopic analyses indicate that a representative signaling protein acts as a nitric oxide sensor, whereas a stand-alone representative exhibits redox-related properties and weak nitric oxide binding. These findings expand the functional repertoire of Cache domains and reveal a mechanism for the evolution of bacterial sensory systems.

papers.title: Glutathione S transferase assembled gold silver nanoclusters activate cGAS STING immunity in breast cancer
papers.abstract: GST-mediated self-assembly of gold-silver nanoclusters activates cGAS-STING signaling and remodels antitumor immunity, enabling photothermal-immunotherapy to inhibit breast cancer growth, metastasis and recurrence.

papers.title: Dynamic climate and ecological expansion drive body morphology evolution in fossil and extant neocoleoid cephalopods
papers.abstract: Cephalopods originated in the Cambrian approximately 500 million years ago, evolving from externally shelled ancestors to forms with diverse morphologies. Despite their morphological diversity, the macroevolutionary patterns and drivers of their diversification remain incompletely understood. Here, we construct a time-calibrated phylogenetic framework for fossil and extant neocoleoid cephalopods and quantify evolutionary rates and morphological disparity over ~490 million years. We identify five peaks in morphological diversification, indicating rapid evolutionary phases during historical periods. Morphological disparity exhibits a time-lagged response to evolutionary rate shifts. Sea surface temperature and ecological factors are macroevolutionary drivers shaping evolutionary rates and morphological disparity. Major environmental perturbations, including the end–Permian and end–Triassic mass extinctions and Early Triassic and Toarcian hyperthermal events, are associated with reduced evolutionary rates, whereas post–Cretaceous conditions correspond to elevated rates driven by ecological release and adaptive radiation. Our results show that cephalopod morphological evolution is governed by coupled environmental and ecological processes that structure evolutionary dynamics over deep time.

papers.title: Time-resolved ligand dynamics revealed in a β-lactamase using room-temperature serial crystallography
papers.abstract: β-Lactamases hydrolyse β-lactam antibiotics and are key antimicrobial resistance determinants in globally important bacterial pathogens. Here, we report on the use of time-resolved room-temperature drop-on-fixed-target serial crystallography, complemented by classical single-crystal crystallography and molecular simulations, to investigate reversible covalent inhibition of the serine β-lactamase CTX-M-15 by the diazabicyclooctane inhibitor avibactam, used to treat infections by β-lactamase producing organisms. A covalent ring-opened avibactam carbamoyl complex is observed in crystal structures 80 ms after mixing, which rearranges on a 1.3 s to 600 s time scale. Together with molecular dynamics simulations and density functional theory calculations based on our experimental structures, our data suggest that in the initially observed species the avibactam N-sulfate nitrogen is poorly positioned to attack the carbamoyl carbon to initiate the 5-exo-trig recyclisation required for inhibitor reformation. This complex then undergoes conformational changes that potentially prime it for this intramolecular reaction. These data reveal the conformational dynamics and stereoelectronic basis of diazobicyclooctane inhibition and demonstrate how the combination of room-temperature serial crystallography and molecular simulations can capture ligand motions in enzyme active sites on millisecond-to-second timescales, delivering mechanistically relevant understanding of the dynamic behaviour of enzyme-bound species.

papers.title: Enhanced sampling enables binding site water reorganization in polarizable absolute binding free energy calculations
papers.abstract: Water molecules shape protein-ligand binding, but their exchange and reorganization within buried binding sites remain difficult to sample in absolute binding free-energy calculations. Here, the authors combine the polarizable AMOEBA force field with Lambda-ABF-OPES to obtain binding free energies across five diverse complexes while capturing persistent hydration motifs, water exchange, and coupled ligand-pocket-solvent relaxation without water-specific collective variables.

papers.title: TARMAC as a taxonomy for robot manipulation in chemistry
papers.abstract: Laboratory automation has made well-defined experimental protocols increasingly executable by machines, yet many physical manipulations remain difficult to generalize, including both those surrounding automated protocols and those not readily accommodated by current automation. Here, the authors propose TARMAC, a taxonomy that organizes these actions into reusable primitives, demonstrating its applicability across various platforms and workflows.

papers.title: Structural and functional insights into the p160 Rho-associated coiled-coil-containing protein kinase ROCK
papers.abstract: Rho-associated protein kinases (ROCK1/2) are critical regulators of fundamental cellular processes and represent promising therapeutic targets for various pathologies, particularly cardiovascular disease. While the terminal globular kinase domain and the PH-C1 tandem (PHn-C1-PHc) are well characterized, the sequence-structure-function relationship of the central amphipathic α-helical segment remains poorly understood. Utilizing an integrative biophysical approach—including multi-angle light scattering (MALS), analytical ultracentrifugation (AUC), small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), negative-stain electron microscopy (EM), X-ray crystallography, and 3D molecular modeling—we elucidate the structural organization of the central coiled-coil region of ROCK1. Notably, the 2.2 Å resolution crystal structure of the homology region 1 (HR1) of ROCK1 reveals a canonical parallel coiled-coil dimer. This structural arrangement diverges significantly from the antiparallel coiled-coil HR1 module found in other Rho effector kinases. Combined with the structural reconstitution of full-length ROCK1, our data demonstrates that the central segment of ROCK1 forms a highly elongated coiled-coil dimer. Furthermore, EM analysis of the isolated full coiled-coil domain uncovers a dynamic oligomerization state, transitioning between a dimer and a tetramer. Together, these biophysical insights establish a foundation that opens avenues for future investigation into ROCK1 regulation, activation, and downstream signaling mechanisms.

papers.title: Phase-binarized auto-oscillation modes in wide nanoconstriction spin Hall nano-oscillators
papers.abstract: Nanoconstriction spin Hall nano-oscillators (SHNOs) are cutting-edge spintronic devices for gigahertz signal generation and neuromorphic computing, offering a CMOS-compatible nanoscale footprint, ultra-wide frequency tunability, and robust synchronization in large networks. Most previous studies have focused on constrictions narrower than 200 nm, where a single dominant spin-wave mode typically emerges. The auto-oscillation dynamics of wide constrictions remain largely unexplored. Here, using micromagnetic simulations, we demonstrate the coexistence of two independently tunable auto-oscillation modes in constrictions wider than 200 nm: a low-frequency in-phase mode and a high-frequency out-of-phase mode, both localized at opposite constriction edges. The out-of-phase mode arises from the interplay of exchange, magnetodipolar coupling, and the antisymmetric Oersted field component, producing strongly edge-localized oscillations with a nearly 180∘ phase difference. We develop an analytical two-mode framework that captures their hybridization and nonlinear competition. Their distinct subharmonic injection-locking responses enable phase-binarized states within a single wide SHNO, opening opportunities for multimode synchronization, unconventional computing, and complex phase locking in SHNO networks.

papers.title: Pain and fifty six subsequent wellbeing and life outcomes in a multicountry longitudinal study
papers.abstract: Macchia et al. use multi-country longitudinal data to explore the longer-term effects of pain across various countries. Authors find that pain is negatively linked to outcomes like flourishing, happiness, life satisfaction, and mental health among others, and positively linked to outcomes such as traumatic distress and anxiety.

papers.title: Facet-dependent molecular adsorption modulates zinc anode work function for the favourable orientation of zinc electrocrystallization
papers.abstract: While additives direct Zn electrocrystallization and impact battery performance, the mechanism remains disputed. Now it has been shown that facet-dependent work function modulation upon additive adsorption governs Fermi-level equilibration and Zn crystallographic texture across 29 additives with 93.1% accuracy, providing an interfacial electronic descriptor for additive screening towards favourable Zn electrodeposition.

papers.title: Pure-blue quantum-dot light-emitting diodes with minimal efficiency roll-off and high brightness
papers.abstract: Quantum-dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs) are promising candidates for augmented reality, virtual reality and other high-resolution microdisplay applications. For these applications, the QLEDs must sustain high efficiency at high luminance while remaining compatible with device-integration processes. However, blue QLEDs still face pronounced efficiency roll-off and processing-related performance degradation. Here we develop pure-blue-emitting quantum dots based on a CdZnSe core with a compositionally graded ZnSe/ZnSeS/ZnS shell, combined with ZnCl2-assisted surface morphology modulation. This design suppresses surface-trap-related recombination and improves processing robustness. We demonstrate bottom-emission QLEDs at 464 nm with a peak external quantum efficiency of 23.8% and a 95% external quantum efficiency retention at 50,000 cd m−2 (L95). The top-emission QLEDs reached L95 = 270,000 cd m−2 and a blue index of 586. We also demonstrate patterned QLEDs via photolithography with a resolution of 560 pixels per inch and peak external quantum efficiency of 16.5%. Our results demonstrate pure-blue quantum-dot emitters that combine Rec. 2020-near emission, minimal efficiency roll-off at high brightness, compatibility with direct photolithographic patterning and top-emission device integration for advanced display applications. Quantum dots with compositionally graded shells enhance quantum-dot LED performance, achieving pure-blue emission with a peak external quantum efficiency of 23.8%, 95% of which is retained at a luminance of 50,000 cd m−2.

papers.title: Deaminative nucleophilic substitution of alkyl amines
papers.abstract: Nucleophilic substitution is one of the most fundamental and widely used strategies for alkyl functionalization. For more than a century, such transformations have relied predominantly on alcohols and alkyl halides as the primary alkylating synthons. Here we report a nucleophilic substitution strategy that uses the unique reactivity of N-alkyl nitroamines, enabling alkyl amines to serve as a latent and readily available class of direct alkylation reagents. Through a systematic investigation of N-alkyl nitroamine reactivity, we have developed a polarity-driven platform for direct deaminative functionalization, enabling broad nucleophilic substitution of alkyl amines to efficiently construct alkyl C−halogen, C−C, C−N, C−O and C−S bonds. The method accommodates primary, secondary and tertiary alkyl amines as well as benzylic amines. This strategy overcomes the intrinsic limitations of aliphatic diazonium chemistry and substantially expands the scope of nucleophilic substitution reactions hitherto inaccessible by conventional approaches. Nucleophilic substitution is a fundamental strategy for alkyl functionalization, traditionally relying on alcohols and alkyl halides as alkylating reagents. Now a deaminative nucleophilic substitution strategy that uses alkyl amines as direct alkylation reagents is reported. Harnessing the reactivity of N-alkyl nitroamines, this process enables the efficient construction of diverse alkyl C–halogen, C–C, C–N, C–O and C–S bonds.

papers.title: Wastewater surveillance captures multi-marker responses to short-term examination stress in a university population
papers.abstract: Using wastewater surveillance of an Australian university population, this study reveals examination-period increases in biomarkers of oxidative stress and suggestive rises in antidepressant use, indicating heightened mental health burden during academic stress.

papers.title: Author Correction: Perovskite lattice compliance enables efficient and stable bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem photovoltaics
Global temperature-related mortality associated with El-Nino Southern Oscillation
papers.abstract: Epidemiological estimates suggest that global heat-related mortality increased by 29% during very strong El Niño years, with the greatest burdens occurring in low- and medium- Human Development Index regions.

papers.title: Perioperative ivonescimab with or without chemotherapy in resectable non-small cell lung cancer: a phase 2 trial
papers.abstract: In a nonrandomized phase 2 trial, patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer received perioperative ivonescimab as monotherapy or with chemotherapy, leading to encouraging pathological response rates in both cohorts, and sustained circulating tumor DNA negativity throughout neoadjuvant therapy may be predictive of response.

papers.title: Digital cell factories for biomanufacturing
papers.abstract: Metabolism-centric digital cell factories offer a pragmatic route to biomanufacturing optimization by emphasizing predictions of production performance and economic outcomes over biological detail.

papers.title: Digital and hybrid interventions for subacute and chronic low back pain: component network meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Digital and hybrid interventions combining exercise, education, and psychological components are increasingly used for low back pain (LBP), but it remains unclear which components and combinations drive efficacy. We conducted a prospectively registered component network meta-analysis (CNMA) to evaluate their efficacy and safety for non-specific LBP. Six databases and two trial registries were searched to May 2025. Data on disability, pain intensity, and adverse events were analysed using a Bayesian random-effects CNMA. Of 2809 records, 56 reports of 46 studies (6717 participants; 80% chronic low back pain) were included. Hybrid interventions combining digital and in-person exercise with in-person psychological components (MD: –22.21; 95%-CrI: –34.11 to –10.67), digital and in-person exercise (MD: –15.75; 95%-CrI: –22.79 to –8.80), or digital exercise with physiotherapy (MD: –13.17; 95%-CrI: –21.18 to –5.16) reduced disability versus no intervention at short-term (minimal clinically important difference (MCID): 4.92/100 Oswestry Disability Index). Digital and in-person exercise (MD: -1.76; 95%-CrI: -2.62; -0.87) and combined digital exercise training with in-person education (MD: -1.73; 95%-CrI: -2.71; -0.83) improved pain intensity beyond the MCID (0.82/10 numeric pain rating scale). No serious adverse events were noted. Multicomponent hybrid interventions appear safe and may provide clinically meaningful improvements for chronic LBP.

papers.title: Cross-paradigm audit of large language model judges for clinical text evaluation
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly being used to evaluate clinical texts, a concept known as LLM-as-a-judge. However, most of the existing evidence focuses on English data and uses pooled agreement metrics that obscure clinically relevant failure modes. This study audited six open-weight models against expert judges on four German clinical datasets covering report and nursing documentation summarization, discharge summary generation, and patient letter generation. The models were evaluated across three paradigms and four prompt configurations. Alignment with experts varied by criterion and corpus, and no configuration proved reliable across paradigms. All judges exhibited position and identity bias. Substituting LLM-as-a-judge for the expert panel shifted 57.2% of pointwise categories, swapped 41.7% of pairwise winners, missed 10.2% of clinical errors, and inverted clinical priorities by overrating the criteria succinct and accurate. Therefore, LLM-as-a-judge is not a safe substitute for experts in German clinical text evaluations, and deployment thresholds should follow decision-impact analysis for LLM-as-a-judge in clinical contexts.

papers.abstract: Small Methods, EarlyView.
