papers.title: iTBS and cTBS to an individualized dlPFC target produce differential working memory improvement and session-dependent putamen deactivation
papers.abstract: We evaluated the effects of individualized left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) theta-burst stimulation (TBS) on working memory performance and task-related BOLD activity in 115 healthy adults (iTBS: n = 63; cTBS: n = 52). Stimulation was delivered to an individually-localized left dlPFC target identified using task-based fMRI, with each TBS visit consisting of five 600-pulse trains delivered as either the intermittent (iTBS) or continuous (cTBS) protocol. Participants completed the Sternberg Working Memory paradigm at baseline and approximately 24 hours after each visit. Groups were well-matched at baseline on all behavioral and neural measures. iTBS produced a significant improvement in working memory accuracy across sessions while cTBS did not, with a significant Group × Session interaction confirming differential trajectories. Both groups showed reaction time speedup across sessions, consistent with a shared practice effect. Despite these behavioral differences, BOLD activity at the dlPFC stimulation site showed no significant effects of Group, Session, or their interaction. Whole-brain analyses revealed significant session-dependent attenuation of bilateral putamen deactivation during the retention interval in both stimulation groups, with greater putamen deactivation at baseline correlating negatively with working memory accuracy. These results demonstrate that individualized task-based fMRI targeting can link TBS to circuit-level behavioral change, and that downstream subcortical responses may be more sensitive indices of TBS effects than activation at the stimulation site. The absence of a sham condition limits causal inference; observed differences reflect stimulation pattern rather than absolute TBS effects.

papers.title: Analysis of structural modifications and metagenomic sequencing during the ensiling of Caragana korshinskii provides insights into how extrusion pretreatment promotes lignocellulose degradation
papers.abstract: In this study, to address the problems of poor silage fermentation quality and difficulty degrading lignocellulose interfering with resource utilization of Caragana korshinskii biomass, the effects of extrusion pretreatment (temperature 140°C and screw speed of 400 rpm) on its ensiling process were investigated. Results showed that pretreatment significantly improved silage quality, with lactic acid and water-soluble carbohydrate content increasing significantly (P < 0.05), neutral detergent fiber content decreasing significantly (P < 0.05), and hemicellulose degradation rate increasing by 31.64 ± 1.20% compared with the normal silage group. Microstructure analysis showed that pretreatment destroyed the dense biomass structure, increased specific surface area and porosityenhanced hydrophilicity, and reduced crystallinity, thus promoting the degradation of hemicellulose and cellulose. Metagenomic analysis further showed that extrusion pretreatment remodeled the microbial community structure, increasing the proportion of lactic acid bacteria such as Weissella and Companilactobacillus, and significantly increased the abundance of genes encoding debranching enzymes (CE3 and CE12) involved in hemicellulose degradation as well as main chain hydrolases (GH43 and GH8) (P < 0.05). This study provides insights into the mechanisms by which extrusion pretreatment improves Caragana korshinskii silage in terms of physical and chemical structure and microbial functions, and this in turn may provide a technical and theoretical basis for understanding how efficient ensiling can be achieved more broadly in high-lignocellulosic feedstocks.

papers.title: A compact set of sea star footprint proteins mediates the adhesion of Asterina gibbosa
papers.abstract: The study highlights a conserved core adhesive toolkit across sea star species, with species-specific reshuffling of single protein domains. Detailed analyses revealed distinct roles for adhesive proteins in forming cohesive and surface-binding layers. These findings refine the molecular understanding of sea star adhesion, emphasizing evolutionary conservation and functional diversity of adhesive proteins. The research provides a foundation for further studies into how these proteins enable strong yet reversible adhesion in marine environments.

papers.title: COX2 contributes to the spatial reorganization of B7H4 + and CD44v6 + niches promoting therapy resistance in ER- breast cancer
papers.abstract: Estrogen receptor-negative (ER-) breast tumors are aggressive subtypes with limited therapeutic options. Cyclooxygenase-2 promotes chronic inflammation, immune suppression, and therapeutic resistance. Whether COX2 signaling organizes tumor microenvironments across oxygen gradients remains unclear. Restricted Exchange Environment Chambers (REECs) were used to explore the COX2 impact on spatial tumor architecture across oxygen gradients. Baseline COX2+, B7H4+, and CD44v6+ cells exhibited distinct distributions, with CD44v6 predominance. Inflammatory stimulation increased and spatially reorganized COX2+, B7H4+, and COX2+CD44v6+ populations. While COX2+ cells occupied oxygenated-to-intermediate zones, B7H4+ populations were enriched in intermediate-to-hypoxic regions, and CD44v6 remained broadly distributed. Diclofenac disrupted this organization and reduced clustering of COX2+, B7H4+, and COX2+CD44v6+ phenotypes. Poor-outcome patients showed high COX2 at the tumor-stroma interface as well as altered COX2+, B7H4+, and CD44v6+ clustering phenotypes. These findings identify COX2-dependent microenvironments as clinically relevant features of therapeutic resistance. Diclofenac preferentially depleted hypoxic compartments preserved following cisplatin treatment alone, supporting the targeting of spatially organized inflammatory niches to improve therapeutic response.

papers.title: Friend advice influences mate choice through brain-to-brain synchrony and computational decision processes
papers.abstract: Individuals often rely on friends’ advice when making mate-choice decisions under uncertainty, yet how such advice is integrated into decision-making remains unclear. Using fNIRS hyperscanning, we simultaneously recorded neural and behavioral activity from 66 adult friend dyads (33 female dyads) during interactive advice phases. Only the bidirectional Social Information Processing (SIP) computational model best fit the behavioral data, indicating that social influence arises from reciprocal interaction rather than one-way transmission. Behaviorally, positive advice from in the relationship advisors increased mate-choice intention, whereas negative advice from single advisors more strongly influenced decision-making. Both conditions elicited enhanced interpersonal neural synchrony (INS) in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), linked to risk evaluation, and in the left superior and middle temporal gyri (l-STG, l-MTG), associated with semantic processing and value transformation. Machine learning analyses showed that task-level INS robustly forecasted overall advice influence. Together, these findings demonstrate that friend advice influence emerges from dynamic brain-to-brain alignment in control and semantic networks—reflecting emotional sharing during positive advice and risk re-evaluation during negative advice. This study extending SIP theory to interactive decision-making and revealing how friend advice influence mate-choice decision.

papers.title: Molecular origin of pressure-induced re-entrant phase separation of CO 2 –H 2 O mixtures
papers.abstract: CO2 and H2O are the predominant fluid components in the Earth’s interior, spanning from the crust to the mantle. Fluid–fluid immiscibility in binary CO2–H2O fluids is of particular interest owing to its implications for geochemical processes and industrial applications, including geological CO2 sequestration. CO2–H2O fluids exhibit re-entrant phase separation upon compression, yet, the microscopic origin of this behaviour remains unclear, in contrast to well-studied temperature-induced re-entrant phenomena. Here, using molecular dynamics simulations, we reveal the microscopic mechanisms underlying pressure-induced re-entrant phase separation in CO2–H2O mixtures. CO2 and H2O exhibit distinct behaviours near their critical solution pressures, which highlights the pivotal role of H2O in fluid–fluid separation. Specifically, H2O–H2O interactions provide the primary contribution to phase separation; strong short-range H2O–H2O attraction accelerates segregation of H2O molecules under high-density conditions, whereas the recovery of hydrogen bonding drives segregation under low-density conditions. A simple united-atom approach demonstrate that intermolecular interactions outweigh differences in molecular size in pressure-induced phase separation. Our findings identify the molecular origin of pressure-induced fluid–fluid separation, suggesting the potential for re-entrant phase behaviour in a broad range of other binary mixtures.

papers.title: Machine-learning-based flow-synthesis of platinum-group-metal high-entropy alloy nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Synthesis of size-controlled and compositionally homogeneous alloy nanoparticles (NPs) is challenging but important, because the particle size and elemental distribution significantly affect NP performance. This is particularly important for high-entropy alloy (HEA) NPs with highly complex compositions and structures. In this study, we established a method for synthesizing size-controlled and homogeneously alloyed RuRhPdIrPt HEA NPs by integrating flow synthesis with interpretable machine learning. The alloy homogeneity was evaluated using compositions derived from X-ray fluorescence and lattice constants from powder X-ray diffraction patterns as target variables, revealing the threshold of reaction temperature required for homogeneous alloying through decision tree classification. Partial least squares regression enabled particle-size predictions via the synthesis parameters (cross-validated R2 value of 0.73) and the quantification of parameter contributions. This study translates empirical knowledge into interpretable mathematical models, thereby providing quantitative guidelines for the reproducible synthesis of complex HEA NPs.

papers.title: Allosteric inhibition of NDM-1 by thanatin preserves the di-zinc center while restricting dynamics
papers.abstract: The New Delhi metallo‑β‑lactamase 1 (NDM‑1) is a major driver of carbapenem resistance in Gram‑negative pathogens, yet the molecular basis by which antimicrobial peptides inhibit this enzyme has remained unresolved. Here, we combine high‑resolution NMR spectroscopy, CSP-driven HADDOCK docking, intermolecular NOE cross-validation, and molecular dynamics simulations to reveal a distinct zinc-retaining dynamic allosteric mechanism. Thanatin binds adjacent to the catalytic groove, preserving the native di‑zinc coordination environment while simultaneously restricting the dynamics of the L3 catalytic loop, as confirmed by Zn‑bound spectral fingerprints and EDTA titration experiments. Real-time NMR and spectrophotometric kinetics confirm that this dynamic restriction induces a dose-dependent functional inhibition, structurally explained by a L3-loop displacement that prevents optimal substrate accommodation. This conformational restriction explains how the peptide inhibits the enzyme while maintaining a zinc-bound but catalytically compromised state, a finding that reconciles prior macroscopic biochemical observations with a new atomic-level structural model. In bacterial assays, this allosteric inhibition translates to a moderate restoration of carbapenem sensitivity, resulting in a 50% reduction in viable cell output even under high-level enzyme expression. Our findings help define a mechanistic framework for designing next‑generation peptide inhibitors that target the dynamic vulnerabilities of metallo‑β‑lactamases.

papers.title: Submicron CsPbBr 3 crystallites prepared through in situ moisture-driven decomposition of Cs 4 PbBr 6 microcrystals
papers.abstract: Achieving stable and controllable optical gain at the micro- and nanoscale remains a fundamental challenge for the development of miniature lasers and integrated on-chip light sources. In this work, the authors use optically inert Cs4PbBr6 microcrystals to show that a moisture-induced confined solid-state phase transformation can generate sub-micron gain units capable of supporting stimulated emission, with individual CsPbBr3 submicron crystals exhibiting clear narrow linewidth emission, a strong linear polarization dependence and lasing.

papers.title: Performance analysis of classical adiabatic annealing on Ising machines
papers.abstract: Ising machines are a promising approach to solve optimization problems. They map them onto the Ising model and search for low-energy configurations. However, navigating the rugged energy landscapes remains difficult. To improve this navigation, classical adiabatic annealing has been proposed as a heuristic optimization method for classical Ising machines. Using this technique, the Hamiltonian of the Ising machine is gradually transformed from an easily solvable Hamiltonian to the target Hamiltonian. However, its claimed effectiveness is primarily motivated by an analogy to quantum adiabatic annealing, and systematic benchmarking has remained limited. In this work, we investigate the potential of classical adiabatic annealing as an optimization strategy for analog Ising machines. Using continuation methods, we analyze its dynamics and identify saddle node bifurcations as a key mechanism limiting performance. Motivated by this insight, we develop an optimized annealing strategy we refer to as hybrid classical adiabatic annealing, designed to circumvent these bifurcations and assess its performance. Although the proposed approach can improve convergence to optimal solutions, numerical simulations show only marginal performance gains compared to other optimization strategies. We therefore conclude that, while the hybrid strategy can offer occasional benefits, it does not provide a sufficient practical advantage over simpler, existing techniques.

papers.title: Twisted shock waves enable ballistic microparticle manipulation
papers.abstract: The ability to control the motion of microscopic objects in liquids is important for applications ranging from microfluidics to the study of fast hydrodynamic processes. However, conventional optical and acoustic manipulation techniques rely mainly on continuous forcing, limiting access to impulsive dynamics on nanosecond timescales. Here we show that spiral-shaped nanosecond laser pulses focused into a thin liquid layer generate twisted shock waves with tunable angular momentum and peak pressures on the order of gigapascals. Time-resolved shadowgraphy and two-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations independently show the same dependence on the spiral geometry, revealing that the angular momentum can be controlled through the excitation shape. We further show that a 10-μm polystyrene particle exhibits loop-like ballistic motion on nanosecond timescales, with complementary measurements along two orthogonal directions supporting this interpretation. These results provide an impulse-driven approach for controlling and probing ultrafast particle dynamics in liquids, with potential applications in high-pressure microfluidics, microrheology, and short-time hydrodynamics.

papers.title: Suppression of stripe-ordered structural phases in monolayer IrTe 2 by a gold substrate
papers.abstract: Metal-assisted exfoliation of two-dimensional (2D) materials has emerged as an efficient route to isolating large-area monolayer crystals, yet the influence of the supporting metal substrate on their intrinsic properties remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate successful gold-assisted exfoliation of monolayer IrTe2 up to the millimeter scale. Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), combined with first-principles calculations, reveals that the low-energy electronic structure closely resembles that of a freestanding monolayer 1T-IrTe2. We find that quasi-covalent hybridization together with substrate-induced strain leads to only modest modifications of the electronic bands. Although strain contributes to phase stability, it is essentially hybridization that drives the stabilization of the 1T-phase of the monolayer IrTe2 by suppressing stripe-ordered phase transitions. These results establish gold-assisted exfoliation as a robust route to prepare a large-area monolayer IrTe2 and highlight the role of metal-substrate interaction in engineering 2D materials with tailored structural phases.

papers.title: Real-time dual-telescope normalization for improved density estimation in absorption muography
papers.abstract: Absorption muography infers path-averaged density from the attenuation of atmospheric muons. Transient flux variations driven by weather, solar activity, and geomagnetism bias sequential measurements that rely on a non-simultaneous background. Here we show a real-time dual-telescope normalization in which two identical plastic-scintillator telescopes operate in parallel, one viewing open sky as a reference and one viewing the target. Their count-rate ratio cancels common-mode flux changes and tracks detector drift. A 140-h no-target run yields a stable calibration, and stacked acrylic slabs give an empirical transmission–thickness curve. Applied to blind targets, the dual-telescope workflow recovers the densities of 20-cm aluminum and 10-cm stainless-steel blocks within uncertainties, whereas a single-telescope workflow shows systematic biases of +18.95% and −22.82%. A vertical stack of the two telescopes further improves common-mode rejection, reducing calibration ratio scatter from 7.6% to 3.3%. The method is model-independent, removes systematic density biases in any campaign where a simultaneous flux reference is feasible, and is directly applicable to field deployments.

papers.title: Synthetic 2D quantum materials from atomic weaving of 1D nanoribbons
papers.abstract: The bottom-up van der Waals (vdW) assembly of quantum materials from low-dimensional building blocks provides a flexible and structurally defined route for designing materials with tailored quantum properties. While stacking two-dimensional (2D) vdW materials has yielded highly tunable platforms for emergent topological and correlated phenomena and has opened pathways toward three-dimensional (3D) layered architectures with extensive lateral design flexibility, the bottom-up vdW assembly of other low-dimensional materials remains largely unexplored. Here, we propose an atomic-scale Lego construction strategy that assembles 2D materials from 1D nanoribbons, embedding design freedom at the structural level through atomic-scale control over lattice geometry, stacking, and edge configuration. Using graphene nanoribbons (GNRs) as a prototype, we develop a general weaving approach that interlaces flat or curved ribbons into stable, periodic 2D networks-analogous to stacking 2D sheets into 3D crystals, but instead progressing from 1D elements to 2D architectures. The resulting woven GNRs (w-GNRs) exhibit geometry-dependent electronic behavior: ribbon width determines the band gap, while inter-ribbon spacing controls the bandwidth and leads to flat-band formation near the Fermi level. By weaving curved ribbons, we construct kagome and square lattice configurations that host symmetry-protected flat bands and orbital degeneracies. This atomic Lego framework enables scalable construction of artificial 2D materials from 1D components, expanding the design space for highly tunable 2D systems with emergent quantum properties.

papers.title: Photoluminescence from Cr 3+ excited orbital states in magnetically ordered CrCl 3
papers.abstract: Control of magnetic order through optical manipulation of orbital states can be realized in a wide range of materials, including insulators. In the latter case, electrons are excited into different electronic states, whose character may be a complex result of spin-orbit-lattice coupling. Here, we use a combination of polarization-resolved photoluminescence spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations to study excited Cr3+ ions in bulk, insulating, antiferromagnetic CrCl3. Our results demonstrate a temperature-dependent preferential polarization direction below ~17 K, which reorients in the presence of an applied in-plane magnetic field. Density functional theory calculations reveal a local distortion of the ligand field and the generation of out-of-plane spin and orbital moments, following the excitation of Cr3+ ion. These changes link the photoluminescence polarization to the magnetic state of CrCl3. Our findings provide insight into the electronic structure of excited-state Cr3+ ions and suggest that CrCl3 is a promising candidate for opto-orbitronic applications.

papers.title: Risk of de novo immune-related adverse events in patients with cancer and autoimmune disease receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) can cause immune-related adverse events (irAEs). Patients with preexisting autoimmune disease are often excluded from clinical trials because of concerns about disease exacerbation or new immune-mediated toxicities, limiting comparative safety evidence. We compared the risk of de novo irAEs among patients with cancer and preexisting autoimmune disease initiating ICIs versus chemotherapy or targeted therapy. A target trial was emulated using Merative MarketScan claims from 2014–2023 with a new-user, active-comparator design. Adults with cancer and preexisting autoimmune disease initiating ICIs, chemotherapy, or targeted therapy were identified. Propensity score matching (1:1) was used to balance measured baseline characteristics. The primary outcome was a de novo irAE. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals overall and across prespecified subgroups by key clinical characteristics. Matched cohorts included 3601 pairs for ICI versus chemotherapy and 1479 pairs for ICI versus targeted therapy. ICI initiation was associated with a higher risk of de novo irAEs than chemotherapy (HR = 1.71, 95% CI = 1.49–1.97) and targeted therapy (HR = 1.43, 95% CI = 1.20–1.70). Estimates varied by ICI class, cancer type, and baseline autoimmune disease category. CTLA-4 inhibitors had the highest estimates among ICI classes, while liver cancer and baseline endocrine autoimmune disease had elevated estimates across both comparisons. ICI initiation was associated with a higher risk of de novo irAEs in this population, with variation by ICI class, cancer type, and autoimmune disease category. These findings may inform individualized treatment decisions, although residual confounding remains an important consideration. Immune checkpoint inhibitors are cancer treatments that help the immune system attack cancer cells, but they can also cause immune-related side effects. People who already have autoimmune diseases are often excluded from clinical trials, so less is known about the safety of these treatments in this population. We used US health insurance claims to compare patients with cancer and preexisting autoimmune disease who started immune checkpoint inhibitors with similar patients receiving chemotherapy or targeted therapy. Patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors had a higher risk of developing new immune-related adverse events. These findings provide additional real-world safety information that may help patients and clinicians better understand treatment risks and guide future research.

papers.title: Fine-mapping of breast cancer susceptibility loci highlights critical methodological dependencies and the value of complementary approaches
papers.abstract: Summary statistics fine-mapping methods are used where individual data cannot be shared, yet their performance on real data remains poorly evaluated. Here we assess candidate causal variant (CCV) prioritisation and concordance between summary statistics fine-mapping methods and published breast cancer results generated by multinomial stepwise regression (MNR). Using the same European-ancestry GWAS dataset as in the published MNR analysis (109,900 cases, 88,937 controls) and partial in-sample Linkage Disequilibrium (LD) data, we applied finiMOM, SuSiE and FINEMAP on 129 breast cancer susceptibility regions. CCV concordance between methods and with MNR was assessed using recall, precision and Jaccard index. Genes were annotated using INQUISIT and compared using recall. Sensitivity analyses assessed out-of-sample LD. Here we show variable method convergence, with SuSiE providing the best balance between number and distribution of predictions and MNR concordance. The assumed number of causal variants affected fine-mapping results, with no setting performing consistently across regions and credible sets lost at higher values. We provide a sensitivity analysis to guide parameter selection. SuSiE and MNR results differ, with 30 MNR credible sets and 52 MNR genes not prioritised by SuSiE. Novel credible sets and genes are also found by SuSiE. Orthogonal evidence supported heterogeneous variant prioritisation. Out-of-sample LD reduces recall by 3%. Data quality, array heterogeneity and LD explain part of the discordance, implicating methodological differences as the main drivers. Fine-mapping results are sensitive to methodological choices and parameters. Comprehensive evaluation, sensitivity analyses, complementary methods and orthogonal evidence are essential for reliable fine-mapping. Some people inherit genetic changes that raise their risk for breast cancer and finding them helps us understand the disease. Fine-mapping is a method that identifies such changes. Although several methods exist, we know little about how well they agree, and it is difficult to tell which results are reliable. Using data from 109,900 people with breast cancer and 88,937 without, we compared these methods against known results across 129 genomic regions. While some results agree, most are method-unique, indicating that combining different methods can matter more than choosing between them. We identify several factors that influence fine-mapping results and show that careful evaluation is needed to obtain reliable findings and improve our understanding of disease.

papers.title: Cognitive frailty typologies and subsequent dementia in a large representative sample of the English population
papers.abstract: Cognitive Frailty (CF), the coexistence of mild cognitive impairment with physical frailty, may represent an intermediate state between functional vulnerability and preclinical dementia. Its potential reversibility makes it an important target for prevention. Distinguishing patterns of CF that are more and less likely to lead to dementia, and associated factors, is important for developing interventions. Using data from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (Waves 4-9), we examined different typologies of CF based on specific cognitive impairments demonstrated. We compared longitudinal outcomes of incident dementia over 10 years for the different typologies. We also examined the impact of inequalities (Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) and household wealth), cognitive reserve (low education), and psychosocial factors (depression and loneliness) on the longitudinal models. CF groups with executive function (using verbal fluency) and/or processing speed impairment (Group 1) are distinguished from those with memory impairment only (Group 2) or impaired memory and executive function and/or processing speed (Group 3). Inequalities, cognitive reserve and psychosocial factors all show association with CF likelihood, but education (odds ratio (OR) of no qualifications compared to degree/higher education = 1.632 (Group 1) and 3.436 (Group 3)), IMD (OR 1.656 (Group 1 quintile 5), 2.083 (Group 3 quintile 4) compared to quintile 1) and loneliness (OR 1.208 (Group 1), 1.185 (Group 3)) are only associated with CF where executive function/processing speed are key characteristics. Longitudinally, only CF groupings with memory impairment (OR 2.024, Group 2; 2.733, Group 3) are predictive of dementia. Distinguishing typologies of CF and associated risk factors is important for estimating future dementia risk, and for targeted design of interventions. Cognitive Frailty is a state in which an older person has mild difficulties with memory and thinking skills at the same time as physical health and strength issues. This may indicate irreversible development of dementia, but can also indicate more reversible conditions. It is important to work out which patterns of cognitive frailty are more likely to lead to dementia, so help can be targeted. Using existing data collected over many years, we separated people with cognitive frailty into three groups. Those with impairments in ability to keep on task, producing words in a particular category, and who processed information slowly were not more likely to develop dementia, but groups with mild memory problems were. Living in a socioeconomically disenfranchised area, low education, depression, and loneliness were associated with a greater likelihood of cognitive frailty, but mainly for the group without memory impairments. Our findings suggest different types of cognitive frailty may need different kinds of help.

papers.title: Thermochemical adsorption at high overpotentials limits molecular CO-to-methanol electroreduction
papers.abstract: Applied potential controls charge-transfer kinetics, but thermochemical steps can limit electrocatalytic rates. Now it has been shown that CO-to-methanol conversion shifts from charge-transfer-limited kinetics to adsorption-limited kinetics as overpotential increases, establishing CO adsorption energy as a descriptor of the thermochemical constraint.

papers.title: Disentanglement of interfacial electric fields and electrochemical potential gradients reveals a multidimensional kinetic landscape
papers.abstract: Electrochemical kinetics are shaped by both the thermodynamic driving force and interfacial polarization. Now it has been shown that that activation energies decrease with increasing potential but increase with greater deviation of the potential from the potential of zero total charge, revealing a multidimensional kinetic landscape.

papers.title: Synthesis of atomically thin amorphous materials
papers.abstract: Atomically thin amorphous materials (ATAMs) combine atomic-scale thickness with the absence of long-range in-plane periodicity, encompassing layered two-dimensional amorphous materials and non-layered atomically thin amorphous films. These materials lack in-plane translational and orientational order yet retain distinct short- and medium-range atomic order within their film-like configurations. The scalable synthesis of ATAMs is essential for advancing both fundamental understanding and technological deployment, bridging the gap from the laboratory to the factory. Here we discuss ATAM synthesis from a mechanism-guided perspective, including thermodynamic suppression, kinetic freezing, template induction and defect- or ion-driven amorphization. We then establish links between local disorder descriptors with functional properties, compare controllable and scalable production strategies and examine outstanding challenges related to stability, standardized performance metrics and wafer-scale integration. Finally, we outline artificial-intelligence-assisted closed-loop strategies for application-targeted scalable synthesis and wafer-scale manufacturing. By integrating mechanistic insights with scalable fabrication principles, here we aim to provide a roadmap for the synthesis and deployment of emerging ATAMs and to offer a forward-looking perspective for accelerating progress in this rapidly evolving field. Atomically thin amorphous materials combine atomic-scale thickness with local structural disorder, creating unusual transport, interfacial, electronic and catalytic properties. This Review outlines the mechanism-guided synthesis of atomically thin amorphous materials, scalable manufacturing and structure–property relationships and discusses AI-assisted closed-loop strategies for application-oriented design and wafer-scale production.

papers.title: Stable anode-free sodium batteries enabled by controlled oligomerization
papers.abstract: Anode-free sodium batteries (AFSBs) offer a promising route to low cost, high-energy-density energy storage, but their practical application is limited by irreversible sodium loss during cycling. Here we report a molecular-level electrolyte design strategy that mitigates sodium loss by simultaneously promoting highly reversible sodium deposition and suppressing electrolyte decomposition, enabled by the cyclic ether 1,3-dioxane (DOX). Weak coordination of DOX with Na+ facilitates Na+ desolvation and reversible sodium deposition, while controlled DOX oligomerization forms a thin and robust solid–electrolyte interphase that suppresses continuous electrolyte decomposition and stabilizes sodium plating/stripping. As a result, 300-mAh-level AFSB pouch cells with a cathode loading of ~20 mg cm−2 retain ~80% capacity after 1,400 cycles at 1 C, operate at rates up to 3 C, maintain 88% capacity at −40 °C and achieve a round-trip energy efficiency up to ~98%. These results demonstrate a molecular electrolyte design strategy for extending the lifetime of AFSBs. Anode-free sodium batteries are limited by irreversible sodium loss during cycling. Here the authors introduce a moderate-strain cyclic ether that redirects electrolyte decomposition to form a thin, robust interphase, thereby minimizing sodium consumption and extending cycling stability.

papers.title: Grain boundary engineering using metallomesogen in formamidinium–caesium lead triiodide for stable perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells
papers.abstract: Formamidinium (FA)-doped caesium lead triiodide, Cs(FA)PbI3, is a promising front-cell absorber for tandem solar cells owing to its good stability, yet obtaining high-quality films remains a challenge. Here we identify that sparse doping of oversized FA cations induces severe grain boundary (GB) distortion, thereby facilitating defect generation and performance deterioration. To mitigate this, we develop a Pb-based metallomesogen that forms a mesophase exhibiting both solid-like and liquid-like properties. The phase characteristics enable the Pb-based metallomesogen to distribute uniformly along GBs of Cs(FA)PbI3 film, alleviating GB distortion, relieving shear strain, preserving lattice integrity and mitigating defect formation. Consequently, perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells based on a 1.66-eV Cs(FA)PbI3 absorber incorporating a Br-containing GB modifier achieve a champion efficiency of 32.08% (certified 31.62%), retaining 95% of the initial performance after ~3,000 h under maximum power point tracking and 93% after 1,500 h under 85% relative humidity and 85 °C damp-heat stressing. Formamidinium–caesium lead triiodide perovskites show promise in terms of stability, yet their solar cell efficiency remains limited. Li et al. use a metallomesogen with mesophase to stabilize perovskite grain boundaries, improving both the efficiency and stability of perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells.

papers.title: Directing solvent reactivity
papers.abstract: Anode-free sodium batteries eliminate excessive sodium on the anode, maximizing cell-level energy density, but are limited by irreversible sodium loss during electroplating–stripping. Now, a low-strain cyclic solvent forms an oligomerized interphase, enabling highly reversible sodium deposition without functional additives or electrode modifications.

papers.title: Global, regional and national burden of cervical cancer in 1990–2023 with forecasts to 2050: a Global Burden of Disease study
papers.abstract: Analyses of the Global Burden of Disease study reported 887,000 new cases and 369,000 deaths from cervical cancer worldwide in 2023, which are forecasted to rise by 2050.

papers.title: Neoadjuvant botensilimab with or without balstilimab in pMMR and dMMR colon cancer: the phase 2 UNICORN trial
papers.abstract: In the phase 2 UNICORN trial, a short course of neoadjuvant botensilimab and balstilimab achieved the primary endpoint of pathological major response rate in patients with pMMR or dMMR colon cancer.

papers.title: Povorcitinib for nonsegmental vitiligo: two randomized, controlled, phase 3 STOP-V trials
papers.abstract: In the STOP-V1 and STOP-V2 trials, povorcitinib (an oral JAK1 inhibitor) was superior to placebo in improvement in F-VASI75 score in individuals with nonsegmental vitiligo.

papers.title: Functional readouts of neural organoids
papers.abstract: Human neural organoids have become powerful systems for investigating neural development, circuit formation and disease mechanisms in a species-specific context. Traditional animal models and two-dimensional cultures have long informed our understanding of neural activity, but they cannot reproduce the genetic, developmental and architectural complexity of the human brain. Neural organoids bridge this gap by enabling direct measurement of neuronal activity at cellular, ensemble and network scales. Functional interrogation now spans calcium and voltage imaging, patch clamp electrophysiology, and multielectrode array recordings, enabled by bioengineering advances that improve organoid viability and electrode–tissue coupling. Multi-regional assembloid models and xenotransplantation approaches further extend functional maturation and enable investigation of inter-regional connectivity. The integration of computational frameworks with functional measurements also enables extraction of quantitative features such as excitability, synchrony and network topology, linking molecular programs to emergent circuit behaviour. Furthermore, emerging studies demonstrate that neural organoids can exhibit synaptic plasticity, adaptive computation and goal-directed learning in closed-loop paradigms, opening research directions beyond spontaneous activity characterization. Functional organoids can also expand disease modelling by revealing mechanisms of network dysfunction across neurodevelopmental, neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders. Nevertheless, the absence of standardized benchmarks, reference datasets and reproducible analysis pipelines continues to limit comparability across studies. This Review synthesizes current technologies and analytical strategies for probing activity in neural organoids; evaluates their translational relevance and limitations; and discusses how interdisciplinary integration of stem cell biology, bioengineering, systems neuroscience and computational modelling could establish robust frameworks for mechanistic and ethically grounded exploration of human brain function. Neural organoids can be used to characterize functional phenotypes across cellular and network scales, extending their applicability beyond studies of development and molecular identity. This Review examines optical and electrophysiological approaches for measuring neural organoid activity; presents a multiscale framework for evaluating network function; and discusses practical considerations for experimental design, data analysis and interpretation.

papers.title: Cortex-wide neuronal dynamics underpin quasi-periodic patterns in resting-state fMRI
papers.abstract: We use simultaneous wide-field Ca 2+ imaging and fMRI to uncover the neural origins of quasi-periodic patterns (QPPs) in fMRI. Cortex-wide Ca 2+ activity closely tracks and predicts fMRI-QPPs, revealing a direct link between neuronal dynamics and fMRI.

papers.title: Epigenetic regulation of cancer drivers and EMT revealed by genome-wide methylome profiling in NSCLC
papers.abstract: Carcinogenesis is driven by dynamic and heterogeneous epigenomic alterations promoting tumour evolution and affecting therapeutic resistance. We performed genome-wide DNA methylation sequencing (RRBS) on 260 lung methylomes from 130 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients. Here we show that gene-body hypomethylation involved lung cancer drivers, while promoter hypomethylation targeted miRNA genes linked to EGFR signalling, EMT, and PD-L1 regulation. Upstream transcription factor analysis also implicated epigenetic control of EMT, EGFR and immune pathways, through SNAIL, SLUG, SMAD3 and BRD4. Promoter hypermethylation represented multi-gene epi-oncodriver mechanism associated with GPCRs. Subtype-specific patterns were additionally observed: adenocarcinoma showed alterations in neurotransmitter signalling, whereas squamous cell carcinoma embraced canonical oncogenic pathways. We provide a genome-wide methylome analysis in NSCLC, revealing epigenetic alterations that may contribute to tumour progression and therapeutic resistance linked to EGFR, EMT and immunological responses. These findings highlight the translational potential of epigenetic profiling to inform clinical strategies in NSCLC.

papers.title: On-demand instantaneous bandwidth microwave receiver via scalable Rydberg Vapor cell array with Stark comb
papers.abstract: Rydberg-atom-based microwave (MW) sensors offer high sensitivity and intrinsic traceability, but their instantaneous bandwidth is fundamentally limited by atomic coherence time. Here, we introduce a scalable sensing architecture that overcomes this limitation by spatially multiplexing atomic detection channels with a Stark comb, in which an MW frequency comb (MFC) and a position-dependent Stark field enable each Rydberg vapor cell to function as an independent frequency-selective heterodyne receiver. We experimentally validate the 210 MHz instantaneous-bandwidth channelized receiver architecture through sequential characterization of individual Stark-shifted channels using a 21-line MFC, while maintaining an overall sensitivity of 326.6 nVcm−1Hz−1/2 despite a 160 MHz tuning of the carrier resonance frequency. Full simultaneous operation across the 210 MHz bandwidth requires parallel implementation and readout of all channels. This scalable architecture enables on-demand instantaneous bandwidth while preserving sensitivity, providing a pathway toward real-time broadband MW detection for radar, communications, and spectrum monitoring.

papers.title: Xenogeneic acellular nerve grafts laden with Schwann cell-like cells repair monkey long-gap facial nerve defects
papers.abstract: This study evaluated whether hair follicle epidermal neural crest stem cell-derived Schwann cell-like cells (HF-EPI-NCSC-SCLCs) could enhance the performance of cable-type porcine acellular nerve grafts (ANGs) in repairing long-gap whole facial nerve defects (WFNDs) in rhesus monkeys. Following chemical decellularization, porcine ANGs lacked S100B, α-Gal and swine leukocyte antigen expression, while laminin was well preserved. Cultured monkey HF-EPI-NCSC-SCLCs expressed Schwann cell markers (GFAP + /S100B +), exhibited low immunogenicity, and demonstrated vigorous growth in porcine ANGs in vitro. Twelve monkeys were randomly assigned to three equal groups: autologous sural nerve graft, ANG alone, and ANG + HF-EPI-NCSC-SCLCs. Each group received a graft to bridge a 35-mm-long WFND. At 8 months postoperatively, the ANG + HF-EPI-NCSC-SCLCs group showed significantly better facial symmetry, mimetic recovery, and recovery ratios of onset latency and amplitude than the ANG group. Severe synkinesis was frequent in the ANG group but only occasional in the other two groups. Nerve regeneration indices were also significantly improved with cell supplementation. No notable systemic or local immune responses differed among the three groups. These findings demonstrate that HF-EPI-NCSC-SCLCs effectively boost the regenerative capacity of cable-type xenogeneic ANGs for repairing long-gap WFNDs in non-human primates, supporting their translational potential for facial nerve reconstruction.

papers.title: Inductive heating for photovoltaic module recycling and near-complete component recovery
papers.abstract: The growing number of end-of-life photovoltaic modules poses a major recycling challenge, particularly the removal of encapsulants without damaging silicon solar cells. Here, the authors develop an inductive heating approach that rapidly enables residue-free separation of encapsulants from silicon solar cells and achieves over 99.8% recovery of photovoltaic module components.

papers.title: Stabilizing silicon-sulfur cells via binder-free xerogel-silicon anode and interfacial network engineering
papers.abstract: Silicon offers high theoretical capacity for next-generation battery anodes, but volume expansion and interfacial instability hinder practical application. Here, the authors report a conductive poly(N-phenylglycine) xerogel-based silicon anode that enables stable, high-energy-density silicon-sulfur batteries.

papers.title: Machine-knitted magnetoactive textiles for wireless charging, biomechanical sensing, and haptic feedback
papers.abstract: A central goal of wearable computing is to understand and augment human physical interactions. This requires equipping wearable devices with functionalities such as wireless charging, biomechanical sensing, and haptic feedback. Most wearable devices integrate each of these functions separately with specialized components, which limits the device’s overall flexibility, comfort, and scalability. Here we present machine-knitted magnetoactive textiles that unify the physical mechanisms of wireless power transfer, biomechanical sensing, and haptic feedback in a single soft architecture. By coupling extruded magnetic fibers with digitally machine-knitted electromagnets, we enable functional textile transducers that can stably charge a 7.4 V battery, sense body movements up to 3000 Hz, and provide perceivable haptic forces up to 4.2 mN. We demonstrate how these transducers can seamlessly integrate into garments for applications like smart home control, motor rehabilitation, and skill acquisition, establishing a foundation for multifunctional wearable interfaces that are intrinsically compatible with everyday clothing.

papers.title: Bayesian optimization-guided closed-loop morphology optimization of block copolymer blends via synchrotron X-ray scattering
papers.abstract: The utility of block copolymers (BCPs) in next-generation nanofabrication and optoelectronics is strictly governed by the long-range ordering and precise periodicity of their microphase-separated domains. However, navigating their multi-dimensional processing space to maximize this structural fidelity can be difficult. Conventional optimization relies on Edisonian trial-and-error, which is resource-intensive, slow, and often fails to identify the global optimum. Here, we address this challenge using a closed-loop morphology-optimization workflow that integrates synchrotron grazing-incidence small-angle X-ray scattering (GISAXS), automated scattering data analysis, and Gaussian process-driven Bayesian optimization (GP-BO). Applied to the swelling-induced assembly of poly(styrene-b-2-vinylpyridine) (S2VP) blends, the BO-guided closed-loop workflow explores the two-dimensional processing space defined by polymer blending ratio and solvent uptake. By jointly optimizing domain spacing and peak sharpness as a measure of structural ordering, the workflow identified target-satisfying conditions using approximately 30 experiments, more than two orders of magnitude fewer than required for uniform coverage at the stated resolution. Overall, we developed a constraint-aware acquisition strategy tailored to morphology optimization, in which domain spacing is treated as a feasibility constraint while structural ordering is optimized within the feasible region. This task-specific formulation differs from applying a standard GP-BO workflow and enables efficient navigation of a coupled landscape containing both monotonic and highly nonlinear responses.

papers.title: Wireless monolithic flexible zinc-ion battery–pressure sensor enabled by a tough anti-freezing hydrogel electrolyte
papers.abstract: Developing wearable sensors that integrate self-powering capability, reliable static and dynamic pressure detection, and miniaturized wireless signal processing remains a formidable challenge. Here, we propose a material–device–system co-design strategy to construct an untethered, all-weather, monolithic flexible zinc-ion battery–pressure sensor enabled by a tough anti-freezing hydrogel, a co-anode architecture, and a miniaturized wireless module. At the material level, a tough, anti-freezing PAM/CMCS-DMSO-Zn hydrogel serves as the core. It combines a low freezing point, superior toughness, fatigue resistance, and high ionic conductivity, enabling a dual role as an active pressure-sensing layer and a stable battery electrolyte. At the device level, a nylon-mesh-spaced co-anode architecture isolates the hydrogel from the Zn anode at rest, establishing a zero-output state that eliminates standby power. Upon loading, interfacial impedance modulation ensures static and dynamic pressure detection with rapid response and recovery times of 20 and 30 ms, respectively. At the system level, integrating the device with a custom printed circuit board creates an end-to-end microsystem for signal acquisition, processing, and wireless transmission, which we successfully validated across diverse harsh conditions. Ultimately, this co-design bridges hydrogel chemistry under extreme conditions with self-powered wearable electronics, providing a versatile paradigm for all-weather, wireless IoT sensing nodes.

papers.title: Skin-mimetic adaptive gradient electrode for ambulatory noninvasive brain-computer interfaces
papers.abstract: Noninvasive brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) need stable, comfortable electrodes for long-term wear. Current rigid or uniformly soft electrodes suffer from scalp mismatch, causing motion artifacts and short operation times. Inspired by human skin’s gradient structure, we created a skin-mimetic adaptive gradient electrode (AGE). Based on the Marangoni effect, we induced heterogeneous crosslinking in the hydrogel within a gradient temperature field. This yields an electrode with a gradual stiffness change—soft at the scalp interface and firm at the circuit connection—along with a gradient pore structure for sustained electrolyte release. This design enabled stable, high-quality EEG recording for over 8 h during free movement and over 14 h at rest, maintaining >94% typing accuracy. This work demonstrated the potential of gradient-designed hydrogels toward noninvasive BCIs in freely moving practicality.

papers.title: Chronic exercise induces a pathway-dependent electrophysiological signature in the mouse hippocampus
papers.abstract: Chronic physical exercise enhances hippocampal function, yet its impact on network activity remains poorly defined. We explored whether treadmill running leaves durable imprints detectable through electrophysiological techniques and spatial transcriptomics. Field potentials (FPs) were recorded in anesthetized male C57BL/6 J mice after a chronic exercise protocol. Using machine learning to analyze FP generators, we were able to reliably classify animals into their correct group by Lateral Perforant Path (LPP) activity alone. Classification rested on a multifeatured signature rather than any single feature. Schaffer Collateral and Lacunosum-Moleculare generators showed changes that did not achieve statistical significance. Exploratory spatial transcriptomics identified a coordinated enrichment of calcium signaling and long-term potentiation programs in the dentate gyrus. These findings demonstrate that exercise-induced plasticity is not a global shift but a localized remodeling of specific synaptic inputs, with changes detectable at both circuit and molecular levels. These durable, pathway-specific imprints persist in the absence of active task engagement, suggesting a reorganization of the brain’s memory circuitry.

papers.title: Specification of bone marrow sinusoids requires TIE2-mediated positive feedback involving COUP-TFII and VEGFR3
papers.abstract: The bone marrow (BM) vascular network drives bone development and hematopoiesis, but the mechanisms governing its specialized sinusoidal architecture remain poorly characterized. Here, we show that the angiopoietin receptor TIE2 is highly expressed by BM sinusoidal endothelial cells (BM-SECs). Its endothelial deletion triggers sinusoidal capillarization, characterized by reduced vessel diameter and aberrant mural cell coverage. Mechanistically, TIE2 insufficiency downregulates VEGFR3 in BM-SECs within 48 h of induced endothelial Tek deletion, while leaving hepatic sinusoidal VEGFR3 unaffected. RNA-sequencing reveals that TIE2 insufficiency suppresses sinusoidal development pathways while upregulating arterial and angiogenic genes. We validate this phenotype using inducible Tek deletion mainly in VEGFR3+ SECs and in Angpt1-insufficient mice. Furthermore, endothelial deletion of the transcription factor COUP-TFII (Nr2f2) recapitulates these defects, reducing both BM sinusoidal TIE2 and VEGFR3 expression. Finally, induced endothelial deletion of Flt4 produces a similar phenotype. Together, our findings imply that ANGPT1/TIE2 and COUP-TFII form a reciprocal regulatory loop essential for BM sinusoidal specification by sustaining VEGFR3 expression.

papers.title: A mMono-Bac1.0 system for recombinant adeno-associated virus vectors with higher flexibility, throughput and yield
papers.abstract: Recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) holds immense promise for therapeutic applications, but high production costs limit its widespread clinical use, underscoring the urgent need for manufacturing breakthroughs. Here, we establish a modular Mono-Bac system with the p24-NanoLuciferase (Nluc) reporter Bacmid for rAAV production, named mMono-Bac1.0, enhancing manufacturing flexibility, throughput and yield simultaneously. The system introduces two key technology to the pFD/Cap-(ITR-GOI)-Rep transfer vector-based Mono-Bac framework. First, a modular pGB-AAV Donor construction strategy enables one-step all-in-one AAV transfer vector assembly and effortless switching of capsids or GOIs, thus facilitating high-throughput combinatorial production. Second, an engineered p24-Nluc Bacmid enables rapid (<5 min) quantification of infectious recombinant baculovirus (rBV) titers and real-time monitoring of Nluc activity in culture supernatants to determine the optimal harvest point (log RLU ~ 6.5), thereby maximizing rAAV yield. This system has the potential to advance baculovirus expression vector (BEV)-based rAAV manufacturing into a data-driven era, supporting efficient industrial-scale production.

papers.title: Pole-to-pole LOV-domain receptor diversity points to an early stramenopile origin and global dominance of aureochromes
papers.abstract: Light regimes are a fundamental environmental cue for marine organisms. Yet molecular adaptations of photoreceptors to the extreme seasonality of polar regions remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that the diversity of candidate blue-light-sensing LOV-domain proteins increases at higher latitudes. We identify aureochromes, blue-light-sensitive transcription factors unique to stramenopiles, as the most frequent LOV-domain receptors across ocean latitudes. Phylogenetic reconstructions reveal early aureochrome diversification in the stramenopile lineage, originating in a heterotrophic ancestor before photosynthesis was acquired. This challenges the assumption that aureochromes are restricted to phototrophs, suggesting an ancestral role in spectral light signaling. We find that, despite changes in light quality and photoperiod by latitude, diatom aureochrome domain architecture remains conserved. This implies adaptation through regulatory tuning, such as altered expression dynamics or post-translational control. Our results emphasise the importance of spectral-light sensing in polar oceans and link the widespread dominance of aureochromes to their ancient origin and conservation.

papers.title: Laser-electrochemical fabrication of nanoporous high-entropy metallic glass films for efficient pH-universal hydrogen evolution
papers.abstract: Efficient hydrogen evolution catalysts that can operate across the entire pH range with a low loading of noble metals are important for scalable water electrolysis, but existing crystalline and amorphous materials seldom integrate activity, durability, and pH universality. Here, the authors report a laser-electrochemical approach to fabricate nanoporous PdPtCuNiP high-entropy metallic glass films on carbon fibers that exhibit low overpotentials in acidic, alkaline, and neutral electrolytes, operating stably for over 200 hours and achieving a 1.8 times higher mass activity compared to commercial Pt/C in acid.

papers.title: PLK4 inhibition-mediated centrosome amplification drives anti-tumor activity across euploid solid tumors
papers.abstract: Muñoz et al. present in vitro and in vivo characterization of PLK4 inhibitors EXEL-0667 and EXEL-1855 to explore dose-dependent effects on the centrosome. They find that TP53-wild-type, near-euploid tumors show the highest sensitivity even at doses causing centrosome amplification, supporting the use of PLK4-targeting agents.

papers.title: Generation of synthetic clinical text: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Generating medical synthetic text represents an effective solution for clinical NLP issues like sparsity and privacy. This paper conducts a systematic review on synthetic clinical text generation by formulating quantitative analysis to three research questions concerning the generation’s purpose, generation techniques, and the evaluation methods. We searched four databases including PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect and Web of Science for publications associated with the topic and identified 87 relevant articles out of 1148. Results showed that the generation purposes were dedicated to Trustworthy, Medical Assistance, and Language Resource themes. Prompting LLMs was the main source of synthetic text (40 articles). GPTs were the main predominant technique used to generate the text (63 articles), especially ChatGPT (47 articles). Additionally, there were four main aspects of evaluation, including similarity, privacy, structure, and utility, where utility was the prevailing method for assessment (52 articles). The synthetic medical text empowered data augmentation and clinical documentation. Using text alteration, controlling real text portions, and federated learning, generative models can produce privacy-preserving medical text. This accelerates the development of new digital health applications.

papers.title: Understanding clinical reasoning variability in medical large language models: a mechanistic interpretability study
papers.abstract: Medical large language models achieving high benchmark accuracy exhibit unexplained variability in clinical tasks, producing errors that clinicians cannot safeguard against. We evaluated clinical reasoning stability in GPT-5, MedGemma-27B-Text-IT, and OpenBioLLM-Llama3-70B using 3035 systematic perturbations from physician-validated oncology SOAP, brief vignette, and MIMIC cases. We trained sparse autoencoders on 1 billion tokens from 50,000 MIMIC-IV clinical notes to decompose their internal representation. We find models exhibit dramatic reasoning instability, shifting staging accuracy by over 50% based solely on prompt format, or generating definitive staging in clinically insufficient scenarios. Sparse autoencoder analysis revealed hierarchical encoding in MedGemma, where high-magnitude features encode lexical identity and low-magnitude features encode contextual meaning. OpenBioLLM distributes information uniformly. We demonstrate that these internal encoding structures differentially affect retrieval and reasoning interventions, suggesting interventions effective for one architecture may harm another. These results motivate architecture-specific safety validation as a component of pre-deployment evaluation for medical LLMs.

papers.title: Interpretability-driven feature engineering enables compact and accurate multi-outcome risk stratification at hospitalization for chronic hepatitis B
papers.abstract: Clinical artificial intelligence (AI) often trades predictive performance against interpretability. This study develops an interpretability-driven feature engineering framework for multi-outcome risk stratification at hospitalization for chronic hepatitis B. A total of 36,024 hospitalization records from 22,001 patients were included. The framework integrating SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based main and interaction effects was used to construct compact machine learning models for classifying disease non-progression, liver cirrhosis (LC), and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). SHAP main effects selected the top 15 features per outcome; TreeSHAP interactions selected four pairwise terms. Performance was evaluated using patient-level data splitting, temporal validation, and independent external validation, with calibration and decision-curve analyses. The full-feature models achieved superior discrimination (AUCs: 0.927, 0.897, and 0.899) for classifying hospitalization-recorded disease non-progression, LC, and HCC, respectively. The corresponding compact models maintained strong discrimination (AUCs: 0.911, 0.882, and 0.890) with 80.8% fewer features. Interaction models yielded subtle AUC shifts (AUCs: 0.912, 0.881, and 0.891) while characterizing potential clinical joint-effect patterns. Temporal validation yielded AUCs of 0.863, 0.827, and 0.847, while external validation yielded AUCs of 0.829, 0.865, and 0.827, respectively. The framework produced compact and transparent models for contemporaneous risk stratification in clinical practice, seamlessly uniting predictive accuracy with multi-level interpretability.

papers.title: Predicting persistent fever in patients with cancer receiving antibiotics: a machine learning approach
papers.abstract: Persistent fever after initiating intravenous antibiotics is common in hospitalized patients with cancer and often leads to additional imaging and antimicrobial escalation. Early identification of patients unlikely to remain febrile could provide additional information during clinical reassessment. We developed and externally validated machine learning models to predict persistent fever 48–72 h after antibiotic initiation using electronic health records from two academic hospitals. Adult cancer patients with fever within 24–48 h of treatment were included. Models incorporated demographics, comorbidities, laboratory results, vital signs, and temperature patterns. The best-performing model achieved an AUROC of 0.82 (95% CI 0.79–0.84) internally and 0.78 (95% CI 0.77–0.79) externally. Temperature-related variables were the dominant predictors. Decision curve analysis demonstrated positive net benefit across much of the evaluated threshold range. Retrospective assessment suggested that approximately one quarter of antibiotic escalations and chest CT scans occurred in patients correctly predicted not to remain febrile, highlighting the potential contextual value of fever predictions. These findings indicate that short-term fever persistence can be predicted with clinically meaningful accuracy using routine data. However, clinical use should be limited to an adjunctive role rather than standalone rule-out decision-making, and prospective studies are required to evaluate safety, clinician uptake, and real-world impact.
