Here, using quantitative proteomics of the left and right visual cortices from monocularly deprived (MD) juvenile mice, we identify phosphodiesterase 10 A (PDE10A) and the cAMP signaling pathway as molecular signatures of juvenile ODP. Juvenile MD is associated with reduced PDE10A and increased phosphorylated CREB (pCREB) in the visual cortex contralateral to the deprived eye, whereas adult mice show no comparable response. In adult mice, systemic administration of the selective PDE10A inhibitor TAK-063 during MD reinstates an experience-dependent ocular dominance shift and reduces visual acuity in the deprived eye. This is accompanied by increased cortical cAMP and pPKA, an inverted-U pCREB response peaking at 0.3 mg/kg, and upregulation of plasticity-related synaptic proteins. TAK-063 does not alter basal visual function, retinal electrophysiology, or locomotor behavior in non-deprived adults, excluding nonspecific sensory/motor confounds. These findings identify PDE10A as a candidate molecular regulator of visual cortical plasticity and support its pharmacological inhibition as a strategy to facilitate experience-dependent plasticity in the adult visual cortex.

papers.title: Mercury contamination impairs the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis of a neotropical caiman
papers.abstract: Reduced physiological stress response is associated with elevated mercury from environmental contamination in wild caimans, supporting a conserved mechanism of endocrine disruption with implications for wildlife resilience.

papers.title: Nucleophilic defluorination of PFAS under mild conditions
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are globally significant water contaminants because of their persistence and associated environmental and health risks. Because PFAS stability and toxicity are closely linked to their fluorinated structures, complete defluorination represents a critical strategy for detoxification. Yet near-complete defluorination of structurally diverse PFAS, particularly short-chain compounds, under mild conditions remains challenging. Here, we report a nucleophile-driven approach for effective PFAS defluorination in DMSO at relatively mild temperatures around 100 °C, yielding free fluoride ions. Five nucleophiles, methanethiolate, ethanethiolate, methoxide, ethoxide, and amide, were evaluated. Under optimized conditions, complete defluorination, as verified by nearly quantitative fluoride recovery, was achieved for a broad range of perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids and fluoropolymers, including short- and ultrashort-chain compounds such as PFPrA and TFA, which are typically resistant to other defluorination methods. Partial degradation of PFOS was also achieved under the same conditions. This approach provides an effective route to PFAS defluorination under comparatively mild reaction conditions.

papers.title: Hierarchical structure of primary and hybridization-induced superconducting correlations in bilayer nickelates
papers.abstract: The discovery of high-pressure superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate La3Ni2O7, with a transition temperature approaching 80 K, has stimulated intense debate regarding its microscopic origin. Although an s± gap symmetry has been widely proposed, the electronic degrees of freedom responsible for pairing remain unsettled. Here we investigate a bilayer two-orbital Hubbard model using the variational Monte Carlo method and reveal a hierarchical pairing structure in bilayer nickelates. The primary pairing tendency originates from the bonding–antibonding splitting of the Ni $$3{d}_{{z}^{2}}$$ orbitals, while orbital hybridization redistributes superconducting correlations to the $${d}_{{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}$$ channel despite its weak intrinsic pairing tendency. This distinction between the origin of pairing and the resulting superconducting correlations explains why the two orbital channels exhibit comparable long-range correlations. The resulting s± state is robust against changes in Fermi-surface topology. These results reconcile apparently competing theoretical scenarios and provide a comprehensive understanding, highlighting the distinctive role of orbital hybridization in multilayer correlated superconductors.

papers.title: Digital home-based monitoring for patients with hypertension and type 2 diabetes in Ghana
papers.abstract: van Andel, Aovare et al. test a smartphone-based home monitoring system for adults with hypertension and type 2 diabetes in Accra, Ghana. The system is feasible and improves long-term blood pressure control, while modestly reducing blood glucose in those with high baseline levels.

papers.title: AI-guided discovery of self-assembled monolayers combining synthetic accessibility and interfacial stability for perovskite solar cells
papers.abstract: Using an artificial intelligence-guided framework combining retrosynthetic prediction, high-throughput DFT screening and chemical expertise, a readily synthesizable self-assembled monolayer for perovskite photovoltaics is identified. The top candidate delivers 27.2% efficiency and retains >95% of its initial efficiency after 2,000 h at 65 °C under maximum-power-point tracking.

papers.title: Carbonation of silicate minerals contributes to atmospheric CO 2 drawdown in glacier-fed streams
papers.abstract: Geochemical analyses of 170 glacier-fed streams reveal widespread CO 2 undersaturation, with 69% of sites below atmospheric equilibrium. Combined streamwater and sediment analyses identify silicate carbonation and secondary Mg-rich carbonate formation as a pathway that can contribute to atmospheric CO 2 uptake and transient inorganic carbon storage under favourable geochemical conditions.

papers.title: Solar-operated interlayer electrothermal evaporator enabling instant high-flux freshwater production across multiple scenarios
papers.abstract: An interlayer evaporator integrating electrothermal and photothermal effects achieves efficient freshwater production from diverse water sources, enabled by reduced heat loss and improved heat utilization.

papers.title: A decade of machine learning for materials development
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, machine learning for materials has expanded from property prediction to generative design and experimental discovery. The next challenge is to understand how materials evolve and function across scales under real operating conditions, and to translate that understanding into reliable materials development.

papers.title: Mitochondrial-targeted strategies for advancing ovarian cryopreservation: enhancing follicular survival and reproductive health
papers.abstract: Global fertility rates are in decline, underscoring the importance of effective fertility preservation strategies. Ovarian tissue cryopreservation and transplantation (OTCT) shows great promise but faces challenges like oxidative stress, ischemia-reperfusion injury, and poor follicle survival due to burn out. Protecting and preserving a greater number of primordial follicles remains pivotal to the success of this technology. While current strategies predominantly rely on antioxidants, their efficacy is constrained by non-specificity and the inability to achieve sustained release at the transplantation site. In this study, we explored the potential of elamipretide (SS31), a novel mitochondrial-targeted antioxidant peptide, to address these limitations. By combining SS31 with a recombinant human granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (rhGM-CSF) gel, we achieved localized and sustained release of SS31 at the transplantation site in rabbits. This combination demonstrated synergistic effects by reducing oxidative stress, improving mitochondrial function, and enhancing follicular survival. Notably, reproductive endocrine function was restored 8 weeks post-transplantation. Proteomics and metabolomics analyses revealed that these improvements were primarily attributed to the activation of energy metabolism pathway. Our findings suggest improved transplantation outcomes in preclinical settings, highlighting the potential of this strategy to serve as an efficient and precise approach for women requiring urgent fertility preservation in the future.

papers.title: A physics-informed peripheral hemodynamic digital twin for personalized estimation of arterial stiffness
papers.abstract: Arterial stiffness, commonly assessed by pulse wave velocity (PWV), is an important biomarker of cardiovascular risk, yet conventional PWV measurements require dual-site recordings that limit scalability in clinical settings. Here we introduce a physics-informed peripheral hemodynamic digital twin framework for estimating central-brachial arterial stiffness from a single brachial pressure waveform. Using our laboratory-developed cuff device, high-resolution brachial pulse waveforms were collected in a cohort of 118 subjects. The digital twin then personalizes a reduced-order wave propagation model through PDE-constrained optimization, generating a compact parameter space that encodes ventricular–vascular characteristics relevant to stiffness. Incorporating digital-twin-derived parameters improved PWV estimation on a blind test cohort (r = 0.67, RMSE = 1.12 m/s) compared with a baseline model using only age and blood pressure (r = 0.22, RMSE = 1.90 m/s). These results indicate that physics-informed digital twins can enable scalable, noninvasive assessment of vascular aging from accessible peripheral waveforms.

papers.title: Enzymatically Active Liposomal Nanobots for the Penetration of Intercellular and Intracellular Barriers
papers.abstract: Small Methods, EarlyView.

papers.title: Cartilage-binding coacervate with therapeutic payload delivery and biomimetic lubrication alleviates osteoarthritis by reducing joint friction and inflammation
papers.abstract: Polyzwitterionic coacervates with therapeutic payload delivery, mimicking physiological lubrication and cartilage-binding functionalities, reduce joint friction and inflammation in rat and mini-pig osteoarthritis models.

papers.title: Direct imaging elucidates ionic memory in two-dimensional nanochannels
papers.abstract: The microscopic origin of ionic memory in two-dimensional (2D) nanofluidic memristors remains debated. Voltage-induced blistering of the confining walls of 2D nanofluidic channels is identified to trigger memristive hysteresis leading to nonlinear ion transport in the channels.

papers.title: III-nitride-based in-sensor computing enabled by interfacial polarization effects
papers.abstract: Intrinsic electric polarization in III-nitride semiconductors is an advantage for large-scale optoelectronic devices but remains largely unexplored in sensory-memristive devices. Polarization-induced spatial separation of photogenerated carriers at the interfaces of III-nitride heterostructures enables efficient and scalable in-sensor computing at room temperature.

papers.title: An open dataset of gas adsorption in deformable metal–organic frameworks for direct air capture
papers.abstract: Engineering economical and scalable processes for direct air capture (DAC) from humid air relies on atomistic modeling to search and identify promising sorbent materials from a vast chemical space. Machine learning has emerged as a powerful tool for predicting material properties in an efficient yet accurate manner, but these models require large sets of carefully curated training data. Here we present the Open DAC 2025 (ODAC25) dataset comprising nearly 60 million DFT single-point calculations for CO2, H2O, N2 and O2 adsorption in ~15,000 metal–organic frameworks (MOFs). ODAC25 introduces functionalized MOFs, high-energy adsorbate placements and synthetically generated frameworks to maximize the versatility of models trained on the dataset. ODAC25 improves upon the accuracy of DFT calculations in previous works and applies engineering intuition from recent work regarding the treatment of adsorbate-induced MOF flexibility. We release state-of-the-art machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on ODAC25 and demonstrate their utility via Henry’s coefficient predictions. ODAC25 enables MOF screening for DAC at a resolution previously unattainable. Direct air capture needs better sorbents, but screening the vast space of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) demands accurate, scalable models. The Open DAC 2025 dataset provides nearly 60 million DFT calculations of CO2, H2O, N2 and O2 adsorption across approximately 15,000 MOFs, with machine-learned potentials enabling high-resolution MOF screening.

papers.title: From footsteps to wireless events: infrastructure-native battery-free interfaces for human–environment interactions
papers.abstract: Future intelligent environments require infrastructure-native interfaces that can sense human activities and directly generate wireless communication events using standard protocols. Achieving this remains challenging because human footsteps are transient, irregular, and often low-force, whereas standard wireless protocols such as Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) require substantial energy consumption. In this work, we present a self-powered floor interface that addresses this challenge through coordinated material, structural, and circuit design. The system integrates a high-performance PMN–PZT ceramic with a piezoelectric charge constant of d33 = 962 pC/N for efficient energy transduction, a carefully engineered metallic substrate for enhanced stress transfer and recoverability, a threshold-regulated energy management circuit that regulates transient outputs into a usable burst-power window, and an ultra-low-power BLE interface for protocol-compatible transmission. With a 4.7 μF storage capacitor, the circuit provides 22.84 μJ of releasable energy, exceeding the approximately 17 μJ required for BLE cold start. Despite a footprint of only 30 mm, sub-millimeter thickness, and a prototype-level unit cost below $5, the system enables direct wireless triggering from a light actuation of approximately 12 N. Across 100 footstep trials involving 10 participants, the system achieved an average of 2.39 BLE packets per actuation, with up to 4 packets generated per event, and successfully delivered at least one wireless transmission in 97% of the trials. The proposed system directly translates irregular footsteps into reliable protocol-compatible wireless events and enables infrastructure-integrated human-environment interactions, including smart-home control, indoor localization, digital-twin interaction, and transportation-safety alerting. These results establish a practical route toward compact infrastructure-native battery-free interaction systems for future intelligent environments.

papers.title: SQSTM1/p62-LC3A–mediated autophagic clearance of stress granules prevents apoptosis under hyperosmotic stress
papers.abstract: Stress granules (SGs) are transient, membraneless assemblies that form in response to cellular stress and typically disassemble when stress resolves. Their persistence has been linked to neurodegenerative disease. Here we show that LC3A has a selective role in the autophagic clearance of SGs formed during hyperosmotic stress. LC3A, but not LC3B or LC3C, associates with SGs, and depletion of LC3A impairs their removal. LC3A also promotes clearance of pathogenic inclusions containing TDP-43 or poly(GR) dipeptides from C9orf72 expansions. Proteomic analysis reveals enrichment of the autophagy receptor SQSTM1/p62 in SGs, supporting its role in SG degradation. SGs are also enriched in mitochondrial and apoptosis-related proteins, consistent with an anti-apoptotic function potentially linked to mitochondrial proximity. However, prolonged stress activates CASP3 and promotes apoptosis, which is exacerbated by defective SG clearance. These findings highlight the critical role of the SQSTM1–LC3A axis in SG turnover and cell survival under chronic stress.

papers.title: Exceptional preservation in cherts reveals complex cuticular architecture in one of the earliest Cambrian ecdysozoans
papers.abstract: Ecdysozoans, animals characterized by a periodically moulted cuticle, became major components of Cambrian marine ecosystems, yet the structural organization of their earliest non-mineralized cuticles remains poorly documented. Here we report Spinosoma reticulatus gen. et sp. nov., a millimeter-scale ecdysozoan from Fortunian cherts on two paleogeographic blocks: the Liuchapo Formation, South China, and the Yurtus Formation, Tarim Block, dating to ca. 538 Ma. This occurrence represents one of the earliest Cambrian ecdysozoan body-fossil records and may predate the classic Kuanchuanpu scalidophoran assemblages. The material preserves a terminal mouth with large circumoral spines and abundant cuticular fragments. Its cuticle comprises a fibrous mesh, short upright plate-like structures, and hollow ridged spines. Morphological and Raman data support an ecdysozoan affinity, whereas scalidophoran placement remains tentative. Spinosoma reveals a previously undocumented cuticular architecture, suggesting that early ecdysozoan ecological breadth and integument diversity are underestimated in the earliest phase of the Cambrian Explosion.

papers.title: Genetic interaction between Adgrg6 and Sox9 reveals a feedforward mechanism for postnatal spinal stability
papers.abstract: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is the most common pediatric spinal disorder and is best understood as a complex polygenic condition. Genome-wide association studies have identified AIS risk loci, including regions near ADGRG6 and SOX9, yet the mechanisms underlying its heritability remain poorly defined. Here we use spatial transcriptomics to characterize gene expression in the spine of a conditional Adgrg6 mutant mouse model, revealing reduced expression of Sox9 and several extracellular matrix genes in the intervertebral disc. We demonstrate a strong genetic interaction between conditional loss of Adgrg6 and a hypomorphic Sox9 allele that increases the penetrance and severity of scoliosis. We further show that SOX9 occupies open chromatin within the Adgrg6 locus in SOX9+ cells isolated from the mouse disc tissue, consistent with direct transcriptional regulation, and provide evidence for SOX9-dependent and SOX9-independent regulation across a variety of spinal tissues. Together, these findings support a self-reinforcing feedforward circuit in which Adgrg6 and Sox9 are co-regulated to maintain extracellular matrix gene expression in the annulus fibrosus and paraspinal tissues. These results provide mechanistic insight into genes implicated by AIS-associated loci and establish combined Adgrg6–Sox9 insufficiency in mice as a tractable model of polygenic scoliosis susceptibility.

papers.title: AI-assisted image-based screening identifies TFEB agonists that restore adipose angiogenesis and reduce adipose fibrosis
papers.abstract: Adipose tissue expansion in obesity frequently outpaces vascularization, triggering hypoxia, fibrosis, and metabolic dysfunction. The molecular mechanisms coordinating adaptive angiogenesis during this expansion remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that myeloid deletion of Transcription Factor EB (Tfeb) in high-fat diet-fed mice exacerbates epididymal white adipose tissue (eWAT) dysfunction, manifesting as profound hypoxia, fibrosis, and systemic insulin resistance. Mechanistically, single-cell RNA sequencing and chromatin immunoprecipitation assays reveal a novel TFEB-VEGFA axis: TFEB directly activates Vegfa transcription in macrophages, and its absence impairs angiogenic compensation under hypoxic stress. To translate these findings, we established an AI-driven, high-content screening platform to quantify TFEB nuclear translocation. We identified and validated Tetrandrine and Pacritinib as potent TFEB agonists. Notably, Tetrandrine acts via an mTOR-independent mechanism. Pharmacological activation of TFEB with these compounds restored adipose angiogenesis, resolved fibrosis, and improved insulin sensitivity in obese mice. These findings establish macrophage TFEB as a critical regulator of healthy adipose remodeling and validate the TFEB-VEGFA axis as a therapeutic target for metabolic diseases.

papers.title: Lactate drives the emergence of tumor cells with centrosome amplification through CP110 lactylation
papers.abstract: Centrosome ampllification is a frequent feature of cancer cells, whose origin is still under investigation. The present study shows that high lactate levels present in cancer cells can induce centrosome amplification via the the lactylation of the centrosomal protein CP110

papers.title: Automated and noninvasive in vivo mapping of brain functions in the human cortex
papers.abstract: Mapping forms the basis for understanding the functional organization of the brain and for developing targeted interventions in neurological and psychiatric disorders. Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is a non-invasive tool that allows causal mapping of cortical functions involved in motor control, speech, and connectivity. Since manual mapping procedures limit standardization, we present an automated cortical mapping method that integrates electronically controlled multi-locus TMS with a Bayesian optimization algorithm for identifying stimulation targets efficiently and objectively through a closed-loop framework. We localized individual motor representation area peaks with high accuracy (average 2.4 mm and 5° deviation from the optimum) in only approximately 4 minutes. This represents a substantial advancement over current mapping approaches, providing the means to greatly accelerate and standardize both research and clinical protocols while maintaining high reliability. We anticipate that our approach can further extend to map other cortical functions that cannot be easily analyzed online by a human operator.

papers.title: Crocin alleviates renal fibrosis through inhibiting mitochondrial dysfunction via regulating HOXD8/PGC‑1α pathways
papers.abstract: Crocin, a key bioactive compound derived from saffron (Crocus sativus L.), a traditional Chinese medicinal and edible herb, exhibits renoprotective effects against fibrosis, but the mechanisms remain unclear. Here we show that homeobox D8 (HOXD8) and PGC1-α are downregulated, while reactive oxygen species levels, mitochondrial dysfunction, and fibrosis are increased in kidney fibrosis models. HOXD8 overexpression increases PGC1-α expression, reduces reactive oxygen species, restores mitochondrial function, and suppresses profibrotic genes. Crocin upregulates HOXD8 and mitigates mitochondrial dysfunction and fibrosis. Mechanistically, HOXD8 binds the PGC1-α promoter and enhances its transcription. DNMT1-mediated promoter hypermethylation drives HOXD8 downregulation, and crocin reduces DNMT1 enrichment and activity at this promoter. Molecular docking and cellular thermal shift assay support a potential interaction between crocin and HOXD8, and crocin reduces HOXD8 ubiquitination. These findings suggest that crocin upregulates HOXD8 by inhibiting both its promoter hypermethylation and protein ubiquitination, thereby ameliorating mitochondrial dysfunction and fibrosis in chronic kidney disease (CKD).

papers.title: SUMOylation and ubiquitination of Viperin dynamically regulate the type I interferon-mediated antiviral response
papers.abstract: Viperin is a broad-spectrum antiviral protein induced by interferon. Viperin in epithelial cells is regulated and degraded by E3 ubiquitin ligase UBE4A. Here, we observed that UBE4A expression was deficient in immune cells such as splenocytes and macrophages, and elucidated how the protein stability and antiviral activity of Viperin are regulated under the condition of UBE4A deficiency. Specifically, PJA2 mediates K48-linked polyubiquitination of Viperin at K358, leading to proteasomal degradation and enhanced viral susceptibility. Upon viral infection, host upregulation of RANBP2 enhances Viperin SUMO3-ylation, which competitively inhibits ubiquitination, thereby stabilizing Viperin and suppressing viral replication. However, prolonged infection recruits SENP1, causing deSUMOylation that promotes Viperin degradation and facilitates immune evasion. Viperin SUMOylation is modulated by small-molecule inhibitors such as Momordin-Ic and SENP1-IN-1. This study reveals a synergistic antiviral mechanism mediated by Viperin ubiquitination and SUMOylation, and further deepen the understanding of the protein homeostasis of Viperin and its role in the antiviral immune response.

papers.title: A neutralizing monoclonal antibody targeting species B adenoviruses largely mimics the DSG2 receptor engagement mechanism
papers.abstract: Vassal-Stermann et al. identified two monoclonal antibodies that neutralize HAdV7 and cross-react with pathogenic species B adenoviruses. Cryo-EM reveals that the potent antibody 5C5 blocks the conserved DSG2 receptor-binding site at the fiber knob apex, defining a vulnerable target for broad neutralization.

papers.title: Albendazole induces ferroptosis through the USP7-GPX4 axis in B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia
papers.abstract: Albendazole, an FDA-approved antiparasitic drug, shows potent anti-leukemia activity in B-ALL by triggering ferroptosis. It targets the USP7-GPX4 pathway, promoting cancer cell death and revealing a promising drug-repurposing strategy and new therapeutic target for B-ALL.

papers.title: eDNA and microscopy reveal traits underlying long-term zooplankton community change
papers.abstract: Zooplankton form a vital link between phytoplankton and higher trophic levels, including commercially exploited fish, making recent declines in copepods and increases in meroplankton a major concern. To investigate underlying mechanisms, we compared weekly, high-resolution net (microscope analysis: 35 years) and surface water (eDNA: 11 years) from Station L4 in the Western English Channel. The two methods showed strong agreement for holoplanktonic crustaceans and gelatinous predators, but weaker correspondence for meroplankton. The far greater taxonomic insight from meroplankton groups provided by eDNA revealed a shift towards higher relative sequence abundance of soft sediment (mainly sublittoral) fauna, rather than from rocky nearshore. Trait-based analysis showed long-term increases were mainly fine filter feeders, including many meroplankton larvae. This suggests that changes in water column processes, linked to declining nutrient supply and a shift towards smaller phytoplankton, were contributing to broader changes in the pelagic food web and benthic-pelagic coupling.

papers.title: A NEST-based framework unlocks massively parallel simulation of networks of multi-compartment neurons with customizable subcellular dynamics
papers.abstract: While subcellular mechanisms in the dendrites of neurons govern the implementation of learning and memory in the brain, large-scale network simulations featuring such processes remain challenging to achieve. This can be attributed to a lack of appropriate software tools, as neuroscientific simulators focus on the one hand on highly detailed models, and on the other hand on massive networks featuring point neurons. Here, we fill this gap by implementing a framework for the massively parallel simulation of simplified dendrite models with customizable subcellular dynamics. We leverage the NEural Simulation Tool (NEST), the neuroscientific reference with respect to efficient massively parallel simulations of point-neuron networks. By co-opting the model description language NESTML, we generate C++ code implementing user-configurable subcellular dynamics. We show that the generated models run efficiently, leading to scalable NEST network simulations. To showcase relevant functionalities, we provide a proof-of-concept demonstration that a key sensory computation – the association of top-down context arriving at distal dendrites in layer 1 and feedforward sensory input arriving perisomatically – can be achieved in a single-shot fashion through apical calcium dynamics. Our work thus unlocks the study of how dendritic processes shape network function and learning at scale.

papers.title: White matter fiber bundles enable robust conduction and time-critical signaling despite axon caliber variation
papers.abstract: Axon caliber determines signal conduction velocity and varies within and across the bundles that form the brain’s wiring. Our knowledge of this organization derives largely from 2D histology, assuming cylindrical axons whose calibers are described by their radius. However, recent 3D histology reveals substantial along-axon variability in radius, calling into question 2D-derived insights into axon radius and conduction velocity. We show in 450,000 3D axon reconstructions from male rats that—despite this individual variation—axon bundles possess stable radius distributions at the ensemble level. These distributions are faithfully captured by 2D cross-sections and yield robust conduction velocity predictions, as along-axon variability has only a modest effect. Conduction in large axons is particularly stable, supporting time-critical signaling. With 2D sampling validated, we leverage 46 million human corpus callosum axons from 2D histology to determine sample size requirements across neuroscience applications. Our findings show how axonal organization gives rise to stable ensemble statistics and conduction, explaining and reinforcing decades of 2D histology-based research.

papers.title: Anisotropic light-electron-phonon coupling and ultrafast carrier separation in ferroelectric BaTiO 3
papers.abstract: Ferroelectric materials with built-in electric fields are useful for ultrafast electronics and conversion of light into electrical energy, yet the interaction of carrier motion with ultrafast relaxation processes remains nontrivial. Combining ultrafast electron diffraction with electron microscopy of electromagnetic fields, we capture ultrafast lattice dynamics and nanometer-scale carrier transport in ferroelectric BaTiO3. We demonstrated that BaTiO3 reacts to light with an anisotropic electron-phonon coupling that depends on the optical polarization of the excitation light. Excited electrons relax two times faster into phonons when the optical electric field aligns to the ferroelectric symmetry break. Furthermore, ultrafast electron electrometry captures the motion and separation of photo-excited electron-hole pairs in presence of the ferroelectric field. These combined results provide insight into the tangled and anisotropic interaction of photons with phonons and the ferroelectric field, producing phonons and voltages in a stepwise reaction path.

papers.title: Reconstruction of SARS-CoV-2 transmissibility within households in the UK Virus Watch Study
papers.abstract: Households provide an ideal setting to study SARS-CoV-2 transmission modes due to the close proximity and extended exposure among members. Understanding the patterns of who infects whom during infectious disease outbreaks is crucial for implementing effective control measures globally. Combining genomic data with epidemiological insights can help clarify and infer pathways of viral spread. We analyse SARS-CoV-2 whole genome sequences from 237 subjects across 162 households recruited to the Virus Watch Prospective Community Cohort Study (n = 372 total participants). We consider minority variants as an indicator of within-host genomic diversity and incorporate these into a phylogenetic model to reconstruct the relationships between genomes, leading to a more accurate reconstruction of transmission than if only the consensus variation were used. Here we show that of the 73 households with multiple infected participants, both consensus and within-host phylogenetic analyses identify eight households in which one or more secondary cases appear to arise from separate community introductions rather than within-household transmission. These households are excluded from the bottleneck and within-host transmission analyses. For the remaining 65 households, including minority variants when reconstructing phylogeny allows us to infer transmission chains that are otherwise uncertain with consensus variants only. Integrating within-host genetic diversity into a phylogenetic model alongside epidemiological data provides a robust approach to accurately identify true household transmission events, assess risk factors for infection acquisition and spread, and improve the estimation of the secondary attack rate When people in the same household get COVID-19, working out who infected whom is difficult using standard genetic testing, because the virus does not always change enough between people to leave clues. In this study, we used a more detailed type of analysis that looks at small, subtle differences in the virus within each person. By combining this with information about who lived together, we were able to identify household transmission events more accurately. We also examined how many virus particles typically pass from one person to another during transmission and found that transmission is usually established by a very small number of virus particles. This work helps improve our understanding of how respiratory viruses spread within families and could support future outbreak investigations.

papers.title: Synthesis and isolation of stable oxoboranes
papers.abstract: Oxoboranes are among the longest-sought species in main-group chemistry. Now, stable crystalline oxoboranes with exceptionally short and strong B–O bonds have been prepared through the reaction of a diboracumulene with carbonyl-bearing compounds.

papers.title: Crystalline neutral and cationic oxoboranes
papers.abstract: The isolation of oxoboranes featuring a genuine B–O triple bond is challenging owing to the instability of the B≡O linkage. Now stable crystalline oxoboranes have been prepared through a carbon-monoxide-triggered transformation, revealing a highly polarized B–O triple bond and enabling access to both neutral and cationic derivatives through ambiphilic reactivity.

papers.title: Combining anionic and neutral ligands for kinetic stereocontrol in nickel catalysis
papers.abstract: Substituted cyclohexanes are key motifs in drug discovery; therefore, stereoselective methods for their synthesis are valuable. However, the synthesis of thermodynamically disfavoured stereoisomers remains challenging. Now, a dual-ligand nickel system enables stereoselective three-component synthesis of substituted cyclohexanes, through Ni-catalysed 1,1-arylfunctionalization of substituted methylenecyclohexanes.

papers.title: Catalyst regeneration enables durable electrochemical ammonia cracking for H 2 production
papers.abstract: A Pt catalyst supported on N-doped C with isolated Fe sites is developed for electrochemical ammonia cracking towards H 2 production at 1.5 A cm −2 . The catalyst suppresses Pt oxidation and promotes the removal of poisonous N species, enabling stable operation for 500 h.

papers.title: A seed-confined strategy to alloy immiscible systems for methanol oxidation
papers.abstract: A thermodynamically guided seed-confined alloying strategy uses a single functional seed and a pre-anchored formation pathway to access nanoscale alloys from highly immiscible elements, enabling compositionally simple WBi–Pt@B/C catalysts with good methanol oxidation activity and durability.

papers.title: Structural improvements to address energy poverty had most substantial thermal comfort and health effects
papers.abstract: Energy poverty is a growing concern, but we still know little about which measures actually improve people’s health and living conditions. Here the authors find that structural measures and consistent financial support deliver the clearest benefits.

papers.title: Persistent and compartmentalized T cell immunity in ALS
papers.abstract: In ALS, persistent T cell responses relate to disease outcome differently in blood than in cerebrospinal fluid, with both intrathecal antigen presentation and cytomegalovirus-specific immunity linked to worse clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Manipulation of ER–mitochondria interactions with mitofusin modulators reduces cardiac damage during myocardial infarction in mice
papers.abstract: Axelrod, Nichtová et al. show that acute pharmacological modulation of mitofusins regulates ER/SR–mitochondria calcium transfer and markedly influences myocardial infarct size in mice, independently of mitochondrial fusion. Notably, mitofusin inhibition limits cardiac injury, even when administered at reperfusion, highlighting a potential therapeutic strategy for myocardial infarction.

papers.title: Radiographer fracture detection with and without AI assistance in prospective emergency department use
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems for fracture detection perform strongly in controlled settings, but prospective real-world evidence is limited. In a three-month deployment in one emergency department, thirteen radiographers in a radiographer-led screening programme independently interpreted 2496 consecutive musculoskeletal examinations (one radiographer per examination), reviewed output from a commercial deep-learning system, then recorded a final decision, giving 2496 paired reads against a radiologist reference standard. Standalone AI sensitivity was 75.6%, falling to 46.2% for subtle fractures, below the radiographers’ baseline sensitivity of 91.6%. Radiographers’ baseline accuracy was high (97.6%; specificity 99.0%) and improved modestly with AI assistance (98.0%; exact McNemar p = 0.0064). With AI assistance, radiographers corrected 11 errors and introduced 1, a net gain of 10 cases. Subgroup gains were directionally consistent but not significant after correction. Radiographers changed their decision in only 11 of 729 discordant cases, and most negative interactions were correct AI recommendations not adopted. No or incomplete AI output was returned for 8.8% of acquired examinations. AI assistance delivered a small, selective benefit arising from complementary rather than superior algorithmic performance. Operational reliability proved as consequential as diagnostic accuracy, and behavioural inferences rest on few events. Downstream clinical outcomes were not measured.

papers.title: An interpretable graph reasoning framework for enhanced diagnosis in fundus fluorescein angiography
papers.abstract: Fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA) is the gold standard for diagnosing retinal vascular diseases. However, interpretable artificial intelligence (AI) systems for FFA image analysis that align with clinicians’ reasoning processes and real-world diagnostic workflows remain scarce. In this study, we introduce an interpretable graph reasoning framework, FFA-RGNet, that explicitly models the temporal patterns of fine-grained lesions across imaging phases and anatomical locations for disease diagnosis from sequential FFA images. FFA-RGNet was trained and validated on a large, fine-grained, multi-center dataset consisting of 25,312 FFA images from 2651 patients. FFA-RGNet outperformed nine baseline models on the internal test set, achieving an F1-score of 95.38% (95% CI: 92.24%–97.88%), and demonstrated consistent performance across multi-center and prospective validation datasets. Its diagnostic performance not only surpassed that of ophthalmologists, residents and ophthalmology students, but also improved their diagnostic F1-score by 7.48% to 14.11% when used as an assistive tool. Comprehensive inference analysis further revealed its superior ability to correctly recognize fine-grained semantic entities, and to learn stable, disease-specific graph reasoning patterns aligned with clinical knowledge. These results suggest that FFA-RGNet enables accurate diagnosis with interpretable reasoning progresses, highlighting its strong potential as a reliable AI system for FFA interpretation and clinical decision support.

papers.title: Performance of artificial intelligence for fracture detection: an umbrella review and second-order-meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Fractures affect approximately 178 million people annually, and artificial intelligence (AI) tools for fracture detection are increasingly approved by regulators. We conducted an umbrella review and second-order meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD42024516414), searching six databases to 4/06/2025 for systematic reviews or meta-analyses of AI fracture detection using any imaging modality. Screening, extraction, and quality assessment were performed in duplicate. We assessed review quality using AMSTAR-2, primary-study overlap using corrected covered area, and certainty using GRADE. Fifty reviews were included (25 systematic reviews and 25 meta-analyses; 387 primary studies). Twenty-one meta-analyses (269 primary studies) contributed to second-order meta-analysis, with slight overall overlap (4.31%). Pooled AI sensitivity was 0.897 (95% CI 0.882–0.911; 95% prediction interval 0.753–0.962) and specificity 0.904 (95% CI 0.891–0.916; prediction interval 0.824 to 0.950). Comparative evidence showed no consistent differences for AI, clinicians, and AI-assisted clinicians: however, this data was sparse and inconclusive. No review reported adverse events or other safety outcomes. Certainty was very low/low for almost all outcomes; all meta-analyses were rated critically low/low on AMSTAR-2. Although published estimates suggest high diagnostic accuracy, real-world and comparative performance remain uncertain. Prospective external validation, multi-reader-multi-case studies, and randomised trials are needed before broad clinical adoption.

papers.title: Scalable drift monitoring in medical imaging AI
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into clinical medical imaging has advanced diagnostics but also poses challenges in maintaining long-term reliability as input data change. To address this, we present MMC+, a modular framework for scalable drift monitoring that builds on our CheXstray framework for real-time drift detection using multi-modal data concordance (MMC). MMC+ provides a flexible architecture that enables cost-effective continuous performance monitoring in real-world healthcare settings. The framework’s capabilities include aggregating information from multiple data streams using statistical tests or distance metrics, leveraging foundation model embeddings to remove the need for site-specific encoder training, and quantifying uncertainty to better communicate drift significance. Validated with data from Massachusetts General Hospital during the COVID-19 pandemic, MMC+ effectively detects significant data shifts that correlate with performance changes and indicates when AI systems may deviate from acceptable performance bounds. The code for MMC+ is publicly available (Link: https://github.com/FJDorfner/MedImaging-ModelDriftMonitoring/tree/MMC_plus), promoting broader adoption of AI solutions in clinical settings. Our framework significantly advances drift detection while promoting transparency and collaboration in clinical AI research.

papers.title: Mobile application-based digital therapeutics for frozen shoulder rehabilitation: a single-center, randomized controlled pilot study
papers.abstract: Digital therapeutics offer promising solutions for frozen shoulder rehabilitation. This single-center, assessor-blinded, randomized controlled pilot trial compared an AI-based digital therapeutic application (ANAPA ME) with YouTube-based home exercises in 18 patients with frozen shoulder. Following baseline assessments, patients were allocated to the digital therapeutics (DTx) or conventional rehabilitation (CON) group, received a single ultrasound-guided intra-articular corticosteroid injection, and completed a 12-week exercise program. Assessments at weeks 0, 2, 4, 8, and 12 included passive range of motion (ROM), Visual Analog Scale (VAS), Constant Shoulder Score (CSS), Shoulder Pain and Disability Index (SPADI), and EuroQol-5 Dimension-5 Level (EQ-5D-5L). At 12 weeks, the DTx group achieved significantly greater side external rotation ROM (p = 0.04) and improvement from baseline (p = 0.042). EQ-5D-5L showed a significant group × time interaction (p = 0.048), with greater improvement from baseline in the DTx group (p = 0.013). No significant between-group differences were observed in VAS, SPADI, or CSS. These findings suggest that AI-based digital therapeutics may offer preliminary advantages in side external rotation ROM and health-related quality of life over conventional video-based exercises, though confirmation in larger trials is needed. This trial was registered with the Clinical Research Information Service, Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency (registration number: PRE20250113-001) on January 13, 2025.

papers.title: Fast and Selective Photochemical Doping of Spiro‐OMeTAD
papers.abstract: Small Methods, EarlyView.

papers.title: Electrochemical Synthesis of Silver Icosahedrons for SERS Sensing Applications
papers.abstract: Small Methods, EarlyView.

papers.title: Cation Vacancy‐Modulated NiOOH for Electro‐Oxidative Alcohol Dehydrogenation and Amide Synthesis Coupled With Hydrogen Evolution
papers.abstract: Small Methods, EarlyView.

papers.title: Rapid Flow Synthesis of Zr‐MOF Nanoparticles in Supercritical CO2 for Toxic Chemical Removal
papers.abstract: Small Methods, EarlyView.

papers.title: Continuous mass photometry by single-molecule trapping
papers.abstract: Continuous mass photometry enables high-resolution observation of biomolecular masses and mass changes.

papers.title: Chemical signal driven supramolecular network evolution for cancer mitochondrial targeting
papers.abstract: Disease-responsive supramolecular hydrogels could enable selective therapy, but adaptive structural reorganization remains challenging. Here, the authors show that a supramolecular hydrogel responds to H₂O₂ by reorganizing into a self-sorted double network, enabling selective cancer cell killing while largely sparing non-malignant cells.

papers.title: Real-time imaging of cobalt mobility in graphite at elevated temperatures for advanced nuclear applications
papers.abstract: High-temperature radionuclide retention is critical for the safe operation of Gen IV graphite-moderated reactors. Here, the authors report, using real-time in situ SEM, that cobalt remains largely immobile in graphite at reactor-relevant temperatures, with significant release occurring only near 1100°C.

papers.title: Light-regulated biomaterial interfaces enable flexible neural bioelectronics with stable adhesion and on-demand detachment for chronic electrophysiology
papers.abstract: Dynamic bioelectronic interfaces are required to simultaneously ensure stable tissue integration for chronic recording and controllable debonding for device reconfiguration or retrieval. This challenge is particularly acute for implantable neural interfaces, where weak adhesion compromises signal fidelity, while permanent adhesion may cause secondary tissue damage during removal. Here, we developed a photo-programmable neural biointerface incorporating a self-healing bPDMS@Fe matrix based on a carboxyl-functionalized polydimethylsiloxane network dynamically crosslinked by Fe3+-carboxylate coordination. The resulting electrode exhibits robust adhesion to diverse substrates and biological tissues, as well as on-demand removal through UV-induced adhesion weakening. Moreover, it supports stable epidermal electrocardiogram recording under various conditions. Furthermore, the biointerface is translated into a 9-channel cortical electrode array that enables stable local field potential recording and spatiotemporal mapping of seizure-associated neural activity in freely moving mice. This work establishes a dynamic adhesive strategy as a new materials design paradigm for neural bioelectronic interfaces toward next-generation chronic electrophysiological monitoring devices.

papers.title: Sexually dimorphic transdifferentiation of endothelial cells in atherosclerosis
papers.abstract: Sex differences in atherosclerosis are clinically recognized, but the contribution of endothelial cell (EC) states and fates to these differences remain incompletely understood. Here, we used EC lineage tracing in male and female Apoe−/−/Cdh5-CreERT2/Rosa26-mTmG mice fed a high-fat diet and performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing of plaque-bearing aortae. We identified nine sex-biased EC subpopulations, including capillary, lymphatic, Sox17+, Myh11+, Mki67+, and Ly6a+ ECs enriched in females and Col8a1+ and Fmo2+ ECs enriched in males. GeneTrajectory analysis and lineage tracing indicated that approximately one quarter of GFP⁺ EC-lineage cells transit into adipocyte-like, SMC-like, or fibroblast-like states. EC-to-SMC-like transitions were more prominent in females, whereas EC-to-adipocyte-like transitions were more prominent in males. Regulatory network analysis using pySCENIC implicated Klf2 and Creb5 in EC fate decisions. These findings reveal sex-specific EC-lineage trajectories associated with distinct plaque phenotypes and nominate candidates for sex-informed therapeutic investigation.

papers.title: Efficient structural information integration into protein language models with implicit mixture-of-experts ProBEiT
papers.abstract: ProBEiT integrates protein sequence and tokenized structure with deterministic implicit MoE routing, enabling efficient sequence structure modeling and strong performance in fitness prediction and thermostability engineering.

papers.title: Hierarchical distortions in structure-function coupling linked to multiscale neurobiological characteristics in autism
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder is associated with widespread alterations in brain connectivity, but how structural and functional networks are jointly reorganized remains unclear. Here, we show that autism is associated with altered structure-function coupling, particularly in the hierarchical organization of sensory and association systems. Using brain imaging data from 91 individuals with autism and 67 typically developing controls, we model functional connectivity from structural networks using Riemannian optimization and examine communication across multiple steps. In the resulting simulated networks, hierarchical organization is comparable between groups at lower communication steps but becomes less differentiated in autism as communication extends across multiple steps. These alterations are associated with excitation/inhibition alterations, neurotransmitter distributions, gene expression, and multisensory processing. We also identify atypical connectivity involving the thalamus and putamen. Importantly, greater hierarchical distortion predicts more severe autistic symptoms, linking macroscale network organization with neurobiology and behavior. These findings highlight hierarchical structure-function coupling as a potential framework for understanding biological and behavioral characteristics in autism.

papers.title: A glutamatergic projection from the central medial thalamic nucleus to the red nucleus regulates states of consciousness during sevoflurane anesthesia in mice
papers.abstract: General anesthetics like sevoflurane are clinically essential, yet the neural circuits governing their induction of unconsciousness and recovery remain incompletely defined. Here, we show the potential involvement of the vesicular glutamate transporter 2 (Vglut2)-expressing glutamatergic neurons in the central medial thalamus (CMTVglut2 neurons) in modulation states of consciousness under sevoflurane anesthesia. Results show that CMTVglut2 neuron activity revealed a reduction during the loss of consciousness and a subsequent elevation upon recovery of consciousness under sevoflurane anesthesia. Chemogenetic activation of CMTVglut2 neurons delays induction and hastened recovery from sevoflurane anesthesia. Moreover, during sustained sevoflurane anesthesia at steady state, optogenetic activation of CMTVglut2 neurons facilitates cortical activation and behavioral recovery. During burst suppression under sevoflurane, this stimulation elicits cortical arousal and declines the burst-suppression ratio. Conversely, inhibiting CMTVglut2 neurons via chemogenetic or optogenetic methods produces greater sensitivity to sevoflurane anesthesia and deepens cortical suppression, respectively. Monosynaptic connections from CMTVglut2 neurons to red nucleus glutamatergic neurons (RNVglut2 neurons) are identified using combined retrograde and anterograde tracing. During sevoflurane anesthesia, optogenetic activation of CMTVglut2-RN terminals triggers cortical activation. Overall, these findings identify the CMTVglut2-RN pathway as a neural circuit regulating cortical activation and behavioral arousal under various stages of sevoflurane-induced anesthesia.

papers.title: Directed differentiation with mechanical simulation enhances alveolar-like features in human pluripotent stem cell-derived lung epithelium
papers.abstract: hPSC-derived distal bud tip organoids that resemble fetal alveolar progenitors are developed and used to show that air-liquid interface culture and cyclic stretch enhance alveolar epithelial maturation and increased segregation of AT1- and AT2-associated cell states.

papers.title: Whole brain modeling reveals subtype specific regulation for adolescent major depressive disorder
papers.abstract: Adolescent major depressive disorder exhibits substantial intrinsic subtype heterogeneity, necessitating the development of subtype-specific therapeutic strategies. Using the Boston Adolescent Neuroimaging of Depression and Anxiety dataset, we identified two subtypes with distinct clinical features. For each subtype, we constructed a whole-brain model and performed virtual stimulation to assess regulatory effects at global (whole-brain) and regional (classical depression-related targets) levels. Here we show that the two subtypes require different but stable stimulation modalities, excitatory or inhibitory, to normalize brain activity. Optimal stimulation intensities for restoring static and dynamic features vary across targets and subtypes, whereas the stimulation modality remains consistent within each subtype. Notably, localized stimulation of subtype-specific targets within classical depression-related regions produces more effective and stable outcomes than whole-brain stimulation. These findings provide a computational framework for identifying subtype-specific regulatory strategies in adolescent major depressive disorder, bridging whole-brain modeling with potential clinical translation.

papers.title: Forced expression of UCP1 counteracts the compromised activity of NK cells in the tumor microenvironment
papers.abstract: UCP1 loss in tumor-infiltrating NK cells drives CD36/FABP4-dependent fatty acid oxidation, mitochondrial DNA release and NLRP3-mediated pyroptosis. Restoring UCP1 preserves NK cell function and antitumor activity in mouse tumor models and patient-derived colorectal cancer organoids.

papers.title: Targeting central thalamus with transcranial ultrasound reduces arousal in healthy volunteers
papers.abstract: Transcranial ultrasound stimulation causally links the central thalamus to arousal and the pulvinar to visuospatial attention in the healthy human brain.

papers.title: Quantitative imaging supports that endoskeletal mineralization in sharks is an adaptive trait
papers.abstract: We quantify whole-body skeletal mineralization across a broad phylogenetic diversity of sharks using quantitative CT. Skeletal mineralization varies extensively among species and is associated with ecological traits, particularly habitat depth.

papers.title: Crystallographic origin of pressure-induced bond order in the frustrated spinel CuIr 2 S 4
papers.abstract: CuIr2S4 is a frustrated pyrochlore spinel in which pressure reshapes competing charge- and bond-ordered states. Here we determine the crystallographic nature of its pressure-induced ordered phases up to about 25 GPa by high-pressure synchrotron powder X-ray diffraction combined with first-principles-guided structural analysis. Pressure first stabilizes the ambient-pressure low-temperature ordered state to room temperature and then induces a distinct high-pressure phase. Using single-phase datasets collected at 19.8 and 25.7 GPa, we perform full-atom refinements that consistently establish the Phase-IV symmetry and Ir–Ir short-bond topology. The resulting Phase IV pattern differs from Phase II and is not captured by a simple orbitally induced Peierls picture. Instead, it is consistent with an Anderson-type local tetrahedron rule on the pyrochlore lattice. Total-energy calculations reproduce a pressure-induced reversal in the relative stability of the Phase-II- and Phase-IV-type structural models.

papers.title: Multi-omics liquid biopsy identifies mitochondrial dysfunction in geographic atrophy and supports intraocular bioavailability of α-ketoglutarate
papers.abstract: The authors sample fluid from inside the living human eye to profile mitochondrial proteins in geographic atrophy and to test whether an oral supplement reaches the eye. They find widespread mitochondrial protein loss in disease and show that oral alpha-ketoglutarate enters the eye and shifts its energy metabolism.

papers.title: Plasma concentrations of gut microbial tryptophan metabolites and risk of complications after colorectal cancer surgery
papers.abstract: Klaassen-Dekker et al. investigate whether plasma indole metabolites are linked to complications after surgery in 1222 patients with colorectal cancer. Higher concentrations of indole-3-acetamide and indole-3-propionate were associated with a lower risk of complications, and preoperative fiber intake is a determinant of these indole concentrations.

papers.title: Changing sarcopenia diagnostic criteria from AWGS2019 to 2025 impacts prevalence and postoperative risk prediction
papers.abstract: Liu et al compare the updated 2025 sarcopenia diagnostic criteria against 2019 criteria in a major surgical cohort, assessing impacts on prevalence and prediction of postoperative outcomes. The updated criteria identify a subgroup with low muscle strength who are at higher risk of needing post-discharge support, without affecting overall prevalence.

papers.title: Enzymatic oxidative esterification with an unconventional regioselective control
papers.abstract: Regioselective esterification remains challenging, particularly when multiple alcohol groups with similar reactivity are present. Now it has been shown that aldehyde dehydrogenases can be engineered into oxidative ester synthases with programmable alcohol selectivity, enabling controlled ester bond formation through active-site remodelling.

papers.title: Three-dimensional cell morphology is mediated by curvature sensing and interfacial stress
papers.abstract: Cells adhering to micro-curved surfaces can exhibit either complete adhesion or partial interior detachment. This is now found to be determined by the balance between the cell contractile stress and the cell–substrate adhesion stress.

papers.title: Machine learning dataset and benchmark for accurate T cell receptor–pHLA binding prediction
papers.abstract: A central challenge in immunology and therapeutic design is accurately predicting the diverse interactions between T cell receptors and peptide–human leukocyte antigen (pHLA) complexes. Existing machine learning tools are hindered by incomplete sequence data and biased nonbinding examples. Here we present Hi-TPH, a large-scale hierarchical dataset featuring an on-the-fly selection method for generating nonbinding data. We further develop Hi-TPH-PLMs, a collection of protein language models (PLMs) with varied architectures and scales, fine-tuned on Hi-TPH. These models achieve a 19.2% performance gain over state-of-the-art tools on an external wet-lab test set. Leveraging the hierarchical structure of Hi-TPH, detailed analyses dissect the contribution of different molecular components to binding prediction and reveal their synergistic interplay; for instance, the prediction contribution of HLA relies on the presence of full T cell receptor chains. Hi-TPH and Hi-TPH-PLMs are publicly released to support the development of more reliable tools for advanced immunoinformatics research and personalized immunotherapy. Hi-TPH is a large-scale hierarchical dataset that enables more accurate prediction of T cell receptor binding to antigens using protein language models and reveals how molecular components jointly contribute to prediction.

papers.title: Neoadjuvant durvalumab plus chemotherapy in resectable or borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer: the phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE trial
papers.abstract: As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026: In the global phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE trial, neoadjuvant durvalumab plus chemotherapy in patients with resectable and borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer, followed by multidisciplinary reassessment, enabled surgery in most patients, leading to encouraging pathological complete response rates, and no additional safety concerns were reported when patients with unresectable tumors continued with chemoradiotherapy and consolidative durvalumab.

papers.title: Bioengineering strategies for prenatal therapy
papers.abstract: Congenital and genetic disorders often cause death or lifelong disability, and treatments after birth are frequently unable to reverse the effects of established diseases. In utero therapies, which intervene during fetal development, offer an opportunity to treat conditions early, as demonstrated by existing fetal surgical therapies. Advances in bioengineering have expanded these approaches and improved their precision and potential effectiveness. However, challenges related to the safe delivery of therapies and the careful consideration of risks to both the mother and the fetus remain. In this Review, we examine emerging bioengineering strategies for fetal treatments, including tissue engineering, stem cell transplantation and gene-based approaches. We further discuss how these methods could overcome existing limitations and improve the translation of in utero therapies into clinical use. The fetal environment is characterized by rapid regeneration, superior wound healing and a relatively tolerogenic immune system compared with the postnatal state, making it an ideal setting to treat many congenital and genetic diseases. This Review discusses in utero bioengineering strategies to address unmet clinical needs and conditions that have no, or inadequate, treatments.

papers.title: Programmable mRNA vaccine materials for temporal control of antitumour immunity
papers.abstract: Advances in mRNA and nanomaterial design have transformed vaccine technology, enabling precise control of antigen expression, delivery kinetics and immune activation. However, several leading clinical-stage mRNA cancer vaccine programmes are being evaluated in the adjuvant setting, in which loss of the primary tumour antigen reservoir and evolving postoperative immune states may alter the conditions for effective priming. Here, we present a materials-driven framework for temporal immunoengineering, in which programmable mRNA vaccine materials are designed to align antigen availability, innate sensing and adaptive priming with changing immune states across the perioperative window. Using the perioperative period as an illustrative model of immune flux, we discuss how distinct mRNA nanocarrier architectures can be engineered to tune the timing, magnitude and anatomical context of innate activation, antigen expression and adaptive priming. A universal neoadjuvant mRNA ‘prime’, formulated in an immunostimulatory nanocarrier, could condition innate and myeloid compartments and remodel the tumour microenvironment, whereas a personalized adjuvant ‘boost’, delivered in translationally efficient formulations, could reinforce clonal expansion and memory of tumour-specific T cells. By treating biomaterials as programmable regulators of immunodynamics rather than passive carriers, this Perspective establishes temporal control as a complementary design axis for next-generation mRNA vaccine systems. mRNA cancer vaccines offer programmable control over antigen expression and immune activation, but their clinical performance may depend on when and where these signals occur. This Perspective introduces temporal immunoengineering and proposes phase-matched mRNA nanocarrier designs to coordinate immune priming and reinforcement across the perioperative window.

papers.title: Decoding the risks of hydrogels for bone regeneration
papers.abstract: Engineered hydrogels provide hydrated, tunable and biointeractive matrices for bone regeneration, but few have advanced from preclinical promise to defined clinical indications. This translational gap reflects application-specific failure in dynamic bone microenvironments rather than a lack of material innovation alone. In this Review, we decode hydrogel risks across craniofacial filling, long-bone reconstruction, osteochondral repair, local drug delivery, cell delivery, implant coating and oral modulation of metabolic bone disease. We organize these failures into mechanical gap, spatiotemporal mismatch and immune dysregulation and further identify emerging long-term and systemic risks. Finally, we position experimental hydrogels against clinical products, manufacturability constraints and large-animal benchmarks to propose risk-controlled design principles for next-generation bone-regenerative hydrogels. Hydrogels offer adaptable matrices for bone regeneration, yet clinical translation remains limited by application-specific failures in dynamic skeletal environments. This Review organizes these failures into mechanical, spatiotemporal and immune risks and outlines translational benchmarks and risk-controlled design principles.

papers.title: Midkine as a context-dependent molecular rheostat in tissue regeneration and aging
papers.abstract: Midkine (MDK) is a dynamic molecular rheostat that operates differently depending on tissue context. It is widely induced after injury across multiple systems, including cardiovascular, neural, musculoskeletal, liver, and kidneys, yet its regulation often becomes disrupted with aging. MDK is also linked to fibrosis, immune aging, and tumor development. In this review, we discuss MDK effects in three tissue injury models and emerging therapeutic approaches to leverage MDK’s rheostat function.

papers.title: Systemwide adoption patterns of ambient AI scribe technology in an integrated academic health system
papers.abstract: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes may reduce documentation burden, but little is known about their adoption during enterprise-scale ambulatory rollout. We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study of 2901 ambulatory clinicians at an integrated academic health system using linked electronic health record and vendor usage data from December 2024 through May 2025. Clinician adoption was defined as any use during the study period, and monthly visit-level uptake as the proportion of eligible ambulatory visits in which the ambient AI scribe was used. Adoption and uptake varied substantially across practice settings, specialties, and clinician types. Clinician-level adoption was highest in community internal medicine (67%), community general pediatrics (69%), and academic neurology (53%), and lowest in academic general surgery (16%), obstetrics and gynecology (18%), and psychiatry (19%). Community attending physicians and advanced practice providers showed marked increases in median visit-level uptake, reaching approximately 80%-90% in some groups by May 2025. Distinct longitudinal patterns included slow and steady adoption, early use followed by discontinuation, transient use, and late adoption. These findings suggest that implementation support and evaluation strategies should be tailored to local practice context rather than applied uniformly across a health system.

papers.title: Multicentre benchmark of PSMA PET/CT and mpMRI fusion for non-invasive clinically significant prostate cancer diagnosis
papers.abstract: Clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) guides-biopsy and treatment decisions, yet its non-invasive diagnosis remains challenging. The incremental value of PSMA PET/CT beyond multiparametric MRI (mpMRI), and the optimal strategy for multimodal fusion, remain unclear. We established a real-world, multicentre benchmark using 527 patients from three hospitals with fully paired PSMA PET, CT, T2-weighted MRI, and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), together with pathology-confirmed biopsy labels. Models were developed in one centre (n = 363) and independently evaluated in two external centres (n = 164). We compared frozen pretrained encoders, fine-tuned 2D and 3D CNN and Vision Transformer models, three fusion strategies, and an interpretable cross-modal Transformer. PSMA PET provided the greatest incremental value, with its removal producing the largest AUC reduction internally (−0.077) and externally (−0.055), supported by the highest attention attribution (αPET = 0.45). PSMA PET/CT also outperformed mpMRI externally (AUC 0.753 vs. 0.653). DWI was the principal source of domain shift, as its exclusion improved external AUC by 0.079 amid inter-centre b-value heterogeneity. Intermediate fusion performed most consistently internally, whereas late fusion and pretrained 2D models generalised better externally. This benchmark supports robust, non-invasive csPCa diagnosis by identifying modalities and fusion strategies that generalise reliably across institutions.

papers.title: GliaDose: An alternative approach for clinical CAR-T dose prediction via PBPK–glioblastoma-on-a-chip integration
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive brain tumor with poor prognosis and limited treatment options. Chimeric antigen receptor T cell (CAR-T) therapy has emerged as a promising immunotherapy for GBM. However, unlike conventional drugs, CAR-T cells are living therapeutics that exhibit non-linear pharmacokinetics, expansion, and complex tissue trafficking, making conventional animal-to-human dose extrapolation unreliable. Furthermore, species-specific differences and the vasculature limit the translational relevance of preclinical models. To address these challenges, we developed GliaDose, a hybrid framework that integrates physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling with a vascularized glioblastoma-on-a-chip (GoC) platform to support quantitative first-in-human dose (FIHD) prediction for CAR-T therapy. The PBPK model was parameterized exclusively with human physiological data and incorporates a brain-tumor compartment to explicitly capture CAR-T transport across the vasculature. Complementarily, the GoC platform recapitulates key features of the GBM microenvironment, including three-dimensional tumor architecture, extracellular matrix, and perfusable human vascular networks, enabling assessment of CAR-T transmigration under flow conditions. Integration of GoC-derived efficacy data into the PBPK framework enabled quantitative dose–response predictions and identified vascular barriers as critical determinants of CAR-T tumor access. GliaDose provides a human-relevant, mechanistic alternative to animal-based dose selection and may improve FIHD prediction and personalized CAR-T therapy for GBM.

papers.title: Visual-affective decoding enhances neurofunctional objective and generalizable signatures in unseen adolescent depression diagnosis
papers.abstract: Adolescent major depressive disorder is a highly prevalent and debilitating condition, yet objective and generalizable neurofunctional signatures remain elusive. Existing neuroimaging approaches largely rely on resting-state fMRI, or controlled tasks often lack ecological validity and generalizable signatures of depression-related neural dysfunctions. This study proposes a Visual–Affective Decoding (VAD) framework integrating cross-subject visual and affective decoding from whole-brain fMRI acquired during naturalistic movie viewing. A dual-pathway anomaly detection model trained exclusively on healthy controls establishes normative brain function and identifies MDD through deviations from this norm. In 200 adolescents (112 MDD, 88 HC), VAD achieved an AUC of 0.87, 95.56% sensitivity, 83.89% accuracy, and 72.22% specificity. Using the same anomaly threshold, it generalized to an independent external adolescent cohort (70 MDD, 68 HC), achieving an AUC of 0.81 with an accuracy of 75.36%, supporting its cross-site generalizability. VAD further revealed interpretable neurofunctional signatures, including blunted emotional reactivity, attenuated visual representation, and affective patterns consistent with emotional rumination. Region-level contribution analyses identified dissociable visual- and affective-sensitive cortical regions, consistent with dysfunctions in visual, default-mode, salience, and higher-order associative networks. These findings demonstrate that VAD provides objective, interpretable, and generalizable neurofunctional signatures for adolescent depression diagnosis and clinically relevant biomarker development.

papers.title: Solvated‐Electron‐Driven Intercalation Enables Electron‐Rich KxNbS2 Construction and Exfoliation
papers.abstract: Small Methods, EarlyView.

papers.title: Symmetry‐Breaking Polarized Ir‐COFs With Ultralow Exciton Binding Energy Enable Directional Charge Allocation for Synergistic Photocatalytic Gold Recovery and BPA Photodegradation
papers.abstract: Small Methods, EarlyView.

papers.title: Scanless Centimeter‐Scale Microstereolithography Enabled by Source‐Plane Angular Conditioning
papers.abstract: Small Methods, EarlyView.

papers.title: Polarity‐Mediated β‐Phase Reconstruction and Dual‐Salt Synergy for Fast Li+ Transport in Solid‐State Li Metal Batteries
papers.abstract: Small Methods, EarlyView.

papers.title: ctDNA clearance and outcomes for resectable lung cancer from NeoCOAST-2
papers.abstract: Patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain at high risk of relapse despite perioperative treatment1-3. NeoCOAST-2 (NCT05061550), a phase 2, randomised platform trial, tested novel perioperative treatments in patients with stage IIA–IIIB NSCLC. At primary analysis, combining standard chemotherapy plus durvalumab (anti-PD-L1 antibody) with oleclumab (Arm 1, n = 76), monalizumab (Arm 2, n = 72) or datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd; Arm 4, n = 54) resulted in pathological complete response (pCR) rates of 20.3%, 25.7%, and 35.2%, respectively4. Here, we present the first report of prespecified secondary endpoints of event-free survival (EFS) and circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) clearance, and exploratory analyses of associations between ctDNA dynamics and clinical outcomes. The 24-month EFS rates were 70.5%, 75.7% and 77.9% in Arms 1, 2 and 4, respectively. Using a tumour-agnostic assay, ctDNA clearance at neoadjuvant Cycle 3 Day 1 was highest in Arm 4 (50.9%, 54.5%, and 72.5% in each arm, respectively). ctDNA clearance correlated with prolonged EFS versus non-clearance (pooled hazard ratio (HR) 0.22; 95% CI = 0.11–0.45, P = 0.0000443). Patients with both ctDNA clearance and pCR had favourable EFS outcomes versus those with neither (EFS HR 0.10, 95% CI = 0.02–0.42, P = 0.002). These findings suggest combined assessment of ctDNA clearance and pCR may improve risk stratification, and that the numerically highest pCR4 and EFS rates with the Dato-DXd combination warrant further evaluation.

papers.title: A role for the BBSome in restricting the entry of non-ciliary proteins into cilia
papers.abstract: Investigating how non-ciliary proteins enter cilia in Caenorhabditis elegans shows that defective cargo loading onto intraflagellar transport, rather than ciliary gate failure, alters ciliary protein composition.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomic insights into conserved and divergent oligodendrocyte lineage programs across species
papers.abstract: Oligodendrocyte lineage cells (OLLCs) are essential for myelination and neuronal homeostasis, yet the evolutionary conservation of their transcriptional programs remains unclear. Here, we integrated approximately one million hippocampal single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomes from humans, rhesus macaques, cynomolgus macaques, and mice. OLLCs emerged as among the most evolutionarily conserved neural cell populations, with oligodendrocyte precursor cells exhibiting highly conserved transcriptional identities, whereas mature oligodendrocytes displayed greater species-specific diversification We identified evolutionarily divergent genes, including the primate-specific gene CNDP1, and uncovered a species-specific temporal shift of the transcription factor ETV1 during oligodendrocyte differentiation. Cross-species analysis of aging revealed conserved chromatin-regulatory programs together with species-specific aging signatures, including coordinated remodeling of a primate-specific Wnt regulatory network in primate OPCs, whereas aged mouse OPCs were enriched for ribosome biogenesis. Disease-risk signatures further underscore the involvement of OLLCs in neurological disorders. Together, these findings provide a comparative framework for understanding mammalian myelin biology, brain aging, and disease.

papers.title: Flat Chern bands and correlated states in spiral magnet
papers.abstract: Flat topological bands provide a promising platform for realizing exotic correlated quantum phases such as fractional Chern insulators. Here, we predict the van der Waals monolayer ReAg2Cl6 hosts isolated flat Chern bands at the Fermi level in its 120∘ antiferromagnetic ground state. Their flatness and nontrivial topology arise from the interplay between coplanar spin order and strong spin-orbit coupling within Re 5d orbitals, providing a mechanism distinct from moiré systems. The spiral spin texture naturally enlarges the unit cell, reducing carrier densities while preserving sizable interaction scales. Many-body calculations show that fractional fillings of the flat bands can stabilize correlated phases, including fractional Chern insulators and charge-density-wave states. Moreover, the mechanism is generic to a broad family of Re-based compounds, with both spin configuration and flat band topology electrically tunable. These findings establish Re-based coplanar antiferromagnets as a robust, tunable, and experimentally accessible platform for flat Chern bands and correlated topological phases potentially at elevated temperatures.

papers.title: Multilayer 3D/2D Perovskite Heterojunctions: Structural Engineering, Interfacial Modulation, and Photovoltaic Applications
papers.abstract: Small Methods, EarlyView.

papers.title: Depth‐Aware Machine Learning for 3D Reconstruction of Fibrous Porous Electrodes by FIB‐SEM Tomography
papers.abstract: Small Methods, EarlyView.

papers.title: Chelation-immobilized gadolinium and dynamic crosslinking enable high-efficiency nuclear radiation shielding polymers
papers.abstract: Polymer radiation shields suffer from poor dispersion and metal leaching. Here, the authors developed a dynamically crosslinked gadolinium-grafted polymer that combines high radiation shielding, mechanical toughness, flexibility, and reusability.

papers.title: Supramolecular nucleotide hydrogel as an artificial carbonic anhydrase for CO 2 sequestration
papers.abstract: Natural metalloenzymes exhibit high catalytic efficiency, but replicating their complexity synthetically remains challenging.
